jobs.title: Coordinateur/rice des Finances - RCA
jobs.description:
INTERSOS est une Organisation Humanitaire Non Gouvernementale, à but non lucratif, qui a l’objectif d’assister les victimes de désastres naturels et de conflits armés. INTERSOS base son action sur les valeurs de la solidarité, de la justice, de la dignité humaine, de l’égalité des droits et des opportunités pour tous les peuples, du respect des diversités, de la cohabitation, de l’attention aux groupes sociales les plus vulnérables.

## **Termes de référence**

**Intitulé du poste** : Coordinateur/trice des Finances

**Code :** SR-46-10112

**Pays :** République Centrafricaine (RCA)

**Lieu d’affectation** : Bangui avec des déplacements dans les zones de mise en oeuvre du projet.

**Date de prise de fonction** :16/11/2026

**Durée du contrat** : 6 mois

**Sous la supervision de :** Chef de mission

**Supervision fonctionnelle :** Regional Finance

**Supervision de :** Responsable des finances

**Lieu d'affectation:** sans famille

## **Contexte général du projet**

La République Centrafricaine est un pays qui a traversé plus de deux décennies des différentes crises multiformes notamment l’instabilité politique avec le renversement des régimes à travers les coups d’Etat, les conflits intercommunautaires entre les Sélékas et les Antibalakas,…

Outre ce conflits armés nous pouvons signaler également la multiplicité des forces et groupes armés dans ce pays entre notamment : l’UPC, 3R, les ex AAKG.

Grâce à la fragilité et la volatilité de la situation sécuritaire au pays, le gouvernement a bénéficié de l’appui militaire de la MINUSCA des mercenaires russes (Wagner) opérants en appui aux forces armées centrafricaines (FACA) dans les zones de Nana-Gbirizi, Bamingui-Bangoran et un bataillon des forces une force multinationale agissant sous le mandat des nations unies. A cela s’ajoute la brigade d’interventions spéciales des forces de défenses du Rwanda en ajout à la sécurité présidentielle.

Une nouvelle constitution a été adoptée en 2Août 2023. Malgré cette adoption le pays a été plongé par une nouvelle crise. En Juillet 2025 un accord de paix a été signé entre le gouvernement et les deux grandes factions rebelles. Une situation qui n’a pas été plus inclusive suite à la méfiance des certains autres groupes rebelles qui ont boycotté le processus de cantonnement et de désarment.

Depuis plus d'une decenie INTERSOS a ouvert son bureau en RCA pour répondre aux beosins humanitaires des populations vulnérables en protection (VBG et protection générale, protection de l'enface), Santé, CCCM, Abris, NFIs et Wash.

## **Objectif général de la position**

Gérer et superviser la gestion économique et financière de la mission (comptabilité, trésorerie, procédures d'audit, etc.) dans le respect des obligations légales et des normes et protocoles INTERSOS afin de fournir une information de qualité, fiable et transparente sur l'utilisation et l'allocation des ressources de la mission.

## **Principales responsabilités et tâches**

### **Comptabilité et budget**

- Dans le cas où il n'y a pas de responsable comptable dans la mission, est responsable de la qualité et de la comptabilité en temps opportun pour l'ensemble de la mission, par exemple les procédures de trésorerie, les transactions des comptes bancaires, les reçus et les documents administratifs et financiers à l'appui, la saisie électronique des données, la consolidation de la comptabilité globale de la mission, les subventions, le processus de clôture mensuelle, le rapprochement bancaire et les documents, en veillant au strict respect des délais et à la conformité aux directives d'INTERSOS et des bailleurs de fonds, Normes et procédures financières
- Est la référence technique pour toute question liée à la gestion financière : budgétisation, allocation des coûts directs et indirects, reporting financier des bailleurs de fonds, conformité fiscale, audit annuel légal et audit des bailleurs de fonds.
- En collaboration avec le coordinateur financier, soutient la préparation du budget annuel de la mission conformément aux prévisions financières et économiques et aux exigences applicables d'INTERSOS (protocoles, lignes directrices, SoP...), en assurant la collaboration
- Soutenir le chef de projet / programme dans la préparation de la prolongation sans frais et de la révision du budget
- Superviser le niveau de liquidité de la mission (trésorerie et banque) et signaler rapidement les écarts dans le livre de caisse au coordonnateur des finances pays

### **Conformité**

- Est chargé d'appuyer le Coordonnateur des finances pays dans le suivi des indicateurs clés de performance économiques et financiers de la mission.
- Est responsable de la gestion financière des contrats avec les bailleurs de fonds, de la préparation et de la vérification de l'adéquation des informations et de la documentation des rapports financiers (intermédiaires et définitifs), ainsi que du suivi et de l'analyse des besoins en matière d'amendements. S'assurer que les exigences en matière de rapports sont respectées.
- Évaluer la pertinence des pièces justificatives pour l'audit (interne et externe).
- Dans le cas où l'organigramme ne prévoit pas le responsable comptable, coordonner et superviser la conduite des audits locaux relatifs à la comptabilité, à la fiscalité, à la main-d'œuvre, à la gestion des stocks et des actifs.
- Garantissez la bonne répartition des coûts sur les subventions en utilisant les modèles pertinents des protocoles.

### **Liquidité**

- Vérifier le déblocage des versements conformément au Contrat et faire le suivi en cas de retard
- Collaborer avec les gestionnaires de projets et de programmes à la mise à jour du plan financier.

### **Administration**

- Traiter le paiement en garantissant le transfert mensuel en temps opportun des salaires du personnel
- Superviser et traiter le paiement des dettes fiscales et de la sécurité sociale
- Superviser l'archivage des pièces justificatives et la réception des copies papier au niveau du bureau pays

### **Gestion du personnel**

- Chargé de s'assurer de l'adéquation en termes d'attitude et de compétence du personnel placé sous sa supervision, en garantissant la bonne application et l'efficacité des processus dans lesquels il est impliqué

## **Profil requis**

### **Education**

- Diplôme souhaitable en comptabilité, en finance ou en administration des affaires

### **Expérience Professionnelle**

- Minimum de trois ans d'expérience professionnelle pertinente dans des postes financiers, de préférence au sein d'ONG internationales

### **Exigences Professionnelles**

- Formation et expérience solides en comptabilité - qualification professionnelle en comptabilité
- Connaissances essentielles en informatique (Word, Excel, Finance DB et Internet)
- Une expérience antérieure avec des donateurs de l'ONU est souhaitable

### **Langues**

- La langue de travail de la mission est essentielle. Langue locale souhaitable

### **Exigences personnelles**

- Gestion et perfectionnement du personnel
- Orientation vers le service
- Orientation vers les résultats et la qualité
- Flexibilité comportementale
- Engagement en faveur d'INTERSOS et des principes humanitaires

## **Conditions générales et avantages :**

- **Fourchette de salaire : 09 - 3.172€ - 3.577€ monthly gross**
- **Rémunération**: La rémunération mensuelle pour chaque poste est définie conformément à la grille salariale et à la grille de fonctions standard internationales d'INTERSOS, en tenant compte de l'expérience du candidat sélectionné. Elle est communiquée lors de l'entretien avec les ressources humaines, ou en tout état de cause lors de la première étape du processus de sélection.
- **Hébergement :** Un logement partagé en maison d'hôtes (guesthouse) est généralement fourni dans les lieux d'affectation sur le terrain (field duty stations). Dans les lieux d'affectation avec accompagnement et les lieux d'affectation familiaux, il existe également une option de remboursement d'une partie des frais de logement et une allocation forfaitaire pour les frais d'installation. Dans les lieux d'affectation familiaux, il y a également une contribution aux frais de scolarité pour les enfants à charge.
- **R&R :** il consiste en 7 jours de récupération psychophysique toutes les 8/10/12 semaines, selon le lieu d'affectation. Une indemnité de 1 000 € y est associée.
- **Congés annuels : 2,5 jours par mois**
- **Assurance médicale:** Assurance décès et invalidité ; assurance responsabilité civile, remboursement des vaccins, du certificat médical et du test PCR pour le déploiement ; soutien psychosocial sur demande pour le travailleur humanitaire et ses personnes à charge. Dans les lieux d'affectation avec accompagnement, également pour le conjoint/partenaire. Dans les lieux d'affectation familiaux, également pour les personnes à charge.
- **Frais d'installation** : Selon le pays d'affectation
- **Frais de scolarité** : Selon le pays d'affectation
- **Transport:** Vols aller-retour pour le travailleur humanitaire et le partenaire. Pour toute mission d'une durée d'au moins 9 mois, un billet d'avion supplémentaire vers le pays de résidence et de retour en mission est pris en charge par l'Organisation pour le travailleur humanitaire. Dans les lieux d'affectation avec accompagnement, également pour le partenaire. Dans les lieux d'affectation familiaux, également pour les personnes à charge.
- **Visa:** INTERSOS prend en charge les frais et l'assistance en matière de visa pour le travailleur humanitaire et le partenaire. Dans les lieux d'affectation avec accompagnement, également pour le partenaire. Dans les lieux d'affectation familiaux, également pour les personnes à charge.
- **Formation d’intégration :** Cours d'orientation en ligne : chaque nouveau membre du personnel reçoit une formation préparatoire avant le départ, adéquate pour fournir les informations nécessaires relatives à la structure d'INTERSOS et aux principaux processus décisionnels et outils de travail, afin de faciliter son intégration au sein de l'Organisation.
- **Remarque 1 :** INTERSOS applique une « politique d'apprentissage et de développement » (Learning & Development Policy) qui inclut la possibilité de bénéficier de formations et de participer à des formations internes et externes. La priorité sera accordée au personnel travaillant pour INTERSOS depuis plus de deux ans.
- **Remarque 2 :** La classification des lieux d'affectation avec accompagnement, R&R et sans accompagnement est soumise à des critères de sécurité, d'accès aux services de santé et d'éducation, et n'est pas négociable.

jobs.title: Global Social and Behaviour Change (SBC) Manager
jobs.description:
**About MSI**

MSI Reproductive Choices is one of the world’s leading providers of sexual and reproductive healthcare. We believe that everyone should have the right to choose. From contraception to safe abortion and life-saving post-abortion care, we are committed to delivering compassionate, affordable, high-quality services for all.

Today, our organisation has around 10,000 team members working in 36 countries across the world. Our success lies in the fact that MSI teams are locally led, entrepreneurial and results-driven, and are passionate about delivering high quality, client-centred care in their own communities. As a social business, we focus on sustainable delivery, efficiency, and funding models that are built to last, so that the women and girls we serve today will have a choice in the future too.

We know that access to reproductive choice is life changing. For some, it can mean the ability to complete an education or start a career. For others, it means being able to look after the family they already have. For everyone, it means the freedom to decide their own future, creating a fairer, more equal world.

**About the Role**

MSI seeks an exceptional Global SBC Manager to support the strategy and implementation of SBC best practice through the provision of technical assistance (remote and in-person) on both design and implementation as well as the coordination and documentation of internal best practice and adaptation of external best practice examples and resources.

In particular, the role will initially support the Gates-funded bilateral projects in Ethiopia and Nigeria as well as other donor-funded SBC programmes across Anglophone Africa and Asia.

The role reports to the Senior Global SBC Manager and will work closely with the others in the global marketing team, regional team and donor management teams.

**About You**

For us, it’s vital that every MSI team member believes in and is committed to our organisational mission, vision and values.

**This means that we will only accept applications from candidates who are unequivocally pro-choice.**

Our values act as guiding principles, providing us with a clear direction. They set the tone for how we approach our work, interact with others and align ourselves as ‘One MSI’. It’s important that our team members truly resonate with our values and demonstrate them consistently, in all that they do.

We recruit talented, dynamic individuals with diverse backgrounds who share our mission and are focused on delivering measurable results. Please see job framework [here](https://www.msichoices.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/International-Job-Framework-Global-SBC-Manager-2027.pdf).

jobs.description:
**Re-advertised**

**The position is open for Jerusalem ID holders only**

**The position is part-time (60%)**

**WHO WE ARE**

Diakonia is an international rights-based and faith-based development organization recognized for its commitment to democracy, human rights, and gender justice with the objective to change unfair structures that generate poverty, inequality, oppression and violence. All work is based on feminist principles. Digitalization plays a key role in enabling efficient, transparent, and secure operations across global contexts.

**OUR VALUES AND COMMITMENT TO SAFEGUARDING**

Diakonia is committed to promoting equality, diversity, and inclusion in the workplace, and strives to be representative of all sections of society. We know that different perspectives, experiences, and competences are key for Diakonia to be a relevant, capable, and successful organization. Diakonia therefore strives to recruit staff with diverse backgrounds and lived experiences.

Diakonia is committed to preventing any type of unwanted behaviour at work including sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, lack of integrity and financial misconduct; and committed to promoting the welfare of children, young people, adults and beneficiaries with whom Diakonia engage.

Diakonia expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment through our code of conduct. We place a high priority on ensuring that only those who share and demonstrate our values are recruited to work for us.

The post holder will undertake the appropriate level of training and is responsible for ensuring that they understand and work within the safeguarding policies of the organisation. All offers of employment will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include criminal records and terrorism finance checks. Diakonia also participates in [the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme.](https://misconduct-disclosure-scheme.org/) In line with this Scheme, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her understanding of these recruitment procedures.

**PURPOSE OF THE POSITION**

As a Grant Compliance Advisor for Palestine Civil Society Program, you are responsible for supporting the financial and administrative capacity of partner organizations across Palestine, ensuring they meet compliance standards and sustain their operations.

You will ensure compliance with Diakonia’s policies, procedures, donor requirements, and grant agreements throughout the grant cycle, from inception to closure. The role contributes to strengthening partner accountability, financial management systems, and organizational sustainability.

You are part of the Palestine Civil Society Program and work closely with the Program Manager, Finance Manager, Global Operational Support and Finance Teams, as well as with partners, donors, and relevant networks.

This position reports to the International Director (direct supervisor).

**ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

***Support PM in partner capacity development and compliance:***

- Support the Programme Manager in Partner Capacity Development and Compliance
- Support partner organizational assessments and collaborate with partners to develop and implement capacity development plans.
- Follow up on partner financial and administrative systems to ensure compliance.
- Ensure partners are well informed about Diakonia’s financial policies, procedures, compliance standards, and grant requirements.
- Provide technical support to partners on work plans, budgets, financial reporting, procurement procedures, audits, and grant management.
- Facilitate and monitor grant disbursements to partners and follow up on grant utilization and reporting requirements.
- Conduct partner financial monitoring, including field visits, virtual meetings, compliance reviews, and follow-up actions.
- Review and assess partner budgets, financial reports, audit reports, and management responses.
- Support partners in addressing audit findings and strengthening internal control systems.
- Promote learning and exchange of good practices among partners in financial management and compliance.

***Support PM in managing donor compliance:***

- Support the Program Manager in Managing Donor Compliance
- Support program staff in meeting donor financial and compliance requirements.
- Ensure compliance with donor agreements, reporting obligations, grant conditions, and relevant policies.
- Monitor compliance risks across the regional portfolio and recommend mitigation measures.
- Support the preparation and review of donor financial reports and grant-related documentation.
- Maintain compliance tracking systems and reporting calendars to ensure timely submissions.
- Contribute to donor audits, compliance reviews, and due diligence processes

***Support PM in managing program finance at the country office/programme entity:***

- Support the Program Manager in Financial Oversight of Palestine Civil Society Programme
- Support budgeting, financial planning, financial follow-up, and grant monitoring across the regional programme portfolio.
- Provide technical input to annual planning and budgeting processes.
- Review programme and partner budgets and provide recommendations to strengthen financial planning and resource allocation.
- Support financial analysis and monitoring of grants and programme expenditures.
- Contribute to the preparation of consolidated program budgets and financial forecasts.
- Support resource mobilization efforts through budget development and financial review of funding proposals.
- Ensure that financial management practices are aligned with Diakonia policies and donor requirements.
- Support coordination of internal and external audits in collaboration with the Finance Manager and relevant global teams.
- Advise program staff on financial, compliance, grant management, and risk-related matters.

***Support FM & ID in managing administrative and HR compliance matters:***

- Support with technical HR matters
- Ensure that payroll is correctly administered
- Ensure that labor law is considered in all staff matters.
- Ensure that all insurance matters are adequately handled
- Oversee computer maintenance and security

***Administrative Support:***

- Maintain custody of office keys, car keys, sim cards.
- Maintain custody of cash, performing monthly cash count with FM, and paying invoices on a timely basis.
- Contact person for service deliverers and the IT consultant and make sure we get monthly invoices (ex. Partner, Bezeq, Gaz, Elite Tech.).
- Following up with cleaner on a weekly basis.
- Checking Palestine office hub email account and directing emails to relevant staff.
- Checking post office regularly.
- Ensuring issuance of permits for staff (if it is applicable in the future).
- Security: Getting the UNDSS security messages auto forwarding them to all staff.
- Contact person with the landlord for office related matters.
- Office Insurance

***Support PM in Risk Management and Accountability:***

- Identify, assess, and monitor financial and compliance risks across the program portfolio.
- Support the implementation and monitoring of risk mitigation measures.
- Strengthen accountability systems and promote adherence to internal controls and ethical standards.
- Support investigations, compliance reviews, and follow-up processes where required.
- Contribute to organizational learning by documenting lessons learned and compliance-related good practices.

**EXPERIENCE AND QUALIFICATIONS**

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in Accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field.
- Minimum of 3-5 years of relevant professional experience in grant management, compliance, finance, or partner capacity development, preferably within an international NGO environment.
- Strong knowledge of donor compliance requirements and grant management processes.
- Demonstrated experience in financial monitoring, audits, risk management, and partner capacity strengthening.
- Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Advanced Excel and financial analysis skills.
- Excellent written and spoken English. Arabic is considered a strong asset.
- Ability to work in Jerusalem.

jobs.description:
We are currently recruiting an **AI and Digital Transformation Advisor** to join our **Quality, Impact and Innovation Department**.

This is a **remote, 12-month position** open to candidates based in **the UK, or any Relief International country of operation within a +/- 4-hour difference from Central European Time (CET)**. The role has a global remit and works across departments and country programmes to help shape how Relief International adopts and benefits from artificial intelligence and digital transformation.

At Relief International, we are committed to building a representative, inclusive and authentic workplace. We strongly encourage applications from candidates from minoritized backgrounds and those who bring lived experience of the contexts in which we work.

This role is classified as requiring **standard pre-employment checks.**

**About Relief International**

Relief International is an international non-profit organization that partners with communities impacted by conflict, climate change and disaster to save lives, build greater resilience and promote long-term health and wellbeing. Our team of more than 4,000 staff and local volunteers work across Africa, Asia and the Middle East, delivering Health and Nutrition, WASH (Water, Sanitation and Hygiene), Education and Livelihoods programming that creates the foundation for community resilience. We do this by working with local actors to develop safe, inclusive and evidence-based programming that is conflict-sensitive, climate-smart and responsive to community needs.

**About the Opportunity**

Artificial intelligence is transforming how organizations work, learn and make decisions. At Relief International, we see AI as an opportunity to strengthen humanitarian impact, improve efficiency, enhance knowledge sharing and support better decision-making across our global operations.

The AI and Digital Transformation Advisor will lead the development and implementation of Relief International's AI strategy, helping departments identify practical opportunities where AI and digital tools can create meaningful value. Rather than acting as a technical implementer, you will serve as a strategic advisor, facilitator and change leader, supporting teams to adopt AI responsibly, effectively and sustainably.

You will work closely with senior leaders, department heads, country directors and IT colleagues to develop an organizational roadmap for AI adoption, coordinate a portfolio of AI initiatives, strengthen staff capability and ensure that innovation remains aligned with organizational priorities, governance requirements and humanitarian principles.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who is passionate about the practical application of AI and digital transformation and wants to help shape how a global humanitarian organization leverages emerging technologies to better serve vulnerable communities around the world.

**Your Responsibilities**

This role includes the following responsibilities.

- Lead the development and continuous evolution of Relief International's AI and digital transformation strategy, translating organizational priorities into a practical roadmap of initiatives and opportunities.
- Identify and prioritize opportunities where AI and digital tools can improve efficiency, effectiveness, quality, knowledge management and decision-making across departments and country programmes.
- Coordinate and oversee a portfolio of AI initiatives, ensuring clear objectives, ownership, milestones and measures of success while maintaining responsibility within individual departments.
- Support senior leaders and functional teams in developing business cases for AI adoption, tracking technology investments, licensing costs and demonstrating organizational value and return on investment.
- Develop and implement organization-wide approaches to AI adoption, change management and capability building, helping staff confidently and responsibly use AI in their day-to-day work.
- Design and deliver practical training, guidance materials, tools and learning resources that make AI accessible to both technical and non-technical audiences.
- Work closely with IT and other stakeholders to ensure AI solutions align with cybersecurity, information security, data protection and governance requirements.
- Promote the responsible use of AI, including appropriate human oversight, data privacy, transparency, accuracy and awareness of bias and limitations.
- Lead initiatives that strengthen organizational learning and knowledge management, including the use of AI-enabled approaches to make institutional knowledge more accessible and useful.
- Manage and support the AI and Knowledge Management Intern, providing direction, mentorship and quality assurance.

**About You**

You will bring the following experience and skills.

- Demonstrated experience leading or supporting AI adoption, digital transformation, organizational change or technology-enabled improvement initiatives within a complex organization.
- Strong practical understanding of generative AI technologies and their real-world applications, including tools such as Microsoft Copilot and similar AI platforms.
- Experience translating business or organizational needs into practical technology solutions and measurable improvements.
- Strong project and stakeholder management skills, with experience coordinating multiple workstreams across departments and influencing without direct authority.
- Experience leading change-management initiatives and helping teams adopt new tools, processes and ways of working.
- Excellent communication, facilitation and training skills, with the ability to engage both technical and non-technical audiences.
- Strong understanding of responsible AI principles, including data protection, confidentiality, cybersecurity, human oversight, transparency, accuracy and ethical considerations.
- Highly organized, pragmatic and collaborative, with the ability to manage competing priorities while building trust and credibility across the organization.
- Experience developing AI strategies, AI adoption programmes, knowledge management approaches or enterprise technology initiatives is highly desirable.
- Experience working within international NGOs, humanitarian organizations or other globally distributed organizations would be an advantage.

jobs.title: Consultancy for Graphic Design Services
jobs.description:
**1. Background**

HAMAP-Humanitaire is an international humanitarian organization working in mine action and other humanitarian sectors. Its activities include explosive ordnance clearance, risk education, and capacity building.

The BRIDGE Project aims to strengthen Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE), promote the inclusion of victims and persons with disabilities, and increase public awareness through community-based and digital activities.

HAMAP-Humanitaire is seeking an experienced freelance graphic design consultant to provide design services on an assignment basis under the BRIDGE Project.

The consultant will support the production of digital and printed communication, awareness, and visibility materials. Assignments may relate to EORE, victim inclusion, persons with disabilities, project activities, and other communication needs.

**2. Objective**

To produce clear, engaging, and professional digital and printed designs that support the project’s communication, awareness, and visibility needs and are adapted to the intended audiences, platforms, and formats.

**3. Scope of Work**

The consultant will:

- Design social media posts, carousels, banners, flyers, posters, and other visual materials.
- Create simple animated videos when requested. Edit videos using footage and materials provided by HAMAP when requested.
- Adapt designs to the required sizes and formats for digital and printed use.
- Follow HAMAP’s visual identity and applicable partner and donor visibility requirements.
- Incorporate consolidated feedback and complete the revisions required for approval.
- HAMAP will provide the content, key messages, scripts, logos, footage, and general creative direction.

**4. Deliverables and Indicative Workload**

The assignment is expected to begin with an initial batch of approximately 14 digital materials, which may include static social media posts, and carousels.

Following this initial batch, additional design support is expected to be requested approximately twice per month, depending on project needs. These assignments may include digital or printed materials such as banners, flyers, posters, visibility materials, animations, or video editing.

For each assignment, the consultant will provide:

- Final approved designs in high-resolution formats.
- Platform-ready versions in the required dimensions and formats.
- Print-ready files for printed materials.
- Editable source files.
- Revisions based on HAMAP’s consolidated feedback. (Number of revision rounds: Between 3 and 6).

The specifications, deadlines, and expected outputs for each additional assignment will be agreed upon in advance. The indicated workload is an estimate and may be adjusted according to project needs.

**5. Required Qualifications**

The consultant should have:

- Proven professional experience in graphic design.
- Experience in humanitarian or social-awareness campaigns.
- Excellent knowledge of digital and social media design requirements.
- Experience in designing printed communication and visibility materials.
- Experience in animation and video editing.
- Previous experience designing EORE materials is an asset.
- Experience in designs related to victim inclusion and persons with disabilities is an asset.
- Ability to work with Arabic and English content.
- Ability to meet deadlines and respond constructively to feedback.
- Access to the software and equipment required to complete the assignments.

**6. Duration**

The deliverables are expected to be completed and submitted within four weeks. However, the contract shall remain valid until no later than 30 April 2027, to cover any additional services that may be required at a later stage, unless terminated earlier in accordance with its terms and conditions.

Assignments will be issued according to project needs, with their respective scope and deadlines agreed upon in advance.

**7. Application Requirements**

Applicants should submit:

- A CV.
- A portfolio containing relevant digital and printed design work.
- A financial offer in USD indicating the unit price and estimated completion time for:
- Static social media post.
- Carousel, specifying the number of slides included.
- Animated video, with prices based on its type and duration.
- Video editing using footage provided by HAMAP, with prices based on the video type and duration.
- Banner design.
- Flyer/Poster design.
- Any applicable taxes or additional costs.

**8. Confidentiality and Use of Materials**

The selected consultant will be required to sign a Non-Disclosure Agreement before starting the assignment.

All information, content, documents, photographs, videos, designs, and other materials shared by or produced for HAMAP must be treated as confidential. The consultant may not publish, share, reproduce, or use these materials, including in a personal or professional portfolio, without HAMAP’s prior written approval.

The final approved designs and editable source files produced under this consultancy will be provided to HAMAP for its use. These confidentiality obligations will remain applicable after the completion of the consultancy.

jobs.title: Project Financial Audit: English & Ukrainian Speaking
jobs.description:
## 1.Introduction

CBM seeks to engage an **independent external financial auditor or an audit firm providing a suitably qualified audit team** to conduct a final financial audit upon completion of the above-mentioned project. The audit shall cover the **entire 12-month project implementation period**. The audit is commissioned and funded by CBM to fulfil **CBM’s internal audit requirements**. It is *neither* commissioned by DG ECHO *nor* a contractual requirement under the project’s DG ECHO grant agreement.

CBM Christoffel-Blindenmission Christian Blind Mission e.V. (herein referred to as “CBM”), together with the National Assembly of People with Disabilities of Ukraine (herein referred to as “NAPD“) and Momentum Wheels for Humanity (herein referred to as “Momentum”), is currently implementing humanitarian action in **Chernihiv, Sumy, Kharkiv and Poltava** **oblasts** from May 2026 to April 2027 funded by The European Commission’s Directorate-General for European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations. The action focuses on health, rehabilitation and protection, with particular attention to persons with disabilities and other groups facing heightened barriers to humanitarian assistance. For more information, please see: [Ukraine: Restoring Access to Health](https://www.cbm.org/news/news-articles/2026/ukraine-restoring-access-to-health.html)

## 2. Scope of services/work

The assignment consists of **one final external financial audit covering the entire 12-month project implementation period,** **May 2026 to April 2027**, including the portions falling within the 2026 and 2027 financial years. The audit shall be conducted following project completion.

For the purposes of this engagement, the project shall be examined as one continuous audit period. Separate annual project audits or separate audit opinions for 2026 and 2027 are not required under these Terms of Reference. The auditor shall nevertheless verify the reconciliation between the project records for both financial years, including year-end balances, amounts carried forward and the correct allocation of transactions to the relevant reporting periods. This arrangement does not alter routine financial reporting obligations or any separate organisational or statutory audit requirements.

The audit is commissioned and financed by CBM to fulfil its internal financial accountability and assurance requirements. It is neither commissioned by DG ECHO nor undertaken as a contractual DG ECHO audit requirement for this project. Any audit separately initiated by DG ECHO falls outside this engagement and remains unaffected by it.

The scope encompasses project funds managed and expenditure incurred by **CBM and both implementing partners, the National Assembly of People with Disabilities of Ukraine (NAPD) and Momentum Wheels of Humanity (Momentum)**. It includes DG ECHO funding, CBM co-financing and relevant project transactions recorded at headquarters level. The assignment is limited to the project’s financial information and related controls; it does not constitute an audit of the organisations’ complete financial statements.

### 2.1Applicable Requirements

The auditor shall assess project financial management and expenditure against the signed grant agreement and its annexes, approved budgets and amendments, partnership agreements, and applicable organisational and national requirements.

For CBM, this includes the relevant provisions of the Finance Handbook and related financial management, procurement and internal control policies. For NAPD and Momentum, the auditor shall assess compliance with their contractual obligations towards CBM and the policies and procedures applicable to their implementation of the project. CBM-specific procedures shall apply to the partners only to the extent required under their agreements.

**Provision and clarification of reference documents**

Before the audit begins, CBM shall provide the auditor with the relevant contractual documents, applicable versions of its Finance Handbook and related policies, and any additional internal audit requirements applicable to this assignment.

Any conflicting or unclear requirements, including questions concerning their applicability or precedence, shall be clarified with CBM during audit planning and documented in the audit work plan.

**Auditing standards and audit opinion**

The audit shall be conducted in accordance with the **International Standards on Auditing (ISA)**, as applicable to the engagement and the financial reporting framework adopted for the consolidated project financial statement.

The auditor shall express an **independent audit opinion** on whether the consolidated project financial statement has been prepared, in all material respects, in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework described in the notes to the statement.

The auditor shall also report significant findings concerning compliance with the applicable project requirements and relevant internal controls in the **management letter**.

### 2.2 Areas of examination

**Financial reporting and reconciliation:** Reconcile the consolidated final project financial statement *in EUR* with the project ledgers, transaction listings and financial reports of CBM, NAPD and Momentum. Verify funding received, CBM co-financing, transfers to implementing partners, reported expenditure, outstanding advances, project-related liabilities, refunds and closing balances. Verify that transfers between the organisations are not counted again as expenditure in the consolidated project financial statement.

The financial statement shall include notes disclosing the basis of preparation, the accounting and currency conversion principles applied, and the treatment of advances, liabilities, exchange-rate differences, closing adjustments, project-related transactions settled after the implementation period and, where applicable, non-cash entries. The auditor shall assess whether the disclosed reporting framework has been consistently and appropriately applied.

**Financial-year reconciliation and closing adjustments:** The auditor shall verify that project-related balances and transactions recorded in the 2026 and 2027 financial years are properly reconciled to the consolidated project financial statement. Examine the continuity of records between the two financial years and ensure that the financial-year split has not resulted in omissions or duplication.

This shall include reviewing relevant year-end adjustments, subsequent corrections to project-related accounting records, and the treatment of project-related payments, refunds and liabilities settled after the end of the implementation period, in accordance with the applicable reporting framework and eligibility rules. Any material discrepancies between the annual accounting records and the consolidated project financial statement shall be reported.

**Expenditure and use of funds:** Examine whether expenditure was incurred for the approved project purposes, complies with the applicable funding conditions, is properly authorised and supported by adequate documentation, and is accurately recorded and classified. Review budget amendments, exchange-rate calculations, shared-cost allocations, tax and VAT treatment, and potential duplicate charging or financing. Where indirect costs are reported on a flat-rate basis, verify the applicable contractual rate and calculation base.

**Procurement and contracted services:** Review the application of relevant procurement procedures, including procurement planning, competition, supplier selection, bid evaluation, contract award, documented exceptions, delivery and payment. Examine relevant safeguards against conflicts of interest and compliance with applicable restrictive measures. For medical equipment, assistive devices and other project supplies, review the quality-assurance documentation required under the applicable project rules and evidence of receipt or handover to the intended facilities or recipients.

**Personnel and operating costs:** Examine project-related employment and consultancy contracts, payroll calculations, timesheets or other accepted evidence of staff-cost allocation, payment records, and relevant tax and social contribution documentation. Verify that personnel, travel and office operating costs charged to the project are supported and allocated in accordance with the applicable requirements, including costs paid or recorded at headquarters level.

**Cash, banking and advances:** Review project-related bank and cash records, reconciliations, payment authorisations, fund transfers and the settlement of advances. Trace selected transactions through the accounting records, supporting documentation and proof of payment. Examine outstanding balances and their treatment at the financial-year boundary and at project closure.

**Cash assistance:** Review the financial procedures and supporting records for cash assistance, including Cash for Health where applicable. Examine documented beneficiary eligibility and approval decisions, payment instructions, evidence of transfer or receipt, reconciliations, and the treatment of failed, returned or unclaimed payments. Access to personal and health information shall be limited to what is necessary for the audit and handled confidentially. Where feasible, anonymised or pseudonymised documentation shall be used.

**Assets and stocks:** Examine project-related asset and stock records, supporting procurement documentation, evidence of existence and project use, and relevant handover, transfer or disposal documentation. Review the financial treatment of assets and stocks remaining at project closure, including any documented losses or damage.

**Internal controls, partner oversight and financial monitoring:** Assess the design and operation of controls relevant to project financial management throughout the implementation period, including segregation of duties, delegated authority, payment approvals, record-keeping, reconciliations and management review.

Particular attention shall be given to whether the enhanced staffing, supervision and financial monitoring arrangements envisaged for the project were implemented and operated during the relevant periods. The auditor shall consider changes in these arrangements over time and examine evidence of ongoing financial oversight, early risk identification and corrective action, rather than assuming their effectiveness solely from the existence of policies or staff appointments.

Review CBM’s monitoring of partner expenditure, the review and reconciliation of partner financial reports, documented financial checks and the follow-up of relevant previous findings. Significant weaknesses and recommendations shall be included in the management letter, with findings clearly attributed to CBM, NAPD or Momentum, as appropriate. This review does not constitute a separate audit opinion on the effectiveness of the organisations’ entire internal control systems.

### 2.3 Audit approach and locations

arrangements. The meeting shall take place either in person in Kyiv, subject to security conditions, or online via Zoom. The auditor shall provide a work plan, a document request list and a proposed timetable.

The auditor shall apply a **risk-based audit approach**, independently selecting samples that provide sufficient coverage of all three organisations and the **entire 12-month project implementation period**, including the portions falling within 2026 and 2027. Particular attention shall be given to significant expenditure categories and **high-value or high-risk transactions**. The auditor shall document the materiality applied, the sampling methodology and the coverage achieved by transaction number and value, and shall expand testing where findings warrant it. No fixed sampling percentage or automatic review of 100% of supporting documents is prescribed under these Terms of Reference.

Fieldwork shall include on-site visits to the **offices of CBM, NAPD and Momentum in Kyiv**, subject to security conditions. Relevant project records held at headquarters level shall be reviewed remotely. Any additional visits to health facilities, warehouses or other project locations shall be agreed with CBM in advance, with any additional costs separately identified and agreed.

Where security conditions prevent planned visits, the auditor shall discuss and agree alternative arrangements with CBM. The auditor shall document the alternative procedures performed and report any unresolved limitations affecting the audit.

**Confidentiality and data protection**

*The auditor shall maintain the confidentiality of all financial, contractual and personal information obtained during the assignment.*

*The auditor shall implement appropriate safeguards for the secure transfer, storage, retention and disposal of audit-related information, in accordance with applicable data protection requirements and the engagement agreement.*

## 3. Expected Deliverables

**Before fieldwork**

The auditor shall submit:

- **Work plan:** The proposed audit approach, team responsibilities and arrangements for on-site visits and remote review.
- **Document request list:** The records and supporting documentation to be prepared by CBM and the implementing partners (English & Ukrainian)
- **Proposed timetable:** Dates for fieldwork, draft reports, management responses and final submission, to be agreed with CBM (English & Ukrainian)

These documents shall be provided in English. The document request list and timetable should also be available in Ukrainian where possible.

**Following fieldwork**

The auditor shall provide:

- **Draft audit report and exit meeting:** Present preliminary findings to CBM and the relevant partners and submit a draft audit report and management letter for factual review and written management responses. This review shall not interfere with the auditor’s independent opinion. (English & Ukrainian)
- **Final audit report:** A signed report expressing an independent opinion on the consolidated project financial statement in accordance with its disclosed reporting framework. The report shall include the audited financial statement in EUR, explanatory notes and financial breakdowns by organisation and financial year. It shall state the auditing standards applied, summarise sampling coverage and explain any limitations or modifications to the opinion.
- **Management letter and findings schedule:** Identify weaknesses in financial records, procedures, controls and compliance, with practical recommendations. A supporting schedule shall list questioned or potentially ineligible expenditure by organisation, transaction reference, amount, currency and reason, distinguishing corrected and unresolved items.

All reports shall be submitted to CBM in English. Presentation of findings in English & Ukrainian. The final audit report and audited financial statement shall be provided as a signed PDF, with the management letter also in Word and supporting schedules in Excel. Suspected fraud, corruption or serious irregularities shall be reported promptly through CBM’s designated confidential channels, without waiting for the final report.

jobs.title: Media and Communications Officer
jobs.description:
This is an exciting opportunity for a skilled Media and Communications Officer to play a central role in delivering the communications strategy of an international NGO in the heart of Madagascar.

Based in the coastal town of Fort Dauphin, the Officer will oversee the daily running of SEED’s social media and content development, manage a junior team member, and strengthen collaboration between the Communications and Programmes teams. The role includes supporting with major fundraising appeals, producing engaging donor updates, and developing innovative content across all platforms, including expanding SEED’s presence on TikTok.

The successful candidate will work closely with both national and international staff, contributing to impactful campaigns that showcase SEED’s work in sustainable development and conservation. Predominantly office-based with occasional travel to rural project sites, the role offers a diverse range of responsibilities for a communications professional looking to develop their leadership skills while contributing to meaningful, community-driven development.

*Location:* Fort Dauphin, Anosy Region, Madagascar
*Commitment:* 24 months, extendable, 40 hours a week
*Salary:* Local salary, up to £1,200 contribution for a return flight and up to £650 contribution towards insurance

**Duties and responsibilities**

- Lead the daily management of SEED’s social media platforms, including developing and scheduling content across all channels, with a particular focus on expanding SEED’s TikTok presence.
- Produce, edit, and publish engaging written, visual, and multimedia content for social media, website, newsletters, and PR, ensuring alignment with SEED’s brand and communications goals.
- Gather stories, photos, and videos from field sites to highlight SEED’s work, ensuring safeguarding, consent, and data protection policies are upheld.
- Develop and edit donor updates in collaboration with programme teams to showcase project impact.
- Oversee the production of blogs and articles, editing contributions from staff and volunteers for external publication.
- Line-manage the Junior Officer or intern, providing day-to-day guidance, feedback, and professional development opportunities.
- Support the development of the Communications team STAGE interns, remote international interns and volunteers, ensuring learning and capacity building within the team.
- Deliver media, consent, and storytelling training to international staff, strengthening best practice across the organisation.
- Manage the relationship between Communications and Programmes teams to deliver major fundraising appeals, from concept to promotion; from storyboarding and gathering updates to shape engaging communication content that highlight SEED’s impact.
- Work with the Coordinator and International Operations Manager to ensure consistent and impactful messaging for appeals and campaigns.
- Contribute ideas for innovative fundraising content and approaches to broaden SEED’s donor base.
- Support the review and evaluation of communications platforms against agreed marketing KPIs.
- Contribute to quarterly communications reports for trustees, providing insights and analysis on content performance and audience engagement.
- Ensure SEED’s brand identity is consistently reflected across all outputs, with oversight from the Coordinator.
- Uphold SEED’s safeguarding, whistleblowing, and anti-corruption policies, ensuring best practice in all communications.
- Work flexibly, including outside standard office hours when necessary, to meet tight deadlines (e.g., donor reports, funding documents).
- Ensure all of SEED’s policies and procedures are evident throughout the work of the department, including those for safeguarding, whistleblowing and anti-corruption, and undertake continual training to ensure these are promoted at all times
- Complete other ad-hoc tasks as required by the International Operations Manager, or Director of Programmes and Operations to further the aims and work of the organisation.

**Person specification**
- A degree-level qualification in Communications, International Development, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.
- At least 1–2 years’ professional experience in communications, marketing, or fundraising, ideally within the non-profit sector.
- Some prior experience in line management, supervision, or project coordination.
- Experience creating and managing social media content and marketing campaigns.
- Demonstrate a working knowledge of producing and managing high-quality photo and video content.
- Confident in editing visual content with software such as Canva (experience with CapCut, GetResponse, or similar tools desirable).
- Excellent writing and editing skills, with proven ability to tailor messaging for different audiences and platforms.
- Ability to communicate an organisation’s ethos and mission to diverse national and international audiences through photography, videography, and writing.
- Strong verbal and written communication skills with a keen eye for detail.
- Demonstrated interest in conservation and community development, with an understanding of international development challenges in the global south desirable.
- Knowledge of PPC, content strategy development, or other advanced communications tools desirable but not essential.
- Strong organisational skills, with the ability to work to tight deadlines and manage multiple priorities.
- Proven problem-solving skills and the ability to deal appropriately with challenging situations.
- Passion, curiosity, and motivation for the role, with the ability to enthuse and inspire others.
- Capacity to build skills and share knowledge across cultures, working with people from diverse economic and cultural backgrounds and across multiple language barriers.
- Awareness of and comfort with increased social and professional responsibility, always working with cultural sensitivity and respect.

- Flexible and patient, with the ability to work both independently and as part of a team.
