jobs.title: Senior AI Technical Specialist
jobs.description:
## About Development Gateway and the Early Grade Education Activity (EGEA)

[Development Gateway: An IREX Venture (DG)](https://developmentgateway.org/) is an international non-profit organization with approximately 80 team members based in more than 10 countries worldwide. By leveraging the combination of programmatic and IT developer capacity and skills within DG, over the last 20 years we have *researched* data ecosystems, *built* digital tools to support those data ecosystems, and *advised* on data strategy and digital transformation to strengthen decision-making, transparency, and service delivery.

DG is one of several consortium partners, led by [IREX](https://www.irex.org/), implementing the Early Grade Education Activity (EGEA, also known as ‘ASAS’) program in Jordan between 2023-2028, funded by the U.S. Department of State. As a large-scale development program, ASAS is a complex, high-paced and outcome-oriented initiative. The consortium itself comprises well over 50 individuals working on the program at any given time (based both in Jordan and abroad). From DG’s side alone, there are likely to be approximately 8-10 personnel supporting implementation at any given time, with at least 4 staff based in Amman, including the Senior AI Technical Specialist.

The overarching objective of ASAS is to improve the quality of early grades (K-G3) education outcomes for children in Jordan. The program aims to achieve this objective by supporting the education of student teachers while they are still at university (pre-service teachers), and also by supporting early grades students and teachers (in-service teachers).

DG’s role within the consortium includes supporting the safe, effective, and responsible integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into Jordan’s education sector, in alignment with the national AI policy. In partnership with the Ministry of Education and Human Resources DevelopmentDG is embarking on an ambitious set of activities that will test AI capabilities in real-world settings.

## Job description

This is an exciting opportunity for an AI specialist who can situate cutting-edge developments in AI within Jordan’s policy context and understand how new technologies can strengthen education systems. Based in Amman, you will turn fast-moving AI advances into practical opportunities for the Ministry of Education, schools, and universities, and explain their value clearly and simply to non-technical audiences.

Rather than executing backend software development or heavy algorithmic coding, your focus is on driving active stakeholder participation, co-designing AI sandbox environments in schools and universities, and explaining complex technical concepts in accessible Arabic and English. You will directly complement IREX’s overarching coordination work by grounding high-level planning into practical, school- and university-level deliverables–ensuring MoEHRD counterparts, school staff, faculty, and administrators remain energized, engaged, and aligned with core project requirements.

Embedded within the ASAS project office in Amman, you will report directly to DG’s Director of Software Development (US) for technical strategy, with a dotted reporting line to DG’s local Project Lead/Advisor for daily operational alignment. Working alongside 30+ Jordan-based consortium colleagues, you will join a creative, globally distributed team that values hard work, practical problem-solving, and collaboration. If you excel at turning institutional friction into clear technical momentum, this role offers the platform to drive meaningful digital adoption across Jordan's education ecosystem.

At DG, we are a creative and dynamic group of people based around the globe. We value and reward hard work, innovative thinking, a commitment to teamwork, and a good sense of humor. With this role, we are looking for a new colleague to join our team and be our Senior AI Technical Specialist on the ASAS program in Amman.

The work you get to do

*In-Service AI: School-Level AI Centers & Sandbox Pilots*

- Provide technical support to establish six AI Centers in MoEHRD-selected schools, including assessing facility readiness, defining equipment and technical specifications, and verifying that installed centers are ready for use.
- Work with the MoEHRD and relevant stakeholders to co-design the scope, governance, school selection, institutional roles and implementation approach for AI sandbox pilots in three schools across the country including facilitating technical consultations and participatory workshops. Support the preparation of a technical brief outlining the objectives, scope, expected outcomes, and implementation approach for the school AI sandbox pilots, aligned with the Year 3 AI Readiness Assessment and policy brief.
- Lead the technical set-up of school sandboxes, support the design and delivery of sensitization workshops and hands-on training, , and help pilot schools shortlist 2–3 priority AI use cases.
- Support monitoring and evaluation of AI sandbox pilots, including assessment of technical performance, usability, pedagogical relevance, user adoption, and documentation of results, challenges, and lessons learned.
- Support the organization and technical facilitation of workshops to present and validate pilot results with MoEHRD, participating schools, and relevant stakeholders.
- Provide ongoing virtual sandboxing support, including a helpdesk that responds to technical questions and pedagogical questions on applying AI to agreed use cases.
- Translate pilot results into evidence and recommendations for MoEHRD leadership, the National AI for Education Forum, and a national approach to scaling successful use cases.
- Support MoEHRD and Field Directorates in assessing technical, institutional, and operational requirements for sustaining school AI Centers and scaling successful AI applications.

*Pre-Service AI: University Engagement & Institutional Integration*

- Serve as the lead technical interlocutor for partner universities, directly tackling engagement friction and driving active academic participation in project activities.
- Uncover operational bottlenecks and university requirements, translating qualitative institutional feedback into structured digital use cases.
- Lead the co-design, testing, and university-level rollout of sandbox AI environments, establishing clear feedback loops with faculty and administrators.

*Requirements Scoping & Technical Translation*

- Scope functional requirements for applied AI initiatives (e.g., automated reporting, documentation synthesis, data collection tools) without needing to write heavy software code.
- Translate complex technical concepts into accessible, bilingual (Arabic/English) specs and guidance notes for non-technical stakeholders, MoEHRD and university leadership, and vendors.
- Establish User Acceptance Testing (UAT) protocols, rollout sequencing, and data stewardship standards for school, university and ministry systems.

*Alignment with IREX Coordination & Programmatic Support*

- Complement IREX's programmatic coordination and oversight by serving as the Jordan-based technical liaison between DG's development team, IREX, MoEHRD, schools, and partner universities, translating agreed plans into actionable technical activities and supporting the timely resolution of implementation challenges.
- Serve as the primary Jordan-based technical liaison between DG's development team, IREX technical teams, MoEHRDHRD counterparts, schools, and partner universities, ensuring timely validation of requirements, coordination of technical implementation, resolution of operational challenges, and alignment with agreed work plans and institutional priorities
- Co-develop SOPs, workflows, and training materials that enable school and university staff to practically adopt AI tools in their daily routines.
- Provide regular, proactive updates on school and university technical readiness, operational risks, and adoption milestones to project leadership.

*Data Governance & Responsible AI*

- Establish practical ethical standards, governance rules, and privacy protections across all school and university AI sandbox pilots.
- Define data de-identification practices, accuracy checks, and hosting protocols to protect sensitive institutional and student data.

## Qualifications and experience requirements

- **Experience:** 5+ years of experience in data systems, digital transformation, or technology adoption, with proven success driving stakeholder engagement within Jordanian universities or national institutions. Experience with AI applications, data science tools, or emerging technologies in education.
- **Technical Alignment:** Demonstrated capacity to map user requirements to applied AI/data tools and structure low-risk use cases (no direct programming required).
- **Language Skills:** Professional fluency in written and spoken Arabic and English, with demonstrated ability to draft technical specifications in both languages.
- **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in STEM, Information Management, Education, or a related field.

## Preferred (desirable) qualifications

- Degree and/or certification in artificial intelligence, machine learning, or computer science is a plus.
- Familiarity with donor-funded programming (e.g., U.S. State Department) and their reporting standards.

Position Details

This is a **full-time staff position**, embedded in the ASAS office in Amman. The role is expected to run for approx. 2 years, pending annual performance reviews. The expected annual salary range is USD 50,000-65,000, depending on relevant experience.

jobs.title: National Legal Expert
jobs.description:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

- **Organization:** UNDP Lebanon Through Stars Orbit Consultants and Management Development
- **VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/195**
- **Position Title**: National Legal Expert
- **Duty Station:** Beirut
- **Duration:** 2 months – ( without exceeding 18 working days per month)
- **Vacancy Date of Issue: 13 October 2026**
- **Vacancy Closure Date: 20 October 2026**
- **National or International consultancy:** National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1skRnV_7T0jSVBLVLW6bam7EcDMuwpN_B/view?usp=drive_link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1skRnV_7T0jSVBLVLW6bam7EcDMuwpN_B/view?usp=drive_link)

**BACKGROUND**

Lebanon enacted Law No. 62 of 27 October 2016 establishing the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), including the Committee for the Prevention of Torture. The NHRC is Lebanon’s independent national human rights institution, mandated to promote and protect human rights, monitor compliance with national and international obligations, receive and follow up on complaints, document violations, issue reports and recommendations, and engage with competent national and international bodies.

Within the NHRC, the International Humanitarian Law Committee provides the institutional framework for monitoring, documenting, and analysing alleged violations that arise in situations of armed conflict, and for supporting advocacy aimed at respecting international humanitarian law (IHL) and applicable international human rights law (IHRL). Its work contributes to the NHRC’s independent reporting, recommendations, engagement with public authorities, cooperation with international mechanisms, and efforts to promote accountability, remedy, and guarantees of non-recurrence.

The 2026 conflict caused serious harm to civilians and civilian objects and generated allegations of conduct that may amount to violations of IHL and IHRL. Reliable documentation requires a consistent methodology, careful corroboration, survivor-centred and conflict-sensitive engagement, secure information management, and legal analysis grounded in the applicable international legal framework. Documentation must also distinguish verified facts, allegations, and legal conclusions, while respecting confidentiality, informed consent, data-protection requirements, and the ‘do no harm’ principle.

UNDP has supported the NHRC since its establishment and seeks to strengthen the Commission’s capacity to fulfill its protection, monitoring, and advocacy mandate. The NHRC International Humanitarian Law Committee has already carried out the principal documentation and preliminary analysis of alleged violations committed during and in the aftermath of the 2026 conflict. Accordingly, UNDP is seeking a National Legal Expert to work under the Committee’s substantive leadership to independently review and corroborate the material collected, address essential evidentiary gaps through limited supplementary verification, and prepare a consolidated legal and analytical report for the Committee’s use.

**OBJECTIVE OF THE ASSIGNMENT**

The objective of the consultancy is to independently review, corroborate, and legally analyze the documentation already compiled by the NHRC International Humanitarian Law Committee and to produce a comprehensive, evidence-based report. The report shall clearly present verified findings, unresolved allegations, evidentiary limitations, applicable legal standards, conclusions, and recommendations that can support the Committee’s protection, advocacy, remedy, and accountability efforts.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

The NHRC International Humanitarian Law Committee has already undertaken the principal documentation, information-gathering, and preliminary analysis concerning alleged violations committed during and in the aftermath of the 2026 conflict.

Accordingly, under the guidance and supervision of the UNDP Rule of Law and Governance Chief Technical Advisor (CTA) and Community Security and Human Rights Project Officer, and in line with the Committee's technical standards, the consultant shall independently review and corroborate the material compiled by the Committee, conduct strictly targeted supplementary verification where required, and prepare a consolidated legal and analytical report as follows:

- Review the documentation package prepared by the Committee, including complaints, testimonies, interview records, incident files, photographs, videos, medical or official records, open-source material, correspondence, and other supporting information made available by the Committee.
- Assess the completeness, internal consistency, reliability, and evidentiary value of the material and determine whether each principal finding is supported by sufficient and appropriately corroborated information.
- Corroborate material facts through cross-checking among independent sources, verification of dates and locations, review of metadata and authenticated open-source information where available, and comparison with credible institutional or public records.
- Prepare and maintain a verification matrix recording each allegation or incident, the supporting sources, the degree of corroboration, relevant inconsistencies, outstanding evidentiary gaps, protection concerns, and the consultant’s assessment.
- Identify material gaps that could affect the accuracy or legal analysis of the report and submit a focused supplementary verification plan to the Committee for prior approval.
- Conduct only the targeted follow-up interviews, consultations, field visits, or requests for information that are necessary to address identified gaps and that have been expressly approved by the Committee. Any such activity shall follow survivor-centred, child-sensitive, gender-responsive, disability-inclusive, and conflict-sensitive standards.
- Review the relevant legal framework, including applicable treaty and customary IHL, IHRL, international criminal law where relevant, and Lebanese law, and establish the legal standards applicable to the verified incidents and patterns.
- Review the verified facts and assess what legal implications they may have, but do not assume, declare, or prejudge whether anyone is guilty or liable, as that decision belongs to the competent courts or judicial authorities, clearly distinguishing facts, credible allegations, unresolved claims, evidentiary limitations, and legal conclusions.
- Identify recurring patterns, trends, geographic concentrations, affected groups, types of civilian harm, and other protection concerns emerging from the Committee’s documentation.
- Prepare a comprehensive, consolidated report setting out the mandate and methodology; factual findings; corroboration process; applicable legal framework; legal analysis; patterns of alleged violations; evidentiary and methodological limitations; conclusions; and recommendations for protection, remedy, accountability, and prevention.
- Submit the draft report to the Committee, participate in technical review meetings, respond to comments, verify contested passages, and incorporate agreed factual, legal, and editorial revisions.
- Prepare a final publication-ready version of the report, together with an executive summary and a confidential annex or case matrix where required by the Committee.
- Support the Committee, when requested, in presenting the report and translating its verified findings into focused recommendations, briefings, or advocacy messages for competent national and international stakeholders.
- Maintain strict confidentiality, secure information handling, and source-protection standards throughout the review and reporting process, and securely hand over all working files and verification records upon completion.
- Immediately notify the Committee of serious inconsistencies, possible falsification or manipulation of evidence, urgent protection risks, threats of retaliation, loss of information, or other matters requiring prompt institutional action.
- Review the Committee’s documentation and applicable legal framework; develop the work plan, corroboration methodology, and verification thresholds; prepare the verification matrix template; conduct a risk assessment; and identify initial evidentiary and analytical gaps.
- Complete or substantially complete the verification matrix; conduct source cross-checking and any approved supplementary verification; document inconsistencies and limitations; undertake pattern and legal analysis; and submit a complete first draft of the consolidated report.
- Finalize the report following fact-checking, legal review, and incorporation of comments; prepare the executive summary, recommendations, and any required confidential annexes or case matrices; maintain a response-to-comments record; prepare a presentation or advocacy brief if requested; and securely hand over all working and verification files.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities, noting that the total duration should not exceed 2 months, with 18 working days per month.

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- The consultant will be directly supervised by the NHRC-NPM and UNDP Governance and Rule of Law Chief Technical Advisor/Project Officer.
- The work is expected to start upon contract signature.
- The consultant will rely on their own means of communication and transportation and shall commute between their place of residence and the duty station at their own expense.
- The title rights, copyrights, and all other rights of whatsoever nature in any material produced under the provisions of this TOR will be vested exclusively in UNDP and NHRC. UNDP and NHRC have full ownership of the activity and of its final product. Thus, any public mention (including through social media) about the activity should state clearly that ownership. In addition, any public appearance related to the activity should be coordinated and approved by UNDP and NHRC.
- In the event of any delay, the consultant will inform UNDP promptly so that decisions and remedial action may be taken accordingly. Delays that would affect the flow of the collaborative work and the delivery of outputs on schedule may lead to termination of the contract.
- Should UNDP deem it necessary, it reserves the right to commission additional inputs, reviews, or revisions, as needed to ensure the quality and relevance of the work.
- The NHRC will assign priorities, approve fieldwork and engagement, review outputs, determine the classification and authorized use of information, and validate completion of deliverables in agreement with UNDP.
- The consultant will work in close coordination with designated NHRC personnel and shall comply with NHRC policies, security procedures, codes of conduct, and applicable UNDP requirements.
- Persistent or material failure to comply with approved deadlines, confidentiality, protection, security, or quality requirements may result in suspension or termination in accordance with the contract.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is two months, without exceeding 18 working days per month.

The mission is expected to commence immediately after contract signature and to be completed within 2 months from the contract signature date.

The time needed to review, comment on, and approve deliverables and outputs is five (5) working days.

**DUTY STATION**

The assignment is based primarily at the NHRC premises in Beirut, with approved field visits across Lebanon and meetings in locations relevant to the documentation and advocacy work. Field visits shall be undertaken only in accordance with the agreed work plan, access arrangements, and applicable security guidance.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- **Education:** A Master’s degree or equivalent in law, with a focus on international humanitarian law, international human rights law, international criminal law, public international law or a closely related field.
- **Experience:** Minimum six years of progressively responsible professional experience in legal research, human rights or IHL documentation, fact-finding, investigation, litigation, accountability, protection or related legal work.
- **Language:** Fluency in written and spoken Arabic and English is required.

**“The Personnel will be covered with Health insurance and Personal accident insurance; the fees shall be deducted from personnel's monthly payment”.**

jobs.title: National Consultant – Policy, Data and Integrity Solutions Specialist
jobs.description:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

- **Organization:** UNDP Lebanon Through Stars Orbit Consultants and Management Development
- **VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/194**
- **Position Title**: National Consultant – Policy, Data and Integrity Solutions Specialist
- **Duty Station:** Beirut
- **Duration:** 6 months (without exceeding 18 working days per month)
- **Vacancy Date of Issue: 13 October 2026**
- **Vacancy Closure Date: 20 October 2026**
- **National or International consultancy:** National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/10yGeBLH-4n82u7Z1HjCBeLJy1lT0D2Ii/view?usp=drive_link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/10yGeBLH-4n82u7Z1HjCBeLJy1lT0D2Ii/view?usp=drive_link)

**BACKGROUND**

Lebanon stands at a pivotal juncture in its governance and reform trajectory. Despite years of overlapping crises, the country has made landmark progress in building an integrity and anti-corruption framework, including the adoption and partial implementation of the National Anti-Corruption Strategy (2020–2025), the establishment of the National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC), and major legislative reforms on access to information, illicit enrichment, whistleblower protection, asset declaration, and public procurement. These milestones have laid the groundwork for the most coherent accountability architecture in Lebanon’s recent history.

However, these achievements remain fragile amid deep economic collapse, weakened institutions, and eroded public trust. While the strategic and legal frameworks are largely in place, implementation and enforcement mechanisms remain underdeveloped, and coordination among oversight institutions is still limited. The evaluation of the NACS highlighted the urgent need to consolidate progress by operationalizing national mechanisms, strengthening institutional capacities, and embedding corruption-risk management practices across public institutions.

In this context, the Integrity in ACTion Project was established with the objective of improving the implementation of an institutionalized and targeted approach to prevent and combat corruption through improved coordination, operationalized oversight, enhanced preventive and enforcement mechanisms, and institutionalized integrity and risk-management practices, thereby advancing transparency, accountability, and public trust.

The Project is designed to achieve this objective through three outputs:

**Output 1:** Institutional capacities to coordinate, monitor, and evaluate the National Anti-Corruption Strategy strengthened and operationalized through participatory and inclusive mechanisms.

**Output 2:** Legal frameworks and oversight institutions for preventing and combating corruption strengthened and effectively operationalized.

**Output 3:** Sectoral Corruption Risk Management mechanisms and integrity systems strengthened across key public sectors.

Under Output 1, the project will strengthen and operationalize Lebanon’s national anti-corruption coordination framework, with a focus on strategic planning, monitoring and evaluation, public reporting, stakeholder participation, and evidence-based implementation of the National Anti-Corruption Strategy and related reforms.

Under Output 2, the project will support the effective implementation and enforcement of Lebanon’s anti-corruption legal framework and strengthen the capacities of the National Anti-Corruption Commission and other oversight, integrity, and enforcement institutions. This will include the provision of support for the practical application of anti-corruption laws, including mechanisms that enable citizens to exercise their rights.

Under Output 3, the project will support the institutionalization of Sectoral Corruption Risk Management (SCRM) and integrity systems across priority public institutions, linking corruption prevention with administrative simplification, process re-engineering, digital transformation, and broader public administration reform. It will also support the development and implementation of practical integrity measures, tools, standards, and solutions that strengthen institutional performance, transparency, and service delivery.

Across these three outputs, the Policy, Data and Integrity Solutions Specialist will provide integrated technical, analytical, and policy support, including research and data analysis, monitoring and reporting, stakeholder coordination, institutional capacity development, and the design and application of data-driven, digital, transparency, and integrity solutions that support the effective implementation of anti-corruption reforms.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the general supervision of the UNDP I-ACT Project Manager, the Policy, Data and Integrity Solutions Specialist will provide integrated technical, analytical, and coordination support to the implementation of anti-corruption, integrity, and governance reform initiatives, with a particular focus on the National Anti-Corruption Strategy and related institutional reform initiatives under the I-ACT Project.

The Specialist will support evidence-based policy development and implementation, data collection and analysis, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, stakeholder engagement and coordination, the development and application of integrity and transparency solutions, and institutional capacity development.

**Task 1: Research, Policy, Data, Monitoring and Reporting**

- Provide research, policy, and analytical support for the development, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, and periodic updating of the National Anti-Corruption Strategy (NACS) and related anti-corruption and integrity reforms.
- Conduct policy, legal, institutional, and comparative research; review policies, institutional arrangements, and implementation practices in line with international standards; and identify gaps, implementation priorities, and opportunities for strengthening Lebanon’s anti-corruption and integrity frameworks.
- Support the development and application of results-based monitoring and evaluation frameworks, indicators, baselines, targets, implementation matrices, reporting tools, and data-collection mechanisms for the NACS and related reforms.
- Collect, consolidate, clean, analyze, visualize, and interpret administrative, survey, and other relevant data on reform implementation, institutional performance, and results, and support national institutions in strengthening data quality, availability, management, and use.
- Prepare evidence-based analytical and policy products, including progress and monitoring reports, dashboards, policy briefs, background and technical papers, concept notes, terms of reference, presentations, and recommendations to inform decision-making and reform implementation.

**Task 2: Stakeholder Engagement, Coordination and Policy Dialogue**

- Support structured engagement and coordination among OMSAR, NACC, relevant ministries, public institutions, oversight bodies, civil society, youth, media, academia, professional associations, the private sector, international organizations, and development partners.
- Support the organization and follow-up of national anti-corruption coordination mechanisms, including MACcom and TACcom, specialized task teams, working groups, and other policy and technical dialogues, through the preparation of agendas, background materials, policy and data inputs, briefing notes, speeches, communication materials, and presentations.
- Coordinate and consolidate stakeholder inputs, prepare minutes and meeting reports, document decisions and recommendations, and maintain follow-up and tracking mechanisms to support implementation of agreed actions and reform priorities.
- Support policy dialogue and coordination between national institutions, international partners, and other relevant stakeholders to promote complementarity, policy coherence, knowledge exchange, and alignment of technical support around national anti-corruption and integrity priorities.
- Support consultations and participatory processes that enable civil society, youth, media, academia, professional groups, the private sector, and other non-state actors to contribute to the development, implementation, monitoring, and communication of anti-corruption and integrity reforms.

**Task 3: Data, Digital and Integrity Solutions**

- Support the translation of anti-corruption, integrity, transparency, and corruption-risk priorities into practical tools, methodologies, institutional processes, data-driven solutions, and, where relevant, digital solutions.
- Provide technical and analytical support for the effective implementation of specialized anti-corruption laws, including the Right of Access to Information Law, through the development and improvement of monitoring, transparency, data, and accountability tools.
- Support the design, development, and continuous improvement of dashboards, databases, digital reporting and monitoring systems, transparency platforms, and other data-driven tools, including defining data requirements, indicators, workflows, functional requirements, and visualization and reporting needs.
- Support the development and implementation of practical integrity solutions emerging from Sectoral Corruption Risk Management (SCRM), including measures related to process simplification and re-engineering, transparency, internal controls, information flows, data use, and digitalization.
- Work with government counterparts, technical experts, developers, and service providers to translate policy and institutional requirements into functional requirements and ensure that proposed solutions respond to identified corruption risks, institutional and user needs, and requirements for transparency, interoperability, sustainability, and effective monitoring.
- Promote responsible, accessible, and effective use of data in integrity and transparency solutions, including attention to data quality, availability, interoperability, and appropriate data management standards.

**Task 4: Institutional Support, Capacity Development and Knowledge Production**

- Provide ongoing technical and analytical support to the Anti-Corruption Unit at OMSAR, the National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC), oversight and integrity institutions, and relevant ministries and public institutions in areas related to NACS implementation, anti-corruption laws, integrity systems, data and monitoring, transparency, and SCRM.
- Strengthen the internal capacities of national institutions, particularly the Anti-Corruption Unit at OMSAR and relevant NACS coordination mechanisms, in strategic planning, results-based management, monitoring and evaluation, data collection and analysis, and reporting on the implementation of the NACS and related anti-corruption reforms.
- Provide continuous technical accompaniment and hands-on support to institutional counterparts and designated focal points to translate NACS priorities, anti-corruption commitments, legal requirements, and integrity priorities into institutional plans, implementation measures, monitoring arrangements, indicators, tools, and practical solutions.
- Design and deliver training and capacity-development activities, complemented by on-the-job technical accompaniment, coaching, and practical guidance, for public officials and institutional focal points on strategic planning, NACS implementation and monitoring, anti-corruption and integrity, access to information, monitoring and evaluation, data collection and use, transparency, SCRM, and related areas within the scope of the Project.
- Prepare technical documentation, analytical notes, institutional briefs, guidance materials, presentations, implementation updates, and follow-up matrices to support senior officials, national coordination mechanisms, public institutions, and technical working groups.
- Develop and adapt training materials, guidance notes, manuals, practical tools, case studies, presentations, and other knowledge products to strengthen institutional capacities and support their effective and sustainable application.
- Document lessons learned, good practices, and emerging approaches and support knowledge exchange and dissemination at national and, where relevant, regional levels.

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- The consultant will work under the guidance of the I-ACT Project Manager.
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely, thorough, and transparent manner. UNDP will also be responsible for providing clarifications and facilitating the work.
- Day-to-day transportation from home to office (and vice versa) shall be covered by the Consultant’s own means. The Consultant will rely on their own means of communication and transportation.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 6 months.

The mission is expected to commence immediately after contract signature and be completed within 6 months from the contract signature date.

The time needed to review, comment on, and approve deliverables and outputs is five (5) working days.

**DUTY STATION**

The duty station will be in Beirut, Lebanon, with the possibility of working from the premises of the Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform and commuting throughout Lebanon.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- **Education:** A Master’s degree in Economics, Public Administration, Political Science, Social Sciences, or other related fields is required.
- **Experience:** A minimum of six (6) year of relevant experience in research, policy analysis, knowledge management, data analysis, and stakeholder engagement, within the public sector or international organizations in areas related to governance, transparency, integrity, and anti- corruption.
- **Language:** Fluency in English and Arabic.

**“The Personnel will be covered with Health insurance and Personal accident insurance; the fees shall be deducted from personnel's monthly payment”.**

jobs.title: Venezuela: Auxiliar de Compras (Caracas)
jobs.description:
La Cruz Roja Venezolana (CRV) es una organización humanitaria cuyo mandato es salvar vidas y mejorar las condiciones de las personas en situación de vulnerabilidad. Como parte del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y la Media Luna Roja, brinda asistencia oportuna en emergencias, desastres y contextos de necesidad humanitaria.

Guiada por sus Principios Fundamentales—Humanidad, Imparcialidad, Neutralidad, Independencia, Voluntariado, Unidad y Universalidad—la CRV actúa como auxiliar de los poderes públicos en el ámbito humanitario, trabajando para reducir el sufrimiento humano sin distinción de raza, género, religión o ideología. Su labor abarca la atención médica de emergencia, el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia comunitaria, la capacitación en primeros auxilios, la respuesta a desastres y la promoción de la salud y el bienestar.

A través de una red de voluntarios altamente comprometidos, la CRV moviliza recursos de manera eficiente y eficaz para estar presente donde más se necesita, cuando más se necesita. Su labor se fundamenta en la solidaridad, el respeto a la dignidad humana y el compromiso con la protección de la vida en todas sus formas.

Si deseas formar parte del equipo y hacer la diferencia, te invitamos a sumarte.

*¿Cómo puedes hacer la diferencia? Funciones claves / Responsabilidades*

El/La Auxiliar de Compras tiene como propósito fundamental proporcionar un soporte operativo y administrativo a la gestión de adquisiciones de bienes y servicios de la Cruz Roja Venezolana. Este rol es crucial para asegurar la ejecución eficiente y transparente del proceso de compra de bienes y servicios (incluyendo insumos médicos, material de oficina, equipos, etc.), desde la recepción de solicitudes, el análisis de proveedores, ofertas, negociaciones hasta la entrega final. Su labor se centra en la documentación, seguimiento y cumplimiento del Procedimiento de Compras de la Cruz Roja, garantizando la transparencia y rendición de cuentas.

Será el/la encargado(a) de:

- Recepción y Revisión de Solicitudes: recibir y validar las solicitudes de compra (requisiciones) de los diferentes departamentos, asegurando que estén debidamente aprobadas y especificadas.
- Búsqueda de Proveedores y Cotizaciones: asistir en la búsqueda de potenciales proveedores y solicitar cotizaciones para compras menores, según los umbrales y procedimientos internos.
- Emisión de Órdenes de Compra (OC): Preparar y emitir las Órdenes de Compra una vez que la opción de proveedor haya sido aprobada.
- Convocatoria de Licitaciones: Colaborar en la preparación de los Términos de Referencia (TDR) o Solicitudes de Propuesta (RFP/RFQ) y asistir en la publicación o difusión de las convocatorias de licitación, siguiendo las normativas de la Cruz Roja Venezolana y/o los donantes.
- Recepción y Registro: Gestionar la recepción formal de las ofertas de los licitantes, asegurando la confidencialidad y el registro oportuno de los documentos.
- Análisis Preliminar: Asistir en el análisis técnico y económico preliminar de las propuestas recibidas en el marco de la licitación, verificando el cumplimiento de los requisitos administrativos y especificaciones técnicas.
- Selección y Adjudicación: Participar en la documentación del proceso de selección y apoyar en la notificación formal de la adjudicación o rechazo a los participantes.
- Documentación del Proceso: Garantizar que el expediente de licitación esté completo y debidamente auditado, incluyendo la matriz de evaluación, actas de apertura, actas de adjudicación y el contrato final.
- Seguimiento de Pedidos: Realizar el seguimiento continuo a las Órdenes de Compra y contratos resultantes de licitaciones para garantizar la entrega oportuna.
- Recepción y Conformidad: Colaborar en la verificación de la recepción física de los bienes y la gestión de la
documentación de conformidad (Actas de Recepción).
- Archivo de Expedientes: Mantener un sistema de archivo completo, organizado y seguro de todos los expedientes de compra y licitación.

*Reporte*

El/La Auxiliar de Compras le reportará a la Coordinación de Compras.

*Lugar de trabajo*

Caracas (CRV Sede Central).

*Para calificar como un constructor del sistema humanitario venezolano deberás cumplir con los siguientes requisitos:*

- Grado Técnico o Licenciatura en Administración, Finanzas o Contaduría Pública.
- Experiencia laboral de al menos tres (3) anos el departamento de compras de organizaciones privadas y/o humanitarias (preferiblemente).
- Conocimientos y manejo de procesos administrativos.
- Conocimientos básicos en normas contables, tributarias y fiscales.
- Conocimientos básicos en el manejo y dominio de sistemas de información financiera y contables.
- Experiencia trabajando con el Movimiento de la Cruz Roja / Media Luna Roja es deseable.
- Excelentes habilidades de comunicación, capacidad para construir relaciones a todos los niveles.
- Capacidad para trabajar de forma independiente y como miembro de un equipo.
- Capacidad y acuerdo para adherirse a los Principios Fundamentales de la Cruz Roja y la Media Luna Roja.
- Capacidad de mantener la confidencialidad.
- Gran sentido de la responsabilidad y ética profesional.

jobs.title: Venezuela: Oficial de Gestión de Riesgos y Desastres (Caracas)
jobs.description:
La Cruz Roja Venezolana (CRV) es una organización humanitaria cuyo mandato es salvar vidas y mejorar las condiciones de las personas en situación de vulnerabilidad. Como parte del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y la Media Luna Roja, brinda asistencia oportuna en emergencias, desastres y contextos de necesidad humanitaria.

Guiada por sus Principios Fundamentales—Humanidad, Imparcialidad, Neutralidad, Independencia, Voluntariado, Unidad y Universalidad—la CRV actúa como auxiliar de los poderes públicos en el ámbito humanitario, trabajando para reducir el sufrimiento humano sin distinción de raza, género, religión o ideología. Su labor abarca la atención médica de emergencia, el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia comunitaria, la capacitación en primeros auxilios, la respuesta a desastres y la promoción de la salud y el bienestar.

A través de una red de voluntarios altamente comprometidos, la CRV moviliza recursos de manera eficiente y eficaz para estar presente donde más se necesita, cuando más se necesita. Su labor se fundamenta en la solidaridad, el respeto a la dignidad humana y el compromiso con la protección de la vida en todas sus formas.

**Compromiso con la Salvaguarda**

La Cruz Roja Venezolana está comprometida con la creación y mantenimiento de entornos seguros y respetuosos para las comunidades, el personal y el voluntariado y con la prevención de la explotación, el abuso y el acoso sexual.

Las personas seleccionadas deberán cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas y estándares de Salvaguarda aplicables. Como parte de su proceso de contratación segura, la CRV podrá realizar verificaciones de referencias profesionales y solicitar información pertinente sobre antecedentes de conducta profesional y Salvaguarda, de acuerdo con sus procedimientos y la normativa aplicable.

**Responsabilidad general de Salvaguarda**

La persona titular del puesto deberá promover y respetar los estándares de Salvaguarda de la Cruz Roja Venezolana, cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas aplicables, mantener límites profesionales apropiados, contribuir a prevenir daños y reportar de forma inmediata cualquier preocupación de Salvaguarda a través de los mecanismos establecidos.

**Adición para puestos de riesgo elevado**

Debido a la naturaleza de sus funciones, la persona deberá identificar y mitigar activamente riesgos de Salvaguarda asociados a sus actividades, mantener estándares reforzados de conducta y límites profesionales y asegurar que su interacción con comunidades y personas en situación de vulnerabilidad se desarrolle de forma segura, digna, inclusiva y respetuosa.

Si deseas formar parte del equipo y hacer la diferencia, te invitamos a sumarte.

*¿Cómo puedes hacer la diferencia? Funciones claves / Responsabilidades*

El/La Oficial de Gestión del Riesgos y Desastres será responsable de apoyar técnica y operativamente la implementación de acciones de preparación ante desastres, reducción de riesgos, coordinación operativa y respuesta rápida de la Cruz Roja Venezolana, en el marco de programas y proyectos orientados al fortalecimiento de capacidades locales, institucionales y comunitarias frente a escenarios multi-amenaza.

Este cargo tendrá un enfoque prioritario en la reducción de riesgos, el fortalecimiento de capacidades territoriales, la actualización de planes de contingencia, la activación de mecanismos del manejo de emergencias y desastres, la interoperabilidad con actores del sistema nacional de gestión del riesgo y la articulación entre las filiales de la CRV, autoridades competentes, Protección Civil y Administración de Desastres, cuerpos de bomberos, organizaciones comunitarias y otros actores humanitarios.

Será el/la encargado(a) de:

- Contribuir a la planificación, implementación, seguimiento y reporte técnico de las actividades de gestión del riesgo de desastres, reducción de riesgos y manejo de emergencias y desastres.
- Apoyar el desarrollo, actualización y validación de análisis multirriesgo en zonas priorizadas, incorporando amenazas hidrometeorológicas, geológicas y climáticas, movilidad humana, escenarios de afectación múltiple, y emergencias complejas.
- Acompañar técnicamente a las filiales y actores locales en la elaboración, actualización y validación de planes de contingencia multi-amenaza a nivel comunitario, municipal o regional, según corresponda y enfoque de protección, género e inclusión.
- Apoyar la identificación de amenazas, vulnerabilidades, capacidades y brechas operativas en comunidades priorizadas, filiales y estructuras locales de respuesta, utilizando metodologías participativas y herramientas institucionales de análisis de riesgos.
- Contribuir a la conformación, fortalecimiento y acompañamiento de Equipos Comunitarios de Respuesta a Emergencias, puntos focales de GRD, personal técnico y voluntariado operativo de la CRV.
- Coordinar y facilitar procesos de formación en gestión del riesgo de desastres, preparación comunitaria, acción anticipatoria, sistemas de alerta temprana, evaluación rápida de necesidades, coordinación operativa y respuesta inicial ante emergencias.
- Apoyar la planificación, ejecución y evaluación de simulaciones, simulacros y ejercicios operativos a nivel comunitario, local, regional y nacional, orientados a fortalecer la coordinación, la toma de decisiones, la activación temprana y la interoperabilidad entre actores.
- Contribuir al diseño, actualización y socialización de procedimientos operativos estándar, protocolos, flujos de activación, herramientas de coordinación y mecanismos de interoperabilidad para preparación, despliegue y respuesta rápida ante emergencias.
- Apoyar técnicamente la preparación de capacidades de despliegue rápido de la CRV, incluyendo criterios de activación, perfiles de equipos, rutas de comunicación, listas de verificación, mecanismos de alistamiento y coordinación con filiales.
- Coordinar con las áreas de logística, compras, finanzas y programas para asegurar que el preposicionamiento de insumos humanitarios responda a análisis de riesgo, escenarios de contingencia, prioridades operativas y criterios de respuesta rápida.
- Brindar insumos técnicos para el fortalecimiento de hubs logísticos estratégicos y mecanismos de preposicionamiento, asegurando su articulación con planes de contingencia, rutas de despliegue, capacidades territoriales y escenarios de emergencia.
- Apoyar la movilización rápida de asistencia humanitaria inicial durante emergencias, en coordinación con la Coordinación de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres, filiales, logística, autoridades competentes y actores aliados.
- Participar en la realización de evaluaciones rápidas de necesidades durante emergencias súbitas o escenarios de afectación múltiple, contribuyendo a la definición de acciones prioritarias de respuesta en las primeras fases de activación.
- Apoyar la activación y seguimiento de mecanismos de respuesta flexible o Crisis Modifier, cuando corresponda, asegurando documentación técnica, coordinación operativa, registro de decisiones y sistematización de evidencias.
- Contribuir a la articulación técnica con Protección Civil y Administración de Desastres, cuerpos de bomberos, autoridades locales, organizaciones comunitarias, actores humanitarios y socios del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y de la Media Luna Roja.
- Apoyar espacios técnicos de coordinación nacional, regional y binacional vinculados a reducción del riesgo acción anticipatoria, sistemas de alerta temprana, manejo de emergencias y gestión de escenarios transfronterizos, previa autorización de la Coordinación de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres.
- Promover la integración de enfoques transversales de protección, género e inclusión, participación comunitaria y rendición de cuentas, acción climática, sostenibilidad ambiental, acceso seguro y no hacer daño en las actividades de GRD.
- Apoyar la incorporación de criterios de sostenibilidad ambiental, adaptación climática y logística verde en las actividades de reducción, simulación, preposicionamiento y respuesta, en coordinación con las áreas responsables.
- Contribuir al desarrollo de indicadores, herramientas de monitoreo, matrices de seguimiento y mecanismos de control de calidad para las actividades de preparación, fortalecimiento de capacidades, simulacros, respuesta rápida y coordinación operativa.
- Recopilar, organizar y sistematizar fuentes de verificación, informes de actividad, listas de asistencia, registros fotográficos, actas, reportes de campo, evaluaciones post-actividad y demás evidencias requeridas por la CRV y los socios del proyecto.
- Elaborar informes técnicos y operativos sobre avances, alertas, brechas, resultados, lecciones aprendidas y recomendaciones relacionadas con la implementación de actividades de GRD.
- Participar en revisiones posteriores a operaciones, After Action Reviews, Real-Time Evaluations u otros ejercicios de aprendizaje institucional, contribuyendo a la actualización de procedimientos y mejora continua de la preparación y respuesta.
- Representar técnicamente a la CRV en espacios de coordinación con actores gubernamentales, comunitarios, humanitarios y del sistema de gestión del riesgo, previa autorización de la Coordinación de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres.
- Asegurar la aplicación de los Principios Fundamentales de la Cruz Roja y de la Media Luna Roja, el Código de Conducta, las políticas institucionales, los estándares de seguridad, protección de datos y confidencialidad en todas las actividades.
- Ejecutar otras tareas asignadas por sus superiores inmediatos que contribuyan al fortalecimiento del área de gestión del riesgo de desastres y al cumplimiento de los objetivos institucionales y del proyecto.

*Reporte*

El/La Oficial de Gestión del Riesgos y Desastres le reportará a la Coordinación de Gestión del Riesgo de Desastres.

*Lugar de trabajo*

Caracas (Sede central de la Cruz Roja Venezolana), con disponibilidad para viajar a nivel nacional.

*Para calificar como un constructor del sistema humanitario venezolano deberás cumplir con los siguientes requisitos:*

- Título universitario en gestión de riesgos, ingeniería, ciencias ambientales, geografía, ciencias sociales, relaciones internacionales, administración de desastres o carreras afines.
- Experiencia mínima de tres (3) años en gestión del riesgo de desastres, preparación ante desastres, reducción de riesgos, respuesta humanitaria, protección civil, coordinación operativa o programas comunitarios de resiliencia.
- Experiencia demostrable en implementación de actividades de preparación ante desastres, planes de contingencia, simulacros, formación comunitaria o fortalecimiento de capacidades locales de respuesta.
- Conocimiento de metodologías participativas de análisis de vulnerabilidades y capacidades, evaluación de riesgos, planificación comunitaria y preparación local.
- Conocimiento práctico de sistemas de alerta temprana, acción anticipatoria, evaluación rápida de necesidades, protocolos de activación y mecanismos de respuesta ante emergencias.
- Experiencia en coordinación con autoridades locales, Protección Civil y Administración de Desastres, cuerpos de bomberos, organizaciones comunitarias, actores humanitarios o estructuras territoriales de respuesta.
- Capacidad para facilitar procesos formativos, talleres, simulaciones y ejercicios prácticos con personal técnico, voluntariado, comunidades y actores institucionales.
- Experiencia en elaboración de informes técnicos, sistematización de información, manejo de fuentes de verificación y seguimiento de indicadores.
- Conocimiento básico de logística humanitaria, preposicionamiento de insumos, organización de equipos de respuesta y mecanismos de despliegue rápido es deseable.
- Conocimiento de enfoques de protección, género e inclusión, participación comunitaria y rendición de cuentas, no hacer daño, acceso seguro y protección de datos en contextos humanitarios.
- Experiencia trabajando con el Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y de la Media Luna Roja es deseable.
- Conocimiento del contexto venezolano, del sistema nacional de gestión del riesgo de desastres y de dinámicas de riesgo en territorios fronterizos es deseable.
- Manejo de herramientas ofimáticas, plataformas de recolección de datos y sistemas básicos de gestión de información.
- Fluidez oral y escrita en español. Conocimientos de inglés son deseables.
- Excelentes habilidades de comunicación, planificación, organización, redacción y trabajo en equipo.
- Capacidad para trabajar bajo presión, adaptarse a contextos cambiantes y mantener criterios de seguridad, neutralidad, confidencialidad y responsabilidad institucional.
- Compromiso con los Principios Fundamentales de la Cruz Roja y de la Media Luna Roja.
- Alto sentido de responsabilidad, ética profesional y orientación a resultados.

jobs.title: Senior Partnership Officer (Support)
jobs.description:
**Job Title**: Senior Partnership Support Officer

**Department:** Programming

**Division :** Programme Implementation

**Duty Station**: Odesa (with frequent travel to NPs programme sites including Mykolaiv, Kherson, Kharkiv, Donetsk/Dnipro)

**Line Manager:** Programme Manager – Partnerships (PM-P)

**Line Management Responsibility:** N/A

**Position Type:** Full-time

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) is a dynamic, international non-governmental organisation. We work with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP). We work to reduce violence, protect civilians in countries affected by violent conflict and its aftermath, and help transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

**Overview**

NP occupies a unique space in the protection response in Ukraine; simultaneously providing direct protection to at-risk civilians and providing hands-on support to front-line volunteer collectives to directly contribute to the sustainability and safety of their actions. NP promotes responsible partnerships and ‘localisation in practice’ and is currently building out its Partnerships Support Department to provide increased direct and dedicated support to its partners in Ukraine including national non-governmental organisations (NNGOs), Community-Based Organisations (CBOs), Civil Society Organisations (CSOs), and local volunteer collectives. In 2024 NP is piloting a Tier system for partnership and an open call for proposals for grants.

**Job summary**

The Senior Partnership Support Officer supports the Programme Manager – Partnerships in the day-to-day operational coordination of NP Ukraine's partnership portfolio, facilitating the consistent application of partnership procedures, quality documentation, timely follow-up and effective implementation of partnership processes throughout the project cycle.

The position combines independent management of an assigned portfolio of partner projects with broader operational coordination and technical support to Partnership Support Officers. Acting as a key operational support to the Programme Manager – Partnerships, the Senior Partnership Support Officer helps address complex implementation challenges, facilitates coordination between partners, Partnership Support Officers, Partnerships Finance Officers and NP field teams, and consolidates relevant information to support management oversight and decision-making.

The role provides technical guidance to Partnership Support Officers, supports partner capacity strengthening and contributes to the continuous improvement of partnership systems and responsible partnership practices, including Duty of Care. While the Senior Partnership Support Officer facilitates operational coordination across the department, overall portfolio accountability and management decisions remain with the Programme Manager – Partnerships, and individual Partnership Support Officers retain responsibility for their assigned projects.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Direct Partner Portfolio Management and Project Cycle Support**

- Serve as the primary operational focal point for an assigned portfolio of partner organisations, maintaining regular communication and providing direct support throughout the partnership project cycle.
- Independently manage the day-to-day programmatic and operational aspects of assigned partner subgrants, including project development, contracting, implementation, reporting, monitoring, amendments and closure.
- Support partner identification, mapping, Calls for Proposals, selection, due diligence and capacity assessment processes, including preparation and review of documentation and follow-up on identified risks.
- Prepare and coordinate partnership agreements, Memorandums of Understanding and amendments for assigned projects, ensuring completeness, accuracy, timely processing and compliance with NP procedures.
- Review partner concept notes, project proposals, workplans, logical frameworks and narrative reports, providing feedback and ensuring alignment with approved activities, project objectives and donor requirements.
- Conduct regular partner check-ins and on-site monitoring visits, track implementation progress, indicators, deliverables and reporting deadlines, and follow up on agreed actions and corrective measures.
- Coordinate with Partnerships Finance Officers and NP field teams on budget revisions, payments, implementation challenges and other matters affecting assigned partner projects.
- Ensure timely and complete project closure, including final narrative reporting, documentation and follow-up on outstanding obligations.

**Portfolio Operations, Technical Coordination and Risk Management**

- Coordinate day-to-day partnership management processes across the department, supporting timely completion of key deliverables, consistent application of procedures and effective follow-up by responsible officers.
- Maintain a consolidated overview of project implementation progress, reporting schedules, partnership agreements, amendments, monitoring activities, outstanding actions and operational risks across the partnership portfolio.
- Provide technical guidance and support to Partnership Support Officers on complex partnership issues, contractual matters, documentation quality, compliance requirements and implementation challenges.
- Coordinate portfolio-wide on-site monitoring planning, consolidate monitoring findings and track implementation of agreed corrective actions, while individual Partnership Support Officers remain responsible for monitoring their assigned partners.
- Identify recurring operational challenges, implementation delays and compliance risks, facilitate practical solutions and escalate significant matters to the Programme Manager – Partnerships.
- Facilitate routine operational coordination between the Partnerships Department, NP field teams and relevant technical departments to support timely resolution of partnership-related issues.

**Partner Capacity Strengthening and Responsible Partnerships**

- Provide practical guidance and mentoring to assigned partners on project cycle management, reporting, compliance, organisational development and implementation challenges.
- Coordinate the identification of partner capacity-strengthening needs and support the planning and delivery of relevant training, mentoring, learning exchanges and resource-sharing activities in collaboration with NP teams.
- Support the operational implementation of partner Duty of Care activities, including identification of needs, coordination with relevant NP teams and follow-up on agreed actions.
- Facilitate partner feedback, mutual learning and meaningful participation in programme planning, promoting equitable, accountable and mutually beneficial partnerships.
- Provide technical guidance and peer support to Partnership Support Officers, encouraging knowledge sharing and consistent partnership management practices without formal line management responsibilities.

**Partnership Systems, Documentation and Continuous Improvement**

- Coordinate the maintenance of partnership mapping, databases, trackers and reporting systems, ensuring accurate and timely updates across the portfolio, with individual officers responsible for their assigned project records.
- Ensure consistent application of partnership procedures, documentation standards and filing requirements, including the use of SharePoint and Salesforce.
- Contribute to the development and improvement of partnership management tools, templates, guidance materials and standard operating procedures to strengthen operational efficiency and quality.
- Consolidate partnership implementation updates, monitoring findings, operational risks and lessons learned, identifying opportunities for improving partnership processes and partner support.
- Prepare consolidated portfolio updates, operational analysis and recommendations for the Programme Manager – Partnerships to support management oversight, planning and decision-making.

Perform other duties and assignments as required within the scope of the position.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

**Education, Knowledge, and Experience**

- Post-secondary education in Project Management, International Development, Social Sciences, Human Rights, Humanitarian Studies or a related field.
- Minimum 3 years of relevant professional experience, including at least 2 years in partnership management, grants management or humanitarian project implementation.
- Demonstrated experience in managing partner projects throughout the project cycle, including project development, due diligence, partnership agreements, narrative reporting, monitoring and closure.
- Experience working directly with local and national NGOs, civil society organisations or community-based organisations, including providing technical support and capacity-strengthening assistance.
- Good knowledge of donor compliance requirements, humanitarian principles, localisation approaches and the operational context in Ukraine.
- Experience coordinating multiple projects, partnership processes or cross-functional activities is an advantage.
- Ukrainian citizenship.

**Skills and Competencies**

- Strong organisational and project management skills, with the ability to independently manage multiple partner projects and competing priorities.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify operational risks, address complex partnership issues and propose practical solutions.
- Ability to coordinate partnership processes across multiple projects, maintain consolidated operational information and ensure timely follow-up on agreed actions.
- Demonstrated ability to provide technical guidance, mentoring and support to colleagues and partner organisations.
- Strong interpersonal, communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work effectively with partners, field teams and other NP departments.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office and experience with project management, reporting and tracking systems; familiarity with SharePoint and Salesforce is an advantage.
- Fluency in Ukrainian and strong working proficiency in English, both written and spoken.

**Key Challenges**

- Working with small and newly created organisations requires very high attention to detail, patience and constant support.
- Building and sustaining collaborative partnerships, negotiating, and resolving contentious issues and conflicts of interest.

**Working Conditions:**

- This position requires travel to insecure locations. You must be prepared to travel and to spend time away from the duty station.
- Demonstrated ability to adhere to strict security protocols and maintain high level of professionalism.

jobs.title: Grants and Reporting Officer
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Grants and Reporting Officer

**Function:** Programme Support

**Job Group:** Programmes

**Duty Station:** Odesa, Ukraine (with potential travel to field locations)

**Line Manager:** Programme Development Manager

**Line Management Responsibility:** N/a

**ABOUT US:**

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) reimagines security and civilian protection in areas most impacted by conflict by working alongside communities to interrupt and prevent violence. NP is a global civil society organization that works with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP) and by helping to transform the world’s response to conflict. Programming is founded on unarmed civilian protection and is thematically focused on protection in displacement, child protection, gender-based violence protection and inter-communal violence reduction, social cohesion, and civic engagement.

NP first established a presence in Ukraine in 2014-15 working on peacebuilding and conflict mediation. NP has had a sustained presence in Ukraine since April 2022 and is operational in Kharkiv, Donetska, Dnipropetrovsk, Kherson, Mykolaiv and Odesa oblasts. NP occupies an established space in the protection response in Ukraine; simultaneously providing direct protection to at-risk civilians and providing hands-on support to front-line volunteer collectives to contribute to the sustainability and safety of their actions.

**JOB PURPOSE:**

The Grants and Reporting Officer (GRO) will collaboratively work with the Programmes, Finance and Operational Teams in NP’s Ukraine Country Office to ensure compliance with donor regulations and monitor grant implementation in-line with agreed workplans and objectives. This includes project activity oversight, donor reporting and supporting proposal development (where applicable).

**KEY OBJECTIVES/RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Grants Management and Reporting**

- Lead in drafting narrative donor reports and relevant annexes (i.e. logical frameworks, impact assessments, case studies), ensuring excellent quality, accuracy and adherence to donor guidelines.
- Support programmes, finance and field teams to understand donor contractual requirements, ensuring grant compliance from the outset of grant roll-out (i.e. through inception workshops).
- Maintain information management and involve all internal stakeholders in communications on fundraising issues for grants.
- Lead on updating relevant online platforms (e.g. UN’s Grants Management System (GMS)) with project data and reports, as well as responding to notifications and/or additional information requests from key donors.
- Compile and analyse data to write field activity reports submitted by staff and partners, aligning with grant deliverables.
- Act as team focal point for Salesforce (NP’s global online project management system), including creating new opportunities / projects, updating project activities, monitoring project outputs, tracking progress and extracting relevant information for reporting.
- Coordinate with the finance department to ensure that financial reports are submitted on time, comply with financial reporting requirements and align with narrative reported activity progress.
- Review donor reports, project proposals and communication materials as required.

**Partnership Support**

- Maintain regular communication and coordination with NP’s Partnership department to collect and synthesise data for activity and donor reports.
- Support NP’s Partnership department to draft sub-grant contracts in-line with donor compliance and agreed logframes, objectives and activities.
- Follow up with partners’ implemented activities and report progress through Salesforce.
- Support ad-hoc capacity development requests from partners and provide trainings, guidance and mentoring as needed.

**Other**

- Support with rolling out NPUA’s country strategy across all project sites.
- Travel to project sites to enhance understanding of the context and programming to develop proposals and report to/liaise with donors.
- Undertake other relevant tasks as requested.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND COMPETENCIES:**

**Education, Knowledge, and Experience**

- Excellent and precise command of English, with exemplary oral and written communication skills, and an ability to develop high quality and engaging communications. There is a significant amount of writing required in this position.
- Significant experience developing narrative donor reports (for multilateral and institutional donors including the UN, FCDO, GAC, ECHO, SDC) under minimal supervision.
- Previous grants management, monitoring and evaluation (M&E) or reporting experience within a non-governmental organisation (NGO).
- Experience in institutional donor compliance and familiarity with basic rules and regulations. An understanding of basic statutory requirements would also be an asset.
- Experience in implementing, analysing and utilising M&E tools.
- Experience implementing programmes, ideally in humanitarian emergencies and/or in Ukraine.
- Knowledge or demonstrable interest in civilian protection, human security, violence reduction, protection and/or peacebuilding.
- Relevant university degree in social sciences, international development or related area of studies is preferred but not required. Corresponding work experience will also be considered.

**Skills**

- Diplomacy, professionalism and adept at relationship building.
- Ability to manage sensitive information with discretion.
- Demonstrable conflict analysis skills, identify entry points and design prevention and protection strategies.
- Ability to communicate effectively with individuals and work and live in a multicultural environment.
- Solutions-focused, creative problem solver.
- Genuine commitment to, and interest in, living and working at the community level.
- Flexibility and adaptability.

jobs.title: Partnership Finance Officer
jobs.description:
**Job Title**: Partnerships Finance Officer

**Department:** Partnerships

**Division:** Finance

**Duty Station**: Odesa (with travel to NP program sites, including Kharkiv and Donetsk)

**Line Manager:** Partnerships Support and Resource Manager (PSRP) (with Technical Line Mangement from Finance Manager)

**Line Management Responsibility:** NA

**Position Type:** Full-time

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) is a dynamic, international non-governmental organization. We work with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP). We work to reduce violence, protect civilians in countries affected by violent conflict and its aftermath, and help transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

**Overview**

NP occupies a unique space in the protection response in Ukraine; simultaneously providing direct protection to at-risk civilians and providing hands-on support to front-line volunteer collectives to directly contribute to the sustainability and safety of their actions. NP promotes responsible partnerships and ‘localization in practice’ and is currently building out its Partnerships Support Department to provide increased direct and dedicated support to its partners in Ukraine including national non-governmental organisations (NNGOs), Community-Based Organisations (CBOs), Civil Society Organisations (CSOs), and local volunteer collectives. NP is currently piloting a ‘Tier system’ for partnerships and an open call for funding.

**Job summary**

The Partnerships Finance Officer is responsible for the day-to-day financial management, monitoring and compliance of an assigned portfolio of partner subgrants across NP Ukraine's partnership programmes.

Working closely with the Senior Partnerships Finance Officer, the Programme Manager – Partnerships, the Finance and Logs Department and Partnership Support Officers, the position supports the full financial subgrant cycle, including budget review, implementation, financial reporting, payments, monitoring, amendments and closure.

The Partnerships Finance Officer works directly with partner organisations to ensure accurate financial reporting, responsible budget management, compliance with NP and donor requirements, and the strengthening of partners' financial management capacities.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Partner Financial Management and Subgrant Oversight**

- Manage the financial aspects of assigned partner subgrants throughout the project cycle, including budget review, implementation, financial reporting, monitoring, amendments and closure.
- Review and verify partner financial reports and supporting documentation, ensuring accuracy, completeness and compliance with NP and donor requirements.
- Conduct regular financial check-ins with assigned partners, monitor expenditure, Budget versus Actuals, spending plans and reporting deadlines, and ensure timely follow-up on identified issues.
- Prepare and process PRs and POs for partner subgrant instalments, ensuring completeness of supporting documentation, required approvals and coordination with the Finance Department for timely disbursement and liquidation.
- Review partner budgets and standard budget revisions, identifying financial discrepancies, budget deviations and necessary corrections.
- Support financial reconciliation and closure of assigned subgrants, ensuring that outstanding financial issues and documentation requirements are addressed.

**Financial Compliance, Monitoring and Risk Management**

- Monitor partner compliance with NP financial policies, donor requirements and financial provisions of partnership agreements.
- Identify financial reporting issues, budget deviations and potential compliance risks, propose corrective actions and escalate complex or significant issues as appropriate.
- Conduct financial monitoring and spot checks for assigned partners, including review of supporting documentation, financial records and relevant financial controls.
- Coordinate with the Finance Department on partner payments, financial reconciliation, reporting requirements and other financial matters related to assigned projects.

**Partner Financial Capacity Strengthening and Coordination**

- Provide practical financial guidance to partner organisations on budgeting, financial reporting, supporting documentation, financial controls and donor compliance.

jobs.title: Paediatric Orthoplastic Surgeon – Gaza Paediatric Injury Programme (GPIP)
jobs.description:
**Role:** Paediatric Orthoplastic Surgeon - Gaza Paediatric Injury Programme (GPIP)

**Hours:** Full time, with some weekend and evening working required to support the humanitarian programme delivery.

**Remuneration:** Negotiable (dependant on experience and within UK-Med humanitarian pay scales)

**Duration:** Up to 31st of December 2026 (funding pipeline dependent) with opportunity for extension.

**Deployment Pattern:** Able to commit to field-based deployments in Gaza, with rotations typically lasting 4 to 6 weeks. Flexibility is available for longer deployments of up to 8 weeks, depending on candidate availability and operational requirements. Shorter rotations may also be considered for suitably experienced candidates, subject to operational needs.

**Location:** Gaza, including UK-Med’s Type 2 Field Hospital in Al Mawasi and the Paediatric Orthopaedic Department at Nasser Medical Complex, with potential regional travel to Amman, Jordan.

*Candidates must be able to travel quickly through Jordan, securing visas on arrival with eligible documentation. If you do not meet this requirement, you can join our register of humanitarian and health professionals for other opportunities.*

**Can you lead high-quality surgical care for children with complex conflict-related injuries in Gaza?**

UK-Med is seeking an experienced Paediatric Orthoplastic Surgeon to join the Gaza Paediatric Injury Programme (GPIP), supporting children with severe limb trauma, amputations and other complex conflict-related injuries.

For many children, these injuries will have a lasting impact on their health, mobility and recovery. This role offers the opportunity to contribute highly specialised surgical expertise where it is urgently needed, while working as part of a wider multidisciplinary effort focused on safe, compassionate and high-quality care.

You will provide specialist surgical input across the patient pathway, from assessment and operative planning through to surgery, postoperative care and longer-term rehabilitation planning. You will work closely with national colleagues, UK-Med clinical teams and programme leadership to support coordinated and consistent care.

We recognise that securing one surgeon for a longer-term commitment may not always be possible. We are therefore open to considering either one surgeon able to provide longer-term continuity, or two suitably experienced surgeons rotating across alternate deployment periods. Where the role is shared, both surgeons will be expected to work closely together, with clear clinical handovers between rotations to ensure continuity of care, consistency of approach and a smooth transition for patients and the wider programme.

The role requires strong clinical judgement, sound surgical decision-making and the ability to work effectively in a complex and resource-constrained humanitarian setting. Relevant experience in paediatric orthopaedics, limb reconstruction, complex extremity trauma, amputations and limb salvage will be particularly important.

We are looking for someone who can combine specialist clinical expertise with compassion, adaptability and a collaborative approach, supporting both individual patient care and the wider development of the programme.

This is an opportunity to make a meaningful contribution to the care and recovery of children affected by conflict, while working alongside colleagues committed to strengthening surgical care in Gaza.

jobs.description:
