jobs.title: External Consultant (Category B) – Endline Evaluation for Displaced Afghans Regional Programme
jobs.description:
Position Title: **External Consultant (Category B) for the Endline Evaluation of the Project "Support to Displaced Afghans in Pakistan, Iran, Central Asia, and Afghanistan (EU/DG INTPA-funded)"**
Duty Station: **Kabul, Afghanistan**
Expected Start Date of Deployment: **01 November 2026**
Deployment Duration: **5 months**

**Background:**

The Islamic Republic of Afghanistan and its neighboring countries Pakistan, the Islamic Republic of Iran, and Tajikistan – together constitute one of the world’s most complex and protracted displacement contexts. Sustained conflict, economic collapse, climate shocks, and large-scale cross-border return have combined to produce acute and overlapping humanitarian, protection, and reintegration needs that extend well beyond Afghanistan’s borders. Since 2021, the region has absorbed sustained, high-volume returns of undocumented and documented Afghans from Iran and Pakistan, while smaller but significant caseloads of Afghans on the move and at risk of displacement remain present in Tajikistan and the wider Central Asia sub-region. It is this regional character of the crisis – and not Afghanistan alone – that defines the programme under evaluation.

IOM’s programme, funded by the European Union through DG INTPA and implemented across three Top-Up phases over a total duration of 63 months (with a revised end date of 31 March 2027), was designed accordingly as a two-outcome, four-country regional response. Outcome 1 covers the regional response in Pakistan, Iran, and Tajikistan; Outcome 2 covers the Afghanistan-based response. Programme design, resource allocation, and results reporting are structured around this regional architecture, and the evaluation must be resourced and scoped to reflect it in full not as an Afghanistan evaluation with regional context, but as a four-country regional evaluation with an Afghanistan component.

**Roles and Responsibilities of the Consultant:**

- Develop and finalize the evaluation matrix, methodology, and country-specific data collection tools, fit for purpose in each of the four programme countries.
- Design and apply an appropriate sampling methodology for each country and for the regional comparison.
- Lead the training and supervision of any locally engaged field data collectors in each country, ensuring adherence to the agreed protocol and methodology.
- Coordinate and technically oversee the two-phase field data collection exercise across all four countries, including locally engaged data collectors and other approved field support, and ensure consistent application of the evaluation methodology, ethical standards and data-quality requirements.
- Assure data quality through supervision and database review.
- Submit the Inception Report, Draft Report, and Final Report using agreed IOM templates.
- Present findings to the Evaluation Reference Group and other key internal and external stakeholders.

**Qualifications and Experience of the Consultant:**
The assignment shall be undertaken by an individual Consultant with demonstrated technical expertise and experience appropriate to the scale, complexity and regional nature of the evaluation. Applicants will be assessed against the following minimum and desirable requirements:

**Minimum Requirements:**

- An advanced university degree (Master’s degree or higher) in evaluation, research, public policy, migration studies, humanitarian assistance, international development, public health, social sciences or another field directly relevant to the assignment.
- A minimum of 10 years of progressively responsible professional experience in evaluation, including the design and implementation of complex evaluations for UN agencies, EU-funded programmes, multilateral organizations or comparable international development/humanitarian actors.
- Demonstrated experience leading or undertaking complex multi-country or regional evaluations, preferably involving displacement, migration, humanitarian response, durable solutions or related programming.
- Demonstrated expertise in mixed-methods evaluation, including quantitative and qualitative research design, sampling, development of data collection instruments, data analysis, triangulation and evidence synthesis.
- Demonstrated thematic experience relevant to the programme, including forced displacement/migration, protection, livelihoods/economic resilience and/or area-based approaches.
- Demonstrated experience integrating relevant cross-cutting considerations, including gender equality, protection, disability inclusion, accountability to affected populations and PSEAH, into evaluation design, data collection, analysis and reporting.
- Demonstrated experience producing high-quality evaluation reports and presenting complex findings and recommendations to institutional stakeholders and donors.
- Excellent written and spoken English.

**Desirable Requirements:**

- Previous evaluation or research experience in Afghanistan and/or the wider regional context covered by the evaluation, including Pakistan, the Islamic Republic of Iran and Tajikistan/Central Asia.
- Demonstrated knowledge of the UN system, IOM's mandate and/or EU/DG INTPA-funded programming.
- Knowledge of one of more relevant regional languages, including Dari, Pashto, Farci, or Urdu is an asset.

jobs.title: Head of HR, Africa Region
jobs.description:
**BRAC International (BI) is Hiring! Join BRAC International to create opportunities for people to realise their potential.**

**Position: Head of HR, Africa Region**

**Job Location:** **Nairobi, Kenya**

**Application deadline: October 31, 2026**

**About the Role:**

BRAC International is seeking a Head of HR, Africa Region- to provide greater support to Country Offices’ HR Functions across several HR-critical areas. The region currently covers Ghana, Liberia, Kenya, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Tanzania, and Uganda and a workforce of over 4,000 staff.

This position will report to the Regional Director, Africa. Collaborating closely with the Dhaka Central Office HR and the Regional Director, this role encompasses both country-specific and Nairobi Central Office responsibilities.

Key to the role will be providing support to both the Country Offices and the Nairobi Central Office, ensuring HR policies are contextualised and adhered to, and that any breaches are thoroughly investigated, with appropriate action taken and lessons learned.

**Key Responsibilities:**

- Lead thedevelopment and delivery of the BI HR Strategy in the Africa region.
- Lead Country Offices in the contextualisation of HR policy in line with national law, roll-out, and adherence, with sign-off from BI Central Office.
- Work with Country Office Senior Leadership to contextualise office structure and organograms, ensuring fit-for-purpose staffing across all units to achieve results.
- Guide recruitment processes in-country for staff below Head of/Deputy, ensuring HR recruitment policy is followed, and the right staff are in place to deliver across signed-off structures.
- Play a liaison role with the Dhaka Central Office in the recruitment of Country Directors and Deputy Country Directors/ Heads of Programme, as well as supporting the induction and onboarding of those staff.
- Play a lead role in the grievance and disciplinary processes for staff below Head/ Deputy, ensuring processes are followed as per policy.
- Drive the rollout of a new salary scale for Country Offices and any subsequent reviews.
- Ensure Performance Management processes are being implemented in Country Offices, including for CD and DCD/ Head of Programme.
- Assist in the development of security guidance and policy, including management of live safety and security issues.
- Work with the Dhaka Central Office HR Team to roll out the talent management process and succession planning for country management teams in the Africa region.
- Work with Country Teams to drive a OneBRAC culture across all teams
- Support the transition to a digital HR system, working in collaboration with the Central Offices staff.
- Training and support to Country Offices in all HR-related issues.
- Lead HR set-up for expansion into new countries, including workforce planning, recruitment of initial staff, employment contracts, payroll and benefits, in line with national law.
- Ensure HR practices meet donor requirements for grant-funded staffing, including staff costing in proposals, time allocation, fixed-term contracts aligned to grant cycles, and fair, well-planned transitions when grants end.

Regional Office Responsibilities

- Ensure the running of HR processes in the Nairobi Central Office in line with the policy.
- Ensure the Nairobi Central Office is fully staffed in line with the signed-off structure.
- Key point of contact for the Central Offices on all Nairobi Central Office HR matters, including running performance management processes, setting objectives, and reviewing staff in the Nairobi Central Office Team.
- Work with the Regional Director as well as HR staff across other units based in the Nairobi Central Office to ensure a one BRAC culture and team.

Safeguarding Responsibilities

- Establish a safeguarding culture by implementing safeguarding policies, hiring staff following safe recruitment and vetting, making any decisions guided by the do-no-harm principle, mitigating safeguarding risks, and maintaining a safe working environment where staff feel encouraged to voice concerns without fear of retaliation.
- Ensure 100% of team members, partners and service providers have access to and receive mandatory training on the safeguarding policies and reporting channels.
- Introduce a mandatory safeguarding agenda in monthly meetings to support continuous dialogue & reminders as part of building a safeguarding culture.

**Academic Qualifications:**

- Minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in any relevant discipline and a recognised professional HR qualification (e.g., CIPD or a national equivalent) is an advantage.

**Experience Requirements:**

- A minimum of 10 years of experience in the HR function, including at least 5 years in the multinational/international development sector.
- Experience in the areas of leadership and people management, and in strategy development and delivery.
- Experience/ working knowledge of multiple human resource disciplines, including talent management, performance management, talent acquisition, compensation practices, organisational diagnosis, employee relations, diversity, and employment laws, is highly preferred.
- Experience driving expansion and country footprint in complex markets.

**Required Skills, Competencies & Knowledge:**

- Strong analytical skills and a data-driven approach to continual improvement.
- Excellent judgment, sensitivity, and integrity.
- Frequent travel across the region and working with geographically dispersed teams.
- Demonstrated expertise in interpreting, navigating, and strategically applying complex employment laws, regulatory frameworks, and organisation policies.
- Competent in managing multicultural staff, working effectively with senior management teams.
- Strong interpersonal skills/ communication skills in English and collaborative mindset.
- Effective stakeholder management and negotiation skills.
- Proficiency in MS Office applications.
- Possess high ethical and moral standards.
- Hold a professional HR certification (e.g., CIPD or a national equivalent).

**Type of Employment:** Contractual

**About BRAC International:**

BRAC International (BI), a leading non-profit organisation, is on a mission to empower people and communities facing poverty, illiteracy, disease, and social injustice. Our vision is to create a world free from exploitation and discrimination, where everyone has the opportunity to realise their potential. We design proven, scalable solutions that equip people with the support and confidence they need to achieve their potential.

BRAC was founded in Bangladesh in 1972 and over the last five decades has grown to become one of the world’s largest non-governmental organisations (NGOs), reaching over 100 million people. We started our first international operation by venturing into Afghanistan in 2002, building on lessons from our work in Bangladesh to support a nation devastated by war. Currently operating in 14 countries across Asia and Africa. Born, proven and led in the Global South, BRAC International brings a unique Southern perspective and commitment to continuous learning, providing a depth of insight, experience and evidence to meet the needs of diverse communities with humility and courage across Asia and Africa. To learn more about BRAC International, please visit [www.bracinternational.org](http://www.bracinternational.org)

**Our Core Values:**

**Integrity:** We approach our work with honesty and integrity.

**Innovation:** We innovate and iterate to improve our impact.

**Inclusiveness:** We foster inclusion to reach those who need it most

**Effectiveness:** We strive for effectiveness to better serve people in poverty

jobs.title: Social Development Officer
jobs.description:
Overview of position

**Project:** Yemen Integrated Urban Services Emergency Project Phase II (YIUSEP II), Yemen Emergency Human Capital Project (YEHCP), and Integrated Water and Sanitation Emergency Project (IWISE)

**Duty Station:** Yemen

**Contract/Level:**

**Contract Type:** Daily Retainer - CTG

**Supervisor:** Project Manager

**Duration**: Initially until end of 2026 with extension possibility

## About the Region

Our client Middle East Region (MR) provides strategic leadership, performance oversight, and support to Our client operations across Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, Yemen, and the State of Palestine. MR is responsible for positioning Our client as a key development partner in the region through high-level engagement with regional bodies, UN coordination mechanisms, development banks, donors, and intergovernmental organisations. By fostering strategic partnerships and promoting operational excellence, the region supports country teams in delivering sustainable solutions to complex development, peace, and humanitarian challenges.

## About the Country/Multi-Country Office

Established in 2004, the Our client Amman Multi-Country Office (MCO) provides strategic and operational support to partners across Jordan, Syria, Lebanon, Iraq, Yemen, and the Gulf countries. The MCO delivers solutions that address development, peace, and humanitarian challenges through infrastructure, procurement, project management, and human resources services. Working in close collaboration with national governments, UN agencies, and donors, the office supports efforts to advance the Sustainable Development Goals. Its portfolio includes large-scale operations focused on improving essential services, strengthening national systems, and enhancing resilience in complex and fragile settings.

## About the Project Office

Our client Yemen Country Office supports partners in restoring essential infrastructure and public services amid a protracted, multifaceted crisis. Operating since 2013, the office delivers integrated interventions in urban services, energy access, health, water and sanitation, transport, and solid waste management sectors. The office also facilitates operational support for UN partners. With strong coordination across the different stakeholders, Our client Yemen supports the strengthening of local capacities and contributes to peacebuilding, recovery, and sustainable development efforts.

## Job Specific Context

The Social Development Officer plays an important role in assisting that our client subprojects in Yemen adhere to high social standards, particularly those set by the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and our client's Environmental and Social Sustainability framework.

Working with the E&S Specialist, this position is essential for mitigating social risks associated with infrastructure rehabilitation, urban service delivery, water, and health sector activities in a fragile, conflict-affected environment (FCV). The role focuses on supporting subproject screening, instrument preparation, stakeholder engagement, labor standard oversight, and the implementation of the Grievance Mechanism (GRM) to safeguard community well-being and project sustainability

Role objectives

## Functions / Key Results Expected

### 1. Compliance Support

● **Subproject Screening:** Assist in preparing, reviewing, and validating Environmental and Social Screening Forms for all proposed subprojects, ensuring rigorous verification of screening documents submitted by Implementing Partners (IPs).

● **E&S Instrument:** Support the drafting, review, and regular updating of site-specific Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs), Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs), and Abbreviated RAPs where applicable, ensuring alignment with WB Environmental and Social Standards (ESS).

● **Inclusive & Protective Design Integration:** Proactively ensure subproject designs embed social inclusion, gender mainstreaming, universal access, protection of vulnerable/disadvantaged groups, and robust prevention of local social conflict.

### 2. Stakeholder Engagement and Social Accountability

● **Inclusive Consultation & Vulnerable Group Outreach:** Facilitate meaningful, culturally appropriate public consultations and information disclosure in line with the Stakeholder Engagement Plan (SEP), utilizing targeted methodologies to ensure the participation of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), female-headed households, and persons with disabilities.

● **Local Governance & IP Liaison:** Maintain continuous, transparent communication and consultation with local authorities, traditional leaders, IPs, and beneficiary communities to manage expectations and mitigate project-induced risks.

● **Continuous Engagement Monitoring:** Oversee and sustain the execution of stakeholder engagement activities at the community level throughout the entire lifecycle of subproject implementation.

● **Social Accountability Documentation:** Capture, categorize, and archive community concerns, feedback, and expectations, verifying that contractors take visible corrective action based on community input.

● **IP & Contractor Compliance Oversight:** Ensure that Implementing Partners and contractors execute standardized engagement protocols before, during, and after the completion of all subproject works.

● **Grievance Mechanism (GM) Operationalization:** Support the establishment, daily operation, and performance monitoring of the project's multi-tiered GM at the IP and site levels, ensuring all complaints are logged, investigated, and closed within established World Bank timeframes.

● **GM Accessibility and Awareness:** Drive the resolution of high-level grievances while proactively ensuring that GM intake channels and system procedures are widely recognized by all project-affected parties and beneficiaries.

● **Functional System Verification:** Validate that all Implementing Partners and contractors develop and maintain functional, responsive grievance systems that strictly adhere to overarching project requirements.

### 3. Field Monitoring and Reporting

● **Non-Compliance Tracking & Rectification:** Conduct regular field visits to identify instances of social non-compliance, co-develop time-bound Corrective Action Plans (CAPs) with contractors, and rigorously track resolution progress.

● **Data-Driven Social Reporting:** Collect, clean, and consolidate field-level data to formulate high-resolution social monitoring inputs, maintaining structured logs, social non-compliance issues, and Grievance Mechanism (GM) performance indicators.

● **Labor Requirements Oversight:** Monitor the implementation of labor requirements (ESS2), verifying that contractor workers receive appropriate training, sign Codes of Conduct (CoC), and have access to a functional, dedicated worker GM. Verifying the workers payments and ensuring workers wages are timely paid by the relevant employers under the Project.

● **Land & Resettlement Verification:** Verify subproject compliance with the project's Resettlement Framework (RF) and monitor any processes involving Voluntary Land Donation (VLD) or asset impacts to ensure zero unauthorized economic/physical displacement.

● **Community Health, Safety & Security Monitoring:** Assess and monitor subproject impacts on community health and safety (ESS4), including traffic safety, exposure to hazards, and security arrangements, ensuring critical incidents are escalated and addressed immediately.

### 4. Capacity Building and Knowledge Management

● Support in developing and delivering targeted training and orientation sessions on social safeguards, worker Code of Conduct, labor requirements, and GM operations for our client personnel, IPs, contractors, and local community committees.

● Maintain organized, audit-ready social documentation archives (consultation minutes, gender-disaggregated attendance sheets, GM registries, and training logs).

● Assist in capturing success stories, lessons learned, and best practices to contribute to HSSE and social safeguard guidance documents and tools.

## Deliverables and Timeframe

The consultant will be remunerated based on the successful completion and acceptance of the deliverables outlined in the assignment, at a daily rate of USD XXXX, for an estimated total contract value of USD XXXX inclusive of applicable CTG management fees.

jobs.title: Grants Manager
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Job Overview:**

The Grants Team at IRC in Sacramento works to leverage public and private funding opportunities through prospecting, proposal development, grants, and subaward contract management. The Grants Manager is primarily responsible for overseeing the full range of pre- and post-award activities required to prepare concept notes, proposals, and budgets, comply with internal approval processes, and align with compliance requirements of public agencies and private foundations. Work is performed under the supervision of a Development Director and in collaboration with IRC Sacramento’s leadership, finance, programs, as well as headquarters’ technical team, and awards and business development units.

**Major Responsibilities:**

***Development and Grants Management***

Prospecting

- Represent Sacramento office in all regional opportunities, particularly for restricted funding, in close coordination with Site Directors, Development Director, Technical Advisors, relevant program leads, and grant coordinators.
- Collaborate with the Development Director in prospecting efforts, utilizing an internal standard operating procedure to support both restricted and unrestricted fundraising needs.
- In collaboration with IRC Sacramento Development Director, work with the Site Director to develop a funding strategy and timeline and perform prospective research on potential public and private funders.

Proposal Development (Pre-Award)

- Develop and manage the Sacramento region’s proposal calendar.
- Lead concepts note, proposal, and budget development, including ensuring log frames, program design, and narrative meet high quality standards in coordination with Programs/Site director, Finance Director, and headquarters’ Resource Acquisition and Management (RAM), and ensure all supporting documentation in the applications are up to date.
- Provide pre-award support and coverage when needed to the local offices.
- Lead negotiation and agreements stage with donors and ensure contract terms are communicated with Finance and Programs through grant kick off meetings and recorded in Asana project tracking.
- Coordinate grant opening and closing meetings for every funded opportunity across the Sacramento office portfolio.

Grants Management (Post-Award)

- Modify final budgets as requested by donor and Site Director/program lead and communicate with Finance and RAM to ensure incoming restricted funds will be tracked.
- Lead negotiation and agreements stage with donors and ensure contract terms are communicated with Finance and Programs through grant kick off meetings and recorded in Asana project tracking.
- Provide support with reports, including copy-editing, coordinating report timelines with headquarters, and submission.
- Serve as a main point of contact for donors across Sacramento office to ensure communication adheres to IRC policy and best practices.
- Develop and ensure the effective maintenance of contract and grant files for each funded program with consistent documentation standards.
- Be a local subject expert for IRC’s Business Development Standards.
- Be a local subject expert for IRC’s internal grants systems (PEERS and OTIS).

Partnerships

- Be a local subject expert in IRC’s internal partnership process, PEERS, to provide technical support to the Partnership Grants Coordinator to ensure subawardees’ contracts are drafted with detailed information on scope of work, deliverables, fund disbursement, and monitoring plans in coordination with the partners and program staff, and in compliance with Finance and RAM.

***Supervision & training:***

- Provide leadership and management of the Grant Coordinator in Turlock, to ensure all tasks are covered and team workload is managed in a way that respects and promotes work life balance and professional growth.
- Provide training and support to new hires ensuring staff meet the expectations of their role and meet responsibilities in a timely manner.
- Be a local subject expert in OTIS and IRC’ RAM’s Business Development processes, and the local Sacramento/Turlock Business Development workflow.

***Systems & Accountability:***

- Maintain proposal calendar, pipelines, grants tracking, and regularly update senior management with up-to-date data
- Ensure the go/no-go review process of opportunities are consistently applied and strengthened by working with senior management to ensure proposals are of high quality and grants staff are at capacity
- Ensure continuous improvement on the utilization of Asana to track opportunity pipelines, award management, and reporting in coordination with senior management, Finance, and program staff
- Establish and continuously update a Standard of Practice (SOP) for Grants staff in coordination with the Finance team and headquarters’ Resource Acquisition and Management (RAM
- Leverage regular communications with Finance, RAM, and the Sacramento office to improve SOP and workflow

**Secondary duties:**

- Work closely with site leads and program staff to prepare interim and final reports to grantors.

**Key Working Relationships:**

- **Position Reports to:** Development Director
- **Position Supervises:** Grants Coordinator (in Turlock office)
- **Indirect Reporting:** Site Director
**Other Internal and/or External Contacts:**
- ***Internal:*** Director of Finance, Sacramento/Turlock Executive Director, Sacramento Program Managers & Coordinators, Technical Advisors, HQ Resource Acquisition and Management department
- ***External***: Foundations and public funders at city, county, state, and federal levels

**Job Requirements:**

***Education:***

- Bachelor’s Degree required in nonprofit management, community development, social sciences, social work, or related fields, or demonstrated work experience of similar knowledge. Master’s degree a plus.
- Certification or continuing education in project management, proposal development and/or fundraising a strong plus.

***Work Experience:***

- Five+ years of nonprofit or public sector experience in development and grants.
- Five+ years of experience in a supervisory role.

***Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:***

- Excellent writing, research, and organizational skills.
- Familiarity with grants process of government funding agency(ies) (federal, state, or county/city level)
- Familiarity with the Sacramento non-profit/philanthropy environment a plus
- Familiarity and comfort working with budgets and finance departments
- Ability to work autonomously in their scheduling and prioritizing within tight deadlines and focused on the work product.
- Self-directed but with strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work well within a team
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications: Word, Excel, Outlook, and project management tools, e.g. Asana
- Experience in IRC systems of PEERS and OTIS a plus (for IRC internal candidates)
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle.

***Language Skills:***

- Excellence in written and spoken English

**Working Environment*****:***

- Standard hybrid office environment (this is not a fully remote position)
- Occasional travel to Turlock office site as needed

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Compensation:** ($84,872-$91,137 - Annually). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**Benefits:** IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include 10 paid sick leave, 10 U.S. holidays, 20-25 generous paid time off based on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163/month, dental starting at $6.50/month, and vision starting at $5/month, flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter), a 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting), disability and life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families.

jobs.title: HR and Administration Coordinator
jobs.description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified HR and Administration Coordinator.

**About the job**

To provide advice, coordination, capacity building and technical support to HR focal person at field location and overall coordination of HR tasks at country level.

The Human Resources Coordinator ensures compliance to DRC's human resource procedures and guidelines within the country operations. The role contributes to the development of country strategies, which are translated into action plans and day-to-day tasks.

The job is based in Tunis with potential 20% travel to field offices.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

**Human Resources Support**

- Provide technical support and advice to the Human Resources team
- Advise and assist managers in Human Resources related issues and concerns

**Recruitment**

- HR focal person for recruitments of national and expat staff (excluding bands C, D & E with HQ)
- Define and ensure proper onboarding process for new staff
- Coordinate and organize inductions on country level on a regular basis, including coordination with facilitators and participants
- Ensure oversight and consistency in position titles and grades, across all field locations.
- Advise hiring managers in development of Job description, inclusive job advertisements and team structures.

**HR Function and compliance**

- Developing/updating HR policies, Employee/HR Handbook, procedures and tools and close monitoring to ensure compliance.
- Collaborate with Senior Management Team in the analysis of the organizational structure across the three countries to ensure consistency, coherency, and efficiency
- Focal point for DRC coordination office legal matters, liaison with legal Advisor and monitoring of ongoing/ new legal cases against DRC.
- Supporting country director in keeping the registration status updated to incorporate changes in legal representative etc. by seeking timely support from legal advisors on the process.
- Advise and train HR and admin focal person in digitalization of HR and Admin tools and platforms.
- Coordination with finance unit to ensure payroll, taxes are captured accurately in the three countries.

**Learning and Development, Performance, and Well-being**

- Support managers & staff with performance management and review processes, including providing specialized trainings like People management skills.
- Act as an impartial mediator in disciplinary procedures and ensure that they follow DRC policies and meet all legal and labor regulations and requirements
- Implementation of Global, regional, and country level HR initiatives example (DRC Voices, minimum standards, staff wellbeing, diversity, and inclusion etc)
- Coordinate with senior managers to develop country wide training calendar.

**Compensation and Benefits**

- Take lead in salary review process in partnership with service provider, Finance team, Senior Management team at country and HQ and coordinate compensation review process and compensation adjustments.
- Analysis of benchmarking reports and the design of new salary grids; Support implementation of DRC’s new Compensation policy, including salary progression
- Prepare monthly payroll for Tunisia and review Algeria and Libya payroll to ensure compliance.
- Register employees in social security for all LE hosted by TUN legal entity.

**DRC Dynamics and Digitalization and reporting**

- Follow up the correct implementation of DRC Dynamics (HR Module) and the quality of the data entered in the system.

- Producing monthly HR reports for TUN, Libya and Algeria
- Ensure org chart for TUN, Libya and Algeria are up to date and produce when required by managers
- Develop/update HR templates digital/manual (recruitment tracker, onboarding and offboarding checklist and forms, recruitment request forms, exit clearance forms, contract request etc)
- Manage digital spaces like Share point (HR), MACH forms etc
- Provide training in Dynamics (HR Module) for HR focal person and relevant module like Employee self-service to new joiners
- Developing and maintaining full record of legal status/file of DRC’s registration in Tunisia.

**Partnerships:**

- Participate actively to the assessment of local partners capacities in terms of HR from the compliance and transparency perspective.
- Provide technical training to local partners in the fields covered by the scope of work of the HR coordinator Position.

**Code of Conduct**

- Will support country director in ensuring that required CoC structure is in place at country office.
- Coordinates with HQ and regional CoC focal person to seek technical inputs on the subject.
- Support country director in managing CoC structure in the country/operation.

**About you**

To be successful in this role we expect you to have at least 3 years’ working experience (officer and above) in Human Resources functions, preferably within an NGO.

Moreover, we also expect the following:

*Required*

- Demonstrated understanding and working knowledge/experience of Human Resources Management principles, concepts & processes
- Ability to interpret and transform local labor laws in DRC internal policies.
- Experience in developing Human Resources strategies and policies, and driving implementation
- Experience using an online system for recruitments and ERP system
- Payroll management and experience in salary benchmarking exercise
- Experience and understanding of local labour laws and managing legal services
- BA in Human Resources, Management, Administration or related subject is mandatory
- Fluency in French and Tunisian language is must
- Working knowledge of English is mandatory

*Desired*

- MA in a related subject is desired

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’ five core competencies:

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**We offer**

Contract length: Open ended with 6 months probation period

Band: Non management G level 1

Designation of Duty Station: Tunis, Tunisia

Suggested Start date: 01 December 2026

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for national employees; please refer to [our website](https://reliefweb.int/void(0)). For questions regarding the vacancy please contact [Us](https://reliefweb.int/void(0)).
