jobs.title: Case Manager
jobs.description:
**General Background**

Mobile Justice Teams (MJTs) are groups of local and international experts, and practitioners collaborating with, and in support of, local justice actors, such as Ukraine’s Office of the Prosecutor General (OPG) and Regional Prosecutor Offices (RPOs), to advance Ukraine's capacity to investigate and build complex command-level cases into international crimes through tailored support and the institutionalisation of international standards and best practices. The MJTs are organised across thematic areas to address context-specific and cross-cutting legal issues. The teams work in the most affected regions of Ukraine to provide advisory and case-building support, focusing on supporting prosecutors and investigators in their investigations and prosecutions.

We are seeking a Case Manager to join our team. The Case Manager serves as the operational and data management anchor of the mobile justice team. The role is responsible for designing, populating, and administering relational databases; establishing and maintaining evidentiary workflows; safeguarding chain of custody; and coordinating electronic disclosure and dossier presentation as well as sharing best practices with project beneficiaries.

This initiative focuses on investigating, documenting, and preparing legal dossiers concerning international crimes (crimes against humanity) committed in the context of the armed conflict in Ukraine. The evidentiary landscape is marked by high volumes of digital or digitized materials.

**Full / Part-time:** Full-time

**Location:** Remote, travel anticipated as needs present.

**The Role**

**Relational Database Administration & Data Architecture:**

- Database Management & Schema Implementation: Configure, maintain, and administer relational databases (e.g., SQL-based platforms, Relativity, Case Matrix Network, Nuix, Airtable enterprise, or bespoke case management systems) to systematically map entities, incidents, sources, locations, units, chains of command, and legal elements of crimes.
- Data Ingestion & Normalisation: Ingest large datasets of structured and unstructured information into the case database. Normalise metadata, run deduplication routines, execute Optical Character Recognition (OCR), and resolve entity disambiguation (e.g., transliteration variations of Cyrillic names, locations, and military call signs).
- Advanced Querying & Cross-Referencing: Execute complex Boolean, SQL, and relational queries to cross-reference evidence across distinct investigation tracks (e.g., linking specific military units and command structures to distinct bombardment incidents or detention facilities).
- System Integration: Collaborate with digital forensics specialists, data engineers, and OSINT analysts to integrate external analytical tools, spatial mapping (GIS), and timeline visualisation software into the primary case database.

**Evidence Management & Chain of Custody:**

- Chain of Custody Maintenance: Implement and monitor strict evidentiary custody procedures from the point of collection/reception through storage, processing, and submission, ensuring compliance with international criminal standards (e.g., ICC Regulations of the Court, domestic criminal codes).
- Digital Preservation & Verification: Ensure digital files, video captures, and web-scraped open-source evidence are hashed (MD5, SHA-256) upon intake, securely archived, and accompanied by comprehensive verification and provenance metadata (including Berkeley Protocol compliance).
- Evidence Logging & Indexing: Catalogue, classify, and register all physical and digital exhibits, witness interview records, expert assessments, and intercept logs into the master evidence registry.

**Case File Organization & Investigative Support:**

- Dossier Compilation: Support legal teams in assembling comprehensive factual and legal dossiers, element-of-crime mapping tables, and witness bundles for pre-trial, indictment, or submission stages.
- Transcript & Translation Coordination: Coordinate the transcription, translation, and verification workflows for multilingual evidentiary materials (primarily Ukrainian, Russian, and English), tracking language versions within the database.
- Information Security & Redaction: Implement data security, access control protocols, and witness protection measures. Manage redactions of sensitive, identifying, or classified material in line with judicial protective orders and Do-No-Harm principles.

**Your Background**

- 4+ years of progressively responsible experience in case management, trial support, paralegal work, or evidence management within an international criminal tribunal, hybrid court, national war crimes unit, specialized human rights documentation NGO, or complex litigation practice.
- Degree in Law, Information Systems, Computer Science, Data Management, Paralegal Studies, Criminology, or a related field; OR Completed secondary education diploma or formal paralegal qualification, combined with an additional 2 to 3 years of qualifying specialised experience in litigation database administration, digital forensics, or trial support.
- Demonstrated hands-on experience structuring and administering relational databases (e.g., PostgreSQL, MS SQL Server, Airtable/Notion enterprise architectures) or specialized e-discovery platforms (e.g., Relativity, Nuix, ZyLAB, Ringtail).
- Proven track record handling digital evidence pipelines, including metadata verification, cryptographic hashing, and chain-of-custody logging.
- Familiarity with the Berkeley Protocol on Digital Open Source Investigations is desirable.
- Understanding of military structures, nomenclature, and geographical contexts relevant to the armed conflict in Eastern Europe is desirable.
- Basic scripting or data wrangling skills (e.g., Python, regex, SQL) for data cleaning, text parsing, or bulk file renaming is desirable.
- Strong understanding of the Ukrainian factual, legal and institutional contexts is desirable.
- Fluency in English, written and verbal skills.

jobs.title: Consultancy - Advocacy on access to justice for children subjected to sexual exploitation and abuse in Uzbekistan
jobs.description:
**ORGANISATIONAL CONTEXT**

ECPAT International is a global network of organisations working together for the elimination of the sexual exploitation of children in all its manifestations i.e., exploitation of children in prostitution, online child sexual exploitation, sale and trafficking of children for sexual purposes, sexual exploitation of children in travel and tourism and some forms of child, early and forced marriage. The ECPAT Network currently consists of 143 members working at national and local levels in 115 countries.

The ECPAT International Secretariat coordinates the global work of the organisation and is based in Bangkok, Thailand. The Secretariat designs and implements global and regional level programmes, and undertakes programming, advocacy and research and facilitates a range of network initiatives.

**THE PROJECT**

In 2024-2025, ECPAT International conducted research on children's access to justice and legal remedies in cases of sexual exploitation in Uzbekistan. The resulting publication, [Access to Justice and Legal Remedies for Children Subjected to Sexual Exploitation in Uzbekistan](https://ecpat.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/FINAL_ENG_A2J-Uzbekistan_Legal-Factsheet.pdf), assessed the extent to which children subjected to sexual exploitation can effectively access reporting mechanisms, child-centred justice procedures, recovery and reintegration services, and remedies, including compensation.

The research identified several strengths within the Uzbek legal and institutional framework, as well as persistent challenges that may hinder children's ability to seek justice and obtain effective remedies. Based on these findings, an Advocacy Roadmap was agreed upon with stakeholders in the country outlining priority actions for strengthening access to justice and legal remedies for children subjected to sexual exploitation. The roadmap includes recommendations aimed at improving legal and policy frameworks, enhancing child-centred justice processes, strengthening multidisciplinary responses, and ensuring that children can access appropriate support and remedies throughout their recovery.

Building on this work, ECPAT International is now entering a new phase focused on advancing the implementation of the Advocacy Roadmap and promoting uptake of the report's recommendations among relevant stakeholders in Uzbekistan. Through targeted advocacy and stakeholder engagement, the project seeks to contribute to policy and practice changes that strengthen children's access to justice and legal remedies and improve responses to child sexual exploitation.

**OBJECTIVES OF THE CONSULTANCY**

The objective of this consultancy is to support the implementation of advocacy actions identified in the Advocacy Roadmap accompanying the 2025 report on access to justice and legal remedies in Uzbekistan.

Based on an assessment of strategic relevance, feasibility and available resources, ECPAT International has identified a number of priority advocacy targets within the Advocacy Roadmap for implementation during 2026-2027. Applicants are expected to develop a proposed advocacy and stakeholder engagement plan that contributes to the advancement of **one or more** of the selected outcomes and targets outlined below, including proposed activities, target stakeholders, expected results and timelines.

**Objective 1: Promote fair and equitable treatment of survivors of child sexual exploitation and abuse in the justice system,**

**Outcome 1.1: Justice and law enforcement professionals are trained in handling child sexual exploitation and abuse cases using gender-sensitive and non-discriminatory approaches.**

- **Target 1.1.3:** Develop and integrate mandatory training modules on gender-sensitive, non-discriminatory approaches to working with survivors in both pre-service and in-service curricula for relevant law enforcement and justice professionals.

**Outcome 1.2: Improved public and professional recognition of the harm caused to survivors by gender-based bias, discrimination, and harmful stereotypes.**

- **Target 1.2.2:** Collaborate with media councils and journalism associations to develop and institutionalise codes of conduct and practical guidance on using rights-based, non-stigmatising language when reporting on cases of child sexual exploitation and abuse.

**Objective 2: Strengthen access to free legal and psychological assistance for survivors of child sexual exploitation and abuse,**

**Outcome 2.1: Referral mechanisms between state bodies and civil society are established to ensure survivors receive timely legal and psychological assistance**

- **Target 2.1.2:** Streamline the referral protocols into the standard operating procedures of relevant frontline professionals, including police, prosecutors, social workers, and service providers, to ensure consistent survivor access to assistance.

Applicants are encouraged to explain which of the above outcomes and targets they intend to prioritise and to justify their proposed approach. While ECPAT International has identified these targets as priority areas for advocacy in 2026-2027, applicants may also propose complementary actions from the Advocacy Roadmap where these are considered relevant to achieving sustainable policy and practice change.

## KEY TASKS AND DELIVERABLES

The exact scope of tasks and deliverables will be finalised with the selected consultant during the contracting and inception phase, based on the proposed methodology and selected advocacy priorities.

## CONSULTANT PROFILE

The consultant (or agency with a team of consultants) should demonstrate:

- Proven experience in designing and implementing advocacy initiatives, stakeholder engagement processes, or policy influencing strategies.
- Strong understanding of child rights, child protection, access to justice and legal remedies, and/or responses to child sexual exploitation and abuse.
- Demonstrated experience engaging with government institutions, justice sector professionals, education stakeholders, civil society organisations and other relevant groups.
- Knowledge of the Uzbek legal, policy and institutional context, particularly in relation to child protection, education, justice or human rights.
- Experience developing advocacy strategies, policy briefs, stakeholder engagement plans, consultation reports, or similar outputs.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English and Uzbek.
- Ability to work independently while coordinating effectively with ECPAT International and relevant national partners.

## TIMEFRAME

The service agreement is expected to take place between November 2026 and July 2027.

The exact duration, level of effort, timeline and milestones will be determined during the contracting phase and will depend on the advocacy approach and implementation plan proposed by the selected consultant. Applicants should therefore include a proposed timeline and indicative level of effort as part of their technical proposal.

Specific deliverables and deadlines will be agreed with the selected consultant and reflected in the final contract and workplan.

**ADDITIONAL INFORMATION**

- This is a home-based position using their own equipment. The consultant(s) should be available for online calls including with different time zones in particular with Thailand where ECPAT International Secretariat is based.
- The Consultant is expected to act at all times in a manner consistent with the values of ECPAT International and in compliance with the organisation’s policies and procedures including Safeguarding Policies and the Code of Conduct.
- Applications from an agency or group of consultants can be accepted.

**OUR COMMITMENTS**

As ECPAT’s International Secretariat we recognise that our strength lies in the diversity of the people who make up our global network, staff, volunteers and consultants. We are committed to being an inclusive workplace where people of all backgrounds and cultures can strive and be themselves. This means we will challenge ourselves to do better and to continue learning, to create and maintain a working environment steeped in respect, tolerance, safety, and where all parties are valued equally.

As a child-focused organisation, ECPAT has a strong commitment to child safeguarding and rigorous procedures, and the successful candidate will be required to sign our 2 codes of conduct.

jobs.title: PSS Facilitators for Adults
jobs.description:
**About World Vision**

For more than 75 years, World Vision has been committed to making a positive and lasting difference in the world. We have become a global leader in improving and transforming the lives of children, their families, and their communities. We help children, families, and communities overcome poverty and injustice, irrespective of religion, race, ethnicity, or gender. Every child deserves a life rich in meaning and purpose. We work with the most vulnerable children in the world so they can experience life in all its fullness.

**Location: Syria, Aleppo**

**Contract end date: 31/12/2026**

**Job purpose:**

The PSS Facilitator will play a vital role in delivering structured psychosocial support (PSS) and contributing to case management services for adults at risk in Aleppo. Operating within World Vision’s protection policies and standards, the Facilitator will conduct assessments, develop tailored intervention plans, provide emotional support, and ensure appropriate referrals to specialized services. Through evidence-based models such as EASE, I Support My Friend, and PM+, the Facilitator will help reduce distress, strengthen coping mechanisms, and promote resilience among vulnerable individuals. This role is essential to fostering safe, inclusive environments and strengthening community-based protection systems.

**Major Responsibilities:**

**Activity:**

- Coordinate, prepare, and implement psychosocial support plans to the adults with the support of the project officer. Also, ensure constant and transparent communication and collaboration with relevant community structures and leaders, in order to get buy-in and support for the project activities.
- Coordinate, prepare, and implement activities related to key messages for parents at primary health care centers on how to deal with children during disasters and emergencies.
- Seek support or consent from concerned people in the communities to ensure the participation of the adolescent boys and girls and their caregivers in the project activities.
- Prepare materials for activity sessions, awareness events and information dissemination on relevant topics with the support of the line manager and the Protection & Safeguarding Coordinator
- Deal with difficult behaviours (conflict, aggressiveness, introversion) and understand the reason behind the behaviour to positively communicate with the situation
- Support adolescents to mobilize parents and caregivers for joint activities within and outside of the CPC centres.
- Plan and implement appropriate recreational activities for affected and most vulnerable children.
- Conduct awareness sessions and implement structured and semi-structured psychosocial support activities.
- Collect data and prepare weekly and monthly project reports as requested.
- Coordinate with all members of the protection team to carry out regular participatory activities with different groups of children and adults, and assist the team in developing appropriate responses.
- Report to the Project Manager and/or to the line manager on any issues, challenges or gaps in implementation.
- Ensure project implementation aligns with protection/child protection standards and in collaboration with protection staff.
- Consult and negotiate with local councils to enhance communication channels and positively influence project goals.
- Ensure the timely implementation of planned program activities.

**Networking & External Engagement**

- When appropriate, represent WV in relevant interagency hub-level coordination forums (ECD, CP AoR, MHPSS WG) in the project location.
- Participate in internal meetings and coordinate with other programme/sector teams.
- Establish strong relationships with local key stakeholders and community structures to facilitate the project acceptance and ownership.

**Other:**

- Adhere to WV Child and Adult Safeguarding policy and standards.
- Adhere to WV accountability standards.

**Knowledge/Qualifications for the Role**.

**Required Professional Experience**

- Minimum of three years of experience working in a relief or development NGO with a focus on protection sector/Case Management.
- At least three years of experience working in protection, child protection, education, MHPSS, adolescent and other relevant programmes in development or humanitarian settings
- Understanding of the situation of adolescents and commitment to improving the lives of adolescents.
- Knowledge of principles and programming approaches for working effectively with adolescents and their families.
- Experience in facilitating activities for or working directly with adolescents in Syria is essential.
- Strong interpersonal skills, ethical sensitivity and ability to effectively communicate with adolescents and their caregivers.
- Ability and willingness to conduct activities and regular outreach in the field/rural areas particularly in engaging families and communities to address issues affecting adolescent boys and girls.
- Ability to negotiate with and mobilize the community and problem-solving skills.
- Ability to work as a team player and collaborate effectively with other stakeholders.
- Commitment to and understanding of WV’s aims, values and principles.
- Experience in implementing and using of WHO Nurturing Care Framework.
- Knowledge and experience in Inter-Agency Cluster/Sector Working Groups and Task Forces.

**Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification:**

- Bachelor degree in early childhood development, education, psychology, social work, and other relevant subjects.
- Certification or other recognized courses on early childhood development, Child Protection, Education in Emergencies, parenting skills, MHPSS or other relevant subjects.
- Excellent understanding of the government system and services for age groups in Syria, especially in a humanitarian/emergency context.
- Strong knowledge and awareness of inter-agency tools, guidelines and other resources.

**Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications:**

- Additional experience with refugees, emergency response and NGO experience preferred.
- Computer skills, in particular email, Microsoft Word, PowerPoint and Excel.
- Fluency in Arabic required, and ability to write and speak English.
- Agrees with the mission, vision and core values of World Vision.
- Finds fulfilment in work through creativity, risk-taking, initiative, and innovation, and encourages the same in colleagues.
- Good report writing skills.
- Detailed oriented and able to verify data quality.
- Strong communication skills (Strong interpersonal skills.).
- Good contextual knowledge of the local community and social/cultural constraints, realities and organizational relationships. Inspires trust within/outside of the organization.
- Develops high levels of credibility and accountability.
- Stays open to internal and external feedback.
- Agrees with the mission, vision and core values of World Vision.
- Finds fulfilment in work through creativity, risk-taking, initiative, and innovation, and encourages the same in colleagues.

**Travel and/or Work Environment Requirement:**

The position requires 90% of the time to be field-based and 10% at office level.

Position requires willingness and ability to continue to function during a crisis, including during a World Vision response to a manmade or natural disaster.

The position requires availability and willingness to work outside regular.

**Physical Requirements:** N/A

**Language Requirements:**

Excellent written and fluent in speaking Arabic.

Ability to write very good quality reports in English is required

jobs.title: Head of Finance & IT
jobs.description:
**EXTERNAL ANNOUNCEMENT**

**TITLE: Head of Finance & IT**

**Contract Type: National**

**TEAM/PROGRAMME: Finance Team**

**LOCATION: Bangkok, Thailand**

**CONTRACT LENGTH: Open-ended**

**ROLE PURPOSE:**

The Head of Finance & IT is a permanent member of the Senior Management Team (SMT) of the Save the Children (Thailand) Foundation (SCT), and shares the responsibility for establishing the direction and overall coordination of SCT. The post holder will be accountable to the Executive Director of SCT, the Board of Directors of SCT, including the Treasurer of the Board, to develop and maintain a secure and effective financial system for SCT, to monitor and ensure its financial sustainability, and to support its growth as an independent organisation.

The Head of Finance & IT ensures accurate and appropriate budgeting, cash flows, financial controls, recording, monitoring and reporting in emergency and development programming contexts to Save the Children and the donors. The position serves as a resource for training and supporting programme staff and partners in their financial responsibilities. The Head of Finance & IT is tasked with driving the organisational culture and ensuring a healthy and productive work environment in SCT.

The desired position holder is expected to be a great team player and work and collaborate effectively across SMT Team members, within Finance team members and with various stakeholders (including local and regional/global Save The Children movement).

**SCOPE OF ROLE:**

**Reports to:** Executive Director

**Staff directly reporting to this post:** 5 ( 1 Finance Manager, 1 Finance Coordinator, 1 Sr. Finance Officer & 2 Finance Officer)

**Staff indirectly reporting to this post:** Finance Assistant (Mae Sot), Finance Assistant (Pattani)

**Role Dimensions**: The post provides overall financial management to Save the Children (Thailand) Foundation (SCT) with 100%.

**KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY:**

**Financial Control**

- Lead day-to-day Finance operations, including using Agresso accounting software and reporting monthly to the Executive Director.
- Manage and monitor bank and cash operations, including cash flow forecasting and supervising the petty cash system, review the cash vouchers along with the supporting documents, ensure quick payments, effective use of cash management; provide reasonable services to the stakeholders, assist in smooth operation of goods and services procurement, including having the full month end process and cash count verified by a person independent of the finance operations.
- Check that all payments comply with SC financial guidelines and donors.
- Ensure that staff salaries and benefits are paid according to contract and increments and cost of living increases are added at the appropriate times; and that all tax liabilities according to the country rules and regulations are met accurately and on time.
- Provide the Senior Management Team (SMT) and all budget holders a monthly update on the budget variance analysis (BVA) in a timely manner after the system hard close, ensuring the analysis meets the needs and standards required by the key stakeholders and budget holders, and provide support in reviewing expenditures and budgets/ forecasts.
- Ensure the integrity of all accounts, prepare the monthly financial reviews (MFRs) with all control accounts reconciled.
- Ensure quarterly effort reporting is prepared, reconciling timesheets with charges made in the finance system. Investigate major variances, make appropriate adjustments, and share the reconciliation with the Regional Office.
- Coordinate submission of control reports, respond to findings and recommend resolutions or action plans.
- Enforce the organization's fraud policy and update financial risk assessment and action plans.
- Ensure that SCT operates within its Bank and Cash procedures, coordinating the funds request from the budget holders to the regional office and ensuring that the minimum level of cash is in the bank accounts and petty cash.
- Support the timely submission of financial reports and attachments to members, individual donor timeframes and requirements and government regulatory agencies.
- Ensure multi-currency accounting involves recording transactions into the system. It includes managing multiple currency balances in the general ledger, tracking exchange rates, calculating gains/losses, and reporting in a base currency.

**Compliance and Iternal Control**

- Ensure SCT complies with all Save the Children Financial Management Operating Standards and Standard Operating Procedures, including the requirements of the SCI Finance Procedures Manual.
- Ensure that effective systems are put in place, and regularly reviewed, to allow adequate financial management and control, including:
- Annual accounts and tax statement preparation;
- Financial procedures during emergency responses, including meeting all relevant responsibilities in the Rules and Principles for Emergency Response;
- Expenditure procedures, especially around procurement;
- Documentation of all controls and procedures;
- Identify and effectively manage all key risks, especially financial, related to SCT's activities
- Ensure that systems are in place for the control of all assets, funds, equipment, property, and facilities.
- Participate in the development of finance policies and procedures to be able to maintain a well-financially controlled environment in both development and emergency contexts.
- Coordinate and assist any internal or external audits.

**Treasury**

- Support the treasury compliance policy, for all financial matters, including the consideration, settling, approving and executing all agreements, documents, certificates, instruments, claims and transactions, and to open, operate and close bank accounts as prescribed by law in any country.
- Ensure the management of SCT's FX exposure and Fx gain and losses.
- Oversee monthly fund requests from projects and associated fund requests to Centre Treasury.
- Ensure the SCT Interest Policy that SCT maximizes interest returns on available funds whilst minimizing risk to available funds.
- Review the monthly arrears, Donor current bank balance report, Fx report, and interest for reporting to the Executive Director.

**Financial Reporting**

- Develop and implement management reporting to support organizational decision-making. This will include the coordination and production of monthly and quarterly management reports and KPI dashboards to agreed timescales (or more frequently as required).

**Planning and Budgeting**

- Lead on the development of budget plans and twice-yearly forecasts.
- Track programme budgets and advise budget holders on budgeting, expenditure patterns and necessary plan adjustments.
- Ensure costs, including shared costs, are properly charged to awards.
- Ensure donor financial conditions are adhered to.
- Assist the Executive Director in the financial management of SCT resources, including (a) the formulation of country resource allocation, (b) providing effective support and guidance to the Senior Management Team and other key program staff during planning and allocation exercises, (c) monitoring the implementation of donor agreements and resource utilization. Highlight variances, provide analyses and recommend resolution or reallocation of resources.
- Participate in ensuring that finance and awards procedures are detailed in the SCT Emergency Preparedness Plan in order to enable rapid scale-up.
- Monitor the organization's financial sustainability and include long-term project/ income expenditure planning.
- Together with operations teams, lead on the development and revision of budgets for new project proposals.

**Finance Support for Fund Raising**

- Ensure compliance with financial regulatory requirements for domestic fundraising, best practices and other relevant organization rules.
- Work closely with our fundraising team to set up and support the achievement of the required targets the Fundraising Team sets.
- Create financial tools for maintaining a fundraising finance database.
- Provide the fundraising financial report highlighting financial trends and analysis.

**Information Technologies (IT)**

- Ensure the implementation of Information Technologies (IT) as per Global guidelines
- Oversee the IT support service provider to manage and maintain the organization's IT infrastructure.

S**taff Management, Mentorship and Development**

- Ensure appropriate staffing within finance through the recruitment and training of finance staff as appropriate and ensure the availability of appropriate professional development opportunities for staff.
- Ensure that all staff understand and are able to perform their duties with regard to financial management through induction and training of key programme staff, and manage the performance of the finance team, setting clear, measurable objectives, ongoing feedback, periodic reviews and fair and unbiased evaluations.

**As a member of the Senior Management Team, will contribute to**

- Role-modelling of an organizational culture that reflects our values promotes accountability and high performance, encourage a team culture of learning, creativity and innovation, support our people to deliver outstanding results for children and excellent customer service for colleagues, members and donors.
- Active and regular working relationships with host government authorities and partner agencies, including humanitarian and development donors and local and international NGOs.
- Close coordinate with the Board of Directors, and the Treasurer of the Board, on financial matters and financial oversight.

**BEHAVIOURS (Values in Practice):**

**Accountability:**

- Hold self-accountable for making decisions, managing resources efficiently, achieving and role modelling Save the Children values.
- Hold the team and partners accountable to deliver on their responsibilities - giving them the freedom to deliver in the best way they see fit, providing the necessary development to improve performance and applying appropriate consequences when results are not achieved.

**Ambition:**

- Set ambitious and challenging goals for themselves and their team, takes responsibility for their own personal development and encourage their team to do the same.
- Widely share their personal vision for Save the Children, engage and motivate others
- Future orientated, think strategically and on a global scale.

**Collaboration:**

- Build and maintain effective relationships, with their team, colleagues, members and external partners and supporters.
- Value diversity, sees it as a source of competitive strength.
- Approachable, good listener, easy to talk to.

**Creativity:**

- Develop and encourage new and innovative solutions.
- Willing to take disciplined risks.

**Integrity:**

- Honest, encourages openness and transparency demonstrate highest levels of integrity.

**QUALIFICATIONS**:

- Thai Nationality
- At least 7 years experience in a senior finance and/ or office management post
- Ability to speak, read and write in Thai and English as working languages
- Proficiency in computer use with various software packages and Advanced user on Microsoft Excel

**EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS:**

- Familiarity with accounting package
- Experience of staff line management
- Experience of negotiating service contracts and procurement, ensuring compliance with organizational policy and value for money
- Experience of budget development and management
- Experience of donor reporting and liaison, including negotiating with donors
- Experience of advising staff on budgetary management and partners on accountability
- Experience of working with international NGOs
- Excellent organizational skills and a track record of consistently delivering on time.
- Excellent communication skills

**Additional job responsibilities**

The duties and responsibilities as set out above are not exhaustive and the role holder may be required to carry out additional duties within reasonableness of their level of skills and experience.

**Equal Opportunities**

The role holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with the SC Equal Opportunities and Diversity policies and procedures.

**Child Safeguarding:**

We need to keep children safe so our selection process, which includes rigorous background checks, reflects our commitment to the protection of children from abuse.

**Safeguarding and Counter Fraud our Staff:**

The post holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with the SC safeguarding and counter fraud policy.

**Health and Safety**

The role holder is required to carry out the duties in accordance with SC Health and Safety policies and procedures.

**“We need to keep children safe so our selection process, which includes rigorous background checks, reflects our commitment to the protection of children from abuse”**

jobs.title: Grants and Collaborations Team Leader – Performance Enhancement
jobs.description:
## ***Description***

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Operations and Integration (O&I) collective** delivers essential enabling services that support the organisation’s scientific and technical portfolio. Our key functions include corporate services, programme support, partnerships, resource mobilisation, and strategic engagement. These services are coordinated through our regional and satellite offices across the Pacific and Europe. Additionally, the O&I collective leads a dedicated workstream focused on organisational change and transformation to drive continuous improvement and adaptability.

The role – **Grants and Collaborations Team Leader – Performance Enhancement** will lead a small team within the Grants and Collaborations Team to ensure the effective and timely delivery of high-quality grant management services across SPC. The incumbent will provide expert advice and support on complex grant-related activities, strengthen grants management processes, and drive continuous improvements in grant systems and practices. The Team Leader will also play a key role in fostering strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders, ensuring grant activities meet SPC’s standards, comply with funder requirements and contribute to the achievement of SPC’s strategic objectives.

The key responsibilities of the role include:

**Systems and processes: Grants Performance, Quality and Continuous Improvement**

- Lead the development and implementation of initiatives to improve the efficiency, effectiveness, quality and consistency of SPC's grants and collaborations function.
- Develop practical improvement plans and oversee their implementation, monitoring progress and reporting results to the Grants and Collaborations Manager.
- Identify and implement improvements to Grants and Collaboration Tools and Systems: Enhance the tools and systems used for managing grants and collaborations, ensuring they support better understanding, compliance, and efficiency across SPC.
- Monitor the performance of grants management processes and identify trends, bottlenecks, control weaknesses, recurring issues and opportunities for improvement.
- Establish and maintain appropriate performance indicators, service standards and quality measures for the Grants and Collaborations function.

**Systems, Data, Digitalisation and Process Improvement**

- Lead the review and improvement of grants and collaborations systems, tools and workflows including supporting the evaluation, selection and implementation of a Grants Management System (GMS) including definition of business requirements and integration with Business Central (PR-to-Pay); and contribute to the transition to a Centre-Led operating model for grants management.
- Identify opportunities for automation, digitalisation and improved use of technology across the grants lifecycle.
- Work with ICT and relevant business units to define business requirements for grants management systems and digital solutions.
- Promote the use of reliable grants data to support operational management, performance monitoring, reporting and decision-making.
- Develop and maintain appropriate management information, dashboards and performance reports.

**Advice and Guidance**

- Provide expert advice on SPC grants and collaborations processes: Provide expert advice to the Grants and Collaborations Manager and senior management on grants management performance, risk, systems and process improvement.
- Provide advice to decision-makers on complex grant and collaboration Issues: Provide evidence-based advice to relevant committees and decision-makers on systemic grants management issues and proposed improvements.
- Brief decision-makers on trends, performance issues, risks and opportunities for improvement.
- Prepare high-quality reports, briefing notes, dashboards and management information for internal stakeholders.
- Support the Grants and Collaborations Manager in preparing reports for senior management, the Executive, governing bodies and the Audit and Risk Committee.

**Management of staff**

- Team leadership and supervision: Lead the staff, ensuring clear direction, support, and motivation is provided to staff.
- Recruitment and staffing: Lead the recruitment and selection process ensuring that staffing level and capabilities are appropriate to meet operational needs.
- Performance management, training and development:
- manage the performance management process for staff ensuring that team performance goals are aligned with SPC objectives.
- manage the training and development needs for staff ensuring continuous learning and skill development within the team.

**Outreach, education and training**

- Develop mechanisms to capture, share and institutionalise lessons learned across the Grants and Collaborations Team.
- Lead communication and change-management activities associated with new or revised grants processes, systems and requirements.
- Provide capacity building: Lead the development and delivery of training programs to internal and external stakeholders to enhance understanding and management of grants and collaborations, including pre-award and post-award processes, and as part of SPC’s performance enhancement work.
- Build collaborative relationships: Lead on fostering strong, collaborative relationships with all SPC stakeholders, ensuring alignment and support for grants and collaborative activities.
- Ensure effective communication: Lead on maintaining open and effective lines of communication with key stakeholders, building strong relationships to support the effective implementation of grants and collaborative initiatives.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

## ***Key selection criteria***

**Qualifications**

- A postgraduate qualification in a relevant field such as law, finance, grants management, business administration or international development or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 7–8 years of relevant experience in grants management, programme/project management, business administration, finance, risk management, compliance, process improvement, international development, law or a related field.
- Demonstrated experience leading or coordinating teams and/or complex cross-functional initiatives.
- Demonstrated experience reviewing and improving organisational processes, systems or operating procedures.
- Experience in performance monitoring, data analysis and management reporting.
- Experience developing guidance, procedures, tools and training materials.
- Demonstrated ability to translate complex information into practical recommendations.

**Language skills**

- Excellent English communication skills (oral and written) with a working knowledge of French being an advantage.

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work in a multicultural, inclusive and equitable environment.

## ***Salary, terms and conditions***

**Contract Duration** – **3 years** – subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – The **Grants and Collaborations Team Leader – Performance Enhancement** is a band 11 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of 3,245‒4,057 SDR (special drawing rights) per month, which currently converts to approximately FJD 10,028–12,535 (USD 4,349–5,436; EUR 3,924–4,905). An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications.Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews. Remuneration of expatriate SPC staff members is not subject to income tax in Fiji; Fiji nationals employed by SPC in Fiji will be subject to income tax.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Suva –** SPC provides a housing allowance of FJD 1,500–5,200 per month. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilingualism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s Privacy Policy.

jobs.title: DIRECTRICE.EUR REGIONAL.E DES OPERATIONS ADJOINT - AFRIQUE DE l'OUEST
jobs.description:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

Sous la supervision de la Directrice Régionale des Opérations du Pool Afrique de l'Ouest, Australe et de la Mission France, vous contribuez à la définition et au développement de la stratégie des bureaux pays d'ACF. En étroite collaboration avec les directeurs-trices pays, les directeurs-trices adjoint programmes et l'équipe du pool que vous encadrez. Vous accompagnez la mise en oeuvre des orientations stratégiques et le développement des activités.
Dans ce cadre, vos missions seront de :
Manager l'équipe du Pool sous son rattachement hiérarchique
recruter les membres de l'équipe en lien avec les référent.es fonctionnement et le département RH du siège
assurer la gestion quotidienne de l'équipe
fixer les priorités, veiller au respect des règles internes et à la bonne interaction entre les membres de l'équipe
initier et suivre les plans d'actions individuels de l'équipe
assurer les entretiens d'évaluation
organiser des points individuels avec les membres de l'équipe
Accompagner la définition et la mise en oeuvre des stratégies pays
Co-animer la réflexion stratégique (programmatique et budgétaire) avec le DRO entre les missions et le pool
S'assurer de compatibilité et d ela cohérence des programmes à fort enjeux stratégiques avec les stratégies pays
Apporter appui et conseil aux missions sur les stratégies de financement
s'assurer de l'organisation des évaluations externes des programmes
en accord avec le DRO, exercer un rôle et des responsabilités directes sur la mission
Accompagner la définition et faciliter le financement de programmes régionaux, multi-pays, multi-acteurs à fort enjeux stratégiques
Conseiller les bureaux pays dans l'élaboration de nouveaux programmes en fonction des besoins
contribuer à la coordination du réseau ACF-IN
Contribuer au recrutement et au développement des RH dans sa filière métier (DPA programmes, grant writer,..)
Valider techniquement les candidatures des directeurs-trices pays adjoint programmes, responsables de département programmes et coordinateur-trice de consortium
assurer les briefings et debriefings des membres de la coordination
assurer le suivi régulier, l'accompagnement et le support aux DPA programmes.
animer des sessions de formation au siège, en région, sur le terrain.

Profile :

Vous êtes titulaire d'un Master 2 en sciences sociales ou politiques ou équivalent. Vous avec au moins 5 ans d'expérience professionnelle en mission humanitaire sur des postes de coordination dans les domaines d'activité d'ACF (Nutrition, Santé, Sécurité Alimentaire, Eau Assainissement Hygiène, Santé Mentale et Soutien Psychosocial ou fonctions Support).
Vous êtes reconnu-e pour vos qualités d'encadrement d'équipe et de leadership.
Votre connaissance de l'Afrique de l'Ouest et Australe, et/ou vos expériences terrains dans cette zone géographique sera un atout.
Vous maîtrisez l'ensemble des leviers des bailleurs institutionnels (écritures de propositions, financements, orientations, conformité).
Vous êtes autonome, diplomate et proactif-ve. Vous avez la capacité à porter une vision et à insuffler une dynamique d'équipe. Vous avez d'excellentes capacités rédactionnelles et orales en français et en anglais.

Conditions d'emploi

Statut : Cadre Intégré - CDD de 3 mois
Temps plein
Lieu : Montreuil (Seine-Saint-Denis)
Rémunération :De 47K à 52Keuros bruts annuels sur 13 mois selon expérience
Avantages:25 jours par an de CP et 21 jours de RTT
Couverture santé, prévoyance : Prise en charge à 80% par ACF
Dispositifs de maintien de salaire (maladie, maternité, paternité)
Indemnités Transport : Prise en charge à 50% du forfait entre le domicile et le lieu de travail
Indemnités Tickets-restaurant (Carte déjeuner Up): Prise en charge à 60% par l'association pour une valeur de 8euros
Ouvres sociales du CSE (chèques cadeaux, remboursement activités culturelles, ...)
Télétravail :Télétravail ouvert à tous et toutes depuis le territoire métropolitain
Il a été défini pour ce poste une présence obligatoire au siège de 1 jour par mois
Temps de présentiels collectifs imposés / également obligatoires par l'employeur : pour les réunions et événements collectifs (jusqu'à 3 jours par mois) et 2 jours de présence obligatoire lors de votre intégration dans l'équipe
Indemnités de télétravail
Formation: Accès illimité et gratuit à la plateforme d'e-learning TalentSoft
Conditions particulières: Possible demande de déplacement (urgence, gap filler) et selon le contexte économique de l'organisation : Côte d'Ivoire, Libéria, Sierra Leone, Burkina Faso
ACF s'engage pour les personnes en situation de handicap et lutte activement contre toutes les formes de discrimination.

jobs.title: Quality Assurance Analyst, METAL
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Background:**

We aim to make our programs a model for the highest global standards and to cultivate power and lasting change not just for our clients but for all people affected by humanitarian crises. To achieve that vision, the IRC’s Technical Excellence (TE) group, located within the Crisis Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) Department, provides technical assistance to IRC’s country program staff and shares what we learn to influence policy and practice.

IRC’s Technical Excellence team is comprised of seven teams which have deep expertise in their respective fields: Education, Economic Wellbeing, Governance, Health, Violence Prevention and Response, MEAL, and Grants & Operations.

**Measurement, Evaluation, Technology, Accountability, and Learning at the IRC**

The METAL Unit is responsible for supporting CRRD to have a culture of strong data and evidence use through stewardship of the Data & Performance Ecosystem, and for coordinating successful piloting and uptake of innovative technology solutions. The METAL Unit provides specialized support across four pillars to strengthen program effectiveness, improve decision-making, and enhance organizational learning.

**This is a hybrid position open to candidates based in New York, US, Kenya and UK. Other Limited IRC Locations may also be considered. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.**

**Job Overview**

The METAL Quality Assurance Analyst will be part of the METAL team which is responsible for delivering products that support day-to-day implementation of CRRD Programs as well as the collection, management, visualization of KPIs relevant to higher-level decision-making.

The QA Analyst is a team member responsible for developing, testing, implementing, and supporting CRRD’s data toolkits, for which the tech stack includes CommCare, Microsoft Power BI, and Microsoft SQL server Azure-based data warehouse.

The Data Toolkits are essential for CRRD’s data collection, management and analysis so it is critical for the success of the team that the QA Analyst have strong skills related to testing data transformation and visualization.

Working in partnership with staff at various levels and locations, the QA Analyst will perform a key role in testing, assuring quality, and improving Data Toolkits with a successful rollout. Should demonstrate a solid focus on responsive application design and an understanding of the diverse subject areas involved in developing user-centric and impactful applications.

Position key attributes are multi-tasking, detail orientation, fast learning, and self-organizing. The candidate is required to not only test the technology products, but also to identify, create, and implement complex use case scenarios; take a lead in efforts to find requirement/specification gaps and work very closely with business teams/analysts to seek answers. Find a balance between keeping high-quality standards without overly exerting on the release timeline. Build a good working relationship between development and product management teams. Be able to turn around testing and regression testing within timelines without compromising on quality.

This role reports to the Product Manager. Program Technology. The QA Analyst will work closely with METAL Developers. They will have a technical line to the Senior Manager, Quality Assurance and maintain regular contact with the QA team to ensure that METAL is following the best practices of the wider organization.

**Major Responsibilities**

Primary responsibilities include but are not limited to:

- Translate functional requirements and specifications into detailed test plans, encompassing functional, system, integration, performance, regression, and user acceptance testing. The individual in this role will implement Agile Software Testing with Scrum principles.
- Work with the project management team closely to ensure that testing processes are implemented and followed by all core team members.
- Maintain high quality of applications developed in CommCare/Microsoft PowerApps meet user needs.
- Perform in-depth data testing of PowerBI dashboards and underlying data pipelines, including data verification across systems, data migration testing, data validation testing, and A/B testing, to ensure the accuracy, integrity, and quality of visualized data and the overall user experience.
- Review products to match design specifications, with an eye to user experience issues such as fonts, colors, and screen size breakpoints with responsive design.
- Verify multiplatform capabilities, cross-browser testing (Chrome, IE, Firefox, Edge, Safari), and mobile testing (iPad, iPhone, android phone, tablet) for build products.
- Ensure all testing is planned, implemented, and delivered per the latest industry standards, and to our quality expectations while meeting ambitious timelines.
- Fully own the assigned project’s testing stream – Perform requirement analysis and proactively find requirements gaps; discover and write test cases in Jira; create and maintain regression test case documents; sign off for release; do release smoke test.
- Identify application defects, seek resolution, process gaps, and make recommendations to improve the functionality and usability of the application.
- Call for the test case review meetings with the core team.
- Clearly communicate the testing timeline for each testing phase. Help the team set a realistic release timeline such that a testing effort is not overlooked or overly simplified.
- Ensure all identified risks from testing are raised and mitigated appropriately

**Key Working Relationships**

- Position Reports to: Product Manager, Program Technology
- Direct Reports: None
- Management in Partnership: Senior Manager, Quality Assurance

**Key Internal Relationships:**

- METAL Technology Development Lead
- METAL Developers

**Desired Experience and Skills**

- 3+ years of data application testing experience, with proven experience managing and executing the full testing lifecycle, including UAT testing support
- 2+ years of Quality Assurance experience testing data processes and products: ETL pipelines, dashboards/reports, etc
- 2+ years of working with CommCare or similar ODK based platforms or any low-code application as an application developer or quality analyst is highly desirable.
- Some Performance and Load Testing experience with open-source tools
- 1 year of automation experience
- Solid ability to lead a project by him/herself from all quality assurance, and quality control aspects.
- Experienced testing in low to no-code environments and processes such as mobile data collection and/or case management tools such as CommCare, Ona, Kobo or Microsoft PowerApps, PowerBI dashboards and Azure.
- Understanding and experience with T-SQL, Azure SQL Server, Data Factory, SSIS/other ETL tools, data modeling and data warehouse.
- Experience testing multilingual platforms along with multicurrency verification preferred.
- Manual functional testing, system testing, along with some automation, and performance testing
- Have great collaboration with all teams involved in the project with self-directed.
- Meticulous in maintaining excellent organization and prioritization skills
- Experience using Jira for bug and test management.
- Experience with full software development process with Agile methodology
- Experience with any open-source performance/stress testing tool e.g., JMeter
- Possess excellent oral and written communication skills
- Self-motivated and a problem solver
- Fast and independent learner
- Work with distributed teams
- Intercultural competence

**Education:**

- Bachelor’s degree or experience in computer science or information systems.
- CSQA, CSTE, or any certification software testing/ quality assurance

**IRC is dedicated to reducing the gender gap in leadership roles and has implemented supportive measures like parental leave, gender-sensitive security protocols, and other benefits to create an inclusive environment for women.**

**Applicants with varied career paths are welcomed, recognizing that employment gaps don't define potential. IRC values transferrable skills and is committed to investing in the growth and development of its team members.**

**The organization strives to offer competitive and equitable Compensation and Benefits programs to attract, motivate, and retain employees who adhere to the IRC Way Standards for Professional Conduct.**

**Compensation:** (**USA:** $68K - $74K / **UK:** GBP 34,653 GBP 41,150). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Haiti - Coordinateur.trice Terrain - Artibonite
jobs.description:
## QUE FAISONS-NOUS...

**Date de début souhaité:** ASAP
**Durée de la mission:** 6 mois
**Localisation**: Artibonite

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL** (SI) est une association d’aide humanitaire internationale qui, depuis plus de 40 ans, porte secours aux populations victimes de conflits armés et de catastrophes naturelles en répondant aux besoins vitaux, boire, manger, s’abriter. Particulièrement engagée dans le combat contre les maladies liées à l’eau insalubre, première cause de mortalité au monde, SI met en œuvre par ses interventions une expertise dans le domaine de l’accès à l’eau potable, l’assainissement et la promotion de l’hygiène mais également dans celui, essentiel, de la sécurité alimentaire et moyen d’existence. Présentes dans 26 pays, les équipes de SI - 3 200 personnes au total composées d’expatriés, de salariés nationaux, de permanents au siège, de quelques bénévoles…- interviennent avec professionnalisme et engagement dans le respect des cultures.

## LA MISSION

La mission Haiti a actuellement une base à Port au Prince et le bureau de la coordination. Les projets concernent la WASH et la SAME/NUT en consortium avec des partenaires nationaux et internationaux. Elle est financée par OCHA, CDCS, SDC, ECHO, UNICEF, IFSAN entre autre. Depuis deux ans, la mission a connu une bonne croissance en terme d'opérations et de budget, répondant aux urgences dans la Zone Métropolitaine de Port au Prince mais également développe des actions de plus long termes. C'est dans cette dynamique que la mission Haiti a décidé d'ouvrir une nouvelle base en Artibonite, basée à Saint Marc afin de répondre aux besoins en EHA des populations dans ce département. La base est en début d'ouverture à l'heure actuelle, la mission principale du.de la CT aura pour but de régulariser la base après son ouverture et de la terminer.

17 expatriés et 80 staffs nationaux dans l'unique base et coordination de Port au Prince. Un premier set-up de 2/3 expats et une petite vingtaine de staffs nationaux est à entrevoir pour la base d'Artibonite.

## DESCRIPTIF DE POSTE

**OBJECTIF GENERAL**

Le/la Coordinateur.trice Terrain a un rôle de Directeur Pays (DP) par délégation sur l'Artibonite pour SI.
Il/elle propose en fonction du contexte géopolitique et humanitaire la stratégie sur l'Artibonite et s'assure de sa mise en œuvre une fois validée.
Il/elle contrôle et garantit que les projets se déroulent en adéquation avec la charte de Solidarités International et dans
le respect des procédures internes et contractuelles.
Il/elle mobilise les moyens matériels et financiers nécessaires à la bonne conduite des programmes et en supervise la gestion.
Il/elle coordonne les équipes en place et est le garant de leur sécurité sur sa zone d’affectation.
Il/elle est l’interlocuteur.trice direct.e et privilégié.e du/de la DP

**ENJEUX ET DEFIS SPECIFIQUES**

Ce poste est une création suite à l'ouverture de la base Artibonite. Nous attendons un.e CT expérimenté sur ce type de niveau sécuritaire mais aussi possédant une grande expérience dans la structuration d'une nouvelle base après la phase d'ouverture.
Les enjeux sécuritaires - niveau 4 chez SI - sont nombreux notamment dans le cadre d'une base nouvelle.

**PRIORITES SUR LES 2-3 PREMIERS MOIS**

Gestion et de la mise en place des projets

Gestion opérationnelle de la sécurité sur la zone et continuité du travail d'accès engagé

Support au développement de nouvelles propositions de projets sur la zone

Travailler en interne sur la structuration de la base, finaliser les recrutements, finaliser l'installation de la base vie et bureaux, formation au travail chez SI, mise en place des procédures.

Accompagner la stratégie sur l'Artibonite et continuer son développement

Contribuer à renforcer le lien avec nos partenaires locaux et internationaux et les clusters de la zone

**CONTRAINTES SECURITAIRES**

Haiti est catégorisé en Niveau 4, La sécurité est très volatile/dégradée en Artibonite dû à la présence des groupes armés et d'affrontements quotidiens, mais n’empêche pas la conduite des activités. Les règles de sécurité de la mission sont strictes (couvre-feu au coucher du soleil).

## VOTRE PROFIL

**DIPLÔME ET EXPERIENCE**

Diploma : Niveau Master

Experience dans le secteur humanitaire : 5 ans et plus

Experience sur un poste similaire : 3/4 ans

**COMPETENCES**

COMPETENCES TECHNIQUES

1. Capacité à suivre et analyser le contexte humanitaire, politique, culturel, social, économique
2. Compétences pour garantir la coordination, le développement, le suivi et l’évaluation des programmes mis en œuvre sur sa zone d’intervention
3. Proposer le dimensionnement humain, financier et logistique pour sa zone d’intervention ainsi que son organisation
4. Gestion des RH, recrutement, induction, création de dynamiques d'équipes, mise en place de la relation base éloignée - coo pour Haiti (l'autre base est à Port au Prince, directement en lien avec la coo)
5. Etre responsable de la sécurité des équipes et des biens sur sa zone d’affectation, sur délégation de la DP

COMPETENCES TRANSVERSALES

1. Analyse, décision et gestion de crise : capacité à évaluer les risques, anticiper, décider et agir sous pression.
2. Leadership et communication : encadrer, former, sensibiliser et transmettre des consignes claires aux équipes et partenaires.
3. Diplomatie et adaptabilité : négocier avec divers acteurs, entretenir des relations de confiance et s’ajuster à un environnement instable.

**LANGUES**

1. Français
2. Anglais apprécié

## SI VOUS OFFRIRA LES CONDITIONS SUIVANTES...

**Un poste salarié :** Selon l'expérience, à partir de EUR 3080 bruts par mois (2800 salaire de base + 10% d'indemnité de congé annuel versée mensuellement) et un Per Diem mensuel de USD 750.

SI couvre également les frais de logement et les frais de déplacement entre le pays d'origine de l'expatrié et le lieu d'affectation.

**Breaks :** Pendant la mission, un système d'alternance entre travail et congés est mis en place à raison de 7 jours ouvrables tous les trois mois (avec USD 850 alloués par Solidarités International). A ces périodes de pause, s'ajoute un jour de repos supplémentaire par mois travaillé.

**Couverture sociale et médicale :** Les expatriés bénéficient d'une assurance qui rembourse tous les frais de santé (y compris les frais médicaux et chirurgicaux, les soins dentaires et ophtalmologiques, le rapatriement) et d'un système de prévoyance incluant les risques de guerre. Les frais de vaccination et de traitement antipaludéen indispensables sont remboursés.

**CONDITIONS DE VIE :**

A l'heure de l'ouverture de ce poste, la mission n'a pas commencé l'ouverture, aucun lieu de vie n'est pour l'instant défini. D'ici l'arrivée du.de la CT, la mission aura identifié un lieu de vie et de bureau.
A Saint Marc, la sécurité reste volatile avec des restrictions sécuritaires importantes. Vie sociale limitée à quelques restaurants et à la présence de MSF et NRC.

jobs.title: SIEGE – Référent santé – H/F
jobs.description:
**A propos de la Chaîne de l’Espoir**

La Chaîne de l’Espoir est une ONG internationale fondée en 1994. Elle a pour vocation de renforcer les systèmes de santé pour donner à chacun et en particulier aux enfants les mêmes chances de survie et de développement.

Nous intervenons dans 28 pays par une approche globale, centrée sur l’enfant mais également sur les mères et les communautés défavorisées :

- Prévention et dépistage dès le plus jeune âge, notamment dans le cadre de programmes de santé à l’école.
- Soin et chirurgie, afin de répondre aux besoins les plus urgents des enfants et de leurs mères.
- Formation et transferts de compétences aux équipes locales grâce à notre réseau international d’experts dans tous les domaines de la chirurgie.
- Construction et équipement de structures hospitalières adaptées aux besoins locaux.

**Poste et missions**

Au sein de la Direction Santé et Ingénierie Hospitalière, et en lien fonctionnel fort avec la Direction des Opérations le Référent Santé joue un rôle essentiel dans la définition, la mise en œuvre et la supervision des programmes de La Chaîne de l’Espoir, en apportant un appui technique aux équipes de coordination des programmes.

Il est placé sous la responsabilité du Responsable du Département médical. Il exerce ses missions en lien étroit avec les équipes de la Direction des Opérations, et en collaboration étroite avec l’ensemble des équipes de la Direction de l’Expertise c’est-à-dire le Département médical et le Département Infrastructure et équipement biomédical.

Par ailleurs le Référent santé réalise toutes tâches et missions nécessaires confiées par sa hiérarchie et qui permettent de contribuer à l’atteinte des objectifs du Département médical et de la Direction Santé et Ingénierie Hospitalière.

- **Appui RH:** Contribution à l’élaboration des fiches de postes du personnel médical et paramédical terrain.

Participation au processus de recrutement des postes de coordination médicale et de responsables de programme de santé.

Contribution aux briefings et débriefings des personnels médicaux.

Participation aux entretiens d’appréciation professionnelle technique des coordinateurs santé terrain.

- **Stratégie Santé Pays et Siège:**

Soutien technique aux équipes siège et terrain dans la préparation et le suivi des missions exploratoires

Collaboration avec les équipes siège et terrain pour l'élaboration des stratégies opérationnelles et le montage des projets, en ligne avec la stratégie globale de l’association

Identification et analyse des besoins médicaux des pays d’intervention.

- **Soutien Technique aux Projets:**

Apport d'un soutien technique aux équipes programmes pour garantir la qualité des programmes médicaux

Appui technique des équipes de terrain tout au long du cycle de projet, notamment via des missions dans les pays d'intervention

Supervision des préparations et validation des commandes médicales, en s’assurant de leur pertinence et cohérence

- **Suivi et Qualité des Projets:**

Émission de recommandations pour assurer la qualité des projets lors des suivis réguliers à distance et des visites terrain

Participation à la définition et à l’élaboration de la politique qualité, avec une mise à jour des cadres de référence

Contribution à la capitalisation des activités médicales, incluant la rédaction de rapports, la relecture des rapports bailleurs et l’analyse des missions médicales

- **Renforcement des Capacités:**

En fonction des besoins, élaboration et animation de formations internes ou auprès de nos partenaires opérationnels. Appui à la coordination et au pilotage techniques des programmes de La Chaîne de l’Espoir.

Accompagnement des équipes terrain pour le pilotage des actions de ses partenaires sur le terrain au besoin.

## Profil recherché

**Formations et expériences**
