jobs.description:
**CONTENT CREATOR /NEWS ANCHOR – TERMS OF REFERENCE**

**Position Overview**

We are seeking a qualified and experienced Content Creator/Producer and News Anchor to research, script, produce and present regular news and analysis content for ADN TV. The successful candidate will combine strong on-camera presentation skills with hands-on production ability, overseeing content from concept and research through filming, editing and publishing. The role requires a sound understanding of regional political, security, economic and social dynamics, a commitment to accuracy and balance, and the ability to deliver high-quality content consistently under tight deadlines.

**Scope of Work:**

**Content Production and Presentation:**

• Produce and anchor regular short-form news and current affairs content in line with the agreed production schedule.
• Present content on camera in a clear, credible, engaging and professional manner suited to both broadcast and digital audiences.
• Develop content formats, segments and storytelling approaches that grow audience reach and engagement across Farsight’s media platforms.
• Conduct interviews with guests, analysts, officials and other contributors where applicable.

**News Updates:**

• Prepare and present regular news updates covering key political, security, economic and social developments in Somalia and the wider region.
• Monitor news sources, wire services, official statements and social media to identify and prioritise newsworthy developments.
• Respond promptly to breaking news and significant developments, adjusting content plans as required.

**Insight and Analysis Programming:**

• Produce and present regular insight and analysis programmes on thematic areas including business and the economy, digital transformation, security, and geopolitics and the Horn of Africa.
• Provide context, background and balanced perspectives that help audiences understand the significance of emerging issues and trends.
• Identify, engage and prepare relevant expert guests and commentators for analysis segments.

**Research, Scripting and Editorial Standards:**

• Research, plan and script all content, ensuring it is clear, well-structured and suited to the intended format and audience.
• Verify facts, figures and sources to ensure accuracy, fairness and balance in all published content.
• Ensure all content complies with the Company’s editorial standards, journalistic ethics and applicable media regulations.
• Exercise sound editorial judgement on sensitive political and security matters.

**Production Coordination and Publishing:**

• Coordinate filming, editing, graphics and post-production for all assigned content.
• Supervise the production and publishing workflow to ensure quality, consistency and timely release of all content.
• Work with camera operators, editors, graphic designers and digital teams to deliver content to the required technical and visual standards.
• Ensure content is optimised and correctly published across broadcast, website and social media channels.

**Planning and Reporting:**

• Prepare and share a content plan in advance, setting out proposed topics, guests (where applicable) and scheduled release dates.
• Track content output, deadlines and audience performance, and share regular progress updates with management.
• Maintain an organised archive of scripts, footage, sources and published content.
• Perform any other duties assigned from time to time.

**Reports Directly To:** Senior Operations Manager

**Works Directly With:** Production, Editorial, Digital and Research teams

**Qualifications and Skills:**

• Bachelor’s degree in Journalism, Mass Communication, Media Studies, Broadcast Production, International Relations or a related field.
• Minimum of 3 years proven experience in broadcast journalism, news anchoring, presenting and/or content production.
• A demonstrable on-camera presenting record, supported by a showreel or portfolio of published work.
• Strong knowledge of political, security, economic and social developments in Somalia and the Horn of Africa.
• Excellent research, scriptwriting, fact-checking and storytelling skills.
• Hands-on experience with video production and editing software (e.g. Adobe Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro, DaVinci Resolve) and basic graphics tools.
• Familiarity with digital and social media publishing, content management systems and audience analytics.
• Sound understanding of journalistic ethics, editorial standards, balance and media law.
• Excellent oral and written English skills; fluency in Somali or other regional languages will be an added advantage.
• Experience interviewing senior officials, experts or high-profile guests will be an added advantage.
• Strong organizational and planning skills, with the ability to manage a high volume of content and multiple deadlines.
• Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a fast-paced newsroom environment.
• High level of integrity, professionalism, credibility and confidentiality.

**Equal Opportunity Statement**

Farsight Africa Group is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and do not discriminate on the basis of gender, age, disability, religion, ethnicity, or any other protected characteristic. All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply.

**Why Join Farsight**

- Work with a fast-growing, innovative African communications and research firm.
- Build your profile on a growing regional news and analysis platform.
- Engage in meaningful content across governance, development, security and strategic communications.
- Dynamic, multicultural team operating across East Africa.
- Opportunities for professional growth, learning, and regional exposure.

jobs.title: Finance Manager Lebanon
jobs.description:
**What we are looking for**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) has been supporting people affected by displacement in Lebanon for 20 years. As we embark on an important period of strategic and operational change, we are seeking an **experienced** **Finance Manager** to provide **strategic financial leadership**, **strengthen financial systems**, and ensure the effective and accountable use of resources to deliver humanitarian assistance.

We are looking for **a strategic, analytical, and solutions-oriented finance leader** who can navigate change, translate financial data into actionable insights, and balance strong financial controls with the operational flexibility required in a dynamic humanitarian context.

This is an exciting opportunity to shape NRC Lebanon’s financial direction, support organisational transformation, and strengthen collaboration with local partners and actors.

***Applicants must be legally eligible to work in Lebanon, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.***

**What you will do**

The Finance Manager is responsible for effective financial management, budgeting, reporting, compliance and internal controls across NRC Lebanon.

This role provides strategic financial leadership by delivering accurate, reliable, and timely financial information, enabling senior management to make informed decisions and ensure the efficient use of organisational resources.

The position holder will ensure that NRC Lebanon is well positioned to respond to current and future needs and shall demonstrate strong engagement and leadership in all major Finance actions, while ensuring capacity building for Finance team members and budget holders across the entire country.

Key responsibilities:

- **Provide strategic financial leadership** across NRC Lebanon, ensuring robust financial systems, policies, internal controls, and compliance with NRC, donor, and local regulatory requirements.
- **Lead budgeting, financial reporting, and analysis**, delivering timely, accurate insights to inform senior management decisions and support effective resource allocation.
- **Oversee accounting, cash flow, and liquidity management**, ensuring operational continuity, accurate financial records, and effective audit preparation and follow-up.
- **Manage financial risks and compliance**, strengthening accountability, implementing anti-corruption measures, and addressing audit findings and financial control gaps.
- **Advise and support budget holders and programme teams** throughout the project cycle, from proposal development and budgeting to expenditure monitoring and reporting.
- **Strengthen financial capacity and team performance** through effective leadership, staff development, and technical support to Finance colleagues and budget holders nationwide.
- **Advance NRC’s localisation agenda** by strengthening financial systems, tools, and capacity to support local partners and actors in delivering compliant, effective, and sustainable humanitarian responses.

**What you will bring**

- A bachelor’s degree in finance, Accounting, or a relevant field.
- **At least four years of finance experience**, including **three years in a managerial or equivalent role** **within a humanitarian or recovery context.**
- **Experience working with local partners** and **institutional humanitarian donors.**
- **Strong financial analysis**, **budgeting, reporting**, and risk management skills, with proficiency in MS Excel and accounting systems.
- Fluency in written and spoken English.
- Experience **developing financial systems during organisational change** is highly desirable; **emergency finance leadership experience** and previous work in the Middle East are an advantage.

Please download [the detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQDykXJd7GUEQZVDhD3vlo8xAUtc9vURiJeSfCAscQg3el0?e=oaBMOR) to learn more about the position.

**What we offer**

- Duty station: Beirut, Lebanon
- Fixed term contract: 12 months national contract, renewable based on performance, funding and need for the position
- Travel: 10-20%
- Salary/benefits: Grade 9 on NRC's national grading structure.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- We invite applications from qualified candidates matching the profile. ***Applicants must be legally eligible to work in Lebanon, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.***
- Please ensure you attach copies of your academic and professional certificates.
- To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email address or click on Opportunity Marketplace.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We receive many applicants for each vacant position.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity

**Join NRC Lebanon and help shape the financial leadership, systems, and partnerships that will enable us to respond effectively to humanitarian needs and deliver greater impact.**

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

[Learn more about NRC Lebanon](https://www.nrc.no/countries/middle-east/lebanon)

jobs.title: Nigeria Regional Warehouse Coordinator (Fixed-term)
jobs.description:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

We started working in Nigeria in 2018, serving just 150 farmers. That figure grew year on year, and we now serve more than 300,000 farmers across three regions in Niger State: Minna, Mokwa, and Iseyin.

Between our tree program and a diverse staple crop program, xx staff are supporting farmers in Nigeria to grow their way to prosperity.

## About the Role

Seeking a supply chain professional with 2-5 years' experience to coordinate warehouse and inventory operations, team supervision, and space optimization to support efficient and scalable program delivery.

## Responsibilities

Regional Warehouse Operations & Performance

- Coordinate day-to-day warehouse operations across assigned regional facilities.
- Ensure warehouses consistently follow approved OAF warehouse processes, and SOPs.
- Monitor warehouse performance against agreed KPIs for inventory accuracy, shrinkage, service, productivity, safety and compliance.
- Identify and share best practices across warehouses to improve consistency and performance.
- Plan ahead for peak periods and ensure warehouses are ready to support field and farmer needs.
- Regularly Go to Gemba to understand operational challenges and drive practical improvements.

Inventory Management & Control

- Lead regular physical stock counts, reconciliations and inventory reviews across assigned warehouses.
- Ensure physical stock is accurately reflected in the relevant inventory management system.
- Investigate inventory variances, identify root causes and ensure corrective actions are completed.
- Monitor inventory ageing, stock movements, transfers and potential losses.
- Strengthen controls that prevent shrinkage, stock errors and unauthorized stock movements.
- Ensure inventory records and supporting documentation are complete and audit-ready.

Warehouse Systems, Documentation & Compliance

- Ensure receiving, dispatch and inter-warehouse movements are properly documented and recorded on time.
- Maintain accurate warehouse records, including stock count sheets, waybills, delivery notes, GRNs, transfer documents and quality records.
- Conduct regular compliance checks and follow up on identified gaps.
- Support internal and external audits by ensuring warehouse records and physical stock are readily available.
- Escalate suspected theft, fraud, significant loss or other serious compliance concerns through the appropriate channels.

Warehouse Layout, Quality & Process Improvement

- Ensure effective warehouse layout, product segregation, palletization, labelling and storage practices.
- Work closely with QA/QC to maintain appropriate product handling, storage and release standards.
- Identify bottlenecks and opportunities to improve warehouse flow, space utilization and productivity.
- Lead practical improvement initiatives using data, root-cause analysis and feedback from warehouse teams.
- Standardize successful improvements across other regional warehouses where appropriate.

Health, Safety & Environment

- Promote a strong safety culture across all assigned warehouses.
- Conduct regular warehouse Gemba walks and safety checks to identify and address hazards.
- Ensure appropriate use of PPE and compliance with warehouse safety standards.
- Maintain clean, organized and safe working environments for employees, casual workers and visitors.
- Ensure incidents, near misses and safety concerns are reported, investigated and followed through to closure.
- Encourage team members to speak up and take ownership of safety.

Distribution & Supply Chain Coordination

- Coordinate with Logistics, Procurement, QA/QC and field teams to ensure smooth warehouse operations and timely movement of inputs.
- Support efficient loading, dispatch and inter-warehouse transfer activities.
- Ensure warehouse capacity and dispatch plans are aligned with operational demand.
- Work with Logistics teams to resolve delivery and dispatch challenges quickly.
- Support efficient use of warehouse and transport resources to reduce avoidable operational costs.

Team Leadership & Development

- Provide day-to-day leadership and support to Warehouse Supervisors and warehouse teams.
- Set clear expectations, priorities and performance standards.
- Coach team members to improve warehouse practices, inventory controls, safety and customer service.
- Build a culture of accountability, teamwork, feedback and continuous improvement.
- Support performance reviews, recruitment, onboarding and development of warehouse staff.
- Lead by example and create an environment where people can take ownership and grow.

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Bachelor's degree or HND in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Business Administration, Agribusiness, Science & Engineering or a related discipline. (A Masters degree with relevant professional certificate in supply chain would be an added advantage)
- At least 2 - 5 years of relevant experience in warehouse, inventory, logistics operations including supervising, managing or coordinating
- Strong leadership skills to effectively lead and motivate a team.
- Organizational skills to efficiently plan, prioritize and delegate tasks.
- Warehouse operations; inventory management and reconciliation; warehouse systems/WMS; stock control; warehouse layout and capacity planning; HSE; basic data analysis; process improvement; documentation and compliance.
- Makes day-to-day operational decisions within approved policies, SOPs and budgets; escalates significant operational, financial, safety and compliance risks appropriately.
- Quick problem-solving abilities to anticipate, identify and resolve issues with deliveries and transport operations.
- High attention to detail to accurately plan, schedule and track all deliveries.
- Excellent communication skills to effectively interact with clients, colleagues and stakeholders.
- Computer literacy to efficiently use software and systems for planning, managing and tracking deliverables.
- Efficient time management capabilities to ensure timely execution of deliveries and transport operations.
- Flexibility to adapt to evolving customer needs and requirements.
- Commercial awareness to identify cost-saving opportunities and make profitable decisions.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Bida, Niger State, Nigeria

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Nigeria.

## Application Deadline

08 January 2027. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @*[*oneacrefund.org*](http://oneacrefund.org/) *address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), **but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.***

*Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.*

*We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.*

jobs.title: Burundi Government Relations Lead
jobs.description:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Burundi program, founded in 2011, operates under the local brand Tubura. 1662 staff serve close to 400,000 hard-working farmers. Our Burundi headquarters in Muramvya is supported by two regional offices in Gitega and Ngozi, and a small support office in Bujumbura. One Acre Fund works in the center and north of Burundi, in the provinces of Muramvya, Gitega, Ngozi, Kayanza, and Mwaro.

## **About the Role**

The External Relations team works to build and maintain strong relationships between One Acre Fund–Tubura and key external stakeholders, including the Government of Burundi, private-sector partners, development partners and international institutions. The team helps create an enabling environment for Tubura to deliver its mission and maximize impact, while ensuring that the organization understands and complies with relevant Government policies, regulations and requirements.

As Government Relations Lead, you will serve as Tubura's senior interface with the Government of Burundi and a key advisor to the Country Director and leadership team on Government policy, stakeholder dynamics, external risks and opportunities, and strategies to build an enabling environment for Tubura's growth and impact.

## **Responsibilities**

Vision Setting & Strategic Planning

- Set the vision and strategy for the Government Relations function, working with the relevant leads to develop annual priorities and goals.
- Support the leadership team in navigating an increasingly complex operating environment and integrate Government and external trends into organizational strategy.

Government Relations & Representation

- Build and maintain strategic relationships with senior Government officials and key public institutions at national, provincial and local levels.
- Represent the Country Director and Tubura in high-level Government meetings, policy discussions and strategic forums.

Policy & Advocacy

- Monitor and interpret Government policies, regulations and priorities relevant to Tubura; develop proactive advocacy and engagement strategies; and advise leadership on their implications, risks and opportunities.

Partnerships & Stakeholder Management

- Develop and oversee strategies for strategic partnerships, Government champions and other priority stakeholders, including private-sector, development and institutional partners.
Identify opportunities to strengthen Tubura’s external relationships and access to decision-makers

Government Enablement & External Risk Management

- Work cross-functionally to identify and address Government-related opportunities and constraints affecting program delivery, including agricultural input policy, fertilizer supply and procurement, importation and other strategic initiatives.
Anticipate and manage Government, regulatory and reputational risks.

Communications & Compliance Oversight

- Work with the Communications and Compliance leads to ensure coordinated external positioning, effective institutional communications and adherence to relevant Government and regulatory requirements.

Team Leadership & Organizational Support

- Lead, coach and develop the Government Relations team while ensuring the function provides effective strategic support to departments across Tubura and actionable Government intelligence to the Country Director and leadership team.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- A Bachelor's or Master's degree in international relations, public policy, political science, communications, development studies or another relevant field.
- At least 7 years of relevant professional experience, including 3+ years in a senior leadership or management role involving significant Government engagement, stakeholder management and strategic decision-making.
- Significant experience working with Government institutions, public agencies, development partners or other senior external stakeholders, preferably in Burundi or elsewhere in Africa.

jobs.title: CDDU - IRAQ - Head of mission
jobs.description:
**About La Chaîne de l’Espoir:**

La Chaîne de l’Espoir is an international NGO founded in 1994. Its mission is to strengthen healthcare systems to give everyone, especially children, the same chances of survival and development.

Helping the most marginalized children is more than an ethical duty, it is a vital requirement for achieving the United Nations 2030 goals for children's health and well-being.

We work in 25 countries with a global approach, focusing on children, mothers and disadvantaged communities:

- Prevention and screening from an early age, particularly through school health programs.
- Care and surgery to meet the most urgent needs of children and their mothers.
- Training and transfer of skills to local teams thanks to our international network of experts in all areas of surgery.
- Construction and equipment of hospital facilities adapted to local needs.

**General scope of the position:**

The Head of Mission is responsible for overseeing and coordinating the orderly closure of La Chaîne de l’Espoir’s mission in Iraq. They ensure that all programme, operational, financial, administrative, logistical and human resources activities related to the closure are completed in a timely, efficient and compliant manner, in line with organisational policies, donor requirements and applicable national legislation.

They oversee the implementation of the mission closure plan, ensuring the completion or appropriate handover of ongoing projects, the fulfilment of contractual and donor obligations, the management of financial and administrative close-out procedures, and the appropriate management of staff, assets and resources.

The Head of Mission represents La Chaîne de l’Espoir throughout the closure process and maintains effective relationships with donors, partners, local authorities and other relevant stakeholders. They ensure effective coordination with headquarters and provide regular updates on the progress of the closure, potential risks and outstanding issues.

They remain ultimately responsible for the safety and security of staff, premises and assets throughout the closure process, ensuring that appropriate measures are maintained until the mission’s final withdrawal.

They coordinate the work of the relevant programme and support teams and liaise closely with headquarters to ensure a smooth, accountable and well-documented closure.

**Essential duties and responsibilities**:

- Mission closure planning and coordination: Develop, implement and monitor the mission closure plan, ensuring that all activities are completed according to the agreed timeline.
- Programme management: Oversee project completion, final reporting, donor compliance and the handover of activities, where applicable.
- Representation and external relations: Maintain communication and coordination with donors, partners, local authorities and other stakeholders throughout the closure process.
- Human resources management: Oversee staff transition and departure procedures, contract termination, final payments and compliance with applicable labour regulations.
- Financial and administrative management: Ensure budget closure, financial reconciliation, settlement of outstanding commitments and completion of administrative and contractual obligations.
- Logistics and asset management: Supervise the management and disposition of assets, equipment, premises, vehicles and supplies in accordance with organisational policies and donor requirements.
- Safety and security: Ensure appropriate security arrangements and risk mitigation measures throughout the closure process.
- Reporting and archiving: Ensure the completion, consolidation and transfer of all relevant documentation to headquarters, and contribute to lessons learned.

**Qualifications:**

- **Education:** Advanced university degree in business administration, political science, international relations, project management or a related field is required.
- **Work experience:** A minimum of 5 years’ experience within the solidarity sector. A minimum of 3 years in a similar position, preferably with an international NGO.
- Experience in Health Sector is desirable
- A solid humanitarian background is necessary.
- **Languages:** Good verbal and written communication skills in English.
- Knowledge of Arabic and Kurdish are desirable.
- French is an asset.
- **Personal qualities:** Adherence to humanitarian principle and La Chaîne de l’Espoir’s code of ethics;
- Strong analytical skills and ability to develop comprehensive and inclusive country strategies and context analysis;
- Excellent interpersonal and diplomatic skills, with a proven track record in forming effective relationships with a range of traditional, local and international authorities, organisations and donors;
- Good reporting skills, with proven ability in financial report writing;
- Demonstrated experience in managing compliance to strategic donors’ requirements;
- Experience of working in insecure environments or complex emergency contexts;
- Computer proficiency in Microsoft Office Package;

**Terms and conditions**

- 06 months full time contract as an expatriate
- Non accompanied status
- Position based in Erbil with missions in all Iraq
- Starting date: December
- Monthly gross salary: between 3 200 euros and 3 700 euros
- Monthly per diem and living allowance: 720 euros net
- R&R: 5 days R&R at 3 months of contract
- Travel: round trip ticket flight beginning/end of contract
- Housing: individual with 100% of employer contribution
- Medical coverage with 50% of employer contribution
- Medical evacuation and repatriation insurance paid by the employer
- Death and disability insurance paid by the employer

jobs.title: Area Manager - Syria
jobs.description:
**Description**

Place: Aleppo, Syria
Starting date: 1st December 2026
Duration of contract: 12 months

Humanity & Inclusion is an independent and impartial aid organisation working in situations of poverty and exclusion, conflict and disaster. The organisation works alongside people with disabilities and vulnerable populations, taking action and bearing witness in order to respond to their essential needs, improve their living conditions and promote respect for their dignity and fundamental rights.

Since its creation in 1982, HI has run development & humanitarian projects in more than 55 countries and responded to numerous emergencies. Today, we have a budget of approximately 200 million euros, with 4,000 employees worldwide

At Handicap International-Humanity & Inclusion, we truly believe in the importance of inclusion and diversity within our organisation. This is why we are engaged to a disability policy to encourage the inclusion and integration of people with disabilities.

Please indicate if you require any special accommodation, even at the first interview.

**JOB CONTEXT:**
HI has been present in Syria since 2012, maintaining uninterrupted operations through various intervention and coordination modalities across the country. Following the fall of the previous regime on 8 December 2024, Syria entered a new phase characterized by the coexistence of significant humanitarian needs with growing early recovery opportunities. Despite these developments, the country remains affected by a protracted crisis, with approximately 15.8 million people still requiring humanitarian assistance, including around 6.5 million internally displaced persons, while more than 5 million Syrian refugees remain in neighboring countries and Europe, some considering return. Widespread contamination from explosive ordnance, damaged infrastructure, limited livelihood opportunities, constrained access to essential services such as healthcare and education, and persistent protection risks continue to hinder recovery efforts and leave many communities highly vulnerable. In this context, HI remains committed to supporting the most at-risk populations, promoting inclusion, strengthening resilience, and contributing to a safe, dignified, and sustainable recovery for all Syrians.

HI is managing a humanitarian program covering most of Syria’s governorates, particularly, in northeast Syria:

Support to health services for the provision of multi-disciplinary rehabilitation services (physiotherapy, provision of assistive devices, prosthetics and orthotics and MHPSS).
Provision of early childhood rehabilitation services such as stimulation therapy for children with malnutrition
Humanitarian Mine Action, including clearance, advocacy, NTS and TS, EORE.
Community based protection for safe returns and support for the inclusion of persons with disabilities and other vulnerable people in the humanitarian assistance.
Disaster Risk Reduction and Preparedness activities against manmade and non-manmade related disasters.
Inclusive Education for children with disabilities
Inclusive Humanitarian Action

The actual intervention was so far managed based on a mix partnership with local structures and organizations, and direct implementation programs.

**YOUR MISSION:**
Under the responsibility of the Operational Manager, the Area Manager contributes within the area where he/she is based to the implementation of the mandate and the 10-year strategy of Humanity & Inclusion.

He/she ensures optimal quality and impact of the projects implemented in the area, through a delegation system with appropriate control mechanisms. He/she shares with all HI managers the responsibility of a sound management and successful functioning of the global organization, through paradigm changes.

**Main Responsibilities**

· The Area Manager is responsible for leading the implementation of Humanity & Inclusion's operational strategy within the assigned geographical area, ensuring high-quality programme delivery, operational effectiveness, compliance, and strategic positioning. Under the supervision of the Operations Manager, the Area Manager oversees project implementation, contributes to programme development, manages operational risks, and ensures strong coordination between programme and support functions.

· The Area Manager monitors contextual developments, identifies emerging risks and opportunities, and advises senior management on operational adaptations and strategic priorities. The position is also responsible for ensuring the effective deployment of HI policies, standards, and management frameworks, including project quality, accountability, safeguarding, security, and donor compliance requirements.

· As the senior HI representative in the area of responsibility, the Area Manager promotes collaboration among programme, technical, and support teams, ensuring that services remain operational, responsive, and aligned with programme objectives. Although not the direct supervisor of all support functions, the Area Manager plays a critical leadership and coordination role in fostering cross-functional collaboration, setting operational priorities, and strengthening the link between field operations and the Country Office.

· The Area Manager is furthermore responsible for overseeing security management within the area of responsibility, with support from the Humanitarian Access and Security Department, ensuring that activities are implemented in accordance with organizational security procedures and risk mitigation measures.
Requirements

**CHARACTERISTICS OF THE POSITION:**

The Area Manager NCA covers Aleppo, Idlib, and Hama governorates, where the security environment remains volatile and requires constant monitoring.

Key risks include explosive ordnance contamination, localized security incidents, movement restrictions, and evolving political and administrative dynamics. Regular field travel is required, often involving long road movements and occasional overnight stays in field locations. Living conditions in major urban centers are generally adequate, although essential services such as electricity, telecommunications, healthcare, and transportation may be disrupted. Flexibility, adherence to security procedures, and the ability to work in a complex and rapidly changing environment are essential.

**YOUR PROFILE:**

Solid experience in the humanitarian sector

· Strong understanding of programme management, donor compliance, and operational planning

Demonstrated ability to manage stress effectively, including in demanding or fast-paced environments
Strong reactivity, flexibility, and adaptability, with the capacity to adjust quickly to changing priorities and contexts
Strong computer skills
Fluency in spoken and written English is compulsory, knowledge of Arabic, both spoken and written, is a strong asset

**Benefits**

**CONDITIONS**

At HI, the conditions offered are up to your commitment and adapted to the context of your mission:

12 months International contract starting from beginning of December 2026 based in Aleppo, Syria;
The international contract provides social cover adapted to your situation:
Unemployment insurance benefits for EU nationals;
Pension scheme;
Medical coverage with 50% of employee contribution;
Repatriation insurance paid by HI;
Salary from 2869 € gross/month upon experience;
Perdiem: 537€ net/month - paid in the field
Hardship: 250 € net/month paid with your salary;
Paid leaves: 25 days per year;
R&R: according to the level of the mission : 5 days every 3 months
Position: Unaccompanied
a child allowance of 100€ per month, per child (from the second child and maximum four) paid in the field ;
Housing: Individual taken in charge by HI;
If you are resident in the country: local package.

jobs.title: Protection Analyst—Research and Advocacy
jobs.description:
**Introduction**

Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

**Project Context and Scope**

Under the overall supervision of the Deputy Chief of Mission and the direct supervision of the Head of Protection, the Junior Protection Analyst – Research, and Advocacy supports the Mobility Pathways and Inclusion (MPI) Unit in donor reporting, analysis and advocacy of programmatic interventions in Iraq.

The scope of this consultancy relates to MPI’s protection monitoring and research activities, as well as reporting. IOM contributes to evidence-based protection advocacy through protection monitoring. Protection monitoring is carried out to identify the protection risks and needs of affected populations to support evidence-based programming and advocacy. Research is conducted using a mixed-method approach and feeds into advocacy with key stakeholders, including government, development actors, and donor communities. The consultant contributes to this work by supporting the production of protection monitoring reports and any other protection monitoring products and activities.

The Junior Protection Analyst also supports MPI with its donor reporting portfolio. The consultant will support the Protection Analyst for MPI donor reports to be submitted to the Programme Support Unit (PSU) for final clearance.

**Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing**

Mobility Pathways and Inclusion (MPI) Unit

## **Responsibilities**

**Tasks to be performed under this contract**

- Provide support to the Al-Amal Protection Monitoring work, including proofreading, copy-editing, fact-checking, and assisting with qualitative and quantitative analysis; coordinate with team members to keep products accurate and up to date.
- Contribute to thematic work on environmental migration, gender-based violence, disability and inclusion, migration, and protracted displacement by conducting desk research, organising literature, and assisting with data analysis for reports and briefs.
- Help maintain knowledge-sharing products, such as thematic notes, policy briefs, and dashboards, by compiling data, verifying consistency, and providing analysis.
- Support the MPI donor reporting portfolio. Analyze data from field reports and monitoring tools to support comprehensive donor reports, ensuring alignment with reporting requirements; support proposals by incorporating key findings from protection monitoring activities and advocacy efforts.
- Work closely with the Programme, IMS, and M&E teams to ensure reporting inputs remain consistent, clarify indicator definitions, and support routine data management tasks.
- Assist with additional tasks that help the MPI Unit deliver its regular monitoring, reporting, and research activities.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

- 6 protection monitoring reports and 5 donor reports

## **Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education, Experience and/or skills required**

- Master’s Degree in Forced Migration, Humanitarian Action, Human Rights, or related discipline
- At least 2-year experience in research, data analysis, protection monitoring, and advocacy within the humanitarian or development sector; experience designing data collection tools and methodologies.
- Proven track record of producing high-quality analytical and written outputs, including concise reports and publications.
- Familiarity with protection challenges faced by displaced populations in Iraq or similar crisis-affected contexts.
- Experience in donor reporting, including data analysis and report writing.
- Experience working effectively and independently in remote or virtual environments.

Experience communicating effectively with a variety of stakeholders, including diverse audiences

**Languages**

For this consultancy,Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

**Travel required (Yes/NO)**

Yes

**Required Competencies**

IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.

**Values** - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:

- **Inclusion and respect for diversity**: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- **Integrity and transparency**: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- **Professionalism**: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- **Courage**: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- **Empathy**: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

**Core Competencies** – behavioural indicators

- **Teamwork**: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.

jobs.title: Programme Associate VAM
jobs.description:
**BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE APPOINTMENT:**

WFP Jordan works with national institutions and partners to strengthen food security, social protection and evidence-based programming. The Vulnerability, Assessment and Mapping (VAM) function generates and manages evidence to support programme design, targeting, market analysis, monitoring and operational decision-making.

The post is based in the WFP Jordan Country Office in Amman. Under the guidance and supervision of the Senior VAM Officer, the VAM Associate will contribute to market analysis, assessment design and implementation, household profiling, targeting analysis, evidence generation and capacity strengthening activities.

**ACCOUNTABILITIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Market Analysis and Price Monitoring**

- Lead the planning, coordination, collection, management and analysis of market price data in collaboration with relevant units, including Supply Chain and Field Offices, and prepare monthly, quarterly and ad hoc market monitoring reports and bulletins to support programme and country office decision-making.
- Serve as a focal point for the resolution of technical and operational queries and problems related to market analysis, price monitoring and economic trends.
- Lead assessments and analysis related to the Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB), affordability and household purchasing power.
- Monitor market trends, inflation and economic risks and support Country Office risk management, including the formulation, updating and monitoring of key economic and market-price risk indicators in the CO risk register.
- Support the generation of evidence on market conditions and economic factors affecting food security and programme implementation.

**Assessment, Targeting and Evidence Generation**

- support the design and implementation of quantitative and qualitative assessments, including periodical vulnerability assessments, surveys and regular monitoring activities, under the guidance of the VAM Officer, covering methodology, sampling, tool development, oversight of enumerator training and field data collection, and quality assurance.
- Conduct data cleaning, validation and analysis using SPSS, R, Excel or similar tools.
- Conduct household profiling, vulnerability and targeting analyses, including regression analysis where appropriate, to identify factors influencing food security and programme outcomes, assess targeting effectiveness, and inform beneficiary selection, prioritization and programme decision-making.
- Analyze indicators related to food security, nutrition, markets, vulnerability, resilience and livelihoods, applying gender, accountability to affected populations (AAP) and protection perspectives, and prepare clear reports and evidence products.
- Support the dissemination of evidence products in accordance with WFP protocols, compile lessons learned and best practices, and contribute to the preparation of external VAM products.
- Contribute analytical evidence to discussions and implementation of WFP assistance, including general food assistance, school feeding and resilience-based programmes.
- Support coordination with government institutions, UN agencies, NGOs and other partners to support assessments, analysis and evidence generation.
- Maintain clear documentation of business processes, methodologies, datasets and analytical processes, and contribute to effective information management and sharing.

**Capacity Building and Partnerships**

- in Coordination with the VAM officer, technically support analytical initiatives between WFP, government institutions and other partners in line with WFP corporate policies and data protection and privacy requirements.
- Support the establishment and implementation of technical agreements and joint analytical activities with national counterparts, including the Department of Statistics of Jordan, as relevant.
- Support capacity strengthening activities for WFP staff, partners and government counterparts in market monitoring, targeting, household analysis and food security analysis.
- Provide technical support to government institutions and other partners to strengthen national capacities in food security information, market analysis, early warning systems and evidence-based decision-making, including but not limited to the Food Security Information Management System, administered by the Higher Food Security Council.
- Perform other related duties as required.

**QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE REQUIRED:**

**Education:** Completion of secondary school education. A post-secondary certificate in a related functional area is desirable.

**Experience:** At least six years of progressively responsible experience, including relevant experience in assessments, data analysis, market monitoring, targeting or food security analysis.

**Knowledge & Skills:**

- Experience in conducting surveys, assessments and quantitative data analysis.
- Good understanding of household vulnerability analysis and targeting approaches.
- Proficiency in SPSS, R, STATA, Excel or other data analysis software.
- Ability to conduct and interpret statistical analysis, including regression analysis, and translate findings into clear recommendations.
- Strong report writing, data presentation and communication skills.
- Experience working with government counterparts and humanitarian or development partners.

**Other Post Requirements**

- Previous experience in humanitarian or development contexts.
- Previous experience in conducting assessments, surveys or research.
- Experience in household-level data analysis, targeting, market monitoring or food security analysis.
- Good report writing and communication skills.

**Languages:** Fluency in oral and written Arabic and English

jobs.title: Grant Management and Learning Coordinator - International
jobs.description:
**Job profile**

The Grant Management and Learning Coordinator fulfils a key function within the Department of Programme Development, Impact and Learning, sitting in the Grant Management Unit. Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Director of Programme Performance and Monitoring, the Grant Management and Learning Coordinator is responsible for ensuring compliance with donor grants, coordinating consolidation of coherent and accurate project data, supporting timely development and submission of high-quality donor reports, building and maintaining relationships with partners and donors, and proactively identifying the need for contract changes. In addition, the role coordinates the production of high-quality research on the organisation's Climate Adaptation work and other programming, translating findings into articles, reports and other documents for donors, the NGO community, and other external audiences.

**Duties and Responsibilities**

The position covers the following key areas of responsibility:

- For assigned grants, serve as the focal point for Afghanaid’s policies and donor contract terms and conditions, maintaining comprehensive knowledge and ensuring that all grant documentation (including proposals, reports, and budgets) is properly stored and available to relevant staff, and that key reporting requirements and other compliance obligations are clearly communicated to finance and project teams.
- Upon the signing of a new grant agreement, facilitate a smooth handover of the project to the Grant Management Unit, following up on outstanding project partnership agreement (PPA) tasks, and confirming reporting responsibilities and processes with relevant parties at the project kickoff meeting.
- Maintain internal and external tracking of reporting timelines, including working with relevant departments to coordinate appropriate data collection, analysis and financial and narrative reporting by Afghanaid and its partners.
- Review and refine high-quality financial and narrative project reports, survey and evaluation reports, and other associated donor communications, ensuring timely submission and compliance with Afghanaid, donor and partner requirements.
- Independently troubleshoot issues raised by project and operational teams, serving as liaison between the project team and donor to address and resolve challenges.
- Facilitate and contribute to regular project review processes, and pre-emptively raise concerns where contractual obligations, quality standards or deadlines are at risk of not being met, especially identifying risks of donor ‘clawback’ and reputational damage.
- In coordination with project teams, partners and the finance team, lead on revisions to project budgets, logical frameworks and other project documents for assigned grants, ensuring timely submission to the donor and follow up on approvals, and communicating updates to relevant departments.
- Support the Consortium Manager in strengthening partner performance and report quality by reviewing and providing input on partner organisations’ annual and semi-annual narrative reports.
- Initiate learning exchanges and facilitate reflection and adaptive management sessions with Afghanaid staff and partners.
- Lead organisational research initiatives, including establishing and managing partnerships with research organisations, individual researchers (including PhD candidates/Masters’ students), universities and institutes, and consultants to facilitate the production of research outputs for Afghanaid. Adapt research findings into policy and practitioner briefs tailored to different audiences, including donors and external stakeholders; and producing reports drawing on the organisational database of past reports and data.

- Represent the organisation at external fora and in meetings with partners and donors to promote the organisation, strengthen external relations and identify opportunities for new and repeat funding and partnerships that contribute to Afghanaid’s funding pipeline.
- Support organisational learning initiatives where possible, for instance through documenting institutional knowledge and expertise and participating in lessons learned workshops.
- Contribute to organisational capacity through developing and facilitating training and workshops for Afghanaid staff, including in provincial offices, on subjects including effective reporting and impact analysis.
- Lead and support on the development of project reporting, analysis and evaluation templates and tools.
- Facilitate field visits with donor organisations, and virtual visits as required.

**PERSON SPECIFICATION**

**Requirements**

**Essential**

**Education**

- A Master’s degree in Development Studies, International Relations, Social Sciences or another relevant programme of study

**Experience**

- 3-4 years of experience of working in a development or humanitarian context, in project support, grant management, programme development or a similar role
- Proven experience of synthesising data and input from various sources into clear and cohesive narrative reports
- Strong experience with logical frameworks and/or theories of change
- Experience working in high-risk or volatile contexts, including humanitarian or emergency settings.

**Knowledge and Skills**

- Native English proficiency and demonstrated ability to write high quality, polished documents and reports that are consistent with a set brand and style
- Experience turning data and research into clear reports for a variety of audiences
- Strong data entry skills, familiarity with use of a databases, and office tools (Excel, Word)
- Experience in contract management
- Experience in donor/client relationship management in the humanitarian / development sector
- Experience in humanitarian project design or management, and/or budget development or management
- Strong organisational skills, able to plan effectively, set priorities, and meet tight deadlines under pressure
- Strong people and coalition-building skills and proven ability to form good working relations, both internally within the organisation and externally with people at all levels

**Personal Attributes**

- Intellectually curious and able to question assumptions
- Ability to work independently and as a team member, including in a coordinating capacity with other departments
- Initiative and drive to achieve results, working quickly and accurately with attention to detail
- An outgoing and engaging personality and strong sense of humour, able to build trust and manage relationships with a variety of stakeholders
- Cultural sensitivity and ability to work in diverse multi-cultural environment
- Ability and willingness to travel for work

**Desirable**

- Experience working on Climate Adaptation projects
- Experience working with, or knowledge of, key institutional donors for development and humanitarian programming in Afghanistan

- Understanding of the cultural, security and operating environment in Afghanistan (or in a similar context)
- Understanding of Dari and/or Pashto

jobs.title: Senior Procurement & Logistics Officer
jobs.description:
**About HEKS/EPER:**
HEKS/EPER (Swiss Church Aid) is a faith-based international development and humanitarian organization committed to justice, human dignity, and sustainable development. In Uganda and South Sudan, our work focuses on supporting marginalized communities and building resilience through a triple nexus approach that integrates humanitarian response, sustainable development, and peacebuilding. We promote a rights-based, participatory, and conflict-sensitive approach that upholds dignity, inclusion, and accountability to affected populations.

**Description of main tasks:**

Under the supervision of the Head of Finance and Administration, the Senior Procurement & Logistics Officer is responsible for an assigned procurement portfolio and provides lead coordination of logistics, fleet and transport management across the Country Programme. The role oversees end-to-end procurement processes, supplier performance, assets and inventory within the assigned portfolio, while ensuring safe, efficient and cost-effective fleet operations, vehicle compliance and staff movement planning. Working alongside the Procurement & Logistics Officer within a common procurement framework, the position also provides technical coordination and operational support on fleet, logistics, safety and security matters.

The role requires regular field engagement to provide hands-on support and respond to procurement, logistics, safety, and security-related operational challenges. The Senior Procurement & Logistics Officer will therefore travel periodically to HEKS/EPER field locations and must be willing and able to travel at short notice when operational needs arise, including to South Sudan where required.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Procurement Planning and Portfolio Management**

- Work with project and department leads to consolidate procurement needs and maintain procurement plans for the assigned portfolio.
- Ensure purchase requests are complete, appropriately approved and processed in accordance with FFAG, HEKS/EPER procurement procedures and delegated authorities.
- Maintain a clear tracker of open and closed procurement actions, lead times, commitments, and delivery status.
- Coordinate procurement schedules with Finance and Programs to support timely project implementation.

**Sourcing, Tendering and Supplier Management**

- Conduct sourcing through approved channels, prepare solicitation documentation, coordinate bid receipt/evaluation, and document procurement decisions.
- Support negotiations and preparation of purchase orders, contracts and framework arrangements within delegated authority.
- Maintain supplier records and conduct supplier due diligence, performance assessment, and market analysis.
- Identify cost-saving and value-for-money opportunities while safeguarding quality, transparency, and fair competition.
- Support local partners with procurement processes where required.

**Procurement Compliance, Documentation and Reporting**

- Maintain complete procurement files, including requisitions, quotations/tenders, evaluations, approvals, purchase orders, contracts, delivery documentation and supplier records.
- Identify procurement risks, conflicts, supplier of non-compliance and market changes and escalate material issues to the HoFA.
- Prepare procurement status and performance information for management review and support procurement-related audits.
- Coordinate with Finance to ensure supplier payment packages are complete; Finance retains payment processing and accounting responsibility.

**Assets, Inventory and General Logistics**

- Maintain accurate asset and inventory records and support periodic physical verification, tagging, and condition checks.
- Maintain records of stock movements and investigate discrepancies.
- Coordinate transportation and delivery of procured goods to required locations and support efficient logistics planning.
- Ensure assigned assets and equipment are appropriately recorded, maintained, and insured in accordance with organizational requirements.

**Fleet and Transport Management - Lead Responsibility**

- Lead Country Programme fleet planning and coordinate vehicle and motorcycle utilization across Country and field offices.
- Directly supervise the drivers’/logistics assistants both at the Country Office and in the different field locations.
- Consolidate weekly movement plans and schedule vehicles and drivers for in-city and field travel in a safe, efficient and cost-effective manner.
- Maintain fleet movement and utilization tracking and ensure trip records, vehicle logbooks and movement documentation are complete.
- Coordinate preventive maintenance, repairs, annual inspection, licensing and insurance renewal for vehicles and motorcycles.
- Review fuel records, mileage, log sheets and consumption trends and prepare monthly fuel and fleet-utilization analysis.
- Coordinate driver schedules and provide technical direction on fleet procedures, road safety, vehicle care and movement controls.
- Monitor accidents, breakdowns and fleet incidents and ensure timely documentation, reporting and follow-up under applicable procedures.
- Advise the HoFA on fleet replacement, disposal, allocation, utilization and cost-control needs.

**Senior Coordination and Business Continuity**

- Provide technical guidance to the Procurement & Logistics Officer on common procurement standards, documentation and complex procurement processes when assigned by the HoFA.
- Coordinate high-value or higher-risk procurement actions assigned by the HoFA and support procurement committees with complete documentation.
- Provide reciprocal cover with the Procurement & Logistics Officer during leave, peak workload, and emergency-response periods.
- Serve as the operational focal point for safety and security matters across the Country Programme, reporting to the Head of Finance and Administration and coordinating closely with the Country Director.
- Facilitate timely communication of security information and incidents; coordinate implementation and follow-up of agreed safety and security measures.

**Minimum Qualifications, experience and skills**

**Qualifications and Experience:**

- Bachelor's degree in Procurement and Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Business Administration or related field.
- Professional procurement/supply-chain qualifications such as CIPS, or active progression toward one, are an advantage.
- Minimum of 5 years’ relevant experience in procurement, logistics or supply chain management, including practical fleet management responsibility.
- Demonstrated experience in procurement planning, sourcing, tendering, supplier management, contracts and asset/inventory management.
- Experience in an international NGO/NPO or donor-funded environment is an advantage.
- Demonstrated experience managing vehicle fleets, transport planning, maintenance, insurance, fuel controls and driver coordination.

**Skills and Capabilities**

- Strong knowledge of procurement processes, sourcing strategies, vendor management, and compliance controls.
- Excellent negotiation, communication, and interpersonal skills.
- Strong analytical and organizational skills with attention to documentation accuracy.
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively under pressure.
- Good IT skills, including Microsoft Office and procurement/logistics tracking tools.
- Ability to ensure internal and external stakeholders understand and follow HEKS/EPER procedures and guidelines.
- High integrity, diligence, and professional judgement.
- Available for frequent local and national travel.
- Professional, cooperative, efficient, and service-oriented working attitude.

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer (COO)
jobs.description:
SwSS is seeking an experienced, dynamic and results-oriented Chief Operating Officer (COO) with a strong background in international development and donor-funded programme management to support the Executive Director in the overall management, coordination and performance of the institution.

The COO will provide institution-wide operational and management leadership, ensuring effective implementation of SwSS's strategy and multiple donor-funded projects across different sectors and locations, efficient day-to-day operations and strong coordination and accountability across Head Office and field locations.

A key focus of the role will be ensuring that projects deliver agreed results within approved plans, budgets and timelines, and that programme, operational and financial functions provide timely, accurate and complete information and inputs required for donor reporting and compliance, working in close coordination with the Fundraising Director.

**Key Responsibilities**

The COO will:

• Drive implementation of SwSS's strategy, annual plans, projects and Board-approved priorities.

• Oversee project implementation across all locations against agreed plans, budgets, timelines and deliverables.

• Oversee day-to-day operations and general administration across Head Office and field locations.

• Provide management oversight of finance, HR, administration, procurement, logistics, assets and other support functions.

• Ensure timely provision and coordination of accurate and complete programme, operational and financial inputs required for donor reporting and compliance, and ensure that operational or implementation issues affecting donor commitments are promptly addressed.

• Strengthen coordination, staff accountability and organizational performance across Juba and field locations.

• Oversee financial and resource management, organizational risks, internal controls and regulatory compliance.

• Monitor implementation of Board, management and audit actions.

• Provide the Executive Director with timely information and advice on project implementation, finances, operations, staffing, risks and organizational performance.

• Support the Fundraising Director in donor engagement and resource mobilization by ensuring the timely availability of reliable programme, operational and financial information.

**Qualifications & Experience**

Candidates should have:

• At least a bachelor’s degree in Management, Business Administration, International Development, Development Studies, Public Administration, Finance or a related field. A relevant Master's degree or postgraduate qualification in international development, project/programme management, organizational management, finance or a related discipline is highly desirable. Recognized professional qualifications in project/programme management or equivalent demonstrated expertise would be an advantage.

• At least 9 years of relevant professional experience, including at least 6 years in a senior management or leadership role, with substantial experience in international development cooperation and preferably within an international NGO, faith-based organization or comparable donor-funded organization.

• Demonstrated experience in managing or providing senior oversight of multiple donor-funded projects/programmes simultaneously, preferably across different sectors and/or geographical locations.

• Strong knowledge of Project Cycle Management (PCM), including project planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation and reporting, with familiarity with Logical Framework Approach, results-based management, indicators and monitoring frameworks.

• Strong experience with donor-funded programmes and a solid understanding of institutional donor requirements, donor reporting, grant compliance, budgeting, financial oversight and the operational and financial management of restricted funding.

• Proven experience managing multidisciplinary teams and coordinating operations across multiple locations.

• Strong leadership, analytical, communication, problem-solving and stakeholder-management skills.

• Good understanding of governance, internal controls, risk management and regulatory compliance.

• Demonstrated experience coordinating programme, finance, HR, procurement, logistics and administrative functions in support of effective project implementation

• Experience operating in complex, fragile or resource-constrained environments, preferably in Sub-Saharan Africa; experience in South Sudan or the wider East African region would be a strong advantage.

• Demonstrated ability to translate organizational strategy into operational plans, clear responsibilities, timelines, performance indicators and measurable results.

• Strong experience in organizational change, capacity strengthening and the implementation of improved management systems and accountability mechanisms.

jobs.title: ER Doctor for international humanitarian missions
jobs.description:
**Médicos Sin Fronteras en México A.C.**

**Seeks**

## **ER Doctor**

## for International Humanitarian Missions

To join our team in International Projects

(Minimum availability of 6 months)

### **\*\*\* Please upload your CV and motivation letter in English \*\*\***

**THIS JOB PROFILE IS IN ENGLISH SINCE THIS IS THE REQUIRED LANGUAGE FOR THE JOB**

**OBJECTIVE OF THE POSITION**

The emergency doctor supervises the operation of the Emergency Service, from the admission to the discharge of the patients, according to the objectives of the project and in relation to the other services of the hospital.

As an ER physician, you are responsible for providing the best medical care to the patient and are involved in the triage system, patient flow, and protocol implementation.

It guarantees the training and supervision of national personnel. For the purposes of knowledge transfer, the training consists of both theoretical and head training to ensure a gradual transfer of responsibilities.

Prescribe the necessary treatment following MSF protocols, deciding in collaboration with other doctors whether patients should be discharged or transferred to other departments, and informing their families about the patient's progress.

- Participate in the collection and analysis of epistemological data, verifying the validity and informing the person in charge or coordinator of the field about any problem or complication in the patient's illness, or medical error. Controls the proper functioning of the department, equipment or material.

- Manages the team under his responsibility in accordance with MSF's HR policies and procedures, supervising its performance, organizing and planning shifts and rotations, and directly participating in emergencies or calls if necessary.

**PROFILE**

**Education and formation**

**Experience**

- **Essential**: Spanish (C1 or higher level)

- People Management and Development
- Commitment to MSF Principles
- Behavioral Flexibility
- Results and Quality Orientation
- Teamwork and Cooperation
- Planning and Organizing
- Cross-cultural Awareness
- Stress Management

**POSITION CONDITIONS**

Private insurance coverage that includes medical coverage and hospital, temporary disability and life insurance. The organization also has an arranged medical evacuation if necessary. Other expenses such as transportation, visas, transfer to the country of destination and Displacements in the field will also be covered by MSF.
