jobs.company: Plan International Latin America and the Caribbean
jobs.description:
**The Organisation**

Plan International is an independent development and humanitarian organisation that advances children’s rights and equality for girls. We believe in the power and potential of every child but know this is often suppressed by poverty, violence, exclusion and discrimination. And it is girls who are most affected.

Working together with children, young people, supporters and partners, we strive for a just world, tackling the root causes of the challenges girls and vulnerable children face. We support children’s rights from birth until they reach adulthood and we enable children to prepare for and respond to crises and adversity. We drive changes in practice and policy at local, national and global levels using our reach, experience and knowledge.

For over 85 years, we have rallied other determined optimists to transform the lives of all children in more than 80 countries.

We won’t stop until we are all equal.

Position: Regional Child Protection in Humanitarian Action (CPHA) Specialist

Reports to: Regional Head of Humanitarian Preparedness and Response. Technical supervised by the Global Hub CPHA Unit.

Functional Area: Programs/Humanitarian

Location: Based in any of the countries covered by the Plan Regional Office of the Americas (ROAH), with frequent travel to Cluster/Country Offices and other countries within the Region, and eventually outside the region.

Elegible countries are: Paraguay, Peru, Ecuador, Colombia, Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, the Dominican Republic, Mexico.

Start date: October 2026

Level: 16

Contract duration: Initial contract duration 8 months

Local contract (based on the salary scale of the Country).

ROLE PURPOSE

Plan International is an independent child rights and humanitarian organisation committed to children living a life free of poverty, violence and injustice. Our purpose is to strive for a just world that advances children’s rights and equality for girls. We have been building powerful partnerships for children for more than 80 years and are now active in more than 70 countries.

Plan International has committed in our global strategy with increased humanitarian ambition to scaling up humanitarian action, including in the Americas. At the heart of humanitarian action lies a simple yet powerful purpose: saving lives and alleviating human suffering. This is guided by the four humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence, that encourages humanity to provide vital humanitarian assistance to those in urgent need, no matter who they are or where they are. Crises and emergencies provide an opportunity to call on humanitarian actors, including governments, donors and other agencies, to respond effectively to the needs and rights of all children. The specific needs of girls, boys, and civilians are critical and humanitarian advocacy is also essential in helping to better support them.

The Regional Child Protection in Humanitarian Action (CPHA) Advisor will lead and provide strategic guidance on child protection initiatives in emergencies across the Countries in Latin America and the Caribbean. This role focuses on enhancing the quality and impact of CPHA programming through technical support, coordination with local and international stakeholders, humanitarian advocacy for children’s rights in crises, and strategic leadership in response to emergencies within the region of Americas.

This role is critical in Plan’s ability to influence as a humanitarian organisation, strengthen our humanitarian profile, liaise with humanitarian peers, and mobilize support to better meet the needs of crisis-affected children in the Americas.

## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

### **1. Leadership and Strategy**

### **· Provide strategic direction and coordination for the development and implementation of Child Protection in Humanitarian Action (CPHA) programs across the region.**

### **· Design and lead the CPHA regional program portfolio, ensuring alignment with broader global strategies.**

### **· Oversee the quality of regional CPHA responses and ensure their adherence to global standards and best practices.**

### **· Support Country Office child protection needs assessments and the development of tailored interventions in CPHA.**

### **· Deploy to support Country Offices within the region in CPHA.**

### **2. Advocacy and External Relations**

### **· Identify and represent Plan International in key regional and global CPHA spaces (e.g. UN, Clusters, HCTs, donors, peer agencies).**

### **· Help to lead and organize peers at other humanitarian organisations on shared influencing efforts.**

### **· Build and maintain relationships with regional agencies, donors, UN bodies, NGOs, and other stakeholders.**

### **· Engage with donors and UN agencies to support strategic alliances, particularly with regional staff across the Americas.**

### **· Participate, if requested by the Regional Head of Humanitarian Preparedness and Response, in regional and global humanitarian and advocacy working groups (e.g. R4V, REDLAC, LAC RMD Coalition).**

### **· Lead advocacy efforts to elevate the visibility and impact of Child Protection in Humanitarian Action (CPHA) programs within the region as well as the situation of children in crises throughout the Americas.**

### **· Liaise regularly with the Global Humanitarian Policy, Advocacy, and Diplomacy Unit to build a region-specific humanitarian advocacy strategy and undertake actions.**

### **· Maintain regular, ongoing coordination with Country Offices to support context-specific advocacy and policy work on the situation of children.**

### **· Define key humanitarian advocacy opportunities and targets at national and regional levels and mobilize international advocacy support for these**

### **· Assist Country Offices in advocacy planning, including stakeholder mapping and contextual analysis.**

### **· Support operational research, document good practices and develop policy briefs and advocacy documents.**

### **· Support in compiling and systematizing evidence and stories from the region to support advocacy and public engagement regarding the situation of children and girls.**

### **· Oversee regular child protection monitoring is conducted at country office level, collate and compile findings, produce and disseminate analysis reports on the needs and vulnerabilities of children affected by crises, with a focus on girls.**

### **3. Resource Mobilization and Program Management**

### **· Support Country Offices in developing proposals and securing funding for CPiE initiatives and the mainstreaming of CPiE in multisectoral initiatives.**

### **· Co-design project proposals for regional initiatives, ensuring they meet strategic goals and leverage local insights.**

### **· Oversee the implementation of CPHA programs, ensuring quality control, adherence to timelines and budgets.**

### **· Identify and develop multi-country initiatives and represent the organization in key cluster and sub-regional meetings and events.**

### **4. Capacity Building and Technical Support**

### **· Provide ongoing training, coaching, and mentorship to country program staff and partners on CPHA.**

### **· Ensure the implementation of CPHA guidance and tools tailored to the context of each country within the region.**

### **· Promote knowledge sharing and learning across the region through regular meetings and forums.**

### **5. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning**

### **· Establish robust monitoring and evaluation frameworks to measure program effectiveness and impact at regional level.**

### **· Lead the global and regional evidence collection initiatives and provide analysis on data collected.**

### **· Ensure that learning from CPHA programming is captured, documented, and disseminated across the organization.**

### **· Use data and evidence to inform and adjust program strategies and interventions.**

### **6. Safeguarding**

### **· Ensures that Plan International’s global policies for Safeguarding Children and Young People and Gender Equality and Inclusion are fully embedded in accordance with the principles and requirements of the policy including relevant Implementation Standards and Guidelines as applicable to their area of responsibility. This includes, but is not limited to, ensuring staff and associates are aware of and understand their responsibilities under these policies and Plan International’s Code of Conduct (CoC), their relevance to their area of work, and that concerns are reported and managed in accordance with the appropriate procedures.**

## QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE:

- Master’s degree in Social Work, Social Sciences, International Development, or a related field.
- Minimum of 5 years of professional experience in Child Protection in Humanitarian action, with at least 3 years in a leadership role.
- Proven experience in program development, team management, and capacity building in diverse and complex settings.
- Experience in humanitarian affairs or related advocacy and representation
- Strong understanding of the humanitarian landscape and child protection standards in the America’s context.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with **fluency in Spanish and proficiency in English**, French is desirable.

## PHYSICAL ENVIRONMENT AND DEMANDS:

- Position may be based in any of the countries with frequent travel to program sites and other countries within the region and eventually outside the region if requested by the Regional Head of Humanitarian Preparedness and Response.
- The position will be working at home when it is not traveling to the offices.
- Foreseen travel requirement: 60%.

## PLAN INTERNATIONAL VALUES AND LEADERSHIP BEHAVIORS

### **We work to achieve a lasting impact**

- I express a clear purpose to staff and set high expectations for our work and its impact.
- I create a climate of continuous improvement, open to challenges and new ideas
- I focus resources to drive changes in practices and policies at local, national and global levels to maximize our long-term impact, responding quickly to changing needs, new priorities or crises.
- I use evidence from inside and outside the organization to understand the root causes of problems, make informed decisions, and evaluate their effectiveness.

### **We are open and accountable**

- I practice and promote a culture of openness and transparency within my work team and beyond, including with our sponsors and donors.
- I hold myself and others accountable for achieving the highest standards of integrity, especially in our use of resources.
- I am consistent and fair in the way I treat people
- I expect myself and others to be open about mistakes and to learn from them.

### **Together we do it well**

- I look for constructive results in discussions. I challenge assumptions, but I listen to others and am willing to compromise when it is beneficial for progress
- I develop constructive relationships across Plan International to support our common goals, even if this requires me to adjust my own team's priorities.
- I develop trusting and mutually beneficial relationships with financiers, partners and communities, creating solutions together to meet our goals and support others in achieving theirs.
- I engage with and challenge civil society and governments to build a better world for girls and children in general.

### **We are inclusive and empowering**

- I actively promote diversity, gender equality and inclusion, within and outside Plan International
- I humbly listen to others and support the people I work with to participate in decisions, assume greater responsibilities and develop their potential.
- I influence civil society and governments to prioritize achieving equality for girls, ensuring children's rights and the safe and successful progression of young people into adulthood.
- I foster a climate that empowers children and young people as agents of change in their own lives.
- I will not tolerate any form of bullying, abuse or discrimination in the workplace

## LEVEL OF CONTACT WITH CHILDREN:

- High level: The role involves direct interaction with children and young individuals, requiring the highest standards of child safeguard.

**Location: Paraguay, Peru, Ecuador, Colombia, Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, the Dominican Republic, or Mexico.**

**Type of Role: Specialist**

**Reports to: Regional Head of Humanitarian Preparedness and Response**

**Contract type: Local fixed-term contract**

**Grade: 16**

**Closing Date: 16 October 2026**

*Equality, diversity and inclusion is at the very heart of everything that Plan International stands for.*

*We want Plan International to reflect the diversity of the communities we work with, offering equal opportunities to everyone regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation.*

*Plan International is based on a culture of inclusivity and we strive to create a workplace environment that ensures every team, in every office, in every country, is rich in diverse people, thoughts, and ideas.*

*We foster an organisational culture that embraces our commitment to racial justice, gender equality, girls’ rights and inclusion.*

*Plan International believes that in a world where children face so many threats of harm, it is our duty to ensure that we, as an organisation, do everything we can to keep children safe. This means that we have particular responsibilities to children that we come into contact with and we must not contribute in any way to harming or placing children at risk.*

*A range of pre-employment checks will be undertaken in conformity with Plan International's Safeguarding Children and Young People policy. Plan International also participates in the* [*Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme.*](https://www.schr.info/the-misconduct-disclosure-scheme) *In line with this scheme we will request information from applicants previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.*

**Location:** Marseille
**Contract:** 6-month contract – maternity leave replacement

**SOS MEDITERRANEE** is a civil European rescue association founded in 2015 to face the humanitarian tragedy and the lack of adequate state rescue capacity in the Mediterranean on the deadliest maritime migratory route in the world since 2014. Created by a group of European citizens, our maritime and humanitarian organisation has three missions:

1. To rescue people in distress at sea.
2. To protect and assist survivors on board our ship.
3. To bear witness and raise awareness about the tragedy unfolding in the central Mediterranean.

Today, **SOS MEDITERRANEE** is a network composed of four European entities (Germany, France, Italy, Switzerland) sharing the objective to support our rescue operations at sea. Search and Rescue (SAR) operations have been carried out since February 2016 in the Central Mediterranean off the Libyan coasts with the chartered ships Aquarius and Ocean Viking. To date, over 43.000 people have been rescued by SOS MEDITERRANEE.

## **Context**

SOS MEDITERRANEE is recruiting a Head of Operational Human Resources to provide partial cover during a maternity leave.

The Operations department operates in a demanding international environment, with specific HR challenges linked to maritime rescue activities, crew management and rotations, and the need to balance operational requirements with staff wellbeing and working conditions.

SOS MEDITERRANEE is currently reorganising its support functions to bring together HR activities under a shared HR department. As this process is ongoing, the scope and responsibilities of the position may evolve during the contract. These potential changes will be discussed and clarified throughout the recruitment process.

We are therefore looking for someone who is comfortable working in a changing environment, able to contribute constructively to this organizational transition.

## **About the position**

As Head of Operational Human Resources, you will oversee HR activities within SOS MEDITERRANEE's Operations department, ensuring that HR policies, processes and practices meet the specific needs of the operations department while remaining consistent with the organisation's overall HR framework.

Reporting to the HR Director and working in close collaboration with the Director of Operations and the Operations leadership team, you will contribute to the HR strategy and priorities, oversee their implementation and support managers in addressing HR challenges.

You will manage a multidisciplinary team covering HR, Crewing, and Staff Care activities, ensuring effective coordination between these functions and the operational teams.

The role combines **strategic HR management, operational oversight, support to managers, team leadership and organisational development**, with particular attention to working conditions, staff wellbeing and the challenges of an evolving operational environment.

## **Main responsibilities**

**HR strategy and organisational development**

- Contribute to the HR strategy definition
- Implement the HR strategy and roadmap for the Operations department.
- Develop, harmonise and formalise HR policies, processes, tools and practices.
- Ensure a consistent HR framework across Operations
- Support the development and evolution of new operational activities.
- Provide advice and support to managers on organisational matters, team management, conflicts and disciplinary situations.
- Contribute to the development of recruitment, onboarding, professional development and internal mobility processes.
- Oversee personnel administration, employment contracts, payroll variables, classification and remuneration processes.
- Support social dialogue, staff representation and initiatives related to health, safety, quality of life at work and psychosocial risk prevention.

**HR compliance and risk management**

- Ensure compliance of HR practices with applicable employment legislation and organisational policies.
- Maintain an active legal watch on employment law.
- Monitor HR-related risks and ensure that alerts are appropriately escalated.
- Contribute to investigations and the implementation of appropriate follow-up actions.

**Budget Management**

- Lead the development and monitor the HR budget for Operations.
- Contribute to budget revisions.

**Team management**

You will directly supervise a small multidisciplinary team covering HR, Crewing, and staff care activities. You will:

- Set objectives and support the professional development of team members.
- Ensure effective workload distribution and a positive working environment.
- Provide leadership, guidance and regular feedback.
- Support recruitment and onboarding within the team.

## **PROFILE SOUGHT**

**Experience & qualifications**

- Master’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration or a related field.
- At least **7 years of professional experience in Human Resources**, including at least **3 years in a managerial position**.
- Solid experience in developing and implementing HR policies, processes and tools.
- Good knowledge of employment law, job classification and remuneration frameworks.
- Previous experience in a humanitarian NGO is required.
- Experience in budget management is an asset.
- Experience in project management is a plus.

**Skills & competencies**

We are looking for someone who combines strategic thinking with a strong ability to operate in a complex and changing environment. You should demonstrate:

- Strong organisational and analytical skills.
- Autonomy, adaptability and a sense of initiative.
- Leadership and the ability to motivate and develop a team.
- Strong communication, negotiation and conflict-resolution skills.
- Ability to make decisions while maintaining perspective and sound judgement.
- Rigor, discretion and confidentiality.
- Ability to analyse, synthesise and formalise information.
- Ability to work collaboratively with different teams and stakeholders.
- Strong interpersonal skills, including active listening and non-violent communication.

**Languages & IT**

- Fluent **French and English**, both written and spoken.
- Excellent command of standard office tools, including MS Office and Excel.
- Experience with HR Information Systems (HRIS).

## **Conditions:**

- Starting date: Mid December 2026
- Fixed term French contract of 6 months, extendable according to the date of return of the employee on the job
- Salary: From 3 450€ to 4000€ gross/month
- Food vouchers, complementary health insurance taken in charge at 100% by the employer
- 25 annual leaves per year and 15 days of additional rest days (pro-ratized to the contract duration)

jobs.title: Institutional Reform Technical Expert - OMSAR
jobs.description:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

- Organization: UNDP Lebanon Through Stars Orbit Consultants and Management Development
- VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/191
- Position Title: Institutional Reform Technical Expert - OMSAR
- Duty Station: OMSAR- Beirut, Republic of Lebanon
- Duration: 2 months (without exceeding 6 working days per month)
- Vacancy Date of Issue: 11 October 2026
- Vacancy Closure Date: 17 October 2026
- National or International consultancy: National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1t2Ibj5TkGDZnczHtD0zST_vA0rLG-ss8/view](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1t2Ibj5TkGDZnczHtD0zST_vA0rLG-ss8/view)

**BACKGROUND**

For over six years, Lebanon has been facing a prolonged economic, financial, and social crisis. The country experienced multiple shocks, including economic and financial collapse, the COVID-19 pandemic, the Beirut Port explosion, and, most recently, more than a year-long armed conflict that caused extensive damage and losses. These developments led to a severe economic contraction, depreciation of the Lebanese Pound, soaring inflation, fiscal imbalances, and a sharp decline in the real value of income, particularly affecting public sector employees. As a result, state institutions have been struggling to deliver on their mandates due to a lack of financial resources and a significant loss of skilled professionals in the public sector. Against this backdrop, the capacity for evidence-based policymaking, regulation, and the delivery of priorities has been severely constrained by the crises.

While the election of a president and formation of a new government mark a positive political turning point, the state continues to face major resource and capacity constraints in responding to the crisis, supporting post-conflict recovery, and addressing structural challenges. At the same time, there is limited visibility over development aid directed to Lebanon. Since the 2019 collapse, most donors have made funding conditional on broad reforms and progress toward an IMF agreement. As a result, only a small share of aid has been channeled through government systems. Most grants and loans remain off-budget, creating a disconnect between aid inflows and national public finance management.

To address the implications of these crises, UNDP has been supporting the Government of Lebanon (GoL) in restoring core functions and in resuming its role in service delivery, and to help in implementing priority reforms, while linking traditional public administration, civil service, and policy reforms with a digital transformation process, with the ultimate aim of reactivating the social contract.

In response, the Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform (OMSAR) has launched “Reinventing Government 2030,” which represents one of Lebanon’s most ambitious efforts to modernize the State and rebuild citizens’ trust in public institutions. The reform vision is structured across three phases:

**Phase 1: Stakeholder Aspirations (Listen, Analyze, Prepare)**

OMSAR engaged thousands of stakeholders—citizens, youth, diaspora, civil servants, municipalities, civil society, unions, media, political and religious leaders—through surveys, workshops, town halls, and interviews. This participatory phase has produced a unified vision and validated national reform aspirations.

**Phase 2: Blueprint Design for Government Restructuring**

This phase aims to reorganize ministries and public agencies by:

1. Redefining mandates;
2. Eliminating fragmentation and duplicated functions;
3. Designing a Target Operating Model (TOM) tailored to Lebanon;
4. Benchmarking against global governance models;
5. Ensuring alignment with stakeholder aspirations and future state needs.

**Phase 3: Full Implementation (2026–2030)**

Execution of the restructuring plan, introduction of digital and process reforms, reskilling of human capital, and establishing performance-based management across government.

After completion of Phase 1, OMSAR has launched Phase 2 of the Reform. Central to this phase is the Baseline Assessment of the current state of affairs of GoL. The Reform’s design is manifested in the Conceptual Framework, which provides a basic outline for the Baseline Assessment. It envisages functional analysis of the Government of Lebanon along horizontal and vertical axes.

The horizontal axis establishes four universal Functions of the Government:

1. National Directions and Policy Setting;
2. Licensing and Regulation;
3. Service Delivery;
4. Delivery Oversight and Surveillance.

The vertical axis provides thematic or area classification of the governance model. In particular, it identified a number of sectors that could reach 28 sectors and around 120 subsectors.

Following several rounds of consultations with OMSAR, UNDP Lebanon has developed and validated a methodology for the Baseline Assessment in line with the priorities enshrined in the Conceptual Framework.

The methodology is based on a rigorous research design that ensures data is collected from multiple sources. In total, it includes four research methods. Each method is designed to build upon the previous one, moving from theoretical mandates to operational realities:

- Desk Research
- Survey
- Key Informant Interviews (KIIs)
- Focus Groups/Validation Workshops

To this end, UNDP seeks to recruit a national Institutional Reform Expert to support the validation and quality assurance of the cluster, sector and entity-level mapping of the governance architecture of the Government of Lebanon (GoL).

The overall objective of this consultancy is to conduct a rigorous functional and institutional review of each subsector/functionality, benchmarked against the GOFOC methodology (Policy Development and Coherence, Regulation and Licensing, Oversight, Service Delivery). This includes validating the existing cluster and sector mapping, cross-checking entity-level mandates to identify structural redundancies, overlaps, gaps and "institutional silos," reviewing the international benchmark underpinning the Target Operating Model, and coordinating with ministries' focal points and stakeholders to confirm findings and secure sign-off.

Ultimately, this work will provide the evidence-based data required to streamline institutional mandates and business processes, informing the next phases of Lebanon's "Reinventing Government 2030" national transformation agenda.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the general supervision of the UNDP Senior Economist and LPARD-P Project Manager, and in close coordination with OMSAR, the Institutional Reform Technical Expert will be tasked with performing a comprehensive functional and institutional governance analysis of assigned subsectors/functions.

The Institutional Reform Technical Expert will be responsible for the following:

- Review the methodology and outputs of the cluster and sector mapping for the sectors of Finance, Education, Social Affairs, Industry, and Central Bank and financial markets, and assess its completeness, consistency and logical structure.
- Validate the baseline mapping of public entities (to feed into the macro Target Operating Model) against the four identified functions (Policy Development and Coherence, Regulation and Licensing, Oversight, Service Delivery), cross-checking entity-level data, identifying inconsistencies, gaps, duplications and overlapping mandates, and maintaining a discrepancy log with proposed corrections.
- Review and validate the international benchmark used to inform the Final Target Operating Model, assessing the relevance and evidentiary basis of the comparator countries and models selected, and the robustness of the resulting recommendations on entities to abolish, merge, or reconstitute as councils or committees.
- Serve as the day-to-day technical counterpart to ministries' focal points, coordinating data validation requests, resolving discrepancies, and securing sign-off on sector-level findings relevant to each ministry.

jobs.description:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link: [https://drive.google.com/file/d/1nlIguZCIKE2oYZbDjRL0bMuJ_2ONOWEo/view](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1nlIguZCIKE2oYZbDjRL0bMuJ_2ONOWEo/view)

**BACKGROUND**

For over six years, Lebanon has been facing a prolonged economic, financial, and social crisis. The country experienced multiple shocks, including economic and financial collapse, the COVID-19 pandemic, the Beirut Port explosion, and, most recently, more than a year-long armed conflict that caused extensive damage and losses. These developments led to a severe economic contraction, depreciation of the Lebanese Pound, soaring inflation, fiscal imbalances, and a sharp decline in the real value of income, particularly affecting public sector employees. As a result, state institutions have been struggling to deliver on their mandates due to a lack of financial resources and a significant loss of skilled professionals in the public sector. Against this backdrop, the capacity for evidence-based policymaking, regulation, and the delivery of priorities has been severely constrained by the crises.

While the election of a president and formation of a new government mark a positive political turning point, the state continues to face major resource and capacity constraints in responding to the crisis, supporting post-conflict recovery, and addressing structural challenges. At the same time, there is limited visibility over development aid directed to Lebanon. Since the 2019 collapse, most donors have made funding conditional on broad reforms and progress toward an IMF agreement. As a result, only a small share of aid has been channeled through government systems. Most grants and loans remain off-budget, creating a disconnect between aid inflows and national public finance management.

To address the implications of these crises, UNDP has been supporting the Government of Lebanon (GoL) in restoring core functions and in resuming its role in service delivery, and to help in implementing priority reforms, while linking traditional public administration, civil service, and policy reforms with a digital transformation process, with the ultimate aim of reactivating the social contract.

In response, the Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Reform (OMSAR) has launched “Reinventing Government 2030,” which represents one of Lebanon’s most ambitious efforts to modernize the State and rebuild citizens’ trust in public institutions. The reform vision is structured across three phases:

**Phase 1: Stakeholder Aspirations (Listen, Analyze, Prepare)**

OMSAR engaged thousands of stakeholders—citizens, youth, diaspora, civil servants, municipalities, civil society, unions, media, political and religious leaders—through surveys, workshops, town halls, and interviews. This participatory phase has produced a unified vision and validated national reform aspirations.

**Phase 2: Blueprint Design for Government Restructuring**

This phase aims to reorganize ministries and public agencies by:

1. Redefining mandates;
2. Eliminating fragmentation and duplicated functions;
3. Designing a Target Operating Model (TOM) tailored to Lebanon;
4. Benchmarking against global governance models;
5. Ensuring alignment with stakeholder aspirations and future state needs.

**Phase 3: Full Implementation (2026–2030)**

Execution of the restructuring plan, introduction of digital and process reforms, reskilling of human capital, and establishing performance-based management across government.

After completion of Phase 1, OMSAR has launched Phase 2 of the Reform. Central to this phase is the Baseline Assessment of the current state of affairs of GoL. The Reform’s design is manifested in the Conceptual Framework, which provides a basic outline for the Baseline Assessment. It envisages functional analysis of the Government of Lebanon along horizontal and vertical axes.

The horizontal axis establishes four universal Functions of the Government:

1. National Directions and Policy Setting;
2. Licensing and Regulation;
3. Service Delivery;
4. Delivery Oversight and Surveillance.

The vertical axis provides thematic or area classification of the governance model. In particular, it identified a number of sectors that could reach 28 sectors and around 120 subsectors.

Following several rounds of consultations with OMSAR, UNDP Lebanon has developed and validated a methodology for the Baseline Assessment in line with the priorities enshrined in the Conceptual Framework.

The methodology is based on a rigorous research design that ensures data is collected from multiple sources. In total, it includes four research methods. Each method is designed to build upon the previous one, moving from theoretical mandates to operational realities:

- Desk Research
- Survey
- Key Informant Interviews (KIIs)
- Focus Groups/Validation Workshops

To this end, UNDP seeks to recruit a national Public Administration Reform Implementation Specialist to support the review, validation and refinement of priority reforms under Lebanon’s “Reinventing Government 2030” Blueprint, with a particular focus on economic governance and the Centre of Government.

The overall objective of this consultancy is to assess and strengthen the 37 Ministry of Economy and Trade (MoET) reforms covering trade, the domestic market, the business environment, investment promotion, food security and insurance, as well as the Agriculture Sector and the 7 Centre of Government reforms under the Presidency of the Council of Ministers (PCM).

This includes assessing the feasibility, sequencing and institutional implications of proposed structural changes at MoET, identifying potential institutional resistance and proposing appropriate mitigation measures, and reviewing the PCM reforms to identify required adjustments or alternative approaches. The consultancy will also support the mapping and assessment of existing councils and committees under the PCM and MoET, including recommendations on those to reactivate, merge or abolish, to ensure that proposed institutional arrangements are based on an accurate and comprehensive baseline.

Ultimately, this work will contribute to the validation and refinement of key economic governance and Centre of Government reforms, providing an evidence-based foundation for their effective implementation under Lebanon’s “Reinventing Government 2030” national transformation agenda.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the general supervision of the UNDP Senior Economist and LPARD-P Project Manager, and in close coordination with OMSAR, the Public Administration Reform Implementation Specialist will be responsible for the following:

1. **Validate the Economic Governance reforms.** Review the 37 MoET reforms, which cover trade, the domestic market, business environment, investment promotion, food security and insurance.
2. **Validate the Agriculture Sector reforms.**
3. **Advise on the proposed structural changes at MoET.** Assess the feasibility and sequencing, as well as the likely institutional resistance, and suggest mitigation measures.
4. **Review the Centre of Government reforms (PCM).** Assess the 7 PCM reforms and propose adjustments or alternatives.
5. **Map councils and committees.** Inventory the existing councils and committees under the PCM and MoET. Recommend which to reactivate, merge or abolish, so the proposed new councils build on an accurate baseline.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

The consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities within 1 month (without exceeding 3 working days per month).

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- With day-to-day management by the designated Project Manager or institutional focal point.
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely, thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will also be responsible for providing clarifications and facilitating the work.
- Day-to-day transportation from home to office (and vice versa) shall be covered by the consultant’s own means. The Consultant will rely on his own means of communication and transportation.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 1 month without exceeding 3 working days a month.

The mission is expected to commence immediately and to be completed by December 31, 2026, at the latest.

The time needed to review, complete and approve deliverables and outputs is five (5) working days.

**DUTY STATION**

The assignment is based at OMSAR- Beirut, Republic of Lebanon

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

- Education: Master’s degree or equivalent in Development Studies, Sciences, Finance, Economics, Public Administration, Public Policy, Governance, or a related field.
- Experience: At least 10 years of progressively responsible professional experience in public administration, economic governance, institutional management and/or public-sector policy, including substantial experience within the Lebanese public administration.
- Language: Fluency in the Arabic and English languages (both written and oral).

**“The Personnel will be covered with Health insurance and Personal accident insurance; the fees shall be deducted from personnel's monthly payment”**

jobs.title: Staff Auditor
jobs.description:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

Habitat for Humanity International (HFHI) is currently seeking a talented professional for the role of a Staff Auditor. The Staff Auditor will help evaluate the adequacy and effectiveness of the internal controls of various departments at HFHI's headquarters, HFHI's international area offices, and selected programs of Habitat's U.S. and international organizations.

This position will be remotely based within the US and will require 40-60% domestic and/or international travel.

**Key Responsibilities:**

- Assist with the planning, execution, and reporting on operational, financial and compliance audits in the designated areas. (20%)
- Assist in the preparation of the audit planning memo, risk-based audit programs and test plans which defines specific procedures to be performed during an audit. (5%)
- Conduct audit fieldwork work papers, findings, and recommendations for compliance with the Institute of Internal Auditor International Professional Standards and HFHI Internal Audit Department (IAD) Standards. (20%)
- Conduct peer reviews of other audit staff's audit documentation and working papers to ensure consistency, quality and compliance with internal audit standards. Provide constructive feedback to support continuous improvement. (5%)
- Draft finding and recommendations audit report in accordance with and monitor the quality of audit reports to ensure compliance with International Professional Practices Framework (IPPF) and HFHI IAD Standards. (15%)
- Document processes, procedures, and test results. (5%)
- Coordinate the monitoring of outstanding audit recommendations. (5%)
- Plan, coordinate and performing consulting and advisory services as appropriate for the organization. (5%)
- Assist in the development of the IAD annual risk-based internal audit plan. (5%)
- Lead auditor assigned to the audit projects under his/her responsibility, will provide guidance and overall review of deliverables. (10%)
- Assists the VP/Director/Manager of Internal Audit on any other duties as assigned by management of Internal Audit as needed. The above duties could include supporting other internal audit units and audit activities, such as the SOAR process, audit committee package and risk assessment process. (5%)

**Key Requirements:**

- Bachelor’s degree in business administration, Accounting, Finance, Information Technology, or a related field.
- 3-5 years of professional experience with external and internal audits, forensic accounting investigations, preferably with a public accounting firm.
- Experience with international travel and/or cross-cultural communications.
- Expert level skills with Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint, as well as a good understanding of the COSO - International Control Integrated Framework.
- Excellent English, verbal and written, communication skills.
- Strong critical thinking and project management skills.

**Preferred:**

- 3 years of domestic and international experience in internal or external audit management, preferably with a large international non-profit government, corporate organizations, or Big 4 Accounting Firm.
- Experience auditing construction activities and Micro-Finance operations.
- Proficiency with auditing software such as Galvanize HighBond or others.
- Experience using data analytics tools to create queries and trend analysis reports.
- Experience in non-profit Internal Audits, particularly executing audits of controls and transactions related to government and corporate grant requirements.
- Spanish, verbal and written, communication skills would be beneficial.

**Hiring Range:**

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance. For work locations in the US, the hiring range for this position is:

$55,600.00 USD

$82,675 USD

/

Annual

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. jobs.title: Venezuela - Gerente de Socios y Subvenciones (Nacional)
jobs.description:
## Acerca de COOPI

COOPI Cooperazione Internazionale es una ONG laica e independiente, fundada en Milán en 1965. Lleva a cabo proyectos de desarrollo para contribuir a la lucha contra las desigualdades y programas de emergencia para apoyar a las personas afectadas por desastres naturales o conflictos. Actualmente, COOPI está presente en 33 países de África, Oriente Medio, América Latina y Caribe.

Desde 2019 COOPI establece una presencia en Venezuela y, a partir de julio de 2020, inicia un programa regional que se implementa en asociación con organizaciones venezolanas y en coordinación con instituciones locales e internacionales, en el marco de los planes de respuesta vigentes. En los últimos años COOPI ha ampliado sus intervenciones y actualmente ejecuta proyectos financiados por distintos donantes en Caracas, Sucre, Delta Amacuro, Bolívar y otros estados del país, en los sectores de protección, salud, WASH, ambiente, seguridad alimentaria, fortalecimiento institucional y respuesta a emergencias.

En el marco del crecimiento y diversificación de su portafolio, COOPI Venezuela busca reforzar la gestión de subvenciones y alianzas mediante una función especializada que asegure el seguimiento contractual, la calidad y oportunidad de los procesos de reporting y formulación, y una coordinación eficaz con socios de los consorcios actuales y donantes.

## Objetivo/descripción del puesto

Bajo la supervisión de la Coordinación País y con acompañamiento funcional de la Coordinación de Programas, el/la Gerente de Socios y Subvenciones será responsable de asegurar la gestión coordinada del portafolio de subvenciones y alianzas de COOPI Venezuela, garantizando el seguimiento oportuno de obligaciones contractuales, propuestas, modificaciones, reporting y procesos de coordinación con socios.

El puesto actuará como punto focal para la planificación y seguimiento de los principales procesos de gestión de subvenciones, facilitando la coordinación entre Programas, Operaciones, Administración, MEAL, Jefes/as de Proyecto, socios, Coordinación Regional y Sede.

Asimismo, apoyará en la coordinación institucional y contractual del Consorcio ÍNTEGRAS y de futuras alianzas o consorcios en los que COOPI ejerza funciones de liderazgo, adaptando el nivel de coordinación a la complejidad y características de cada alianza.

La posición se coordinará estrechamente con Programas, los equipos de proyecto y Administración País, articulando sus respectivos aportes para asegurar una gestión coherente, oportuna y alineada con los compromisos asumidos con donantes y socios.

**Áreas de responsabilidad**

**Gestión del portafolio de subvenciones:**

- Mantener actualizado un calendario consolidado de obligaciones contractuales, reportes, modificaciones, auditorías, entregables y principales hitos de todos los proyectos de la misión.
- Dar seguimiento a los plazos y responsabilidades asociados a cada subvención, alertando con suficiente anticipación sobre entregables y riesgos de incumplimiento.
- Asegurar la adecuada circulación de información entre Jefes/as de Proyecto, Programas, Operaciones, Administración, MEAL, Coordinación País, Región y Sede.
- Mantener organizados y accesibles los principales documentos contractuales, versiones aprobadas, modificaciones, comunicaciones con donantes y documentación relevante para la gestión de cada subvención.
- Apoyar la interpretación y difusión interna de requisitos contractuales y lineamientos de los donantes.
- Identificar oportunamente riesgos de cumplimiento, reporting o gestión contractual y escalarlos a las funciones responsables.

**Reporting y seguimiento contractual:**

- Coordinar el calendario y proceso de preparación de informes narrativos intermedios y finales.
- Solicitar y consolidar los aportes de Jefes/as de Proyecto, equipos técnicos, MEAL, Administración y socios.
- Revisar la coherencia, integridad y consistencia de los informes antes de su validación por Programas y Coordinación País.
- Asegurar la coherencia entre información narrativa, indicadores, ejecución operativa y datos financieros, en coordinación con las áreas responsables.
- Dar seguimiento a comentarios y solicitudes de aclaración de donantes hasta su cierre.
- Mantener control de versiones y trazabilidad de los principales documentos enviados y aprobados.
- Coordinar la revisión y consolidación de informes y otros entregables, articulando la validación técnica con Programas y los equipos técnicos, y la validación financiera con Administración País.

**Formulación y modificaciones de proyectos:**

- Coordinar, en estrecha articulación con Coordinación País y Programas, los procesos de preparación de nuevas propuestas, notas conceptuales y expresiones de interés.
- Establecer cronogramas de formulación, distribuir responsabilidades y asegurar la entrega oportuna de los distintos componentes.
- Consolidar los aportes de Programas, MEAL, Administración, Operaciones, equipos de proyecto y socios.
- Asegurar la coherencia entre narrativa, marco lógico, indicadores, cronograma, plan operativo y presupuesto.
- Coordinar los procesos de modificación contractual, extensiones, realineamientos, adendas y reprogramaciones.
- Preparar o consolidar las justificaciones y documentación requerida por donantes.
- Mantener actualizada la información sobre oportunidades de financiación y apoyar a Coordinación País y Programas en la planificación del pipeline de propuestas.
- Apoyar la formulación de nuevas propuestas a partir de las prioridades estratégicas y orientaciones técnicas definidas por Coordinación País y Programas, asegurando su adecuada traducción en los documentos de proyecto.

**Gestión de socios y alianzas:**
- Mantener una visión consolidada de los socios institucionales, co-solicitantes, co-partners y organizaciones implementadoras vinculadas a los proyectos de COOPI.
- Facilitar la coordinación contractual y documental con socios durante formulación, implementación, reporting y cierre.
- Dar seguimiento a acuerdos de partnership, calendarios de reporting y otras obligaciones de los socios, en coordinación con Administración y los responsables de proyecto.
- Facilitar procesos de due diligence, documentación institucional y seguimiento de capacidades cuando corresponda.
- Identificar dificultades recurrentes en la gestión de alianzas y proponer medidas de mejora.
- Contribuir al fortalecimiento de herramientas y procedimientos internos de COOPI para la gestión de socios.
- Coordinar con los/las Jefes/as de Proyecto el seguimiento de los socios implementadores en los aspectos contractuales, documentales y de reporting, articulando los requerimientos del grant con la gestión operativa del proyecto.

**Apoyo a consorcios y alianzas:**

- Apoyar la gestión de consorcios y alianzas en los aspectos vinculados a grants, reporting, propuestas, modificaciones y obligaciones contractuales.
- Facilitar la consolidación de aportes de socios y equipos internos para propuestas, informes y otros entregables conjuntos.
- Dar seguimiento a compromisos, plazos y requerimientos documentales vinculados a subvenciones gestionadas en consorcio.
- Apoyar, junto con Coordinación País y Programas, los procesos de formulación y gestión contractual con donantes y socios.

**Coordinación interna y calidad de la gestión de subvenciones:**

- Trabajar estrechamente con Programas para asegurar la coherencia técnica y programática de propuestas, modificaciones e informes.
- Coordinar con Operaciones y los equipos de proyecto el seguimiento de avances, hitos y riesgos de implementación relevantes para las obligaciones contractuales.
- Coordinar con Administración la preparación de presupuestos, modificaciones financieras, informes y seguimiento de requisitos administrativos.
- Coordinar con MEAL la disponibilidad y consistencia de indicadores, medios de verificación y resultados reportados.
- Promover herramientas comunes para calendarios, reporting, seguimiento contractual y archivo.
- Facilitar reuniones de lanzamiento, revisión y cierre de subvenciones cuando resulte necesario.
- Contribuir a identificar aprendizajes y mejoras en los procesos de gestión de subvenciones de la misión.

**Relación con donantes y representación:**

- Mantener, por delegación de la Coordinación País, comunicación operativa con donantes sobre reporting, modificaciones, aclaraciones y procesos contractuales.
- Apoyar en la preparación de reuniones, revisiones y visitas de donantes asegurando la disponibilidad y coherencia de la información requerida.
- Apoyar a Coordinación País y Programas en reuniones de seguimiento, negociación y diseño de nuevas intervenciones.
- Representar a COOPI en espacios relacionados con gestión de subvenciones y partnerships cuando sea requerido.

**Actividades complementarias:**

- Promover el cumplimiento de las políticas, procedimientos y Código Ético de COOPI.
- Contribuir a un ambiente de trabajo colaborativo y a una comunicación fluida entre departamentos.
- Apoyar el fortalecimiento de capacidades de equipos y socios en gestión de subvenciones, reporting y requisitos de donantes.
- Ejecutar aquellas tareas inherentes al puesto y que sean solicitadas por la Coordinación País, según contexto y necesidades de la intervención.

## Perfil deseado

Profesional con experiencia sólida en gestión de subvenciones, formulación de propuestas, reporting y gestión de alianzas en organizaciones humanitarias o de cooperación internacional. Se busca un perfil altamente organizado, con capacidad para manejar simultáneamente distintos donantes, proyectos y plazos, coordinar aportes de múltiples departamentos y socios y producir documentos de elevada calidad.

### ESENCIALES

- Título universitario en Cooperación Internacional, Relaciones Internacionales, Ciencias Sociales, Administración, Economía, Derecho o áreas relacionadas.
- Al menos 5 años de experiencia relevante en cooperación internacional o acción humanitaria, incluyendo experiencia demostrable en gestión de subvenciones con donantes institucionales.
- Experiencia en formulación de propuestas, notas conceptuales, marcos lógicos, modificaciones contractuales y preparación/consolidación de informes narrativos.
- Conocimiento de procedimientos y requisitos de donantes institucionales, particularmente Unión Europea/ECHO y/o agencias de Naciones Unidas.
- Experiencia en trabajo con consorcios, alianzas y socios implementadores, incluyendo seguimiento de compromisos, reporting y coordinación documental.
- Capacidad para coordinar procesos complejos con múltiples actores, áreas y plazos simultáneos, asegurando coherencia entre componentes programáticos, operativos y financieros.
- Excelentes capacidades de redacción, análisis, síntesis y atención al detalle, manteniendo al mismo tiempo una visión global de los procesos.
- Alta capacidad de organización, planificación y priorización, con orientación a resultados y cumplimiento de plazos.
- Excelentes habilidades de comunicación, trabajo en equipo y coordinación transversal, con capacidad para facilitar acuerdos y mantener relaciones de trabajo constructivas con equipos internos, socios y donantes.
- Empatía, escucha activa, flexibilidad y adaptabilidad, especialmente en contextos de trabajo exigentes y con prioridades cambiantes.
- Autonomía, proactividad y capacidad para trabajar bajo presión y gestionar varios procesos concurrentes manteniendo rigor y calidad.
- Dominio del español e inglés oral y escrito.
- Buen manejo de herramientas de Microsoft Office.
- Compromiso con los principios, Código Ético y políticas institucionales de COOPI.
- Nacionalidad venezolana o permiso de residencia en el país.

### DESEABLES

- Experiencia con AICS, Unión Europea/INTPA, OIM, UNICEF u otras agencias de Naciones Unidas.
- Experiencia en due diligence y gestión de acuerdos con socios locales.
- Experiencia previa con COOPI.

jobs.title: Venezuela - Coordinador/a de Operaciones (National)
jobs.description:
## Acerca de COOPI

COOPI Cooperazione Internazionale es una ONG laica e independiente, fundada en Milán en 1965. Lleva a cabo proyectos de desarrollo para contribuir a la lucha contra las desigualdades y programas de emergencia para apoyar a las personas afectadas por desastres naturales o conflictos. Actualmente, COOPI está presente en 33 países de África, Oriente Medio, América Latina y Caribe.

Desde 2019 COOPI establece una presencia en Venezuela y, a partir de julio de 2020, inicia un programa regional que se implementa en asociación con organizaciones venezolanas y en coordinación con instituciones locales e internacionales, en el marco de los planes de respuesta vigentes. En los últimos años COOPI ha ampliado sus intervenciones y actualmente ejecuta proyectos con diferentes donantes en Caracas, Sucre, Delta Amacuro y Bolívar, en protección, salud sexual y reproductiva, WASH (agua, saneamiento e higiene), alimentación escolar, ambiente y fortalecimiento institucional.

Tras los sismos ocurridos el 24 de junio de 2026, COOPI en Venezuela ha ampliado adicionalmente su cartera de intervenciones mediante proyectos de respuesta a la emergencia.

## Objetivo/descripción del puesto

Bajo la supervisión directa de la Coordinación País, el/la Coordinador/a de Operaciones será responsable de supervisar y acompañar la implementación operativa del portafolio de proyectos de COOPI en Venezuela, asegurando el cumplimiento de planes de trabajo, cronogramas, presupuestos y compromisos operativos.

Acompañará a los/las Jefes/as o Gerentes de Proyecto en la gestión de sus proyectos, facilitando el seguimiento de la ejecución, el fortalecimiento de sus capacidades y la resolución oportuna de bloqueos y desviaciones.

Trabajará en estrecha coordinación con Programas, Administración, Logística, MEAL, RRHH, Coordinaciones de Base y otras funciones de la misión, respetando los ámbitos de responsabilidad técnica y funcional de cada departamento.

La función estará principalmente orientada a la gestión y ejecución de proyectos, sin sustituir las responsabilidades de las Coordinaciones de Base en la gestión territorial de las oficinas y servicios de soporte, ni las responsabilidades técnicas y programáticas de la Coordinación de Programas.

El puesto buscará reforzar la autonomía y capacidad de gestión de los/las responsables de proyecto, proporcionando acompañamiento y soporte proporcional a las necesidades y experiencia de cada perfil. Se priorizarán perfiles nacionales.

**Áreas de responsabilidad**

**1. Supervisión de la implementación de proyectos**

- Acompañar y dar seguimiento a los/las Jefes/as y Gerentes de Proyecto en la definición de prioridades, objetivos y mecanismos periódicos de seguimiento.
- Asegurar que cada proyecto disponga de planes de trabajo, cronogramas, herramientas de seguimiento y responsabilidades claramente definidas y actualizadas.
- Dar seguimiento sistemático al avance de actividades, productos, resultados y principales hitos contractuales, identificando oportunamente retrasos, desviaciones y riesgos de implementación.
- Trabajar con los/las responsables de proyecto en la definición y seguimiento de medidas correctivas cuando existan retrasos o dificultades de ejecución.
- Promover una gestión proactiva de los proyectos, apoyando a los PM en la identificación de alternativas y soluciones ante bloqueos operativos.
- Asegurar el seguimiento y cierre oportuno de decisiones, procesos y acciones pendientes relacionados con la ejecución de los proyectos.
- Realizar visitas regulares a las áreas de intervención y reuniones de seguimiento con los equipos de proyecto y de base.
- Informar regularmente a la Coordinación País sobre avances, riesgos, necesidades de decisión y situaciones que puedan comprometer la ejecución de los proyectos.

**2. Gestión y desarrollo de los/las Jefes/as de Proyecto**

- Acompañar a los/las Jefes/as y Gerentes de Proyecto en la planificación, organización y priorización de su trabajo y en la gestión de los equipos bajo su responsabilidad.
- Fortalecer capacidades y desempeños en gestión del ciclo de proyecto, planificación, seguimiento financiero, gestión de equipos, anticipación de riesgos y resolución de problemas.
- Realizar reuniones individuales y colectivas de seguimiento y proporcionar retroalimentación periódica sobre desempeño y prioridades.
- Participar, junto con RRHH y la Coordinación País, en los procesos de selección, inducción, evaluación y desarrollo de los/las Jefes/as de Proyecto.
- Identificar necesidades de formación y acompañamiento, particularmente para perfiles nuevos o junior.
- Favorecer una cultura de responsabilidad, iniciativa, cumplimiento de compromisos y colaboración entre proyectos y departamentos.

**3. Seguimiento financiero y planificación operativa de los proyectos**

- Asegurar, en coordinación con Administración País y sin sustituir sus responsabilidades de control financiero y administrativo, el seguimiento periódico de la situación financiera de sus proyectos.
- Revisar con los PM el presupuesto, burn rate, previsiones y proyecciones de gasto, verificando su coherencia con los planes de actividades y cronogramas.
- Identificar tempranamente desviaciones entre ejecución programada y ejecución financiera y asegurar la preparación de medidas correctivas.
- Asegurar que las proyecciones financieras y necesidades operativas de los proyectos sean preparadas con suficiente anticipación y compartidas con Administración.
- Facilitar la coordinación entre PM y Administración cuando existan bloqueos o decisiones que puedan afectar la ejecución presupuestaria.
- Dar seguimiento, desde la perspectiva de ejecución del proyecto, a modificaciones presupuestarias, realineamientos y otras necesidades identificadas durante la implementación.
- La validación contable, financiera y de elegibilidad de los gastos seguirá correspondiendo a Administración.

**4. Seguimiento de procurement y logística de proyecto**

- Asegurar, en coordinación con Logística País, Administracion y las Coordinaciones de Base, que cada proyecto disponga de un plan de compras y adquisiciones actualizado y coherente con su plan de trabajo y cronograma.
- Asegurar que los PM y equipos de proyecto anticipen adecuadamente las necesidades de bienes, servicios, transporte y demás recursos necesarios para la ejecución.
- Dar seguimiento al estado de los principales procesos de compra y contratación vinculados a proyectos, identificando tempranamente posibles retrasos que puedan afectar actividades o resultados.
- Facilitar la coordinación entre PM, Logística y Base cuando existan bloqueos operativos.
- Asegurar que los PM integren adecuadamente los tiempos de los procedimientos logísticos y administrativos en su planificación.
- Dar seguimiento a la disponibilidad y utilización de recursos de proyecto desde la perspectiva de su impacto sobre la implementación.
- La gestión de proveedores, procedimientos de adquisición, flota, almacenes, activos y demás funciones logísticas institucionales seguirá siendo responsabilidad de Logística País y, en su ámbito territorial, de las estructuras correspondientes de Base.

**5. Coordinación de la ejecución y relación con otros departamentos**

- Actuar como principal punto de articulación entre los PM y las diferentes funciones de coordinación cuando existan necesidades o bloqueos relacionados con la ejecución.
- Mantener una coordinación sistemática con Programas sobre aspectos técnicos, calidad programática, indicadores, MEAL y modificaciones que puedan afectar el diseño de las intervenciones.
- Coordinar con Administración los aspectos financieros y contractuales vinculados a la ejecución.
- Coordinar con Logística los procesos operativos necesarios para la implementación.
- Coordinar con RRHH sobre necesidades de personal, desempeño y gestión de equipos de proyecto.
- Mantener una coordinación regular con las Coordinaciones de Base para asegurar la adecuada articulación entre la gestión del proyecto y las condiciones operativas de cada territorio.
- Favorecer una comunicación clara sobre responsabilidades, decisiones y plazos entre proyectos, departamentos y bases.
- La Coordinación de Operaciones no ejercerá supervisión jerárquica sobre las Coordinaciones de Base ni sobre los departamentos de soporte, salvo delegación temporal y expresa de la Coordinación País.

**6. Seguimiento de reporting y compromisos de proyecto**

- Asegurar que los PM mantengan actualizado el calendario de principales entregables, hitos contractuales y obligaciones de sus proyectos.
- Dar seguimiento a la preparación oportuna de los insumos técnicos, operativos y financieros requeridos para informes internos, informes a donantes, modificaciones y otros procesos contractuales.
- Asegurar que los PM proporcionen información completa y dentro de los plazos establecidos a las funciones responsables de consolidación y revisión de informes.
- Alertar oportunamente sobre retrasos o dificultades que puedan comprometer entregables contractuales.
- La revisión técnica, consolidación programática y gestión especializada de grants se realizará en coordinación con las funciones responsables de Programas/Grants.

**7. Gestión de riesgos y resolución de bloqueos**

- Identificar, junto con los PM, riesgos operativos, financieros, contractuales, de recursos humanos o de implementación que puedan afectar los proyectos.
- Asegurar que se definan medidas de mitigación, responsables y plazos para los principales riesgos identificados.
- Facilitar la resolución de bloqueos entre proyectos, bases y departamentos y escalar a la Coordinación País aquellos que requieran decisiones de nivel superior.
- Mantener una visión consolidada de los principales riesgos y necesidades operativas del portafolio de proyectos.
- Contribuir al aprendizaje institucional identificando problemas recurrentes, cuellos de botella y oportunidades de mejora de los procesos internos.
- Los riesgos técnicos serán abordados con Programas; los financieros con Administración; los logísticos con Logística; y los relativos a seguridad de acuerdo con la estructura y responsabilidades establecidas por la misión.

**8. Apoyo temporal a proyectos, bases y nuevas intervenciones**

- Por solicitud expresa de la Coordinación País, proporcionar refuerzo operativo temporal durante el lanzamiento de nuevos proyectos, transiciones, fases críticas o períodos de alta carga de trabajo.
- Asumir temporalmente funciones de gestión de proyecto cuando exista una vacante de PM, hasta la incorporación de la persona responsable.
- Apoyar excepcionalmente una Base cuando exista una vacante o necesidad temporal de refuerzo de coordinación, con un mandato y período previamente definidos.
- Apoyar la puesta en marcha de nuevas operaciones y facilitar su posterior transferencia al responsable correspondiente.
- Contribuir a respuestas de emergencia o incrementos rápidos de operaciones cuando la misión requiera capacidad adicional de gestión.
- Estas funciones tendrán carácter temporal y no modificarán las responsabilidades permanentes de las estructuras de Proyecto, Base o departamentos nacionales.

**9. Actividades complementarias**

- Promover el cumplimiento de los procedimientos institucionales de COOPI y del Código de Conducta en los equipos bajo su supervisión.
- Contribuir a un ambiente de trabajo profesional, colaborativo y respetuoso.
- Participar en reuniones de coordinación y planificación de la misión.
- Representar a COOPI, cuando sea delegado por la Coordinación País, en reuniones vinculadas específicamente a la implementación operativa de proyectos.
- Ejecutar aquellas tareas inherentes al puesto y que sean solicitadas por la Coordinación País, según contexto y necesidades de la misión.

## Perfil deseado

Profesional con sólida experiencia en gestión e implementación de proyectos humanitarios y/o de desarrollo, supervisión de Project Managers y coordinación entre equipos multidisciplinarios. Se busca especialmente un perfil con fuerte capacidad de project management, seguimiento, resolución de problemas y desarrollo de equipos, capaz de combinar una visión global del portafolio con acompañamiento práctico a los responsables de proyecto.

### ESENCIALES

- Título universitario en Cooperación Internacional, Gestión de Proyectos, Ciencias Sociales, Administración, Ingeniería, Relaciones Internacionales o áreas afines.
- Al menos 5 años de experiencia relevante en gestión de proyectos humanitarios o de desarrollo con ONG internacionales, agencias internacionales u organizaciones similares.
- Experiencia demostrable como Coordinador/a de Proyectos Senior, Coordinador/a de Operaciones o posición equivalente.
- Experiencia comprobada en supervisión, acompañamiento y desarrollo de Project Managers o equipos de gestión de proyectos.
- Dominio del ciclo de gestión de proyectos: planificación, ejecución, seguimiento, reporting y cierre.
- Experiencia en seguimiento financiero de proyectos, incluyendo presupuestos, forecast, spending plans, análisis de ejecución y planificación de gasto.
- Experiencia en planificación y seguimiento de adquisiciones y necesidades logísticas vinculadas a proyectos.
- Conocimiento de procedimientos y requisitos de donantes institucionales, particularmente Unión Europea/ECHO, Naciones Unidas y/o cooperación bilateral.
- Capacidad demostrada para detectar bloqueos, analizar problemas y desarrollar soluciones prácticas.
- Experiencia en gestión de equipos, evaluación de desempeño, feedback y fortalecimiento de capacidades.
- Excelentes capacidades de organización, priorización y seguimiento.
- Capacidad para trabajar de manera transversal con equipos técnicos, administrativos, logísticos y territoriales, respetando los diferentes ámbitos de responsabilidad.
- Liderazgo colaborativo, orientación a resultados y capacidad para acompañar y desarrollar equipos.
- Capacidad para trabajar bajo presión y gestionar simultáneamente múltiples proyectos y prioridades.
- Excelente comunicación interpersonal, capacidad de negociación y manejo constructivo de desacuerdos.
- Idioma castellano imprescindible; buen nivel de inglés oral y escrito.
- Manejo de herramientas informáticas y ofimáticas, con buen dominio de Excel.
- Disponibilidad para viajar regularmente a las diferentes áreas de intervención de COOPI en Venezuela.
- Respeto de la Visión y Misión de COOPI, de su carta de valores y de las políticas institucionales.

### DESEABLES

- Experiencia previa en Venezuela o en contextos latinoamericanos de elevada complejidad.
- Experiencia en contextos de emergencia y en lanzamiento o escalamiento rápido de proyectos.
- Experiencia previa con COOPI.
- Experiencia en proyectos financiados por ECHO, Unión Europea, AICS y agencias de Naciones Unidas.
- Formación de posgrado en gestión de proyectos, acción humanitaria, cooperación internacional o áreas relacionadas.
- Nacionalidad venezolana o permiso de residencia en el país.

jobs.title: MEAL Incentive Worker-Raqqa
jobs.description:
**Basic Information / About the International Rescue Committee (IRC):**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world’s worst humanitarian crises, helping people survive and rebuild their lives. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC delivers lifesaving and life-changing care to refugees forced to flee war or disaster. Today, the IRC operates in over 40 countries and 22 cities across the United States, restoring safety, dignity, and hope to millions uprooted by conflict or catastrophe. The IRC leads the way from harm to home.

**Job Overview / Summary:**

This position is part of the implementation of the Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) team’s work. The IW will carry out tasks in coordination with the MEAL Assistant at the International Rescue Committee (IRC) to ensure that the data required for monitoring project progress is collected in line with IRC’s commitments and that quality monitoring processes are properly conducted in the field.

IRC’s and partners’ activities are monitored to enhance program quality, adjust projects when necessary, and ensure timely availability of data to provide decision-makers with the information needed for evidence based decision making. This is achieved through activities such as data collection, data entry, coordination with response programs, field visits, and evaluations for both partner-implemented and IRC direct-implemented projects.

**Responsibilities:**

- Collect field data from beneficiaries and targeted communities using approved MEAL tools and questionnaires.
- Monitor the implementation of activities in the field, including distributions, awareness sessions, and other program-related activities.
- Accurately complete MEAL forms in accordance with the supervisor’s instructions.
- Conduct regular household visits to assess the use of provided assistance and measure beneficiary satisfaction.
- Submit concise field reports after each monitoring visit, highlighting key observations, challenges, and recommendations.
- Enter and upload field data using mobile phones or tablets, ensuring accuracy and compliance with approved templates.
- Coordinate with field program teams to ensure accurate and comprehensive data collection.
- Adhere to the IRC’s policies, protection standards, professional conduct, and code of ethics.
- Perform any other related duties as requested by the direct supervisor to support MEAL activities.

**Key Working Relationships:**

Position reports to: MEAL Assistant or his/her line manager in the absence of the MEAL Assistant.

Other Internal and/or External Contacts: Regular coordination with humanitarian actors and other partners in Syria.

**Job Requirements:**

Essential:

\- A technical institute diploma or a university degree.

\- Relevant previous experience in data collection, surveys, or assessments (experience in humanitarian programs is preferred).

\- Good command of the English language.

**Work Environment:**

Field-based work environment inside Syria.

All IRC staff are required to adhere to the IRC Way – our Code of Conduct – which is built on the principles of Integrity, Service, and Accountability. In line with these values, the IRC implements policies related to beneficiary protection from exploitation and abuse, child safeguarding, workplace harassment prevention, financial integrity, and protection against retaliation.

jobs.title: Procurement Officer-Damacus
jobs.description:
**Background/Context:**

The IRC has operated in Syria since 2012, providing protection, health, economic recovery, and early childhood development programs in Idleb, Aleppo, Ar-Raqqa, Hassakeh, and Deir ez-Zor, with new programs expanding into Hama, rural Damascus, and Homs. With a team of over 350 members, the IRC has established trust and strong community relationships, ensuring access and effective service delivery.

Our longstanding experience in the country to date provides a strong foundation for the IRC to further adapt and expand its programming across Syria, in order to respond to the new realities, with a greater focus on resilience and recovery initiatives. Alongside this, the IRC also plays a significant role in Syria’s NGO, donor, and coordination forums, holding key positions and actively engaging in advocacy efforts.

**Job overview:**

Reporting to the Procurement Manager, the Procurement Officer is responsible for the efficient procurement support of functions for IRC’s office in Damascus and Homs, Syria. The Procurement Officer must be able to rapidly procure Program supplies, services, and equipment, whilst ensuring best practices and maintaining audit-compliant records.

**Responsibilities:**

- Ensure that procurement is carried out in accordance with IRC and donors-specific police.
- Ensure documentary records are updated and archived in sequential order to avoid audit observations.
- Assist program staff in preparing the PIF (Procurement Initiation Form) and PRs, by reviewing the item description as per the product list, prices, delivery lead-time, and guidance on the necessary approvals required
- Ensure integrated internal controls and auditable support documentation.
- Generate all required procurement documentation and impeccably maintain records and files.
- Ensure that all materials purchased are of appropriate quality and price and are delivered as per the Pos delivery dates.
- Preparation of procurement contracts, service agreements, and purchase orders.
- Prepare Bid Analysis and score sheets before submitting to PM/SCM/SCC for validation, ensuring that rating is not deviating from IRC standards. For threshold required bid analysis, like RFQ and RFP processes.
- Update relevant staff about the status of his/her request and delivery and maintain regular contact with the supervisor on matters of procurement.
- Conduct regular market surveys in coordination with PM regular market surveys and maintain an up-to-date supplier database with key supplier information.
- Hold meetings with suppliers/service providers to negotiate prices in the best interest of program activities with assistance from the Procurement Manager.
- Establishment and maintenance of ethical, professional working relationships with suppliers.
- Maintain supplier information for regularly purchased items and be informed of current local market conditions.
- Engage in delivering requests for quotations and quotations from authorized suppliers.
- Any other duties or tasks delegated by the Procurement Manager or Coordinator.
- Ensure that RFP/RFQs are complete in all respects and that targeted vendors understand the objectives of IRC.
