jobs.title: ToR: Consultancy for a Podcast Production (Recording Support, Editing, English/French Subtitles, Upload/Publishing
jobs.description:
**The consultant reports to:**

Ednar Musyoka- Mental HealthProject Manager

**Description of consultancy**

To support online and in-person recording in Kenya, edit and package three (3) video podcast episodes, produce subtitles for, create 5–10 short clips, and upload/publish final content on agreed platforms.

## Background and rationale

CBM Global is an international development organization committed to improving the quality of life of persons with disabilities in the poorest countries in the world. In one of its unique approaches, CBM firmly commits to establishing authentic partnerships with disability movement by working alongside people with disabilities and their representative organizations. This has effectively been done through inclusive programmes, advocacy and advisory work led by people with lived experience. In addition, CBM Global’s Federation Strategic priorities 2025 - 2030 commits to working with those most left behind and shifting power in partnership among other key strategic priorities. Working together with like-minded stakeholders, complements our effort to ensure meaningful and effective participation of persons with disabilities, by removing barriers and creating enablers to realize their participation on an equal basis with others.

The Mental Health Leadership Programme (MHLP) is a regional programme that seeks to strengthen mental health leadership, coordination, and advocacy for mental health across Africa. Its overarching aim is to address the continent’s growing mental health challenges by empowering individuals, Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and Organizations of Persons with Psychosocial Disabilities (OPDs) to, provide accessible and quality mental health services, shape policies, and to implement inclusive, evidence-based programmes.

Funded by Wellcome Trust, MHLP contributes to the Africa CDC’s continental strategic priorities on Non-Communicable Diseases, injuries, and mental health, which provide coordinated framework for supporting member states in advancing public mental health. Through its Pillar 4, the programme strengthening networks, CSOs, people with lived experience and their representative organizations (OPDs). This work is being done by CBM Global in partnership with the Mental Health Innovation Network (MHIN), the Pan African Network of Persons with Psychosocial Disabilities (PANPPD), and other key stakeholders.

As part of this effort, there is an opportunity to leverage digital communication platforms to expand reach, facilitate knowledge exchange, and amplify lived experience of voices across the continent. Thus, MHLP envisioned setting up a podcast on mental health in Africa to create an engaging space for dialogue on mental health across Africa.

To achieve this, MHLP seeks to hire a consultant for ongoing support through the production of the podcast.

## Purpose and Objectives:

The purpose of the consultancy is to support online and in-person podcast production.

The objectives are:

1. Participate in a kick-off meeting, confirm production workflow, timeline, and review process
1. Support production (3) video podcast episodes (each up to 45 minutes).
2. Produce 10 short clips (~60 seconds each) optimized for social media distribution of episode.

## Deliverables

1. **Inception Package (Week 1–2)**.
1. Draft of a production plan (timeline + workflow)
2. Guest and recording templates (briefing note, consent/release, questionnaire, checklist)

**Draft Outputs (Rolling, per episode)**.

1. Draft edit of each episode (Episode 1 to 3)
2. Draft English subtitles for each episode
3. Draft 10 short clips of 60 seconds each (initial set for early review)

**Final Outputs (Publish-ready)**

1. 1 final edited French video episodes of 1 in-person recorded podcast
2. 1 English subtitle file for the French podcast
3. 2 final edited English video episodes of 2 online recorded podcast
4. French subtitle file for the English podcast
5. 5–10 final short clips (~60 seconds each) + relevant subtitles
6. Final export set formatted for YouTube and social platforms
7. **Publishing Confirmation + Handover**
1. Upload/publishing completed (or scheduled) on agreed channels
2. Handover folder with final exports, subtitle files, and metadata

## Timeframe and duration

This consultancy is expected to be delivered over a maximum of 4 (Four) weeks (dependent on guest scheduling and review cycles) from the date of contract signing.

## Place/ location of service delivered

This service will be provided remotely to CBM Global by the Consultant who will be based in Kenya. There will be no local or international travel for this consultancy.

## Required Expert Profile

- Proven experience producing/editing video podcasts and short-form social clips (portfolio required).
- Demonstrated ability to produce accurate English subtitles for French content and vice-versa (or a clear QA workflow).
- Ability to provide in-person recording support in Kenya and manage remote workflows (e.g., Zoom).
- Strong communication and ability to collaborate with a multi-stakeholder review group.

Applicants with disability are strongly encouraged to apply.

## Payment schedule

The payment will be made based on approved invoices in accordance with CBM Global’s specifications (see the CBM Global Consultancy Invoice Information).

The consultancy rate is agreed as following:

Payments will be paid as follows

- 30% upon acceptance of inception package.
- 70% after delivery of all the deliverables.

## Compliance with CBM Global policies

All consultants are required to sign and be bound by CBM Global code of conduct for consultants and CBM Global Safeguarding Policy and Behaviour Code and CBM [Accessibility](https://www.cbm.org/fileadmin/user_upload/CBM-Policy-on-Accessibility.pdf) [Policy.](https://www.cbm.org/fileadmin/user_upload/CBM-Policy-on-Accessibility.pdf) These will be provided upon contracting.

Canvassing of any kind by applicants, whether direct or indirect, with the intention of influencing the selection process may result in immediate disqualification from consideration.

jobs.title: International Consultant CC-2026-23
jobs.description:
Position Title: **International Consultant**

Duty Station: **Yerevan, Armenia**

Classification: **Consultancy**

Type of Appointment: **40 working days during November 2026 – March 2027**

Estimated Start Date: **As soon as possible**

Closing Date: **26 October, 2026**

*Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations, and as the leading UN agency in the field of migration, works closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners. IOM is dedicated to promoting humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It does so by providing services and advice to governments and migrants.*

***Context:***

The consultancy will support the Government of the Republic of Armenia in advancing integrated border management reforms and strengthening interagency cooperation in line with the draft Integrated Border Management (IBM) Strategy and related Action Plan priorities, as well as European Integrated Border Management principles.

The consultancy will focus on enhancing cooperation among the National Security Service Border Guard Troops, State Revenue Committee, Ministry of Internal Affairs, Migration and Citizenship Service, and other relevant border management stakeholders in line with European Integrated Border Management (EIBM) principles and international best practices.

The assignment will support the institutionalization of interagency cooperation and operational coordination mechanisms, the application of integrated risk analysis approaches based on the Common Integrated Risk Analysis Model (CIRAM), the development of standard operating procedures and joint operational practices, and the strengthening of information-sharing and coordinated response capacities.

The consultant will develop an interagency training package with primary focus on interagency cooperation, operational coordination, information exchange, and risk analysis, while integrating relevant aspects of border security, human rights, integrity, and emerging border management challenges.

Through a combination of assessment, curriculum development, practical exercises, simulation-based learning, and capacity-building activities, participating institutions will strengthen their ability to conduct coordinated border management operations, apply common risk analysis methodologies, enhance information exchange, and respond effectively to border security challenges in accordance with EU IBM standards.

***Background of the activity:***

The Project is implemented in Armenia to further strengthen the capacities of the national authorities to tackle cross-border organized crime and independent border management capacities. The primary national partners benefiting from its outcomes are the National Security Service of the Republic of Armenia (NSS) and its Border Guard Troops (BGT). The Project will build on the results achieved in recent years and will further advance the alignment of the border guard training/ educational system and standards with European and international best practices, enhance capacity to autonomously manage borders through enhanced secondary inspection as well as capacity to detect and counter irregular travellers, including terrorists and serious criminals through setting up Advance Passenger Information (API) and Passenger Name Record (PNR) data.

***Core Functions / Responsibilities:***
Under the overall supervision of the Head of Office and direct supervision of the Project Coordinator, the International Consultant shall deliver the following outputs:

**Assessment and Planning**

- Build on the findings and recommendations of the ongoing Border Check Point (BCP) assessment and conduct targeted consultations to validate and translate identified gaps, challenges, and priorities into a Training Needs and Capacity Assessment for the development of the interagency training package and simulation exercise.
- Conduct consultations with NSS Border Guard Troops, State Revenue Committee, Ministry of Internal Affairs, migration authorities, and other relevant stakeholders to identify institutional and operational capacity gaps.
- Assess the status of existing IBM-related reforms and institutional priorities, including relevant provisions of the draft IBM Strategy and Action Plan, where applicable.
- Produce a Training Needs and Capacity Assessment Report with recommendations.

**Development of Training Package**

Develop a comprehensive interagency training package covering:

- Interagency cooperation and coordination;
- Risk analysis and CIRAM methodology;
- Information exchange and operational coordination;
- Joint operational planning and decision-making.

The package shall include:

- Training curriculum;
- Trainer guides;
- Participant handbook;
- Presentations;
- Practical exercises;
- Case studies;
- Group work assignments;
- Evaluation and assessment tools.

**SOP and Operational Coordination Components**

- Develop practical training modules and reference materials supporting the application of interagency SOPs and coordinated operational procedures.
- Develop an interagency training package with primary focus on interagency cooperation, operational coordination, information exchange, and risk analysis, while integrating relevant aspects of border security, human rights, integrity, and emerging border management challenges.

**Multi-Agency Simulation Exercise**

1. Design a comprehensive simulation exercise based on realistic border-security and cross-border crime scenarios.
2. Incorporate elements related to:

- risk analysis;
- information exchange;
- operational coordination;
- crisis management;
- irregular migration;
- document fraud;
- human rights considerations.

1. Prepare facilitator guides, participant instructions, observation tools, and evaluation methodology.

**Capacity Building Delivery**

- Deliver a 4-5 day interagency training programme for relevant border management agencies.
- Facilitate practical exercises and group activities.
- Conduct a multi-agency simulation exercise and after-action review.
- Support the identification of future Training-of-Trainers (ToT) candidates to contribute to sustainability of national training capacities.

**Reporting**

Prepare a Report including:

- assessment findings;
- training results;
- identified capacity-development priorities;
- simulation exercise outcomes;
- recommendations for strengthening interagency cooperation;
- recommendations on risk analysis, information exchange, joint training, and operational coordination;
- recommendations contributing to implementation of the IBM Strategy and IBM Action Plan.

**Deliverables**

- Training Needs and Capacity Assessment Report.
- Comprehensive IBM Interagency Training Package.
- Multi-Agency Simulation Exercise Package.
- Delivery of one 4-5 day interagency training programme.
- Delivery of one multi-agency simulation exercise and after-action review.
- Training Completion Report and participant evaluation results.
- Final Report with recommendations and finalized training materials.

**Performance indicators for the evaluation of results**

- Demonstrated capacity to conduct a comprehensive assessment of the existing border management training needs and institutional capacities.
- Development and submission of a high-quality training package consistent with international standards and European Union Integrated Border Management (IBM) principles.
- Development of practical and operationally relevant simulation exercise materials tailored to the Armenian border management context.
- Effective delivery and facilitation of the training programme using appropriate adult learning methodologies and interactive approaches.
- Demonstrated ability to integrate risk analysis, interagency cooperation, border security, and human rights considerations into the training content.
- Successful facilitation of a multi-agency simulation exercise that reflects realistic operational challenges and coordination requirements.
- Provision of practical and actionable recommendations for strengthening national capacities in integrated border management and interagency cooperation.
- Timely submission of all deliverables in accordance with the agreed work plan and contractual requirements.
- Quality, completeness, and usability of all reports, training materials, and exercise documentation produced under the assignment.

***Required Qualifications and Experience***

**Education**

- Completed advanced university degree in a relevant field.
- Specialization in Border management and Customs operations.
- Other formal education as relevant for the assignment.

**Experience and Skills**

- Advanced university degree in border security, law enforcement, public administration, customs, security studies or related field;
- Minimum 10 years of professional experience in border management and border security, risk analysis and intelligence-led border management;
- Demonstrated experience in Integrated Border Management programmes;
- Practical experience with EU/Frontex methodologies and risk analysis frameworks;
- Experience designing and conducting multi-agency exercises;
- Previous work in EU Eastern Partnership, Western Balkans, Caucasus, or similar contexts is an advantage.
- Risk Analysis Expert
- Experience with risk indicators, profiling and threat assessment;
- Experience developing training materials and conducting capacity-building activities.

**Skills**

- Integrated Border Management (IBM) & EIBM expertise
- Border security operations and risk analysis (including CIRAM)
- Interagency cooperation and information-sharing mechanisms
- Training design, delivery, and capacity-building programs
- Simulation exercise development and facilitation
- Policy advisory, SOP development, and institutional strengthening

**Languages**

- Fluency in English is required (oral and written).
- Proficiency in Armenian or Russian would be beneficial.

**Travel** **required**

Yes.

**Required Competencies**

**Values**

- ***Inclusion and respect for diversity:*** respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
- ***Integrity and transparency:*** maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
- ***Professionalism:*** demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
- ***Courage:*** demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
- ***Empathy:*** shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

**Core Competencies** – behavioural indicators *level 1*

- ***Teamwork:*** develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
- ***Delivering results:*** produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
- ***Managing and sharing knowledge:*** continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
- ***Accountability:*** takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
- ***Communication:*** encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

***Other***

IOM covers Consultants against occupational accidents and illnesses under the Compensation Plan (CP), free of charge, for the duration of the consultancy. IOM does not provide evacuation or medical insurance for reasons related to non-occupational accidents and illnesses. Consultants are responsible for their own medical insurance for non-occupational accident or illness and will be required to provide written proof of such coverage before commencing work.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances.

IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities.

IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts.

IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the [IOM e-Recruitment](https://fa-evlj-saasfaprod1.fa.ocs.oraclecloud.com/hcmUI/CandidateExperience/en/sites/CX_1) system (for internal candidates link [here](https://fa-evlj-saasfaprod1.fa.ocs.oraclecloud.com/fscmUI/redwood/internalmobility)). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application.

No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: [IOM Careers and Job Vacancies](https://www.iom.int/careers)

jobs.title: Head of Advocacy and Evidencing
jobs.description:
**Location:** Ethiopia, India, Italy, Jordan, Kenya (as long as HelpAge International holds the registration in this country), Nepal, Pakistan, Spain, Tanzania, Thailand, Türkiye, United Kingdom and Zimbabwe

**Department:** Global Impact

**Reports to (Line Manager):** Director of Global Impact

**Responsible for (Line managing)**

- Humanitarian Advocacy Advisor
- Social Protection Advisor
- Health Advisor
- Rights Advisor

**Grade:** F

**Contract Type:** Open-ended contract

## **About HelpAge**

HelpAge International works with a diverse global network of around 200 organisations across 99 countries to promote the rights of older people to lead dignified, healthy and secure lives. Through partnership and collaborations, we work to ensure the inclusion of older people across society and strive to deliver a just and fair world for everyone as they get older. Our work is driven by our desire to achieve real impact for older people, to be inclusive, to work in partnership and to learn from our shared experience.

## **About the Job**

The Head of Advocacy & Evidencing provides strategic leadership and organisational accountability for HelpAge’s global advocacy, policy and research agendas, ensuring that external engagement is grounded in rigorous evidence, shaped by the lived experiences of older people, and aligned with organisational priorities.

## **Key areas for impact/influence and responsibilities**

To deliver impact, the Head of Advocacy & Evidencing will:

- Lead the delivery and evolution of HelpAge’s global advocacy and research agenda, ensuring it reflects lived experience and drives progress on rights, inclusion, and equity for older people.
- Strengthen the capacities of network members and older people to lead and participate meaningfully in advocacy efforts, and ensure inclusive engagement in the design and implementation of influencing strategies.
- Cultivate strategic partnerships with policy, academic, and research institutions to co-produce high-quality, policy-relevant evidence and promote HelpAge’s thought leadership on rights, healthy ageing, humanitarian inclusion, and social protection.

## **Key Responsibilities**

**Strategic Leadership and Advocacy**

- Lead and be accountable for the development, implementation and results of HelpAge’s global advocacy and evidencing strategy, aligned with HelpAge’s impact areas and co-created with network members.
- Monitor and respond to global, regional and national policy trends,advising colleagues and network members on opportunities for engagement and influence.
- Champion inclusive, partner-led advocacy approaches that centre the voices and leadership of older people and civil society actors.
- Collaborate with the Fundraising and Strategic Partnerships Director and supporting members to align donor advocacy efforts with organisational priorities and global influencing strategies.
- Advise the Executive Leadership Group and the Board on HelpAge's advocacy positions and external positioning, and lead the preparation and quality of the related papers and briefings. Where appropriate, represent HelpAge's positions externally alongside senior leaders.
- Lead and coordinate HelpAge's influencing in priority global and regional policy and donor markets, including Europe, identifying opportunities to position ageing and the rights of older people within relevant policy, development and humanitarian agendas and, in collaboration with Fundraising, strengthen HelpAge's positioning with institutional donors and partners.
- Be accountable for achieving the agreed Advocacy & Evidencing income target. Working in partnership with the Fundraising & Strategic Partnerships team, play a lead technical and relationship role in shaping fundable propositions, contributing to pipeline development, and donor cultivation and stewardship for advocacy and research.
- Ensure that advocacy, research and evidence-generation activities comply with HelpAge’s ethical, safeguarding, data protection and relevant organisational standards, and hold team members accountable for compliance within their areas of responsibility.
- Represent HelpAge at senior level in key global and regional coalitions, alliances and policy forums, proactively building strategic relationships with governments, multilateral and donor institutions, policy actors and other influential stakeholders to advance HelpAge’s advocacy priorities and strengthen its external positioning.

**Evidence and Research**

- Lead and be accountable for HelpAge’s global research and evidence agenda, ensuring that it is coherent, ethical, inclusive and aligned with organisational advocacy and programme priorities.
- Provide strategic oversight of HelpAge’s global portfolio of evidence generation, policy analysis and advocacy initiatives across key impact areas, ensuring coherence, quality and alignment with organisational strategy and drawing on the network as a central source of evidence and insight.
- Foster partnerships with academic institutions, think tanks, and research bodies to co-produce and validate robust, policy-influencing evidence.
- Ensure that research outputs are accessible, actionable, and designed for strategic influence at global and national levels.

**Capacity Strengthening and Network Engagement**

- Lead on advocacy capacity strengthening of HelpAge network members and older people through mentoring, training, and tailored support.
- Promote knowledge exchange and peer learning across the global network, ensuring inclusive participation in advocacy platforms and decision-making spaces.
- Collaborate with regional colleagues to support the development and implementation of national and regional advocacy strategies led by network members.

**Team and Resource Management**

- Lead, manage, and coach a multidisciplinary team of advocacy advisers, ensuring high performance and alignment with organisational goals. These are hybrid roles, with approximately 50% of their time dedicated to global advocacy and the remaining 50% focused on technical support to network members and contribution to programme development.
- Manage advocacy and research budgets effectively, ensuring compliance with donor requirements and strategic resource allocation.

**Cross-Organisational Collaboration**

- Work closely with Programme Support, Network Development, MEAL, Fundraising, and Communications teams to embed evidence and influencing in all areas of work.
- Coordinate joint advocacy and research initiatives that connect policy engagement with programme delivery and impact measurement.

## **Skills and experience required**

*Essential*

- Proven strategic leadership in global advocacy, policy influencing, and research within the international development, humanitarian, or human rights sectors.
- Strong leadership, planning, and performance management skills, with a track record of delivering results through high-performing, diverse, and remote multidisciplinary teams.
- Deep understanding and practical application of rights-based, inclusive, and intersectional approaches—especially relating to age, gender, disability, and displacement.
- Demonstrated success in designing and implementing partner-led advocacy strategies that centre lived experience and community priorities.
- Experience influencing policy at national, regional and international levels through coalition-building and senior-level relationships with governments, multilateral bodies and donors.
- Strong analytical and research skills, with experience designing or overseeing ethical, participatory research and translating evidence into compelling policy and advocacy outputs.
- Demonstrated ability to build and sustain high-impact partnerships with academic institutions, think tanks and policy platforms.
- Track record of securing income for advocacy or research, including developing fundable propositions and engaging institutional donors with fundraising colleagues.
- Skilled in budget oversight and resource management, including accountability in donor-funded initiatives.
- Ability to monitor advocacy impact, policy trends, and funding landscapes, and to adapt strategies accordingly.
- Experience of strengthening the capacity of civil society, networks or grassroots movements, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, through mentoring, training and tailored support.
- Lived experience of the Global South or extensive professional experience working in Global South contexts.

*Desirable*

- Strong knowledge and networks in European/global institutional policy and donor environments
- Experience engaging with media to support advocacy.

**Education and Qualifications**

- Degree in international development, public policy, human rights, social sciences, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience).
- A postgraduate qualification is an asset but not essential where practical experience is strong.

**Other Requirements**

- Willingness to travel internationally
- Ability to work across cultures, sectors, and geographies in inclusive and equitable ways.
- Excellent communication skills in English (spoken and written); additional languages used in the Global South (e.g., Spanish, French, Arabic) are highly desirable.
- Deep commitment to locally led development and the principles of Partner-Led Programming.
- We actively value and encourage candidates with lived experience of inequality, marginalisation, or systemic exclusion—especially related to age, gender, disability, displacement, or economic injustice.
- Familiarity with ageing, inclusion, and rights issues in Global South contexts is a key asset.

**Key Behavioural Competencies**

**Working Collaboratively with Others:** Work collaboratively, building mutual trust and respect, with external organisations and partners to achieve our strategic aims and objectives; being accountable for the work we do together.

**Adaptability and Flexibility:** Adapt to new directions or opportunities arising within the organisation and in our work area; being flexible in our role, constantly using the feedback to learn more and evolve further.

**Supporting and Facilitating Change:** Lead behavioural and cultural change through embracing a supportive, collaborative and highly inclusive environment where everybody feels supported, respected and engaged.

**Extend HelpAge’s Reach and Impact:** Extend HelpAge’s reach and impact by creating and identifying new business development opportunities and building relationships with new partners.

**Diversity and Inclusion:** Lead and promote a culture of including the voices of older people across our support, convening and thought leadership roles, in a way that is transformative, empowering and highly inclusive of those marginalised by gender, economic status, disability and other factors of discrimination.

**Leading Others (for managers):** Demonstrate strong leadership to own unit/department and manage people in a well and reputable manner. Create an atmosphere of trust and an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential.

**Safeguarding**

HelpAge International is committed to safeguarding the communities with which we work, our partners, staff and any others who we come into contact with. The post holder will also be responsible for:

- Preventing harm and abuse from our people, operations and programmes to anyone that encounters our work.
- Reporting all safeguarding incidents you see, hear, hear about or suspect, using our internal reporting mechanism.
- Complying with all safeguarding framework policies and practices.
- Completing mandatory training courses relating to our safeguarding policy framework and complying with HR vetting procedures.

**SAFER RECRUITMENT**

All employments at HelpAge International will be subject to satisfactory references and appropriate screening checks, which can include misconduct disclosure schemes and terrorism finance checks.

jobs.title: Coordination Unit (Forum) Coordinator Sudan Kauda
jobs.description:
**Background:**

South Kordofan, particularly Region 1 (R1) Nuba Mountains, continues to experience significant humanitarian needs driven by protracted conflict, displacement, and limited access to basic services. The complexity of the operational environment is characterized by hard-to-reach areas, fragmented service delivery, and dynamic population movements requiring strong, well-coordinated humanitarian action to ensure effective and timely assistance.

R1 benefits from long-standing coordination structures that have been in place for decades, including efforts led by the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) and the existing Coordination Unit (CU). These structures have played a critical role in facilitating humanitarian response on the ground.

In this context, the position will look at reinforcing coordination of humanitarian response on the ground. The position will strengthen and reinforce existing coordination mechanisms rather than establish parallel systems, ensuring efficient use of limited resources and building established operational foundations. This approach aligns with global humanitarian coordination principles that prioritize localized, context-driven, and system-strengthening interventions over duplication of structures.

This position will be hosted by NRC (and subject to NRC safety and security protocols) and will sit within the Coordination Unit in Nuba Mountains and report to the CU management team, ensuring direct integration into existing coordination frameworks while benefiting from NRC’s operational support. This role is explicitly designed as an enabling and facilitative function, fully complementary to existing structures. Technical leadership and strategic direction will remain under the relevant coordination unit and other related frameworks, with the position holder will serve as a field-level interface to enhance operational coherence, collaboration, and responsiveness.

**What you will do:**

This position will serve as a neutral convener of multi-sectoral humanitarian coordination in R1/ Nuba Mountains. This role is central to supporting collective planning, identifying and addressing service gaps, improving referral pathways, and strengthening the interoperability between emergency response and longer-term programming. Under the supervision of the CU management the position holder will support the local coordination structure and will engage with OCHA and other coordination mechanisms. Under the CU leadership, the position will ensure that key assessments to inform broader planning, that clusters are engaged to support cluster-specific coordination and technical harmonization, and that all humanitarian actors—regardless of consortium membership—can participate in and benefit from joint planning and alignment processes.

This position will ensure that existing national and cluster-level tools, SOPs, and coordination protocols apply. Any local contextualization or adaptation will be done in consultation with relevant stakeholders were needed. The supporting role of the position requires strong facilitation, diplomacy, coordination, and contextual knowledge of the humanitarian landscape in Sudan and Nuba Mountain in particular.

General Responsibilities:

1. Ensure adherence to NRC, and donor policies, tools, handbooks, and guidelines.
2. Support CU in the facilitation and coordination at the area level, ensuring inclusive, neutral, and solutions-oriented engagement of humanitarian and development actors.
3. Support CU in the design, implementation, and adaptation of joint response strategies and operational plans based on identified needs, service mapping, and gaps analysis.
4. Support capacity strengthening, learning exchanges, and peer-to-peer engagement among local and international partners under leadership of CU
5. Identify lessons learned, promote adaptive management approaches, and contribute to continuous improvement of the area-based coordination model.
6. Supporting CU to ensure joint planning and prioritization among humanitarian actors across sectors,
7. Enhancing information flow and feedback loops from field-level coordination structures to national platforms within CU protocols.

**Specific responsibilities:**

1. **Programmatic Coordination & Strategic Alignment**

- Support the CU management to facilitate the coordination in the R1/Nuba Mountains ensuring regular coordination meetings are inclusive, neutral, and solutions oriented.
- Participate in the A-ICCG meetings to ensure alignment with sector strategies, especially in relation to technical standards, referral pathways, and cross-cutting concerns.
- Support CU to ensure alignment with existing coordination structures in the R1/ Nuba Mountains (e.g., clusters, INGO Forum, OCHA)
- Supporting CU to ensure joint planning and prioritization among humanitarian actors across sectors,
- Collaborate closely with INGO field focal points and ensure coordination of first line and second line response strategies.
- Under the leadership of CU, support coordination with relevant secretariates and other local networks.
- Identify key response gaps and facilitate joint resource planning or referrals to address them in coordination with the A-ICCG and relevant clusters.

**2. Information Management & Interoperability**

- Support CU to maintain a live, up to date existing service mapping platform capturing who is doing what, where, and with what capacity based on CU systems.
- In consultation with CU facilitate the rollout of shared tools, including multi-sectoral enrolment formats, referral trackers, and dashboards.
- Contribute to the development of localized response strategies and area plans based on needs analysis and data from active stakeholders, and cluster partners.
- Support CU to ensure that service mapping, referral tracking, and other data outputs are integrated into OCHA and cluster IM systems, contributing to national dashboards and Situation Reports as appropriate.

**3. Access**

- Under the guidance of CU management and protocols support coordination with OCHA, INGOs, NNGO support the engagement with local authorities to discuss and advocate on access-related issues.

**4. Learning, Peer Exchange, and Capacity Strengthening**

- Support learning exchanges between actors on best practices in integrated, area-based programming.
- Identify local capacity gaps and collaborate with OCHA and relevant clusters to organize training or mentoring not limited to technical gaps.
- Capture lessons learned, support after-action reviews, and contribute to adaptive management in coordination with OCHA.
- Encourage equitable participation of local actors through co-chairing opportunities, rotating facilitation, and adapted meeting modalities that consider access and resourcing constraints.

**What you will bring:**

**Generic professional competencies:**

- Bachelor’s degree in humanitarian affairs, development studies, or social sciences (master’s preferred).
- Minimum 5 years of experience in humanitarian response, coordination, or multisectoral programming.
- Experience engaging with INGOs, NNGOs, UN agencies, and coordination mechanisms
- Proven facilitation, negotiation, and coordination skills, especially in conflict-affected or access-constrained contexts.
- Fluency in English required; Arabic added advantage.
- Knowledge of the South Kordofan, Nuba Mountains context and local actor landscape is a significant asset.
- **What we offer:**
- Duty station: South Kordofan – Region1/Nuba Mountains
- Contract: 6 Months (renewable based on funding and performance)
- Travel: 40%
- Salary/benefits: grade 8 on NRC’s **International** salary scale.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- *For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity MarketPlace.*
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Applicants who do not fill in the required information will not be considered for the role.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Mandatory to submit the below when applying:
- **Your most updated English CV and remove all previous outdated CVs.**

jobs.description:
**Join MSF OCG as a Medical Technologies and Innovation Intern!**

**We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.**

**Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.**

This internship is part of an academic training program, a professional training program, or a socio-professional integration program, and must comply with the [conditions](https://www.ge.ch/engager-personne-stage/stages-formation-insertion-reconnus) set by the Employment Market Supervisory Council (CSME). The duration of the internship, as defined by the tripartite agreement, is 6 to 12 months at 100%

**Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF**

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.

We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.

**Context & mission**

Médecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).

The MSF movement is built around 5 operational centers supported by 24 sections and offices worldwide. MSF Operational Center Geneva (MSF OCG) is one of these centers.

OCG has a long history of supporting Medical Technologies and Innovation, as an early adopter of innovation in humanitarian organizations in the early 2000s. It continues to work to leverage medical technology and innovation advances in line with the strategic objectives through a mix of key transformational initiatives, and quick wins that utilize existing tools through acceptable adaptation process. Emphasis and focus are placed on field driven initiatives and scalable tools that mirror current OCG ambitions, achieving transparency, proactive communication and prioritization through a platform-based repository for innovations. The current Medical Technologies unit consists of the Medical Technologies and Innovation Coordinator, and the Digital Health Advisor, who focuses on projects and challenges in the digital health space.

The Medical Technology and Innovation Unit coordinates technological initiatives in 1) medical devices 2) digital health solutions and 3) innovation, the exceptions being drugs and vaccines.

**Tasks & Responsibilities**

*Admin Support 30%*

- Supports the unit in the organization of meetings (i.e. project planning meetings with both internal and external stakeholders), including the preparation of agendas, taking minutes and the archiving of meeting documentation.
- Supports the unit in the management of information such as unit archiving, is the focal point for the online platforms such as Kompas and Share Point
- Supports the preparation of key project documents, presentations and communication material for either internal or external use.

*Project Support 40%*

- Provides ad hoc support to the Digital Health Advisor and the Medical Technology and Innovation Coordinator as needed in following the project portfolio and promoting the unit and its work
- By delegation from the unit can support specific projects through direct interaction with stakeholders to advance the topic
- Undertake background research pertinent to certain key projects or thematic areas of importance to the Unit, in order to support the direction of the work

*Think Up Platform support 30%*

- Act as the owner and moderator of the ThinkUP platform, the Units online platform which collects ideas for innovation and reports on the projects undertaken back to the member of the community
- Ensure the think up platform is up to date, update regularly on the projects, engage with community members via the platform
- Design and prepare campaigns on specific topics to run through the platform to promote and advance certain areas of interest to the group
- Participates to the weekly innovation med tech unit meeting and keeps an overview of the tasks and ongoing status of each project under the units control.
- Engages the community and proposes ideas to keep the platform updated

**Your profile**

- Have a tripartite internship agreement
- Finished or in progress Master’s degree in a subject related to the Medical or para medical professions, Design and Technology, Innovation, Humanitarian or Development Studies, or other relevant degree.
- Strong proven interest in technology and innovation related to health
- No specific requirements in terms of work experience but having some form of employment in the past is considered an advantage.
- Capacity of analysis and synthesis;
- Planning and organization;
- Knowledge of key issues of the humanitarian environment;
- Excellent writing skills;
- Excellent knowledge of the MO environment (Powerpoint, Excel, Word)
- Fluent English and French (written and spoken).
- Team player; ability to coordinate with numerous stakeholders;
- Ability to work autonomously;
- Pro-active and solution-oriented
- Flexible and capacity to adapt quickly

**Terms of employment**

- A tripartite internship agreement is mandatory.
- 6 to 9 months, according to internship agreement.
- Full time (40h/week).
- Based in Geneva, Switzerland
- Start date : Beginning of January 2027
- Gross monthly remuneration 2'000.- CHF

Program Description (Background)

## ***The successful candidate can be based anywhere in the world where International Medical Corps has a program office. It is a remote position with significant travel to country programs as requested.***

## **Advisor, Global MHPSS Technical Unit**

## **About International Medical Corps**

International Medical Corps is a global, humanitarian, nonprofit organization dedicated to saving lives and relieving suffering through health care training and relief and development programs.

Established in 1984 by volunteer doctors and nurses, International Medical Corps is a private, voluntary, nonpolitical, nonsectarian organization. Its mission is to improve the quality of life through health interventions and related activities that build local capacity in underserved communities worldwide. By offering training and health care to local populations and medical assistance to people at highest risk, and with the flexibility to respond rapidly to emergency situations, International Medical Corps rehabilitates devastated health care systems and helps bring them back to self-reliance.

## **Job Summary**

## **As a member of the HQ TU MHPSS Team, provide technical quality oversight and programmatic guidance and support to global and country-level MHPSS activities and programming.**

## **Essential Duties & Responsibilities**

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential function with or without reasonable accommodation

1. **Program support**: Support country teams and provide guidance and oversight in the development and running of culturally appropriate mental health and psychosocial activities, including MH PHC integration, MHPSS case management, Early Childhood Development, Psychological First Aid, designing holistic recreational, vocational and social activities for children and youth targeting refugees and vulnerable populations across the region, peer support programs for people with chronic or severe mental illness, mental health advocacy and other programs in line with global guidelines and IMCs approach.
2. **Proposal Development**: Assist country teams in developing further MHPSS programming as appropriate and in the development of project proposals
3. **Standards and principles**: Ensure that all MHPSS work is in keeping with IASC guidelines on MHPSS support in emergencies.
4. Promote global guidelines such as IASC MHPSS guidelines where appropriate opportunities arise
5. Ensure and promote complementary and holistic coordinated community based MHPSS programming compliance with IMC’s MHPSS approach and Technical Unit Guidance notes on minimum and comprehensive quality standards for MHPSS programs.
6. **Crosscutting integration**: Provide support to country teams based on identified needs and working to ensure IMC holistic and crosscutting approaches across MHPSS, Nutrition, Health, Child Protection and GBV program areas.
7. **Coordination**: Support country level coordination WG efforts, promoting IMC’s active participation and/or leadership, and contribution to WG advocacy, coordination and mapping activities.
8. Support country teams in coordinating activities with relevant Government Authorities, International and National Organizations, advocating for best practices, and partnerships in line with national strategies.
9. **M&E**: Develop and employ consistent, standardized tools for monitoring and evaluating processes and outcomes of IMC MHPSS programs across the region, with attention to record of lessons learned through evidence-based practice for the purpose of project replication or expansion.
10. **Representation and visibility**: Represent IMC and its MHPSS programmes in relevant national and international conferences and meetings.
11. **Travel**: Support teams remotely and in person through frequent field visits

**Reporting**

1. Regular reporting and updates to TU Senior Global MHPSS Advisor and regional Senior Director
2. Regular contact with Senior Global MHPSS Advisor about planning, methods and tools used, and progress.
3. Expected Outputs for each country technical assistance field visit will include:
- Field trip report that includes a situational analysis, program(s) assisted, assistance provided, and recommendations for follow up/improvement.
- Annexes that include all work products including any new or improved MHPSS tools or measures used during the assignment.

## **Skills & Qualifications**

1. The qualified candidate will be a mental health professional (psychologist, clinical social worker, psychiatrist, or psychiatric nurse) with professional practice experience in clinical mental health
2. At least 5+ years’ experience in setting up, establishing and running MHPSS programs in humanitarian and low-resource settings
3. In-depth knowledge of global guidelines (e.g. IASC Guidelines on MHPSS In Emergency Settings)
4. Training and capacity building experience
5. Very good ability to mentor, support and motivate others
6. Strong organizational and supervisory skills
7. Strong reporting and writing skills
8. Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work within different cultural environments
9. Honest, hardworking and a self-motivated
10. Ability to work within a team structure or in isolation, flexible, and can cope with stressful workloads and working with limited resources
11. Ability to travel often and on short notice to project sites
12. An excellent command of verbal and written English and French

International Medical Corps is a ‘first-responder’ both to natural and men-made disasters and has a mandate of working in remote locations. The organization has a comprehensive security management policy and plan in place and committed to do everything possible within its remit to ensure safety and security. Notwithstanding, the mandate and programming choices of International Medical Corps require staff with high degree of resilience, extremely decisive quality and ability to move fast. International Medical Corps is proud to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, age, disability or status as a veteran.

Fluency in French required

### **ETHICAL CONDUCT AT INTERNATIONAL MEDICAL CORPS**

As part of a global, humanitarian team dedicated to saving lives, easing suffering, and building self-reliance, International Medical Corps staff are responsible for adhering to our Code of Conduct and Ethics and for knowing and abiding by International Medical Corps policies and standards. All staff play a vital role in preventing violations of our Code of Conduct and Ethics, including conflicts of interest, fraud, corruption, and any kind of exploitation or abuse. International Medical Corps is also committed to providing a safe and healthy work environment free of harassment, bullying, and other misconduct, enabling staff to build and maintain professional, respectful working relationships.

International Medical Corps prioritizes safeguarding the populations with whom we work from exploitation, neglect, or abuse of children and adults at risk, and/or any form of trafficking in persons. International Medical Corps is committed to engaging members of crisis-affected communities to participate in meaningful ways in a crisis response, including making informed decisions about the assistance they receive, mitigating potential risks, and holding us accountable for the commitments we make. All staff are expected to support International Medical Corps’ culture of accountability toward our stakeholders, particularly the crisis-affected communities and individuals we serve.

As part of International Medical Corps’ commitment to a speak-up culture and as one of the primary ways we collectively hold ourselves accountable for complying with the ethical principles and standards of conduct outlined in the Code of Conduct and Ethics, all staff are required to report suspected or actual misconduct or violations of organizational policies. Our Code of Conduct and Ethics and Whistleblower Policy prohibit any form of retaliation against whistleblowers or individuals who report a concern in good faith. Staff who violate these protections may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment or contractual relationship with International Medical Corps.

### **EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES**

International Medical Corps is proud to provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, age, disability or status as a veteran.

### **MISCONDUCT DISCLOSURE SCHEME**

All offers of employment at International Medical Corps are subject to satisfactory references and background checks. International Medical Corps participates in the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme from the Steering Committee for Humanitarian Response (SCHR). In accordance with this, we will request information from an applicant’s previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms his/her understanding of these recruitment procedures.

Share this job as a link in your status update to LinkedIn.

jobs.title: Regional Programme Coordinator (MENA)
jobs.description:
The Red Cross Red Crescent Movement is the world's largest humanitarian organization, and we are looking for a **Regional Programme Coordinator** in the **International Department, Middle East and North Africa (MENA) Region**. As **Regional Programme Coordinator**, you will be responsible for coordinating and managing multi-country regional programmes, ensuring high-quality implementation, monitoring, reporting, learning, and stakeholder engagement across the MENA region. The role focuses particularly on the implementation and expansion of the **Non-Communicable Diseases (NCD) Programme** and the **Pathways to Protection (P2P) Programme**, while supporting strategic programme development, partner capacity strengthening, and donor compliance.

Danish Red Cross has been present in the Middle East and North Africa region since 2002, working closely with Red Cross and Red Crescent National Societies in Syria, Lebanon, Iraq, Yemen, the occupied Palestinian territory, Egypt, and other countries in the region. DRC supports programmes in health, migration, disaster preparedness and response, National Society Development, and community resilience. The current regional portfolio includes the NCD Programme, supported by the Novo Nordisk Foundation and the World Diabetes Foundation, and the Pathways to Protection Programme, funded by the Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs and implemented through a consortium approach focused on migration and protection across North Africa.

**Your main tasks include:**

- Coordinate and oversee the implementation of regional programmes, ensuring activities, budgets, and deliverables are delivered on time and to a high standard.
- Lead programme planning, reporting, monitoring, learning, and donor compliance processes across multiple countries and partners.
- Support National Societies and country teams through technical guidance, capacity strengthening, coordination, and knowledge sharing.
- Facilitate programme development, assessments, evaluations, research initiatives, and fundraising opportunities for regional programmes.
- Represent Danish Red Cross in relevant regional coordination forums, partnerships, and technical networks.

As Regional Programme Coordinator, you will become part of a team of passionate colleagues in the MENA Regional Office. The Regional Office is responsible for strategic programme development, technical support, partnership management, humanitarian response, organizational development, and support the proposal development across the region. Teamwork, ambitions, and collaboration are key elements of our everyday work, while maintaining a strong focus on quality, accountability, innovation, and results.

As Regional Programme Coordinator, you will report to the Deputy Head of Region, MENA.

The position will be based in Amman, Jordan.

**We believe that you fit this position if:**

- You have a minimum of 7 years of experience in programme management, project implementation, or humanitarian and development programming.
- You hold a relevant postgraduate degree in Health or another relevant discipline related to programme management, public health, humanitarian action, or international development.
- You have proven experience managing multi-country programmes in development and/or conflict-affected settings.
- You have demonstrated experience in project cycle management, monitoring and evaluation, donor reporting, and financial oversight.
- You possess excellent English communication and writing skills.
- Knowledge of Arabic is an asset.
- You have strong coordination, facilitation, networking, and relationship-building skills.
- You are comfortable working in culturally and politically sensitive environments and can manage competing priorities effectively.
- You are proficient in standard IT applications, including Microsoft Office tools.
- Experience in health programming, migration, protection, or disaster management is considered an advantage.
- Experience working with the Red Cross Red Crescent Movement is a strong assets.

**You will become part of the World's largest humanitarian organization**

The Red Cross Red Crescent Movement is the world's largest humanitarian organization. We help people on both sides of a conflict and in the remotest corners of the world, regardless of their religion, race or political views. The Red Cross is always there. We save lives every day, and we equip people with the tools they need to get through crises and disasters. We are part of your local community no matter where you live. With your help, we can be wherever we are needed, always.

International Department in the Danish Red Cross supports vulnerable people in Africa, Asia, Europe and the Middle East in close cooperation with Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies in more than 20 countries and manages an annual turnover of more than 1 billion Danish kroner. We work specifically on strengthening preparedness and response capacities and implement both long-term development interventions and emergency response programmes within health, disaster preparedness and humanitarian action.

We offer meaningful work in a purpose-driven organization with highly engaged colleagues. We focus on professional development, employee well-being, flexibility, and a collaborative work environment where everyone contributes to delivering impactful humanitarian results.

**Application, conditions, and further information**

This recruitment is for international profiles. For further information regarding the job, see the [job description](https://rodekors.emply.com/api-v2/shared-files/4ceb1c0e-84d8-466e-aea3-18eeb3503f4a/shared-access-keys/41rb5u6us5yaa99jd4ypwy64w1zeuj8rx5izkbbgvwyc98s5ov224ip8wfvc9st3). We look forward to receiving your application and CV no later than **23/10/26**. Applications and CVs in English are accepted only through our online recruitment system.

The contract duration is **two years**, with the possibility of extension. We offer seven weeks of holiday per year and cover accommodation in Amman.

This position includes regional travel, estimated at approximately **30-60 travel days per year**.

The contract will be administered in accordance with the Danish Red Cross [Terms and Conditions for Delegates](https://rodekors.emply.com/api-v2/shared-files/87f32d89-f812-4ded-a44f-c326949f1c9d/shared-access-keys/fhgj95ihhqmh5w3sqsst7zhqiyhjy74i6zs9ugqfa7k2lmi4umm28knittf9v6a6).

The expected starting date is ideally no later than **15 December 2026**.

We may, with your consent, contact references prior to employment.

We look forward to hearing from you!

jobs.title: Head of Systems and Operations for Myanmar
jobs.description:
**Duty Station:** Yangon, Myanmar

**Line Manager:** Country Director

**Start Date:** November 2026

**People in Need (PIN)** is a Czech-based international non-governmental organization (NGO) that has provided humanitarian and development assistance across more than 20 countries since 1992. Today, PIN stands as one of the largest organizations of its kind in Central and Eastern Europe, supporting vulnerable communities in Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Eastern Europe. PIN empowers civil society, advocates for human rights, and promotes social inclusion both at home and abroad.

## **About the Myanmar Programme at People in Need**

People in Need (PIN People in Need (PIN) is an international, non-profit organization providing humanitarian and development assistance around the world. In Myanmar, People in Need started to work in 2002, when it launched financial assistance to civil society groups and provided humanitarian response to people affected by Cyclone Nargis in 2008. PIN supports local civil society partners with a focus on strengthening local civil society organizations and providing them with the necessary knowledge and funding. Through humanitarian response, development and education projects and community cohesion-building programmes tailored to local conditions, and by working closely with local actors, PIN helps local communities cope with both water-induced disasters and human-made crises.

## **Position Summary**

The Head of Systems & Operations (HoSO) is a core member of the Country Management Team (CMT) for People in Need’s Myanmar Country Programme (CP) and jointly ensures the effective, efficient and accountable management of the entire CP and shares responsibility for the effective and efficient delivery.

The HoSO is responsible for strategically leading and continuously improving all key support functions — **Procurement & Logistics**, **Finance**, **Human Resources**, and **Administration**. In performing this role, the Head of Systems & Operations will ensure an enabling environment for the implementation of the Country Programme, while maintaining operations and systems that meet the accountability requirements of People in Need and its donors.

HoSO also directly leads the process of development and staff capacity building across the departments in terms of systems and operations.

## **Duties & Responsibilities**

- Strategic leadership
- Ensuring External and Internal Compliance
- Management of Human Resources and capacity development
- Finance management
- Logistics and procurement management

**And fulfils any other tasks as required.**

### **Requirements:**

- Hands-on approach
- Background in finance, operations, or a combination of both
- Experienced in managing teams
- Ability to coordinate and communicate clearly with different groups of people and to respect different cultural backgrounds
- Ability to work independently and effectively
- Ability to deal with a complex compliance agenda
- Analytical skills and systematic approach
- Responsibility, ownership, proactive approach, flexibility
- Experience with project management is welcome
- English language proficiency

## **PIN Offers:**

- Working environment in a well-established humanitarian organisation in a challenging context;
- Salary and benefits according to PIN salary scale and HR policies; expected salary 3250-3500 EUR super gross (based on experience), plus monthly subsistence allowance of 1395 EUR;
- Housing Allowance or accommodation arranged by PIN;
- 25 days of holiday and 10 sick days per year;
- Travel health insurance (covers health care incl. repatriation);
- Reimbursement of travel expenses with travel to the country of residence once every 6 months of work;
- Reimbursement of costs of visas and vaccinations; assistance with the visa application procedure;
- Reimbursement of the medical check-up before and after the deployment;
- Free 24/7 medical helpdesk and psychological consultation available online;
- Free access to e-learning sites, global PIN’s Induction Training, Knowledge and Learning department onboarding, and individually tailored capacity-building opportunities; incl. HEAT training.

jobs.title: Field Volunteer – Women's Empowerment & Self-Defense in Athens
jobs.description:
## **About EmpowerVan**

[EmpowerVan](http://www.empowervan.org) is a non-profit organization dedicated to empowering women and girls on the move through self-defense and empowerment training. Our mission is to enable them to lead autonomous lives free from violence.

We currently operate programs in refugee camps and shelters for unaccompanied minors in Greece. There, we have a fully furnished van with martial arts equipment, that we drive to refugee camps, in order to teach self-defense to the people living there. We also go to shelters for unaccompanied minors and other spaces in Athens, to empower asylum seekers and refugees.

This year we have expanded our holistic approach to Kenya, bringing empowerment programs directly to women and girls in Kakuma Refugee Camp, where we certified refugees living in the camp as Empowerment Self-Defense Instructors, and men as Male Agents of Change, driving positive change in their community.

**Field Volunteer – Women's Empowerment & Self-Defense in Athens**

EmpowerVan is looking for a woman that is driven to advance gender justice, loves connecting with community members and has a passion for movement and sport. We are a small team and are looking for a volunteer to help us in Athens. You will be supporting us by going to classes in camps and shelters to support our instructors as you assist them, help with attendance, and you will also help us do reach-out to new community members, drive the van (is you have a license) and support us in daily tasks.

**What we’re looking for**

- **Teaching Skills**: Ability to teach sport, self-defense, or martial arts.
- **Gender Requirement**: Female applicants only (due to the nature of our work).
- **Personal Attributes**: Adaptable, well-organized, able to work independently, and at least 22 years old.
- **Experience**: Prior experience in sport and movement (hobby or work), experience working with displaced communities or minorities is preferred but not necessary.
- **Availability**: Able to be on the ground in **Athens for a minimum of 5 weeks**. Preferably afor at least 16 hours per week, up to full-time.
- People with a driver’s license highly preferred
- **Language skills:** Good spoken English is a must, as the team communicates in English.
Additional language skills are a huge plus, especially Persian, Arabic and French

## **Important Notes:**

- This is an **unpaid volunteer position**.
- Applicants must be self-sufficient and able to cover their own expenses during the volunteering period.
- We are not able to support with any visa process

If you’re ready to make a meaningful impact and join a dynamic team dedicated to creating a world free of gender-based violence, we’d love to hear from you!
