- At least 2 years of experience in the humanitarian sector and/or field-based roles in fragile or development contexts.
- Experience with designing and implementing primary research, in particular large-scale quantitative surveys and/or humanitarian needs assessments. Experience in leading multi-sectoral assessments is an asset.
- Demonstrated experience designing and delivering training or capacity-building for adult professionals, including remote and online delivery considered a strong asset.
- Experience developing e-learning content (e.g. Didask, Moodle or comparable platforms) an asset.
- Excellent communication and drafting skills for effective reporting.
- Strong interpersonal skills, including good external engagement and coordination skills, and the ability to build partnerships with regional and national actors.
- Familiarity with the humanitarian system and global humanitarian policy frameworks, in particular the Grand Bargain, the HPC and the JIAF.
- Willingness and ability for short term deployments, including to complex and challenging security environments.
- Ability to operate in a cross-cultural environment requiring flexibility.
- Fluency in English and French required, given the regional remit of the position; Arabic, Spanish or Portuguese an asset.
- Prior experience leading the design or implementation of MSNAs an asset.
- Prior experience working in West and/or Central Africa an asset.
- Ability to operate InDesign, a strong plus.
- Ability to operate R, or a related statistical programming language, an asset.

## **COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

- For this position, salary between 2’460 CHF and 2’520 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere.
- Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse.
- Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance.
- Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered).
- Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance)
- Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable.
- Predeparture induction - 3 days at IMPACT Initiatives’s HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training;
- IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

jobs.title: Digital Prevention and Capacity Development Consultants
jobs.description:
**LOCATION: Home-based, with travel to Baghdad, Iraq, as required**

**NUMBER OF POSITIONS: 4–6 consultants across leadership, technical delivery and specialist roles**

**CONTRACT: Short-term consultancy with intermittent inputs, anticipated November 2026 to October 2027**

## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Human Relief Foundation (HRF) is seeking experienced consultants to strengthen institutional capacity in preventing and countering violent extremism (PVE/CVE), with a focus on the digital environment. This is a single recruitment process for a Team Leader, a Technical Lead and 2–4 Specialist Consultants. HRF will assess applicants and match them to roles according to their qualifications and experience. Applicants are not expected to meet the requirements for every role or specialism.

The work combines learning-needs assessment, curriculum development, practical workshops, online learning and mentoring for institutional participants. Engagements are subject to funding and confirmation of the assignment. Responsibilities and reporting lines will depend on the role assigned.

Responsibilities will include:

- Assess learning needs and develop a capacity-development programme tailored to institutional roles and the Iraqi context.
- Develop or deliver practical training, exercises and reference materials within the consultant’s area of expertise.
- Support analysis of online radicalisation, extremist narratives and prevention approaches, using lawful and ethically appropriate methods.
- Coordinate with institutional counterparts and other consultants to ensure consistent, timely and high-quality delivery.
- Monitor learning progress and contribute to assessments, activity reports and documentation of results.
- Apply conflict sensitivity, Do No Harm, human-rights, privacy and data-protection principles. Use fictional, non-identifying scenarios in exercises.
- Participate in online meetings and travel to Baghdad where the agreed role requires in-person delivery, following applicable security procedures.

## PERSON SPECIFICATION

Applicants should meet the criteria for at least one of the roles described below. Relevant experience must be clearly evidenced in the CV with month and year dates, responsibilities and project examples. Strong written and spoken English at C1 level is required for all roles. Arabic language skills and relevant regional experience will also inform team composition.

## TEAM LEADER

Reporting to HRF Programme Management, the Team Leader will provide overall coordination, strategic oversight and quality assurance. Indicative input: up to 15 working days, including limited travel for coordination and review meetings.

**Role responsibilities**

- Oversee the Technical Lead and Specialist Consultants and coordinate communication with relevant partners.
- Quality-assure the learning-needs assessment, curriculum, training methodology, exercises, learning evidence and reports.
- Oversee workplans, milestones, risk management and reporting; lead key coordination and review meetings.

**Qualifications and experience**

- Master’s degree or equivalent in political or social sciences, peace and conflict studies, security studies, international relations, development studies or a related field.
- At least 7 years of experience in development cooperation, peacebuilding, stabilisation or closely related fields.
- At least 5 years of experience in PVE/CVE or related prevention activities.
- At least 5 years of management or leadership experience as a project team leader, project manager or in a comparable role.
- Demonstrated experience working with governmental or institutional counterparts in Iraq or the Middle East.

## TECHNICAL LEAD

Reporting to the Team Leader, the Technical Lead will manage technical design and delivery, coordinate Specialist Consultants and lead implementation with institutional counterparts. Indicative input: up to 60 working days, including repeated missions to Baghdad for preparation and workshop delivery.

**Role responsibilities**

- Lead the learning-needs assessment and translate findings into a tailored curriculum and practical capacity-development programme.
- Develop and oversee workshop materials, scenario-based exercises, mentoring and learning assessments.
- Coordinate technical contributions and institutional engagement; monitor participants’ progress and prepare reports and results data.

**Qualifications and experience**

- Master’s degree or equivalent in political or social sciences, peace and conflict studies, security studies, international relations, development studies or a related field.
- At least 7 years of experience in development cooperation, peacebuilding, stabilisation or closely related fields.
- At least 5 years of experience in PVE/CVE, online radicalisation or prevention policy, and at least 5 years in institutional capacity development or advisory services.
- Demonstrated experience managing and coordinating technical assignments or projects.
- Demonstrated experience working in Iraq or the Middle East, and experience with governmental or institutional counterparts in the Middle East or similar contexts.

## SPECIALIST CONSULTANTS

Reporting to the Technical Lead, 2–4 Specialist Consultants will support assessment, develop and deliver specialist sessions, facilitate exercises and contribute to materials and reports. Up to 100 working days will be shared across the pool; individual inputs and travel will depend on the expertise required.

**Qualifications and experience common to specialist roles**

- Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in political or social sciences, security studies, international relations, law, communications or media, information technology, data analysis or a field relevant to the proposed specialism.
- At least 7 years of professional experience relevant to the proposed area of expertise, and at least 5 years in capacity development, training or advisory services.

**Specialist areas**

Applicants should demonstrate one or more of the following areas. The selected pool will cover all five collectively; individual applicants do not need to cover every area.

- PVE/CVE and online radicalisation: at least 7 years in PVE/CVE, online radicalisation, extremist narratives, recruitment or mobilisation dynamics.
- Digital monitoring and analysis: at least 5 years in open-source research or intelligence (OSINT), platform-aware monitoring, digital content analysis, or narrative, trend or network analysis.
- Strategic communication and prevention: at least 5 years in strategic communication, prevention-oriented narratives, audience analysis or coordinated prevention approaches relevant to PVE.
- Legal, human-rights and ethical considerations: at least 5 years in legal, human-rights, privacy, digital-governance or ethical issues relevant to digital monitoring and prevention.
- Training design and adult learning: at least 3 years in scenario-based learning, adult learning or practical training design.

Arabic proficiency at B2 level or above and at least 3 years of relevant professional experience in Iraq or the Middle East are strongly preferred. The pool will include at least two consultants meeting each of these criteria. Candidates combining several specialisms are welcome.

jobs.title: Senior Research Monitoring Evaluation and Learning Officer
jobs.description:
**Role Summary**

Siren is seeking a Senior Research, Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Officer to join a dynamic, multi-disciplinary team to help us bring together evidence from across our work, identify connections and emerging insights, and communicate the wider story.

This role will connect information across project activity, identify patterns, tensions and emerging questions, and turn complex findings into clear, credible and compelling narratives for a wide range of audiences.

The successful candidate will be an excellent researcher and writer with a strong understanding of the Lebanese socio-economic and political context. They will combine analytical rigour with curiosity and judgment, helping teams, partners and decision makers understand not only what is happening, but why it matters and what to do next.

Siren already runs a robust MEL system, and we are looking for the right person to join our team and help us draw even greater value from the evidence we generate. This is not primarily a role for designing or administering a MEL system. The priority is to connect and interpret evidence across our work, identify the bigger picture, and communicate with clarity and purpose.

Want to learn more about us? Check our digital brochure: [https://materials.sirenassociates.com/brochure](https://materials.sirenassociates.com/brochure)

**Key Responsibilities**

**Insight, synthesis and learning**

- Bring together quantitative and qualitative evidence from across projects to identify cross-cutting patterns, relationships, gaps and implications.
- Interpret findings in light of Lebanon's political, institutional, social and economic context.
- Contribute to regular sense-making and learning processes that help teams test assumptions, reflect on unexpected findings and adapt their work.
- Frame forward-looking questions and practical recommendations for programmes, leadership and partners.

**Research and evidence**

- Contribute to rigorous, proportionate research using qualitative, quantitative and mixed methods.
- Develop research questions, methodologies, sampling approaches and analytical frameworks suited to the decision at hand.
- Undertake data collection, analysis and synthesis, ensuring quality, ethics, inclusion and responsible data use.
- Assess the strength and limitations of evidence, triangulate across sources.

**Communication and evidence storytelling**

- Produce excellent written outputs in clear, precise English, including research reports, project narrative reports, policy briefs, learning products, articles, presentations and public-facing content.
- Translate technical findings into accessible stories tailored to audiences ranging from the general public to Lebanese institutions, international governments and development partners.
- Use data visualisation and narrative structure thoughtfully to translate evidence.Work with technical and programme colleagues to ensure that external communications are accurate, useful and grounded in evidence.
Present findings confidently and facilitate discussion with senior and non-technical audiences.

**RMEL quality and collaboration**

- Support credible evaluation and learning approaches, including theories of change and contribution analysis, while remaining attentive to non-linear change and unintended outcomes.
- Support the strengthening of an organisation-wide culture of inquiry and learning.
- Manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality work when contexts, information and timelines shift.

## **Requirements**

**Essential**

- At least five years of relevant professional experience in research, evaluation, learning, policy analysis, applied social research or a closely related field. A relevant university degree or equivalent combination of professional experience and training.
- Strong understanding of the concepts and theories that underpin monitoring and evaluation practice.
- Demonstrated ability to synthesise varied and sometimes incomplete evidence, make connections across datasets and contexts, and generate useful insights.
- Strong qualitative and quantitative research skills, including research design, data collection, analysis, triangulation and critical appraisal of evidence.
- Excellent English writing and editing skills, with a portfolio of clear, engaging outputs for different audiences.
- Ability to communicate data through compelling narrative, well-chosen visualisation and concise presentation.
- Strong contextual understanding of Lebanon, including its institutions, political economy and social dynamics. Candidates do not need to be Lebanese.
- Experience working collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams and a range of senior, technical and community stakeholders.
- High integrity, sound judgment and discretion, particularly when handling sensitive evidence or relationships.

**Desirable**

- Professional proficiency in Arabic.
- Knowledge of security sector reform, security sector governance or public sector reform.
- Experience working with government institutions, civil society, donors or international partners.
- Experience with data visualisation, statistical analysis or qualitative analysis tools.
- A postgraduate qualification in social research, public policy, political science, development studies, evaluation or a related discipline.

**How we work**

Our approach is agile and multidisciplinary. We look for colleagues who act with integrity, stay curious and work cooperatively across disciplines. The Senior RMEL Officer will be comfortable making progress amid complexity: adapting as evidence changes and maintaining high standards when priorities or conditions shift. They will be intellectually confident and open to challenge, ready to test assumptions and attentive to perspectives that complicate the expected story.

**What success looks like**

- Teams and decision makers can see the larger story across projects, articulated in various reporting formats (contractual project reports, research pieces, communications products, data visualisation)
- Evidence reaches the right audience in a form they can understand and use.
- Learning leads to sharper questions, better decisions and timely adaptation.

## **Benefits**

***Competitive Employment Conditions***

jobs.title: Programme Development and Quality Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Overall purpose of the role**

The Program Development and Quality Coordinator (PDQC) is responsible for the coordination and management of key program processes, particularly in proposal development and grants management and reporting, ensuring timely reporting to donors, ensuring communication tools and strategies are in place. The PDQC contributes to increased quality by ensuring program coherence, adherence to program standards and appropriate learning from lessons learnt across the country program. The Coordinator is also responsible for donor compliance, application of correct procedures and guidelines, and liaison with support and partnership teams in support of grants processes.

**Responsibilities**

***Grants Support***

- Be responsible for the delivery of quality narrative reports, reflecting the progress and status of projects, in a transparent, timely and professional manner
- Contribute to addressing all comments and issues on proposals or reports, liaising with relevant Managers and finance to ensure coherence between financial and narrative reports;
- Ensure the DRC grants management system is regularly and fully updated. Includes Dynamics ERP system (creating grants, uploading documents, managing instalment tracking and billing rules, updating checklists and tasks assigned); internal funding tracker and reporting deadlines communications;
- Support grant relationships and communications with donors to ensure correct, compliant and smooth flow of information;
- Support the maintenance of simple grant tracking tools, such as reporting calendars, compliance trackers and MoV trackers.
- Support with communication and visibility tools and items as per donor and internal guidelines including their dissemination and availability to DRC teams and donors.
- Support / facilitate Go/No Go, Kick Off and grants closing meetings
- Help follow up on donor requirements, reporting deadlines and outstanding documentation.
- Support programme teams with questions around donor rules, budget flexibility and required approvals.
- Contribute to preparations for donor visits, TPMs, spot checks or other reviews.
- Support Grants & Business Development Manager in managing fundraising strategy, donor engagement plan, donor mapping by conducting research, maintaining and updating engagement plan and donor database.

***Program Development and Quality***

- Work closely with the Head of Humanitarian Disarmament and Peacebuilding (HDP), PDQS, and Programme Manager to transform content and conceptual designs into competitive final proposals responsive to the donor guidelines.
- Coordinate and provide oversight to all aspects of the proposal development process from the development of a writing guide, proposal calendar, through to delivery and timely submission of proposals.
- Review proposals for consistency with the requirements of solicitations, requests or calls for proposals, predicting or preventing bottlenecks in the proposal development process and securing the necessary information to complete process.
- Ensure the proposal development and project implementation process takes into consideration the mainstreaming of CHS, global cross cutting themes such as Age, Gender and Diversity, AAP, and lessons learnt from previous programming
- Help track donor visibility requirements and planned communication outputs.
- Support the collection of case studies, success stories, photos and related consent/documentation.
- Ensure that the Technical teams and Managers provide input into reports and proactively communicate planned requirements of program design and implementation to the relevant area and country office functions.
- Ensure an appropriate level of technical assistance and capacity building is provided to DRC’s implementing partners.
- Support the Operations Manager in monitoring of project technical goals, objectives and policies. Link DRC’s MEAL processes with HDP IM processes to establish clear ways of working and project implementation monitoring and ensure project data and indicator tracking are aligned with reporting requirements.
- Assess opportunities to improve program quality through alignment with DRC’s Programme Quality Framework
- Support regular internal reviews of project progress and outstanding actions.

***Program Support***

- Collaborate with the HDP tech team to ensure field-based implementation processes and documentation are properly managed and compliant with DRC requirements and sector best practices.
- When necessary, support HDP team in developing comprehensive procurement plans. Upon receipt of project related goods and services, collaborate with the logistics and procurement teams in quality assurance. From time to time, support or facilitate tendering processes, procurement committee meetings and in the review of bid analyses.
- Ensure development of work plans and budgets for DRC projects. Ensure that appropriate management systems are followed and that the programs make progress towards objectives.
- Capacitate field teams to manage timely and quality completion of program deliverables and reports in accordance with donor guidelines.
- Support the development of project work plans and contribute to development of performance monitoring plans.
- Provide support to project technical managers in the interpretation of donor guidelines in the implementation of project activities.

***Partnerships***

- Support the development of partnerships such as implementing partner identification and mapping, due diligence, support with selection, relationship management, capacity building and any closure processes.
- Support partners with reporting requirements, documentation standards and donor compliance where needed.
- Review partner narrative and technical inputs and provide feedback before consolidation.
- Contribute to follow-up on partner agreements, scopes of work and related documentation

**Qualifications, experience and technical competencies**

- Bachelor's degree in communications, political science, international development, law or other relevant discipline
- Minimum 5 years of UN/INGO experience in proposal writing, including conceptualizing and technical writing under strict deadlines with demonstrated success
- Excellent project management skills
- Recognized leadership role in program development and quality
- Ability to work rapidly with staff in the field directly, and remotely in writing and where necessary revising concepts, proposals and reports.
- Capacity to work in a multi-sector team, including coordinating technical input into proposals
- Familiarity with requirements of key humanitarian donors and capacity to work in a multi-donor environment, including EU/ECHO, FCDO, UN donors among others.
- Good humanitarian and development programming skills, including capacity to prepare logical, coherent and consistent documents including log frames.
- Communication skills: excellent written and articulate oral communication skills, particularly in English.

**Languages:**

- Excellent written and spoken English.

**About you**

*In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’s five core competencies:*

- *Striving for excellence:* You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- *Collaborating:* You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- *Taking the lead:* You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- *Communicating:* You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- *Demonstrating integrity*: Upholding and promoting the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to DRC’s values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**Conditions**

*Contract:* Six Months’ contract with possibility of extension, subject to funding and performance. Salary and conditions in accordance with the Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for International staff. This position is graded at Band NM.G

*Start Date:* November

*Duty Station:* Omdurman

Reports to: Head of HDP

jobs.title: Account Manager
jobs.description:
Overview of position

The Account Manager is responsible for the overall management and delivery of services to clients, ensuring CTG’s operations align with client requirements, contractual obligations, and financial goals. This role oversees the end-to-end management of assigned projects, including client engagement, scope management, compliance, and team supervision. As the primary point of contact for clients, the Account Manager is accountable for resolving issues and ensuring that recruitment, onboarding, payroll, consultant contract issuance, and reporting processes are executed efficiently and within agreed timelines. They balance client expectations with CTG’s operational and financial interests.

Role objectives

**Project Management**

- Lead initial client engagements, clearly articulating CTG’s services and project scope as per contract terms and conditions.
- Ensure alignment between the scope of work, client expectations, and CTG’s service delivery, proactively managing and agreeing on any adjustments.
- Act as the focal point for clients, maintaining strong relationships and addressing concerns promptly to ensure satisfaction and smooth project execution.
- Take ownership of issue resolution, ensuring timely and effective solutions related to service delivery, consultant performance, or client concerns.
- Monitor financial performance, ensuring proper management of costs, revenue, and resource allocation to maintain project profitability.
- Ensure the timely and accurate delivery of monthly reports to clients, covering key metrics such as headcount, payroll, DSA amounts, consultant activities, and financial status.
- Contribute to financial forecasting and planning for ongoing and future projects.

**Operations, Legal, and Compliance Management**

- Oversee recruitment, onboarding, payroll, and contract issuance processes for CTG consultants, ensuring efficiency and compliance with CTG policies and legal frameworks.
- Ensure all operations related to the project comply with CTG policies, local labor laws, and client requirements, including adherence to deadlines, quality standards, and financial controls.
- Support the timely and compliant onboarding of international consultants per contractual requirements.
- Ensure the accurate and timely issuance of consultant contracts, ensuring compliance with CTG policies, local labor laws, and client agreements.
- Provide regular operational and financial updates to internal stakeholders, including the Country Operations Manager and Regional Director, regarding the status of client accounts, project delivery, and financial performance.
- Proactively implement measures to prevent mismanagement of resources, client expectations, or deliverable
- Ensure strict compliance with CTG’s operational policies to mitigate legal and financial risks
- Obtain necessary approvals for any deviations from CTG’s standard operating procedures to prevent legal or financial repercussions.
- Notify in-country management of any client-recommended deviations from CTG’s processes.
- Report any fraudulent activities or irregularities to in-country management immediately.
- Maintain professional and official communication channels to avoid disputes with clients.
- Uphold CTG’s ethical standards, ensuring all interpersonal interactions remain professional, culturally sensitive, and aligned with CTG’s core values.
- Foster a respectful and inclusive work environment that acknowledges diverse cultural values and beliefs.
- Promote CTG’s values in all aspects of team operations and client interactions.

**Client Relationship and Communication**

- Serve as the primary liaison for clients, maintaining long-term relationships and addressing any concerns or issues that arise.
- Ensure clear and transparent communication with clients to build trust and maintain satisfaction.
- Take ownership of any challenges that arise in client relationships, whether related to service delivery or internal operations, and ensure appropriate solutions are implemented swiftly.
- Ensure that client expectations are met without compromising operational efficiency or profitability.

**Business Development Support**

- Support the establishment and growth of CTG's presence in Afghanistan by building and maintaining relationships with clients, partners, government counterparts, and other key stakeholders.
- Monitor the humanitarian and development landscape, identifying upcoming opportunities, market trends, and potential areas for CTG engagement, and share relevant intelligence with Country Management and the Business Development team.
- Contribute to business development efforts by providing local market knowledge, operational insights, staffing plans, and technical inputs for proposals, concept notes, and client presentations.
- Represent CTG at client meetings, coordination forums, and networking events to strengthen the organisation's visibility and develop strategic relationships.
- Support the mobilisation and operational planning of newly awarded projects, ensuring a smooth transition from business development to implementation.
- Work closely with Country Management and the Business Development team to support the successful establishment and expansion of CTG's operations in Afghanistan.

Project reporting

This position reports to Regional Operations Manager

Key competencies

- Outstanding people management skills and very familiar with delegation, performance management, and providing feedback and guidance to team members.
- Strong communication, problem-solving skills.
- Financial acumen, ideally with experience managing budgets and financial reporting.
- Proficiency in HR systems and Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint).
- Strong attention to detail, especially in managing contracts, consultant data, and reporting.
- Proactive and results oriented.
- Ability to work under pressure and manage multiple priorities simultaneously.

Team management

This role does not have team management responsibilities.

Further information

Female candidates are encouraged to apply.

jobs.title: Legal Officer, Competition and Consumer Protection (Temporary Job Opening), P3
jobs.description: Org. Setting and Reporting This position is located in the Competition and Consumer Policies Branch of the Division on International Trade and Commodities of the United Nations Trade and Development (UNCTAD). The Legal Officer reports to the Head of the Competition and Consumer Policies Branch. Responsibilities Within delegated authority, the Legal Officer will be responsible for the following duties: • Conducts extensive legal research and analysis and prepare studies, comparative studies, briefs, reports and correspondence on competition and/or consumer protection, including its relationship with trade and development. • Undertakes basic or extensive review of legal documents, instruments, or other material; identifies important issues, similarities, and inconsistencies, etc. • Prepares or assists in the preparation of drafts of background papers, studies, reports, legislative texts and commentaries on those texts, teaching materials in the field of international trade law and competition and/or consumer protection law for Government officials, enterprises, consumer organizations and academics. • Prepares or assists in the preparation of agreements and contracts with governments, NGOs and other public and private entities, as well as in the negotiation and settlement of claims and disputes and in handling private international law and international trade, competition and/or consumer protection law matters. • Services UNCTAD intergovernmental meetings dealing with competition and/or consumer protection law and policy, including the UNCTAD Intergovernmental Group of Experts on Competition Law and Policy and the Intergovernmental Group of Experts on Consumer Protection Law and Policy, including preparation of background materials, summaries of issues and views of delegations, meeting reports, etc. • Prepares programmes of technical assistance and provides substantive backstopping to technical assistance activities on competition and/or consumer protection laws and policies, including the organization of field national and regional seminars and workshops for Government officials, enterprises, consumer organizations or academics on competition and/or consumer protection law and policy, and training of officials responsible for application of such laws. • Prepares or assists with the preparation of international trade law seminars and symposia, lecture on various legal issues at such events. • Prepares inputs to for communication activities, speeches, statements and other inputs for presentations by senior staff. • Attends international, regional, and national meetings to collect information and to hold discussions with colleagues in other institutions. • Provides guidance to more junior staff. • Performs other duties as assigned, including a variety of administrative tasks necessary for the final delivery of the Branch’s services. Competencies • Professionalism: Knowledge of, and ability to apply, legal principles, concepts and procedures and terminology for review, examination, and processing of a range of legal documents, in particular on competition and/or consumer protection laws and policies. Ability to manage technical cooperation programmes on competition policy and/consumer protection. Knowledge of various legal research sources, including electronic, and ability to conduct research and analyze information on a wide range of legal issues. Knowledge of the civil law and/or common law legal systems and principles. Ability to interpret and apply legislative instruments, develop and present results, recommendations, and opinions clearly and concisely. Ability to draft legal papers and work under pressure. Ability to apply good legal judgment in the context of assignments given. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. • Communication: Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; tailors language, tone, style and format to match audience; demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed. • Teamwork: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others’ ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings. • Planning & Organizing: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. Education Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in international law is required. A first-level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Job - Specific Qualification Not available. Work Experience A minimum of five years of progressively responsible experience in law, including legal analysis, research and writing is required. Such experience in competition and/or consumer protection laws and policies is desirable. Experience in international competition and/or consumer protection research, policy formulation and analysis and technical cooperation and capacity building is desirable. Experience in intergovernmental support and project or programme management in the field of international competition and/or consumer protection is desirable. Either French or Arabic or Chinese (Mandarin) or Russian or Spanish is desirable. Special Notice This is a project funded position and its duration is subject to the availability of funds. The initial duration is for three months, starting in January 2027. The United Nations Secretariat is committed to achieving 50/50 gender balance in its staff. Female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply for this position. Candidates should have no expectation of any fixed-term appointment possibility after the end of this temporary assignment. If the selected candidate is an internal staff member of the UN Secretariat, the selection will be recorded as a temporary assignment. Subsequent to the initial temporary appointment, new and successive temporary appointments may be granted for service in the same office or in a different office any number of times, for any duration, provided that the length of service does not exceed the period of 364 calendar days. Upon separation from service, including, but not limited to, expiration or termination of, or resignation from, a fixed-term, continuing or permanent appointment, a former staff member will be ineligible for re-employment on the basis of a temporary appointment for a period of 31 days following the separation. In the case of separation from service on retirement, a former staff member will be ineligible for re-employment for a period of three months following the separation. A current staff member who holds a fixed-term, permanent or continuing appointment may apply for temporary positions no more than one level above his or her current grade. A staff member holding a temporary appointment shall be regarded as an external candidate when applying for other positions, and may apply for other temporary positions at any level, subject to section 5.7 below and staff rule 4.16 (b) (ii). Therefore, a staff member holding a temporary appointment in the General Service or related categories may only apply to positions within those categories. For full information on eligibility requirements, please refer to section 5 of ST/AI/2010/4Rev.1 on Temporary Appointments. In its resolution 66/234, the General Assembly further “stressed that the Secretary-General should not recur to the practice of temporarily filling posts in the Professional and higher categories with General Service staff members who have not passed the General Service to Professional category examination other than on an exceptional basis, and requests the Secretary-General to ensure that temporary occupation of such posts by the General Service staff shall not exceed a period of one year, effective 1 January 2013…” Consequently, eligible candidates in the General Service or related categories for temporary job openings in the Professional category that have not passed the competitive examination may be selected only on an exceptional basis endorsed by the Office of Human Resources Management where no other suitable candidate could be identified. While this temporary assignment may provide the successful applicant with an opportunity to gain new work experience, the selection for this position is for a limited period and has no bearing on the future incumbency of the post. An external candidate selected for this position is bound by the prevailing condition of the staff selection system under ST/AI/2010/3, as amended, and ST/AI/2010/4/Rev.1. A staff member holding a temporary appointment who is recruited in the Professional and above categories on a temporary appointment, and placed on a position authorized for one year or longer may not apply for or be reappointed to his/her current position within six months of the end of his/her current service. This provision does not apply to staff members holding temporary appointments and placed on positions authorized for one year or more in duty stations authorized for peacekeeping operations or special political missions. For more details on the administration of temporary appointments please refer to ST/AI/2010/4/Rev.1. For information on special post allowance, please refer to ST/AI/1999/17. Candidates may be subject to screening against these standards, including but not limited to whether they have committed, or are alleged to have committed criminal offences and/or violations of international human rights law and international humanitarian law. Candidates will not be considered for employment with the United Nations if they have committed violations of international human rights law, violations of international humanitarian law, sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment, or if there are reasonable grounds to believe that they have been involved in the commission of any of these acts. Due regard will be paid to the importance of recruiting the staff on as wide a geographical basis as possible. The United Nations places no restrictions on the eligibility of men and women to participate in any capacity and under conditions of equality in its principal and subsidiary organs. The United Nations Secretariat is a non-smoking environment. Reasonable accommodation may be provided to applicants with disabilities upon request, to support their participation in the recruitment process. By accepting a letter of appointment, staff members are subject to the authority of the Secretary-General, who may assign them to any of the activities or offices of the United Nations in accordance with staff regulation 1.2 (c). jobs.title: Project Coordinator [Open to Tier 1 & 2 applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Country Office in Tajikistan has been active since 1994 and is guided in its work by the Country Programme Document, which in turn builds upon the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP has made a significant contribution to developing the National Development Strategy, with an outline of policies and investments necessary to reach the SDGs by 2030. Together with the Government of Tajikistan, civil society and the people of Tajikistan, UNDP works towards identifying local solutions to global and national development challenges. Its main focus is reaching sustainable development by enhancing accountability of the current governance system, mitigating natural disaster threats, and contributing to environmental sustainability and biodiversity conservation.

The Climate Change, Energy and Environment (CCEE) Cluster of UNDP Tajikistan manages a diverse and growing portfolio of various projects currently under implementation across the country. The Cluster provides strategic, technical, and operational support to national counterparts in addressing Tajikistan’s key environmental, climate, and energy challenges, in line with national development priorities and international commitments. The Cluster’s programmatic focus spans several interrelated thematic areas, including climate change adaptation and mitigation, integrated water resources management, sustainable land management, urban resilience to disaster and climate risks, promotion of renewable and green energy solutions, and biodiversity conservation and ecosystem restoration.

In particular, with regard to biodiversity conservation and it’s biodiversity portfolio, UNDP's Country Office in Tajikistan is currently supporting the country’s National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) update and implementation in alignment with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF). As countries move from updating their NBSAPs towards implementation, targeted support is required to translate national biodiversity priorities into concrete actions and address critical implementation gaps.

In this context, the NBSAP Accelerator Action Account Multi-Partner Trust Fund (NBSAP AAA MPTF) provides targeted support to countries to accelerate implementation of their NBSAP priorities and translate national biodiversity commitments into concrete action. The Fund supports high-priority interventions that address critical policy, institutional, technical and financing gaps and that have not been sufficiently covered through other available resources. Its support is intended to strengthen national readiness for sustained biodiversity action, increase implementation ambition and create foundations for further investment in achievement of national biodiversity priorities and the KMGBF.

In Tajikistan, the project directly contributes to the objectives of the NBSAP AAA MPTF by providing targeted support for NBSAP implementation, with a particular focus on operationalizing KMGBF Target 6 on invasive alien species (IAS). The project will strengthen the scientific, technical and policy basis for the prevention, monitoring and management of IAS, including through establishment of a national IAS database and development of the country’s first State Programme and Action Plan on Invasive Alien Species. These interventions will help address critical data and policy gaps, strengthen national capacities for ongoing biological risk monitoring and management, and establish a more coherent framework for coordinated action on invasive alien species.

The project further contributes to strengthening the core functions of NBSAP implementation through institutional capacity development and strategic policy support, applying a “whole-of-government” and “whole-of-society” approach. It also contributes to KMGBF Target 23 on gender equality by integrating gender-responsive approaches and promoting the equitable participation of women and vulnerable groups within IAS knowledge, monitoring and policy systems. The initiative will additionally promote youth engagement and digital innovation in biodiversity information management, thereby supporting an inclusive, sustainable and potentially scalable approach to implementation of KMGBF priorities in Tajikistan.

Under the direct supervision of UNDP Programme Specialist on Climate Change, Energy and Environment, and overall guidance of the Deputy Resident Representative, the Project Coordinator will coordinate project interventions, liaise with national partners and support effective teamwork and strong partnerships. The Project Coordinator will provide technical and programmatic support to ensure the timely delivery of high-quality project results that strengthen national capacities, data systems and policy frameworks for the prevention and management of invasive alien species, in line with Tajikistan’s NBSAP and the KMGBF.

He/she will ensure implementation mechanisms and technical working groups are established and meet regularly, that all planned workshops, technical studies and other activities are organised in a timely manner, and that they meet expected quality standards. He/she will also specifically be responsible for outreach activities to relevant stakeholders, and the preparation of synthesis reports, policy briefs, press releases and briefing notes for Government, donor, UNDP, etc.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Ensure effective technical support to the project focusing on achievement of the following results:

- General coordination and liaison of project activities with national counterparts, scientific institutions and relevant stakeholders.

- Coordinate the development and validation of the National IAS Catalogue and Database.

- Facilitate the development, testing and validation of standardized IAS risk assessment protocols.

- Coordinate the development of the multi-sectoral National IAS Programme and Action Plan.

- Ensure alignment of the project’s technical outputs with the NBSAP, the KMGBF, national biodiversity reporting processes and other relevant national policies and strategic frameworks.

- Facilitate technical assessments, field data collection, consultations and other analytical work required for the development of the National IAS Catalogue, risk assessment protocols, IAS Database and National IAS Programme and Action Plan.

- Provide substantive support to project stakeholders in reviewing and validating technical methodologies, assessments, databases, policy documents and other project outputs.

- Coordinate project activities among relevant stakeholders, including but not limited to the National Biodiversity and Biosafety Centre under the Committee for Environmental Protection, National Academy of Sciences of Tajikistan, Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry Agency, Customs Service, Food Security Committee, other relevant ministries and agencies, civil society organizations, academia and local communities, as specified in the Project Document.

- Facilitate the establishment and effective functioning of the Multi-Stakeholder Platform and Task Force Group/Thematic Working Group for technical coordination, policy dialogue and development and validation of project outputs.

- Ensure the elaboration of the Stakeholder Engagement and Gender Action Plan before the kickstart of project implementation, and further ensure their effective implementation and regular monitoring.

- Ensure that gender-responsive approaches and meaningful participation of women, youth and vulnerable groups are appropriately integrated into IAS assessments, data systems, consultations and policy development in line with the project’s Results Framework.

- Coordinate and follow up on implementation of relevant environmental and social safeguard measures.

- Review all technical reports as required. Fulfil substantive activities under the Project Work Plan which are not covered by consultants or other contracted experts.

- Support the timely technical review, validation, finalization and submission to relevant national authorities of key project outputs, including the National IAS Catalogue, standardized risk assessment protocols, national IAS Database and National IAS Programme and Action Plan.

- Provide necessary inputs to showcase project’s experience at national, regional and international forums/events as required.

- Upon request of the Programme Specialist, participate in and make presentations at conferences, working meetings, workshops, round-table discussions and other relevant events on the IAS project and its linkages with biodiversity conservation, NBSAP and KMGBF implementation.

2. Ensure effective operational and programmatic support for the project:

- Ensure operational and programmatic coordination of the project in accordance with the Project Document, approved work plans, Results Framework and applicable UNDP rules and procedures.

- Support the overall management and coordination of project implementation, ensuring timely and proper execution of activities by consultants, experts, contractors and project partners.

- Prepare Terms of Reference (ToR) for national and international consultants, experts, contractors and other service providers in line with the Project Document and relevant UNDP procedures; coordinate and guide their work and ensure compliance with agreed work plans and respective ToRs and the quality and timely delivery of outputs.

- Facilitate organization of the project Inception Workshop and support the establishment and functioning of the Project Steering Committee, Multi-Stakeholder Platform and Task Force Group/Thematic Working Group.

- Support communication and coordination with government institutions, scientific organizations, civil society organizations, local communities and other stakeholders involved in implementation of activities specified in the Project Work Plan.

- Prepare meeting agendas and background materials, take notes/minutes of project meetings and ensure timely follow-up on decisions and agreed actions.

- Support preparation and implementation of annual and detailed project work plans, including monitoring of implementation progress and follow-up on planned activities and deliverables.

- Monitor project progress against the Results Framework, including achievement of indicators and targets, and coordinate collection, verification and consolidation of supporting evidence.

- Collect and analyze project-related data and information from government counterparts, consultants, scientific institutions, implementing partners and other relevant sources for project monitoring and reporting purposes.

- Assume responsibility for the timely preparation of project progress reports and other required inputs in line with the reporting requirements of NBSAP AAA MPTF and corporate standards of UNDP.

- Support preparation of the project’s final report and project operational closure upon completion of project activities.

- Monitor project risks and issues in accordance with the Project Document and risk framework and ensure that emerging risks are promptly brought to the attention of the Programme Specialist and relevant project governance bodies.

- Support regular updating of project risk log and follow up on agreed risk mitigation measures.

- Monitor project expenditures, commitments and balances against approved project budget lines and work plans and bring potential deviations requiring management attention to the Programme Specialist.

- Coordinate project activities with other relevant biodiversity, climate and environmental initiatives and programmes in Tajikistan to ensure complementarity, avoid duplication and promote synergies, including with NBSAP update and national reporting.

- Provide assistance and substantive inputs to the Programme Specialist in preparation of project briefs, presentations, reports, talking points and other relevant materials.

- Ensure effective dissemination of and access to information on project activities and results, and support project outreach and communication activities in coordination with UNDP communications staff.

- Liaise with the NBSAP AAA MPTF focal point and relevant UNDP regional focal point(s) to ensure effective project implementation, seek and follow up on technical and operational guidance, address project-related issues and queries, and ensure alignment with applicable programme requirements and guidance.

- Support resource mobilization efforts by providing inputs to the new project ideas, concept notes, funding proposals, and other relevant resource mobilization materials.

3. Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing and advocacy relevant to the assigned thematic area.

- Organize trainings, technical workshops, consultations, awareness-raising events and capacity-building activities in a participatory manner, involving relevant government institutions, scientific / academic institutions, civil society organizations, local communities, women and youth groups, and other stakeholders.

- Support capacity building of decision-makers and relevant technical institutions on IAS identification, risk assessment, Geographic Information System (GIS)-based monitoring, data management, use of the national IAS Database to be established under the project, and relevant NBSAP and KMGBF frameworks.

- Support development and dissemination of technical guidance, IAS field guides, training materials, project briefs, factsheets, awareness materials and other knowledge products generated under the project.

- Identify, synthesize and document good practices, lessons learned and implementation experience generated by the project and its partners, including through maintenance of relevant project knowledge and lessons-learned records.

- Participate in and ensure substantive contributions to relevant knowledge networks, communities of practice and technical exchanges on IAS management, biodiversity conservation and implementation of the NBSAP and KMGBF.

- Promote awareness and advocacy on IAS-related biodiversity risks, prevention and management measures, and opportunities for collaboration in coordination with project partners, stakeholders and UNDP communications staff.

- Support engagement of women, youth and local communities in knowledge generation, awareness raising and dissemination of biodiversity information, in line with the project’s whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office/Project and the Organization

Institutional Arrangement

The Project Coordinator will be based in Dushanbe, at the premises of either the National Biodiversity and Biosafety Center or the National Academy of Sciences, subject to management decision with frequent visits to the UNDP Country Office. Within his/her role, the incumbent will coordinate the achievement of the expected project results by providing strategic guidance to project staff and consultants and liaising among the targeted stakeholders to facilitate the implementation of relevant activities. The Project Coordinator will be accountable and report to the UNDP Programme Specialist on Climate Change, Energy and Environment.

Competencies

Core competencies:

- Achieve Results: ​​LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline​

- Think Innovatively: ​​LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements ​

- Learn Continuously: ​​LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback​

- Adapt with Agility: ​​ LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible ​

- Act with Determination: ​​LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident​

- Engage and Partner: ​​ LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships​

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: ​​LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination ​

People Management competencies:

- UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site .

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies:

2030 Agenda: Planet

- Nature Ecosystems and Biodiversity Programme: Protected and Conservation Areas and Systems

- Gender Gender and Environment

Business Development

- Knowledge Generation Ability to research information and turn it useful knowledge, relevant for content, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

Business Management

- Communication Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

- Partnership management Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

Business Direction & Strategy

- Systems Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced University Degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in Environment/Natural Resource Management, Biodiversity, Climate, Public Administration, Economics or related field is required, or

- A first level university degree (Bachelor's degree) in the fields mentioned above, in combination with an additional 2 years of relevant experience, will be given due consideration in lieu of advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Applicants with a Master’s degree (or equivalent) in a related field of study are not required to have professional work experience.

- Applicants with a Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) are required to have a minimum of two years of experience of working in nature resource management projects.

Desired skills:

- Experience in implementing multi-stakeholder initiatives that promote sustainable environmental management and biodiversity conservation.

- Experience in managing work teams and coordinating technical assessments, reports and technical documents.

- Experience in the use of computers and office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and advanced knowledge of web-based management systems.

- Experience in working with Government and a wide range of donors, the UN, international organizations, and/or civil society;

- Experience in Tajikistan biodiversity conservation and/or sustainable use programs or projects.

- Experience in analysis, research in the field of ecology, environment protection, sustainable resource management.

Languages:

- Fluency in English and Russian or Tajik is required.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

Data Privacy

jobs.title: ICT Analyst, Short-Term
jobs.description:
Background

Over the past three decades, corruption has remained one of the most persistent and structurally embedded challenges confronting the Republic of Moldova. The anti-corruption reforms initiated over the years have, for the most part, been normatively correct, yet lacking in real transformative impact in practice. At the same time, the phenomenon affected multiple sectors and manifested in increasingly sophisticated forms, ranging from petty administrative corruption to organised crime, large-scale fraud, and money laundering. The combination of perceived impunity, selective enforcement, and lengthy proceedings in corruption-related cases has contributed to a general belief that accountability mechanisms remain fragile. This environment has, in turn, affected citizens’ trust in the state’s ability to prevent, detect, investigate, and sanction corruption and related financial crimes in an effective and impartial manner.

In this context, UNDP has been engaged in the implementation of the EU funded “Support in Combating and Preventing Corruption and Organized Crime in the Republic of Moldova” project.

The project seeks to reduce corruption and financial crime, including money laundering, by strengthening effective, efficient, independent, and accountable justice, prosecution, and investigation systems. It responds to persistent weaknesses in Moldova’s anti-corruption framework, including fragmented institutional interventions, limited inter-institutional coordination, uneven implementation of integrity mechanisms, gaps in specialized expertise, and insufficient use of analytical and risk-based approaches. These challenges have limited the ability of public institutions to translate policy and legislative reforms into sustainable and measurable results.

The project is closely aligned with Moldova’s European Union accession agenda, the National Programme for Accession to the European Union 2025–2029, and the National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Programme 2024–2028. The latter provides the principal national framework for mainstreaming integrity and anti-corruption measures across public institutions, while the National Anti-Corruption Centre is responsible for coordinating, monitoring, and evaluating its implementation. The project will support the application of EU standards and relevant OECD and GRECO recommendations, strengthen institutional ownership, and promote preventive, risk-based, and evidence-driven approaches to integrity management.

Digital transformation will serve as an important enabling element of the UNDP-led component, supporting more effective monitoring, reporting, analysis and institutional coordination. The project will facilitate the development, adaptation and use of digital tools and platforms for cross-institutional data collection, visualization, analytical reporting, integrity monitoring, risk identification, learning and stakeholder engagement. This may include digital dashboards, improvements to existing governmental and civic platforms, online learning solutions, and interoperability between relevant information systems. The interventions will be developed in close cooperation with beneficiary institutions to ensure that the solutions are user-friendly, responsive to institutional needs, technically sustainable and capable of supporting evidence-based decision-making, policy adjustments and long-term institutional ownership.

Through these interventions, the component is expected to establish a more coherent, preventive and data-informed integrity system, improve institutional accountability and interoperability, strengthen national ownership of digital solutions, and enable public authorities to identify and address corruption risks more systematically. The ICT Analyst will support the implementation of this digital portfolio by ensuring that the solutions developed or enhanced under the component are technically feasible, secure, interoperable, user-centred and sustainable within the national institutional environment.

Duties and Responsibilities

The ICT Analyst will support the end-to-end implementation of digital solutions under the UNDP-led component, ensuring structured planning, technical design, procurement support, implementation monitoring and quality assurance in line with UNDP standards and beneficiary requirements. The Analyst will translate institutional and analytical needs into functional and technical specifications, support the selection and coordination of external service providers, monitor technical deliverables, and help ensure that developed solutions meet agreed requirements and are fit for institutional use.

The Analyst will also support testing, validation, deployment and handover of digital tools, including monitoring dashboards, analytical solutions, interoperability arrangements and enhancements to relevant government or civic platforms. Particular attention will be given to system usability, data quality, interoperability, sustainability, and effective knowledge transfer to beneficiary institutions.

Through this support, the ICT Analyst will help ensure that digital interventions under Component 3 are coherent, practical, institutionally owned and capable of strengthening data-driven monitoring, integrity risk analysis, reporting and evidence-based decision-making across public institutions.

In addition, the ICT Analyst will serve as the principal technical focal point between UNDP, the National Anti-Corruption Centre, other beneficiary institutions, government ICT entities, service providers and relevant stakeholders, ensuring that digital solutions under the UNDP-led component are appropriately designed, procured, implemented, integrated and handed over in line with institutional needs, applicable national requirements and UNDP quality standards

The ICT Analyst applies and promotes the principles of results-based management (RBM), as well as a client-oriented approach consistent with UNDP rules and regulations. S/he is responsible and accountable to the Project Board for the project results within the limits of the assigned project.

The incumbent is expected to exercise full compliance with UNDP programming, financial, procurement and administrative rules, regulations, policies and strategies, as well as implementation of the effective internal control systems.

1. ICT advisory and digital solution design:

- Conduct ICT needs assessments covering existing systems, databases, reporting processes, institutional workflows and user capacities.

- Translate institutional and operational requirements into functional and technical specifications for digital products and system improvements.

- Provide technical advice on the design and configuration of digital monitoring dashboards for the National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Programme.

- Support the development of digital tools for cross-institutional reporting, data collection, validation, analysis, visualization and preparation of data-driven reports.

- Support the configuration of dashboards for monitoring integrity and work ethics guidelines, mitigation measures and sectoral corruption risks.

- Advise on indicators, reporting templates, data fields, validation rules, visualization formats and access permissions.

- Advise on the use or adaptation of existing governmental platforms, including MLearn, reLAWed, e-Expertise and Particip.gov.md, where relevant.

- Assess interoperability requirements between project-supported solutions and existing government information systems.

- Advise on data governance arrangements, including data ownership, access rights, institutional responsibilities and data-quality requirements.

- Support the standardization of data structures, definitions and reporting formats across participating institutions.

- Recommend appropriate technologies, hosting arrangements, licensing options and maintenance approaches.

- Ensure that proposed digital solutions are user-friendly, accessible, interoperable and suitable for sustainable administration by beneficiary institutions.

- Liaise with third-party service providers and technical partners to ensure effective collaboration, coherent implementation

2. Procurement and vendor support:

- Prepare technical inputs for Terms of Reference, technical specifications, statements of work and evaluation criteria for ICT products and services.

- Define functional requirements, minimum technical standards, expected deliverables and acceptance criteria.

- Develop technical requirements for software development, dashboard configuration, hosting, system integration, maintenance and technical support.

- Support market assessments and comparative analyses of available ICT solutions.

- Review licensing, intellectual property, data ownership and maintenance provisions for proposed solutions.

- Participate in the technical evaluation of proposals, bids, demonstrations and prototypes in accordance with UNDP procedures.

- Prepare technical clarification questions and provide technical inputs during procurement processes.

- Review suppliers’ proposed methodologies, technical solutions, implementation approaches and deliverables.

- Liaise with service providers and beneficiary institutions to clarify technical requirements and address implementation issues.

- Review technical deliverables submitted by contractors and provide recommendations on their acceptance or revision.

- Provide independent quality assurance of the developer’s deliverables, verifying compliance with functional specifications and agreed standards.

- Review and validate system functionalities and workflow configurations delivered by the developer, flagging risks, gaps, or deviations in a timely manner.

- Support the project team with regular status updates, including progress tracking, identification of bottlenecks, and recommended priority actions.

3. Implementation, quality assurance and capacity building:

- Coordinate technical activities with the Project Team, beneficiary institutions, government ICT entities, suppliers and relevant development partners.

- Facilitate consultations between institutional users, policy specialists, data specialists and ICT service providers.

- Participate in technical working groups, project meetings and coordination forums, as required.

- Monitor the technical implementation of ICT activities and identify delays, dependencies and implementation challenges.

- Provide regular technical updates on progress, outstanding issues and recommended actions.

- Prepare technical assessments, briefing notes, progress inputs and recommendations for UNDP and beneficiary institutions.

- Monitor institutional adoption and use of the digital solutions, including functionality, data quality and user feedback.

- Document technical decisions, implementation challenges, lessons learned and good practices.

- Identify opportunities for compatibility and complementarity with other national digitalization initiatives.

- Perform other ICT-related tasks required for the effective implementation of Component 3.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The ICT Analyst will work under the supervision of the Project Manager and Effective Governance Cluster Lead, in close cooperation with Programme, Operations, Communications and other teams in the Country Office (CO) for an effective achievement of results, anticipating and contributing to resolving project-related issues and information delivery.

In addition to internal collaboration, the incumbent maintains effective working relationships with implementing partners, government counterparts, civil society organizations, and other relevant stakeholders. This includes participating in coordination meetings, joint planning processes, and field missions, where applicable. The role also involves contributing to knowledge exchange and lessons learned within the project and across the broader UNDP portfolio. Throughout the assignment, the Analyst ensures full compliance with UNDP’s operational standards and promotes the organization’s values, including transparency, inclusivity, and accountability.

He/She will be given access to relevant information necessary for execution of the tasks under this assignment. The PSA holder will be responsible for providing her/his own working station (i.e. laptop, internet, phone, scanner/printer, specific software, etc.) and must have access to a reliable internet connection. All communications and documentation related to the assignment will be in Romanian and/or English.

Competencies

Core Competencies

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Information Management & Technology - User Experience and Business Analyst

- Capacity to translate efficiently users’ needs into IT requirements around human-centered design principles. Knowledge of Oracle Cloud, Service Now, SalesForce.com, and Microsoft product an asset.

Information Management & Technology - IT Project Management

- Capacity to manage ICT projects, using IT methodologies and approaches such as agile deployment and/or waterfall system development methods. PMP and PRINCE2 certification or equivalent desirable.

Business Management - Project Management

- Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals.

Information Management & Technology - Solutions Architecture

- Ability to design and manage the Information system architecture supporting corporate business processes.

- Design integration strategies and approaches to integrate one or more applications or services to maintain a coherent and effective IT architecture.

- Knowledge of OWASP, ITIL, ISO/IEC 270002 and IT operations.

Information Management & Technology - IT Quality Management

- Ability to manage quality of IT services. ISO 9001, 20000.Certification in ITIL desirable.

Digital - Digital product management

- Ability to design and lead digital product development including testing, ongoing product iteration, product strategy and delivery.

2030 Agenda: People - Gender

- Inclusive governance and women’s participation and representation

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (Master’s Degree or equivalent) in Computer Science, Information Technology, Cybernetics, IT Management or a related field relevant to the position is required; OR
