jobs.title: Public and Digital Investment Specialist (Open to all applicants).
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is the United Nations’ lead agency on international development. We support countries and communities as they work to eradicate poverty, implement the Paris Agreement on climate change and achieve the Sustainable Development Goals. We advocate for transformative change, and we connect countries to the resources they need to help people build a better life. Additionally, UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan.

The UNDP Rome Centre for Climate and Energy (the “UNDP Rome Centre”) is the key platform for the strategic engagement between UNDP and the Italian Government. It focuses on the critical policy areas of climate finance, youth engagement in climate action, and energy for development. These objectives are pursued through the effective implementation of its four main programmes:

• PISTA (Platform for Investment Support and Technical Assistance)

• Youth4Climate

• Energy For Growth

• Digital Flagship

PISTA, the Platform for Investment Support and Technical Assistance, aims to mobilise finance for climate, energy and the environment. Specifically, PISTA aims to support projects that contribute to the decarbonization efforts of developing economies and to their transition to climate-resilient economies, and it aims to catalyse international financial resources toward these initiatives. Matching impactful projects with investors and capital providers goes hand in hand with the engagement with financial institutions - both institutional and private - at Italian and global level. In its current portfolio, PISTA is supporting 24 projects across Africa, to which it is providing technical assistance with the goal of strengthening their bankability - from developing financial models, to enhancing environmental and social impact management, to more ad hoc project supportYouth4Climate promotes youth engagement in climate action, contributing to SDG13. Youth4Climate supports the implementation of youth-led and youth-inclusive solutions to environmental and climate challenges, both financially and through capacity development. It also gives young people around the world who are committed to fighting climate change a platform to engage with policymakers and global leaders.

Energy For Growth (“E4G”) aims to promote access to sustainable energy in developing countries, contributing to SDG7. The goal of the initiative is to assist partner countries in unlocking finance to scale up the diffusion of clean energy solutions, increase access to energy and boost the energy transition. E4G aims to foster the mobilization of public and private capital toward projects aligned with the international policy agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals. It does so by connecting UNDP's capacity and connections in emerging economies and developing countries with the public-private ecosystem of Italy and other G7 countries, in the crucial sector of energy.

The Italy–Africa Digital Flagship is a key initiative under the Italian Mattei Plan, implemented by the UNDP Rome Centre under its Strategic Initiatives portfolio, it is delivered in close partnership with national governments, the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Italian public and private sector partners. It focuses on advancing digital public infrastructure, digital identity systems, agritech solutions, and data-driven governance, contributing to sustainable development and inclusive economic growth.

Duties and Responsibilities

UNDP Rome Centre requires an additional team member to work as a Digital and Public Investment Specialist to contribute to its growing pipeline of large, impactful, and bankable projects. The UNDP Rome Centre, through PISTA and other programmes, provides support to projects across sectors in the climate and energy space, helping them on project development (e.g., technical feasibility studies, financial viability assessments, environmental and social impact assessments, impact framework development, advanced stakeholder engagement etc.) and connecting such projects with financiers.

Among such projects, UNDP is providing preparatory phase technical support to the Government of Cote d'Ivoire under the Italy-Africa Digital Flagship Programme to translate strategic investment concepts in the thematic areas of climate-resilient agriculture, smart irrigation, AI and data innovation into structured, bankable and implementation-ready public sector projects.

Given the nature of the assignment, UNDP seeks to hire a specialist with experience in structuring public sector and public-private investment projects for multilateral development banks (MDBs), development finance institutions (DFIs), and sovereign or blended finance platforms.

The successful candidate will make a crucial contribution to the Digital Flagship and PISTA team as a technical expert. The Specialist will play a pivotal role in overseeing and managing the post-origination phase of projects, that is ensuring interventions are designed to fit Italian and international DFIs/MDBs criteria to unlock climate finance and lead the investment structuring in collaboration with relevant DFIs/MDBs.

The Public and Digital Investment Specialist will report to the Digital Flagship team lead, and will have a secondary reporting to the PISTA team lead; she/he will engage with other UNDP Rome Centre colleagues as needed.

The scope of work over the course of the period may vary depending on the specific assignment and development of the programme.

A. Investment Structuring and Bankability Advisory

• Contribute to quality-assure the structuring of the two investment packages so that they are suitable for appraisal, financing and implementation, in line with the project's objective of producing executive feasibility studies and investment-ready project documents.

• Support the definition of a clear and financeable investment perimeter for: (i) the integrated climate-resilient agriculture and smart irrigation package; and (ii) the AI and Data Innovation Hub.

• Ensure that technical proposals are translated into coherent investment packages with clear CAPEX/OPEX assumptions, implementation sequencing, institutional responsibilities, and financing pathways.

• Assess the bankability of proposed investments, identify critical gaps, and recommend measures to strengthen technical credibility, revenue logic where applicable, affordability, public value, sustainability, and implementation feasibility.

• Support development of trancheable and modular investment options to preserve financing optionality and enable phased financing and implementation, as envisaged in the project strategy.

• Ensure alignment of the financial structuring with likely appraisal requirements of CDP and other prospective financiers engaged in climate, digital infrastructure, agriculture, and public sector modernization.

• Based on the project’s needs, support the identification of suitable co-financing partners and windows, including MDBs, bilateral development partners, climate funds, impact investors, and other DFIs to move to financial close.

B. Appraisal Readiness and Transaction Support

• Review feasibility outputs to ensure they meet the level of definition needed for financing review, procurement preparation and smooth implementation without further design work, consistent with the project document.

• Contribute and support on due diligence expectations commonly applied by MDBs/DFIs, including requirements related to technical feasibility, economic justification, safeguards, climate rationale, governance, procurement, operations and maintenance, and institutional readiness.

• Support the development of investment memoranda, decision notes, financing briefs, and presentations tailored to prospective financiers and government decision-makers.

• Contribute to the packaging of documentation required for downstream engagement with financing institutions, including review of procurement strategy, implementation roadmap, governance arrangements, and risk mitigation measures.

• Identify issues that may affect appraisal timelines or financing decisions and propose mitigation measures early in the preparation process.

C. Coordination with Feasibility Study Teams and Stakeholders

• Work closely with the multidisciplinary consulting teams engaged for the agriculture-irrigation and AI Hub feasibility studies, whose scopes include engineering, hydrology, climate analysis, digital systems architecture, cybersecurity, institutional modelling, financial structuring, and safeguards.

• Participate in technical working groups, validation workshops, and review sessions convened under the project governance arrangements.

• Advise UNDP and government counterparts on strategic engagement with key sectoral ministries and technical agencies to ensure investment structuring is grounded in national systems, implementation realities, and institutional mandates.

• Support structured engagement with Italian partners and other strategic stakeholders to ensure alignment with financing priorities, appraisal standards and market expectations.

• Provide targeted advisory inputs for discussions with engineering firms, technology providers, agritech companies, cloud and data infrastructure providers, and other relevant market actors, in compliance with transparency and procurement rules.

D. Quality Assurance and Knowledge Contribution

• Provide expert review and written comments on inception, interim and final feasibility outputs, with particular focus on investment logic, financing strategy, implementation readiness and institutional sustainability.

• Contribute to the quality assurance of project outputs against international infrastructure and development finance appraisal standards, as well as UNDP's investment preparation standards reflected in the sample ToR.

• Capture lessons learned and good practices on structuring integrated public sector investments that combine physical infrastructure, digital systems, climate resilience and institutional reform.

• Contribute to internal knowledge products or strategic notes that may support replication of the model in other countries under the Italy-Africa Digital Flagship Programme.

E. Knowledge Sharing, Monitoring and Evaluation

• Monitor activities to track progress, results, and identify areas for improvement for assigned investment projects

• Report on project effectiveness and impact, contribute to the development of the PISTA's annual report by providing data and insights on performance of projects under the Specialist’s responsibility

• Assist with donor engagement and relationship management activities as required, including for the timely publication and dissemination of reports against the Digital Flagship and PISTA milestones and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).

• Contribute to knowledge sharing initiatives within the Digital Flagship and PISTA team and with UNDP Country Offices.

The incumbent may also be requested to perform other related tasks necessary for the successful delivery of the assignment.

4. Institutional Arrangement

• The incumbent will be office-based;

• The incumbent will report to the Digital Flagship team lead and will have a secondary reporting to the PISTA team lead, and will work in close coordination with UNDP Country Office, relevant UNDP technical teams, the Project Board, and the Technical Working Groups established for the two feasibility studies.

• The incumbent will be given access to relevant information necessary for execution of the tasks under this assignment.

• International mission travel may be required.

Competencies

- Core Competencies:

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

- Cross-Functional & Technical competencies:

Business Direction and Strategy-System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Management-Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritize and control the organization’s programmes and projects, in line with its strategic objectives and capacity; ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives and the maintenance of business-as-usual, while optimizing return on investment

Business Management & Partnerships Management: Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

Finance & Development Finance Expertise: Ability to develop and work with innovative financing mechanisms and instruments, e.g. social/development impact bonds, guarantees, climate finance, etc.

Digital & Alternative Finance: Ability to identify potential alternative forms of finance and mobilise them for the purpose of addressing development challenges. Ability to review the skills, capacities, procedures and protocols that are needed to enable new financial mechanisms, and to assess the risks, limitations and implications of using them. Ability to set up the processes and structures to design, test and implement new financial mechanisms, including managing outreach and stakeholder engagement.

Digital & Digital Transformation Design: Practical and strategic skills in digital transformation design for governments and organisations.

Business Management & Communication: Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. .Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in Finance, Economics, Public Policy, Infrastructure Finance, Engineering, Business Administration, International Development, or a related field is required, OR

- A first-level university degree (bachelor´s degree) in the above fields in combination with additional 2 years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of an advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum of 5 years (with master’s degree) or 7 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible professional experience in project development, investment structuring, transaction advisory, infrastructure finance, development finance, or related fields is required.

- Proven track record of experience in preparing, structuring, appraising or financing complex public sector or sovereign-backed investment projects, an emerging market or developing country is required.

- Demonstrated experience working on projects involving one or more of the following: irrigation or water infrastructure, climate-resilient agriculture, digital public infrastructure, data centers/cloud systems, innovation ecosystems, or public sector digital transformation is required.

- Strong experience reviewing or developing feasibility studies, business cases, investment cases, financial models, implementation roadmaps and procurement strategies for major projects in emerging economies and developing countries is required.

- Prior professional experience with, or directly advising on projects financed by, institutions such as the World Bank Group, African Development Bank, Islamic Development Bank, European Investment Bank, or other multilateral development banks and development finance institutions is desired.

- Experience with sovereign lending, blended finance, climate finance, or large public investment programmes supported by MDBs/DFIs is desired.

- Experience in structuring projects to meet lender appraisal requirements and investment committee standards is desired.

- Experience with entire investment management cycle including demonstrated ability to structure blended finance support and/or advisory services to enhance project bankability is desired.

- Demonstrated experience with safeguards, climate finance rationale, institutional assessments, and implementation arrangements required for investment approval is desired.

- Experience engaging public authorities, technical ministries, implementing agencies, and private sector actors to develop implementable, financeable investment projects is desired.

- Experience in Africa, including Francophone Africa is desired.

- Fluency in French is highly desirable.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP’s Rule of Law Programme in Pakistan is working to strengthen the rule of law and to ensure equal access to justice and security services, particularly for women and marginalized groups across Pakistan in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) including the merged districts (MDs), Balochistan, and Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT). In close collaboration with a range of government, rule of law and justice sector institutions, the overall Programme aims to enhance and sustain peace and stability for the longer- term in Pakistan.

The Programme activities and interventions therefore directly correspond with the government of Pakistan’s strategies and commitments to rule of law and justice reforms, as well as improving the efficiency and effectiveness of institutions to deliver accountable and affordable security and justice services to the public.

The Rule of Law Programme implementation is guided by the following four strategic objectives:

- Policy, legal and regulatory frameworks strengthened to warrant people-centered, equitable, timely, affordable justice and security delivery to all people with an emphasis on women, marginalized and vulnerable groups, and digital technologies.

- Capacity of justice and security stakeholders (duty bearers) enhanced to deliver inclusive, timely, and accessible services to all people with an emphasis on women and digital technologies.

- Capacity of women, and the most vulnerable and marginalized (rights holders) strengthened to access referral pathways to justice and security.

- Justice and security sector institutional facilities enhanced to deliver inclusive, timely, and accessible justice and security services, through women friendly and gender- responsive infrastructure development support with an emphasis on flood resilience and green energy.

Against this backdrop, UNDP actions and interventions are aimed at restoring public confidence and service delivery in the formal justice and rule of law sectors through a range of initiatives i.e. policy development and reform, fostering justice and security sector governance, as well as oversight and accountability at an institutional level with emphasis on inclusive and gender-responsive programming. The overall engagement strategy, therefore, involves both federal and local levels. The Programme is implemented in partnership with the Judiciary, Police, Prosecution, Prisons, Probation and Reclamation, Bar Associations, Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and the academia both at federal and provincial levels.

The Project Operations & Finance Analyst will provide financial management, operational coordination and administrative support for the effective implementation of the Rule of Law Programme. The Analyst will support sound budget planning and monitoring, financial analysis, forecasting, expenditure review, financial reporting, risk management, internal controls and the coordination of programme operational processes in accordance with UNDP rules, regulations, policies and procedures and applicable donor requirements.

The Analyst will provide advice and support to programme management on the efficient, accountable and timely use of programme resources and will coordinate closely with designated other team members and relevant Country Office colleagues to anticipate operational requirements, address implementation bottlenecks and maintain audit-ready financial and operational records.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Operations & Finance Analyst will report directly to the Team Lead – Programme Specialist. The Analyst will provide specialized financial management, operational coordination and administrative support for the Rule of Law Programme, helping ensure that programme resources are planned, utilized, monitored and reported in an efficient, accountable and compliant manner.

The Analyst will support budget preparation and revisions, financial forecasting, expenditure and commitment monitoring, financial reporting, internal controls, audit readiness, risk management and the coordination of operational processes required for timely programme implementation. S/he will provide regular financial and operational analysis to support management decision-making and promote value for money and effective resource utilization.

The Analyst will maintain effective coordination with designated other team members and relevant UNDP Country Office functions to ensure that financial and operational requirements are anticipated and addressed in a timely manner and that programme implementation remains consistent with UNDP policies, procedures and applicable donor requirements.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams and projects in multidisciplinary teams to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Manage programme financial planning, budgeting and forecasting.

- Support preparation, review and consolidation of programme budgets, annual workplans and financial plans in line with approved programme documents, available resources and implementation priorities.

- Prepare and regularly update financial forecasts and cash-flow projections to support timely implementation and informed management decision-making.

- Monitor budget availability and utilization across programme activities and cost categories and identify potential funding gaps, underutilization, over-expenditure or other variances requiring management attention.

- Support preparation and processing of budget revisions, reallocations and other financial adjustments in accordance with UNDP procedures and applicable donor requirements.

- Analyse the financial implications of programme implementation decisions and provide timely financial advice to programme management.

- Support results-based budgeting by linking financial planning and expenditure monitoring with approved workplans, implementation progress and programme priorities.

Monitor programme expenditure, financial performance and resource utilization.

- Monitor programme expenditures, commitments, advances and available balances on a regular basis and maintain accurate financial monitoring records.

- Review financial transactions and supporting documentation for completeness, accuracy, budget availability and compliance with applicable UNDP policies and programme requirements.

- Prepare periodic budget-versus-expenditure analyses and other financial management reports, highlighting variances, trends, risks and recommended corrective actions.

- Monitor delivery rates and financial performance against approved workplans and forecasts and follow up on delayed or outstanding actions.

- Support reconciliation and resolution of financial discrepancies, outstanding commitments, advances and other financial issues in coordination with relevant UNDP Country Office colleagues.

- Maintain financial information required for management oversight, donor reporting, audits and programme closure, and promote efficient resource utilization and value for money.

Support financial reporting, compliance, audit and internal controls.

- Prepare and coordinate financial information and supporting schedules required for programme and donor financial reporting, ensuring accuracy, completeness and consistency with UNDP financial records.

- Support compliance with applicable donor requirements and UNDP financial rules, regulations, policies and procedures.

- Maintain organized and complete financial and operational records and supporting documentation to facilitate accountability, verification and audit readiness.

- Support internal and external audits, spot checks, financial reviews and other assurance exercises, including preparation of documentation, coordination of responses and follow-up on recommendations.

- Support identification, documentation and monitoring of financial and operational risks and contribute to appropriate mitigation and internal-control measures.

- Advise designated other team members on applicable financial procedures, controls and documentation requirements and promote consistent compliance.

- Support financial aspects of programme closure, including reconciliation of accounts, outstanding obligations, asset-related financial records and final financial reporting, as required.

Coordinate programme operational and administrative processes.

- Coordinate day-to-day operational and administrative requirements of the Programme to support timely implementation of approved activities.

- Support operational planning and sequencing of finance, procurement, contracting, human resources, travel, logistics and other administrative actions in coordination with designated other team members and relevant Country Office colleagues.

- Maintain an integrated overview of key operational actions and deadlines and follow up on bottlenecks that may affect programme delivery.

- Support budget availability checks, financial clearances and contract-related financial matters while respecting the responsibilities of designated UNDP functions.

- Support programme management with administrative processes related to personnel, consultants, travel, missions, workshops and programme events, including budget planning, financial monitoring and coordination of required operational actions.

- Liaise with relevant UNDP Country Office operations, finance, human resources, procurement and administrative functions to facilitate timely and compliant programme implementation.

Provide financial and operational advice, quality assurance and management support.

- Provide regular financial and operational updates to programme management, including analysis of expenditure, forecasts, delivery, commitments, operational risks and pending actions.

- Support preparation of programme workplans, implementation reviews, management meetings and donor discussions by providing relevant financial and operational analysis.

- Contribute financial and operational inputs to programme progress reports, donor reports, briefing notes, presentations and other management documentation.

- Support periodic reviews of implementation arrangements and operational processes and recommend practical measures to improve efficiency, compliance and timeliness.

- Review relevant financial and operational documentation and support quality assurance of financial information, budgets, forecasts and supporting records.

- Keep abreast of changes in relevant UNDP policies, procedures and systems and applicable donor financial requirements and advise on their application.

- Contribute to a collaborative working environment and effective coordination between programme and operations functions.

Ensure facilitation of knowledge building and knowledge sharing and guidance to all stakeholders on financial matters

- Provide support in identifying training needs of UNDP personnel for the purpose of capacity development in finance compliance.

- Organize and conduct training for the operations/programme/projects staff on financial management and RBM. Assist in providing regular training and technical guidance/advice on audit and compliance matters, including implementation of Internal Control Framework (ICF).

- Synthesize lessons learned and best practices in Finance.

- Provide sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Rule of Law Programme is placed within the Democratic Governance Unit of the UNDP Country Office in Pakistan, and the Analyst will work under the supervision of the Team Lead – Programme Specailist and coordinate with designated other team members and relevant Country Office colleagues.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical Competencies Finance

- Financial planning and budgeting: Ability to create and manage processes to achieve UNDP's long and short-term financial goals, including through planning, budgeting, forecasting, analysing and reporting

Business Management

- Resource Management Allocate and use resources in a strategic or tactical way in line with business needs and priorities and principles of accountability and integrity

- Risk Management Identify and organize action around reducing, mitigating and proactively managing risks

- Operations Management Ability to effectively plan, organise and oversee different parts of corporate operations, simultaneously and in an integrated way, in order to convert the organisation’s assets into the best results in the most efficient way. Knowledge of relevant concepts and mechanisms.

- Systems Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

- Project Management Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals

Administration and Operations

- Inventory management Each office to ensure sufficient inventory items are available for use as well as reporting for items which are beyond the corporate threshold of $5K and above

Required Skills and Experience

Min. Education requirements

- A professional accounting qualification from an internationally accredited institute of accountancy, and/or Advanced (Master´s) University Degree in Finance and/or Accounting is required. Or a first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

- Candidates with professional accounting qualifications from an internationally accredited institute of accountancy will have a distinct advantage.

- Candidates with no professional accountancy qualifications, but with degrees that major in accountancy and/or finance must complete the Finance Training and Certification Programme (FTCP), if recruited.

- Candidates satisfying the two above criteria are exempted from undertaking the UNDP Advanced Accountancy and Finance Test (AAFT).

- Candidates with MBA or master's in finance with no accountancy qualification but with relevant experience must successfully undertake the UNDP Advanced Accountancy and Finance Test (AAFT) to be eligible for shortlisting.

Min. years of relevant work experience

- Minimum of two years (with master's degree) or four years (with bachelor's degree) of relevant professional experience in financial management, programme operations, budgeting, administration or related areas is required.

Required Skills

- Demonstrated experience in programme or project financial management, including budget planning, expenditure monitoring, forecasting and financial analysis.

- Experience in preparing financial reports, budget revisions, reconciliations and management financial information.

Desired Skills

- Experience in programme or project operations and administration, including coordination of operational processes and compliance requirements.

- Experience applying financial rules, internal controls, audit requirements and risk-management procedures.

- Experience supporting donor-funded programmes and working with donor financial and contractual requirements; experience with European Union-funded programmes.

- Experience supporting audits, financial reviews, spot checks or other assurance exercises.

- Experience using enterprise resource planning and financial management systems; including UNDP Quantum or comparable ERP systems.

- Experience coordinating with procurement, human resources, travel, logistics and other operations functions in support of programme implementation.

- Experience in financial analysis, cash-flow planning and preparation of management dashboards or financial monitoring tools.

- Experience applying UNDP financial rules, regulations, policies and procedures.

- Previous work experience with UNDP, UN agencies or international development organizations.

Required Language(s)

- Fluency in English and Urdu is required.

2. Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, and culture. Individuals from minority groups, indigenous groups and persons with disabilities are equally encouraged to apply. All applications will be treated with the strictest confidence.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

UNDP is the leading United Nations organization in fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and planet. Learn more at undp.org or follow at @UNDP

The project aims to strengthen social cohesion in Türkiye by supporting the effective implementation of the national harmonization strategy. It enhances opportunities for meaningful participation in social, economic, and civic life, with a particular focus on women. Through a combination of institutional support, community-based initiatives, and targeted services, the project contributes to a more harmonious society and improves well-being for Syrians under Temporary Protection (SuTP), International Protection Status Holders and Applicants (IPSHA), and Turkish Citizens.

To expand access to decent employment, the project reinforces institutional coordination, regulatory frameworks, and labour governance systems while facilitating work permits and labour mobility across regions. It provides market-oriented vocational training, counselling, and job-matching services—especially in the green and digital sectors—and introduces tailored measures to increase women’s employability, including addressing care-related barriers. In parallel, the project supports voluntary relocation by delivering comprehensive resettlement and integration packages that help SuTP and IPSHA settle in new locations and participate effectively in local labour markets and community life.

The project also enhances language proficiency by scaling up accessible language and literacy programmes, with dedicated support for women and girls through enabling measures such as child-care provision. Additionally, it strengthens social cohesion by addressing cultural and social barriers, discrimination, and misinformation that hinder the participation of SuTP, IPSHA in Turkish society. These combined efforts foster mutual understanding, reduce tensions, and create an enabling environment for sustainable integration and cohesive development. I

In light of the above, the Project Assistant will support the implementation and coordination of project activities at the field level

3. Scope of Work

Support the implementation and follow-up of project-supported activities within Premises of the Presidency of Migration Management (PMM)

- Assist in providing day-to-day technical and operational support to PMM personnel in the planning, implementation and follow-up of project-suported activities in line with the annual work plans.

- Support coordination and information exchange among relevant PMM units and project partner institutions to facilitate project-supported activities and coordinated migration management responses.

- Support continued collaboration between PMM and relevant labour market institutions on migrants’ access to formal employment, work permit-related processes, labour market participation and other related policy areas.

- Support the collection, compilation and follow-up of PMM inputs, comments and approvals required for project reports, guidelines, tools, presentations and other project outputs. Prepare routine working documents and inputs in Turkish.

- Provide operational support to PMM for project activities, including meetings, workshops, consultations, trainings, field visits, missions and other events organized in cooperation with PMM and relevant stakeholders.

- Maintain organized project-related documentation, correspondence, meeting records, approvals and supporting documents are properly filed at PMM databases, regularly updated in line with institutional procedures.

- Support the collection and compilation of sex-disaggregated data and other relevant PMM inputs on gender equality. Assisst in preparing factual background materials, as required for project-supported activities.

Support PMM’s activities on social cohesion at the central and provincial levels

- Support PMM in the implementation and follow-up of social cohesion activities and compile relevant information for their planning and evaluation.

- Support coordination and information exchange among PMM central units, provincial directorates, local authorities, civil society organizations and other relevant stakeholders involved in social cohesion activities.

- Assist in collecting and and compiling information on local needs, implementation challenges and emerging priorities related to social cohesion and local-level engagement.

- Assist in preparing activity concept notes, agendas, background information, participant lists, meeting notes and follow-up tables for social cohesion activities.

- Assist in collecting and organizing the information on lessons learned, good practices and implementation experiences emerging from activities carried out at the central and provincial levels.

Support PMM’s field activities, research, outreach and monitoring

- Support field-level research, outreach and monitoring activities by collecting and organizing information on migration management, spatial concentration, social cohesion, labour market access and other project-related themes.

- Assist in organizing and documenting field visits, monitoring activities, consultations, workshops, roundtable discussions and other meetings with provincial structures and local stakeholders.

- Support collection, consolidation and preliminary review of qualitative and quantitative information obtained from field activities, provincial institutions, stakeholders, beneficiaries and service providers.

- Assist in maintaining up-to-date tracking tools to follow up on field-level decisions, recommendations, actions, timelines and responsibilities.

Support inter-institutional coordination, partnerships and stakeholder engagement

- Assist with the regular communication among relevant PMM units, public institutions, labour market institutions, local authorities, civil society organizations, NGOs, service providers and other project stakeholders. Facilitate communication with UNDP and UN agencies through designated focal points.

- Support PMM’s coordination with institutions relevant to migrants’ access to formal employment, including labour market actors and public institutions responsible for employment, vocational training, work permits and social security.

- Assist in organizing and documenting coordination meetings, technical consultations, working group meetings and other stakeholder engagement activities carried out under the project.

- Assist in Maintain and regularly update project-related contact lists, stakeholder databases and coordination tracking tools.

- Collect, compile and follow-up on feedback, inputs and recommendations received from PMM, provincial institutions, project partners, stakeholders and beneficiaries.

- Collect and compile factual information and PMM inputs required for project communicationand visibility materials and follow up on relevant PMM comments and approvals

Support data collection, data management, analysis and evidence-based decision-making

- Assist data collection of project-related data and information from PMM units, provincial directorates, responsible parties, service providers and other relevant stakeholders.

- Support the collection, organization, review and presentation of data on migration, labour markets, formal employment, spatial concentration and social cohesion activities.

- Support the collection and updating of PMM-related monitoring information and provide the project team with the relevant data and inputs.

- Assist in compiling and and presenting basic information on the implementation of project-supported activities against agreed plans and indicators.

- Collect and communicate information on implementation challenges, operational issues and emerging risks identified through project-supported activities.

- Regularly update relevant databases, monitoring tools, activity trackers and reporting templates with information received from PMM units and provincial directorates.

Support the collection of information on relevant policy and operational developments

- Assist in collecting and compiling information on relevant policy, legislative, institutional and operational developments in the areas of migration management, social cohesion, spatial concentration, labour market access and formal employment

- Assist in preparation of summaries and background notes on relevant developments to support PMM and UNDP in adapting project activities to evolving national and local contexts.

- Collect and organize information on emerging trends, implementation challenges, risks, opportunities and good practices relevant to project-supported activities.

- Assist in sharing approved factual information and updates with relevant PMM units and the UNDP project team.

Support project-supported knowledge sharing and capacity-building activities within PMM

- Assist organization of trainings, briefings, workshops, consultations and capacity-development activities for PMM personnel, provincial institutions and other relevant stakeholders.

- Support the preparation and adaptation of training materials, guidelines, tools, presentations and other capacity-development documents developed under the project.

- Collect and organize approved project materials, lessons learned, good practices, tools and guidelines and support their sharing among relevant PMM units and provincial structures

- Assist in maintaining organized records of institutional and field-level experiences, lessons learned and good practices emerging from project-supported activities

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary by PMM and UNDP for the efficient implementation of project-supported activities.

4. Institutional Arrangement:

The Project Assistant will be based at PMM premises in Ankara for the duration of the assignment and will report directly to the UNDP Project Manager. The incumbent will work in close coordination with designated PMM counterparts and relevant UNDP project personnel.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The Regional Programme Management Support Unit (RPMSU) at the UNDP Bangkok Regional Hub (BRH) plays a central role in supporting the effective management, oversight, quality assurance, compliance, and performance monitoring of the Regional Programme (RP) and Regional Projects throughout the project lifecycle. RPMSU works closely with programme and project teams to ensure that regional initiatives are designed, implemented, monitored, and reported in accordance with UNDP Programme and Project Management (PPM) standards and corporate compliance requirement while promoting high-quality programme implementation and results delivery.

As BRH enters the implementation phase of the Regional Programme 2026–2029, there is an increasing need to strengthen evidence-based management, portfolio oversight, and proactive performance monitoring. At the same time, corporate requirements related to project transparency, data quality, risk management, quality assurance, results reporting, and audit readiness continue to expand, requiring greater consistency and accuracy in project data management and programme monitoring practices.

In responding to these needs, PMSU has led a series of initiatives under the Project Managers Peer Learning Network and the Regional Programme Digitalization and Automation Initiative to strengthen project management practices, improve access to programme management knowledge, and modernize RP monitoring systems. A key milestone of these efforts has been the development of the Regional Programme Performance Dashboard, which provides an integrated platform for monitoring regional programme delivery, pipeline management, portfolio performance, and management analytics through automated data integration and visualization tools.

To ensure sustainability and continuous improvement of these digital solutions, PMSU seeks a Regional Programme and Data Management Associate to support dashboard management, project data quality, transparency compliance, programme and project quality assurance, and regional project risk monitoring. The incumbent will work closely with Regional Project Managers and Programme Teams to strengthen Programme and Project Management and data management practices in corporate systems. The position will also support PMSU Programme Specialists in conducting RP compliance monitoring, programme and project quality assurance reviews, risk management exercises, and annual results reporting.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Regional Programme and Data Management Associate will work under the direct supervision of the Regional Programme Management Specialist. On the day-to-day basis, the incumbent will work closely with RBM Specialist and PA Coordinator as well as regional project team members and relevant Project Assistants / Associates to strengthen compliance with Programme and Project Management (PPM) requirements, improve data quality and transparency, support portfolio-level risk and quality reviews, and continuously enhance the effectiveness of the Regional Programme Performance Platform (RP³) as a management and decision-support tool.

Under the direct supervision of the Regional Programme Management Specialist, the Regional Programme and Data Management Associate will support PMSU in strengthening Regional Programme performance monitoring, project quality assurance, compliance oversight, and digitalization initiatives through the management of the Regional Programme Performance Dashboard and related data management systems.

The incumbent will perform the following functions:

A. Regional Programme and Project Database Management and Enhancement

- Serve as the focal point for the day-to-day management and maintenance of the Regional Programme Performance Dashboard;

- Monitor dashboard functionality, data synchronization, accessibility, and user experience to ensure reliable and timely performance reporting;

- Coordinate with ICT teams, data warehouse focal points, dashboard developers, and corporate system administrators to troubleshoot technical issues and improve dashboard functionality;

- Monitor project compliance with mandatory project setup and data management requirements reflected in the corporate Transparency Dashboard;

- Conduct periodic testing, validation, and quality reviews of dashboard data and analytics;

- Develop a set of data management guidelines (data governance) for both physical and electronic data including protocols for data entry, storage, security, and sharing, among others, to ensure data integrity and security;

- Develop a Data Quality Assessment (DQA) plan that sets the standards for data accuracy, consistency, and completeness—setting benchmarks and criteria for evaluating the quality of data;

- Develop data and digital products including, but not limited to, collection tools, dashboards, and reports, that are critical for accountability, transparency, and learning.

B. Regional Programme and Project (RP) Compliance, Risk Management and Quality Assurance

- Support RPMSU in monitoring compliance with UNDP Programme and Project Management (PPM) standards and procedures across the Regional Programme and Projects (RPs);

- Conduct regular RP compliance reviews and identify emerging compliance risks and implementation challenges;

- Monitor and track high-quality completion of project setup in Quantum in responding to PPM standards and corporate requirements;

- Support PMSU Programme Specialists in conducting programme and project quality assurance exercises throughout the project lifecycle;

- Review project management documentation and provide recommendations to improve compliance, project design quality, implementation effectiveness, and results reporting;

- Support PMSU in strengthening regional project risk management practices;

- Monitor regional projects risk treatments using the Regional Programme Risk Dashboard and other corporate systems;

- Conduct periodic reviews of regional project risk logs to assess quality, completeness and updated risk treatment measures.

C. RP Management and Implementation Support

- Support the management and improvement of digital technology solutions, including POCOMAS and relevant web- based project results management platforms, to enhance scalability and sustainability in line with UNDP digital standards;

- Support the regional programme and project evaluations and results monitoring as assigned;

- Provide administrative support to assigned projects and GPN thematic areas by maintaining internal expenditure systems, reviewing technical reports and payments for quality assurance, coordinating follow-up with relevant units, and ensuring timely corrective actions;

- Make preparations for external and internal programme / project audits, and support implementation of audit recommendations.

D. Capacity Development and Knowledge Management

- Provide day-to-day guidance and capacity-building support to regional project teams on: Use of the Regional Programme Performance Dashboard Transparency Dashboard requirements Project data quality management Programme and Project Management standards Risk management practices Quality assurance requirements Develop guidance notes, SOPs, FAQs, job aids, and training materials related to project compliance, data quality, risk management, and performance monitoring.

- Support PMSU learning initiatives, including the Project Managers Peer Learning Network and Digitalization and Automation Community of Practice;

- Document lessons learned and good practices from dashboard implementation, programme monitoring, compliance reviews, and quality assurance exercises.

Competencies

Core Competencies:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

Cross-Functional & Technical Competencies:

Business Development

- Knowledge Generation: Ability to research and turn information into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need.

Business Management

- Project Management: Ability to plan, organize and control resource, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals.

- Digital Awareness and Literacy: Ability to monitor new and emerging technologies, as well as understand their usage, potential, limitations, impact, and added value. Ability to rapidly and readily adopt and use new technologies in professional activities, and to empower others to use them as needed. Knowledge of the usage of digital technologies and emerging trends.

- Working with Evidence and Data: Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions and supporting decision-making.

Digital & Innovation

- Data strategy and management: Knowledge to draft or execute a data strategy or a data management framework.

- Digital product management: Ability to design and lead digital product development including testing, ongoing product iteration, product strategy and delivery.

- Data governance: Knowledge of data science, skills to develop data management tools, organize and maintain databases and operate data visualization technologies.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Secondary education is required. OR,

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in Business, Public Administration, Law, Economics, Finance, Accounting, Political Science, International development, International Relations and Social Sciences or a relevant related field will be given due consideration but not a requirement.

Experience:

- Minimum 7 years (with secondary education), or 4 years (with Bachelor’s degree) of experience in project management, administration and financial management or closely related field is required.

Required skills and competencies:

- Experience in the usage of computers and office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.), database packages, and web-based management system such as ERP is required;

- Proven experiences in project management, knowledge-sharing and/or capacity building sessions particularly in the areas related data management and compliance assurance is required.

Desired additional skills and competencies:

- Experience in implementation support to development projects;

- Good knowledge of UNDP’s policies, procedures and practice including familiarity of ERP e.g. Quantum and Quantum+;

- Experience working with international organizations.

Required Language(s) (at working level):

- Fluency in English and Thai is required.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The Office of Audit and Investigations (OAI) reports to the Administrator and is responsible for internal audit and investigations services to UNDP and its affiliated entities. It is comprised of the Audit Section and the Investigations Section. The Investigations Section (OAI/IS) is charged with conducting misconduct investigations and with compliance review of UNDP’s social and environmental policies and procedures and has sole responsibility for the conduct of all investigations within UNDP.

In its performance of misconduct investigations, OAI/IS addresses allegations of misconduct, such as fraud, theft and embezzlement, corruption, abuse of privileges and immunities, sexual exploitation and sexual abuse, workplace harassment and abuse of authority, retaliation, or other acts or omissions in conflict with the general obligations and policies that govern the conduct of UNDP staff and other personnel. OAI also investigates allegations of fraud and other financial irregularities committed by contractors, implementing partners and other third parties, deemed to be detrimental to UNDP. OAI’s capacity includes specialized Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (SEAH), Information Technology (IT) forensics, Artificial Intelligence (AI), data analytics, and proactive investigations units and resources.

As the provider of a professional, secure and reliable mechanism that responds to and addresses reports of possible misconduct or fraud, OAI is the sole and centralized custodian of a unique dataset of information regarding possible irregularities across UNDP’s operations. As such, OAI has a role to play in providing real-time and data-supported advice to management on wrongdoing risks, controls, lessons and mitigation strategies, and to use this information to develop intelligence-led detection, diversion and proactive investigation strategies that prevent and deter wrongdoing without relying solely on received reports.

OAI conducts misconduct investigations in accordance with the Uniform Principles and Guidelines for Investigations endorsed by the 10th Conference of International Investigators, with the UNDP Legal Framework for Addressing Non-Compliance with the United Nations Standards of Conduct, and with the OAI Investigation Guidelines.

OAI’s Investigations Section has established Units, under the supervision of Investigation Chiefs, that are comprised of (a) functionally specialized teams and (b) regionally focused misconduct investigation teams. This structure facilitates the accessibility of specialized functions to the entirety of the Investigations Section under the guidance and leadership of a manager and ensures close and rigorous oversight of investigation matters, also under the appropriate level of leadership.

Duties and Responsibilities

As the Chief, Investigations, Unit 2, which is comprised of Misconduct Investigations regional teams and the Sexual Misconduct Team (SMT), the incumbent is charged with leading OAI’s misconduct investigations in Central and West Africa (CWA) and East and Southern Africa (ESA).

The Chief, Investigations, Unit 2, also operates within a cross-functional model to provide specialized investigation and policy support for Sexual Misconduct matters.

The Investigation Chief functionally reports to the Deputy Director (Investigations).

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

1. Leads Workplace Culture and Teambuilding

- Leads by example, setting the tone for the Unit. Consciously build a supportive, collegiate and positive team culture within the Unit, while supervising staff, promoting best practices, and fostering professional development.

- Works collectively and collaborates professionally with peers and the Head of Investigations to provide thought leadership and constructive challenge to ensure the Office is a dynamic, high-performing, reflective unit that keeps pace with best practice.

- As part of the management team, actively engages and promotes discussions aimed at continued improvement of the Office and the investigation function, ensuring highest impact and efficient, effective practices.

- Supervises staff and non-staff personnel in the Investigations Section and provides clear, fair, supported, and balanced performance feedback and reviews.

- Engages productively, professionally, collaboratively and efficiently with peers, team members, and parties internal and external to the Section to problem-solve as necessary, seek solutions and achieve positive and impactful collective outputs.

- Actively employs management techniques that ensure balance in prioritizing quality output of a high standard and a healthy workplace culture.

- Supports the professional development of staff and/or recruit appropriate personnel to ensure the Unit has the optimal blend of skills necessary to deliver high quality investigations and advisory work.

2. Leads Investigations Management

- he Chief, Investigations, Unit 2 manages investigations teams and the respective caseload, ensuring timely, professional and resource-effective completion and reporting of investigative activity. Assumes accountability for achieving investigation objectives and results.

- Ensures that investigative activity is performed in accordance with international guidelines, relevant institutional policies, and OAI internal policy at a high standard through close oversight of investigative activity and output.

- Leads, manages, and motivates a diverse team based in multiple locations; upholds UNDP and OAI values; sets the right tone for the team; and creates a working environment and culture where everyone can achieve their best.

- Produces, reviews, and ensures the team’s production of, well-evidenced, high-quality reports to form the basis for disciplinary proceedings and/or for referrals to national authorities for criminal investigation and prosecution, as appropriate.

- Conducts regular case reviews to manage the investigation caseload, monitoring the status and timelines of each case.

- Ensures that all appropriate lines of inquiry are identified and pursued; investigation resources are used effectively and efficiently to factually determine the issues relevant to an investigation; and matters are closed as expediently and efficiently as appropriate.

- Provides senior investigation expertise and advice to investigators on all investigative activity, particularly on complex, high-priority and/or otherwise sensitive cases.

- Enhances investigations by leveraging IT forensics, financial forensics, analysis software, AI applications, internal data, open-source tools and information, while adhering to applicable information security and confidentiality principles.

- Ensures the appropriate collection, recording, handling, and securing of evidence.

- Ensures the application of specialist investigation services as and when appropriate (e.g., handwriting analysis, document examination, financial forensics).

- Oversees and, in exceptional circumstances, conducts professional, thorough and timely interviews of witnesses showing appropriate communications skills, accurate recording and verification of testimony using interpreters as required, in accordance with applicable Investigations Section policies.

- Oversees and, in exceptional circumstances, conducts professional, thorough and timely interviews of subjects in accordance with generally accepted best practice procedures in order to obtain reliable information relating to specific allegations of misconduct, while affording due process, in accordance with applicable Investigations Section policies.

- Oversees and, in exceptional circumstances, undertakes, as required, missions to UNDP offices worldwide, including areas with hazardous working conditions.

- Oversees, reviews, and, in exceptional circumstances, undertakes the drafting of investigation reports and other written output of a high standard that require minimal further editing and provide an objective and factual summary of the investigation, with soundly based conclusions and recommendations supported by all evidence obtained in the course of the investigation.

- Ensures accurate and timely maintenance and updating of information held in the investigative database, case files, and evidentiary records, as related to cases under incumbent’s oversight.

- Operates with a cross-functional approach by assisting other investigative units within OAI.

- Improves OAI's capacity to perform thorough and professional investigations through knowledge-sharing and training programs.

- Identifies and addresses underperformance, skills gaps, or conduct issues at first instance through coaching, feedback, and performance management measures, in accordance with UNDP procedures where required.

- Supports the professional development of team members through mentoring, on-the-job guidance, and contributions to performance assessments and development planning.

- Undertakes missions to UNDP offices worldwide, including areas with hazardous working conditions.

3. Ensures Effective Management of the Sexual Misconduct Team (SMT)

- Oversees and manages investigations into allegations of sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse within UNDP's operations.

- Ensures the overall management of the OAI SMT response.

- Oversees the investigation caseload, monitoring the status and timelines of each case

- Provides expert guidance to UNDP’s SMT, other OAI investigative teams, and institutional key stakeholders in handling sensitive cases of sexual misconduct.

- Liaises with the UNDP Sexual Misconduct Taskforce, the Office of Legal Services, the Office of Human Resources, the Ethics Office, and other relevant offices in UNDP, on matters related to SMT cases.

- Assesses the potential for sexual misconduct and other misconduct in UNDP offices and operations and provides advisory services to the relevant organizational units to mitigate emerging and actualized risks.

4. Provide leadership and management of high-quality client services, ensuring strategic coordination

- Maintains a role as a visible, active and accessible regional representative, including by liaising with senior officials within the region and bureau; sharing insights from the regional caseload with senior managers; receiving and considering feedback on investigation services; participating in regional or country level conferences or meetings to raise awareness of OAI services.

- Negotiates and liaises with officials from governments, national and international agencies, stakeholders, and partner organizations on investigation-related matters.

- Oversees planning of investigation missions as necessary with investigators, Country Office management, UNDP Security and other stakeholders.

- Liaises with the Office of Legal Services (OLS), the Ethics Office, the Procurement Support Office, operational units and Country Offices, the Social and Environmental Compliance Unit and other relevant business units in UNDP.

- Liaises with the investigation sections of other international organizations and with national anti-corruption and law enforcement agencies as appropriate.

5. Represents OAI, Risk Management and Facilitate Knowledge Management

- Represents OAI at the United Nations Representatives of Investigative Services(UNRIS), the Conference of International Investigators (CII), and other forums, as required.

- Contributes to the ongoing development of professional practices within OAI and UNDP’s management practice and stays abreast of developments in the investigation field.

- Participates in the implementation of his/her personal learning and training development plan.

- Provides testimony at relevant tribunals, as required and as appropriate relative to tasks overseen, performed, or over which the incumbent has qualification and expertise.

- Provides timely information to OAI senior management on investigation-related matters and ad-hoc assignments.

- Prepares risk-based information for dissemination to stakeholders at different levels in UNDP for continuous improvement of risk management.

- Implements and enforces appropriate measures to ensure handling of all investigation-related information in accordance with appropriate confidentiality requirements.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: Supervision and performance management of Investigations Specialists, Investigations Analyst(s), Non-personnel, Interns

Competencies

Core:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact.

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems.

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences.

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands.

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results.

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration.

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity.

People Management:

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

Cross Functional and Technical:

- Investigation - Investigation management and investigative techniques: The ability to manage an investigation, choose avenues of inquiry and apply different techniques during an investigation, including investigative interviewing; seizure of documentary and electronic evidence; identification, collection, review and analysis of all types of evidence, including project, procurement and commercial business documentation and electronic communications; forensic analysis; verification site visits; open-source research.

- Investigation - Collection and analysis of evidence: Ability to extract and analyze all relevant types of evidence and be able to draw reasonable inferences and conclusions.

- Investigation - Investigative Interviewing: Ability to conduct investigative interviews with all types of investigation participants, including witnesses and subjects, using an approach tailored to the interviewee and the investigation.

- Investigation - Technology tools and applications for investigations: Ability to understand key application and system software, IT infrastructure, IT Control frameworks and the use of forensic investigation software.

- Business Management - System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

- Business Management - Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity. Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management.

- Business Direction & Strategy - Business Acumen: Ability to understand and deal with a business situation in a manner that is likely to lead to a good outcome. Ability to make good judgments and quick decisions within such frameworks. Knowledge and understanding of the operational frameworks in the organization.

- A first level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the fields of study mentioned above, in combination with an additional two (2) years of qualifying experience, which will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- A minimum of 10 years (with master’s degree) or 12 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible professional experience in the field of complex criminal and administrative investigations is required.

- Experience in conducting criminal and/or administrative investigations across multiple geographic locations and conducting quality assurance reviews and legal assessments in the field of investigations is required.

- Experience in supervising a team of investigators and managing a large and varied caseload of administrative or criminal investigations is required.

- Experience designing and executing risk assessment frameworks to manage and prioritize a high-volume portfolio of complex administrative, misconduct, fraud, corruption, sexual misconduct, or safeguarding investigations is desired.

- Experience providing strategic advice to senior leadership on sensitive investigative matters and organizational risk is desired.

- Experience in policy development through consultation and collaboration with institutional partners is desired.

- Experience leading or supervising complex investigations into sexual misconduct, applying victim-centered methodologies, is desired.

- Experience conducting field-based investigations in complex, high-risk, or fragile/conflict-affected operational environments is desired.

- Proficiency in leveraging data analytics, digital evidence, artificial intelligence applications, and forensic resources to enhance investigative outcomes is desired.
