jobs.title: Associado(a) de Cerimonial e Eventos (1 vaga) (Home Based) - [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

Este processo seletivo busca contratar profissionais para atuar de forma compartilhada no apoio técnico e operacional de duas iniciativas estratégicas desenvolvidas no âmbito da parceria de cooperação técnica internacional entre o Programa das Nações Unidas para o Desenvolvimento (PNUD) e o Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ):

- Justiça 4.0: o Programa, iniciado em 2020, visa desenvolver e aprimorar soluções tecnológicas para tornar os serviços oferecidos pela Justiça brasileira mais eficientes, eficazes e acessíveis à população, além de otimizar a gestão processual para magistrados(as), servidores(as), advogados(as) e demais atores do sistema de Justiça. O Justiça 4.0 é um dos maiores programas de transformação digital do Poder Judiciário e também dialoga com os Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável e com a Agenda 2030 da ONU.

- Justiça [+Segura]: firmado em 2025, o Programa foca no fortalecimento da segurança cibernética no Poder Judiciário. O Justiça [+Segura] desenvolve e implementa ferramentas e estratégias para o fortalecimento da segurança cibernética, da preservação digital e da integridade da informação, ampliando a proteção dos sistemas e dos usuários do Judiciário. A iniciativa fortalece a segurança institucional e promove a transparência, a boa governança e a eficiência dos processos judiciais, contribuindo para a economia de recursos e para uma atuação mais ágil da Justiça em benefício dos cidadãos e da sociedade. Nesse cenário, o(a) profissional integrará a equipe compartilhada dos programas, atuando sob a supervisão direta da Unidade de Gestão de Projetos do PNUD e em estreita articulação com as coordenações técnicas do CNJ, com o propósito de garantir a excelência operacional, a sinergia entre as ações e o alcance dos resultados pactuados.

Duties and Responsibilities

O(a) Associado(a) de Cerimonial e Eventos será responsável por apoiar o planejamento, a organização e a execução de eventos e missões institucionais no âmbito dos programas e projetos, assegurando a adequada articulação logística, protocolar e administrativa, em estreita coordenação com as equipes do CNJ e do PNUD. A posição será exercida em regime remoto, sendo requisito que o(a) candidato(a) tenha residência no Brasil. Quando houver necessidade de cobertura presencial de eventos, poderão ser realizadas viagens nacionais, com as despesas correspondentes custeadas pelo projeto.

Para o alcance desse objetivo, o(a) profissional desempenhará as seguintes responsabilidades principais e atividades:

1. Planejamento e coordenação operacional de eventos institucionais:

- Planejar e executar as atividades e fluxos logísticos dos eventos no âmbito dos programas e projetos, em especial aqueles realizados em articulação com tribunais parceiros;

- Garantir o alinhamento das ações com os cronogramas, diretrizes e objetivos previstos para cada evento, em colaboração com a Secretaria de Cerimonial e Eventos do CNJ e equipes envolvidas;

- Organizar reuniões periódicas de alinhamento com as equipes internas e externas, visando assegurar a conformidade dos aspectos protocolares, cerimoniais e logísticos dos eventos.

2. Elaboração e gestão de documentos protocolares e administrativos:

- Elaborar e organizar planos de execução, cronogramas operacionais e formulários de coleta de dados para eventos;

- Redigir e estruturar documentos protocolares e cerimoniais, incluindo roteiros, scripts, nominatas, lista de autoridades e termos afins;

- Estruturar e manter planilhas de controle, cadastros de viajantes, listas de participantes e relatórios executivos de pós-evento.

3. Gestão de processos de compras, contratações e suprimentos para eventos:

- Conduzir e acompanhar os processos administrativos necessários para a realização de eventos e missões institucionais;

- Realizar prospecção e pesquisa de mercado de fornecedores e prestadores de serviços (locação de espaços, equipamentos, tradução, cenografia, hospedagem e correlatos);

- Apoiar a instrução de processos de contratação de bens e serviços, em estreita colaboração com a Unidade de Gestão de Projetos do PNUD e segundo as normas aplicáveis.

4. Orientação administrativa e acompanhamento de prestação de contas:

- Orientar palestrantes, participantes e fornecedores contratados sobre as normas e procedimentos administrativos e de prestação de contas após a realização das atividades;

- Conferir documentações comprobatórias de despesas, passagens, diárias e notas fiscais de fornecedores;

- Acompanhar e consolidar os fluxos de liquidação e prestação de contas em colaboração direta com a Unidade de Gestão de Projetos do PNUD.

5. Suporte operacional in loco e acompanhamento de missões:

- Realizar acompanhamento presencial de agendas, missões técnicas e eventos de âmbito nacional e internacional;

- Prestar suporte administrativo, logístico e operacionaldurante a execução dos eventos para a resolução tempestiva de eventuais intercorrências;

- Apoiar a articulação interinstitucional e a negociação de entregas e serviços relacionados às agendas externas dos projetos.

6. Gestão do conhecimento, monitoramento e guarda de registros:

- Coletar dados e aplicar instrumentos de monitoramento e avaliação de satisfação e resultados dos eventos realizados;

- Manter organizados e atualizados os arquivos físicos e digitais contendo os registros técnicos, fotográficos e documentais dos eventos;

- Apoiar a equipe de comunicação e gestão do conhecimento na consolidação de relatórios e divulgação de resultados.

O(a) titular desempenhará outras funções dentro do seu perfil funcional que considere necessárias ao bom funcionamento do Projeto.

Arranjo Institucional

O(a) contratado(a) será supervisionado(a) pela Analista Técnica de Gestão e Ações Estratégicas.

Competências

Alcançar Resultados: NÍVEL 2: Escalar soluções, simplificar os processos, equilibrar o tempo e precisão na realização do trabalho

Pensamento Inovador: NÍVEL 2: Oferecer novas ideias/aberto a novas abordagens, demonstrar pensamento sistémico/integrado

Aprendizagem Contínua: NÍVEL 2: Oferece novas ideias, aprende com os outros e apoia a sua aprendizagem

Adaptar com Agilidade: NÍVEL 2: Adaptar a novas processos, envolvendo outras pessoas no processo de mudança

Atuar com determinação: NÍVEL 2: Capaz de perseverar e lidar com múltiplas fontes de pressão simultaneamente

Engajar-se e ser Parceiro: NÍVEL 2: É facilitador/integrador, aproxima pessoas, constrói/ mantém coligações /parcerias

Promover Diversidade e Inclusão: NÍVEL 2: Facilita conversas para superar diferenças e considerar na tomada de decisões

Competências multifuncionais e técnicas

Direção e Estratégia de Negócios | Pensamento Estratégico

Desenvolver estratégias eficazes e planos prioritários alinhados com a missão e os objetivos do PNUD, baseando-se em uma análise sistêmica de desafios, oportunidades e riscos potenciais; conectar a visão geral à realidade no campo para criar soluções tangíveis e direcionadas; aprender a partir de diversas fontes para antecipar e responder de forma eficaz às tendências atuais e futuras; demonstrar capacidade de previsão.

Direção e Estratégia de Negócio | Perspicácia Empresarial

Capacidade de compreender e lidar com situações de negócios de forma a alcançar bons resultados. Habilidade para tomar boas decisões e fazer julgamentos rápidos dentro de tais contextos. Conhecimento e compreensão dos marcos operacionais da organização.

Desenvolvimento de Negócios | Design Centrado no Humano

Capacidade de desenvolver soluções para problemas envolvendo a perspectiva humana em todas as etapas do processo de resolução. Conhecimento e compreensão dos princípios e práticas de design centrado no ser humano.

Gestão de Negócios | Gestão de projetos

Capacidade de planejar, organizar, priorizar e controlar recursos, procedimentos e protocolos para alcançar objetivos específicos.

Gestão de Negócios | Trabalhar com evidências e dados

Capacidade de inspecionar, limpar, transformar e modelar dados com o objetivo de descobrir informações úteis, informar conclusões e apoiar a tomada de decisões.

Agenda 2030: Paz | Estado de Direito, Segurança e Direitos Humanos

Instituições Eficazes do Setor de Justiça

Agenda 2030: Paz | Estado de Direito, Segurança e Direitos Humanos

Habilidades e experiência necessárias

Requisitos mínimos de educação:

- Diploma do Ensino Médio é requerido;

- Diploma Universitário (Ensino Superior) nas áreas de Administração, Relações Internacionais, Comunicação, Ciências Sociais ou áreas afins será dada a devida consideração, mas não é um requisito.

Anos mínimos de experiência profissional relevante:

jobs.title: Programme Analyst -Transparency Global Support Programme (Open to all applicants).
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan.

Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policy and guidance to support the results of UNDP's Strategic Plan. BPPS's staff provides technical advice to Country Offices, advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas. BPPS works closely with UNDP's Crisis Bureau (CB) to support emergency and crisis response. BPPS ensures that issues of risk are fully integrated into UNDP's development programmes. BPPS assists UNDP and partners to achieve higher quality development results through an integrated approach that links results-based management and performance monitoring with more effective and new ways of working. BPPS supports UNDP and partners to be more innovative, knowledge and data driven including in its programme support efforts.

The newly established UNDP Planet Hub will drive UNDP’s vision of a world where economies and ecosystems thrive together — where energy systems are clean and accessible, nature is protected and restored, communities are resilient to climate impacts, and pollution is minimized. By 2030, the Hub seeks to help countries achieve this vision through systemic change that aligns policy, finance, integrated solutions, and societal ownership to advance sustainable human development. Backed by diverse partnerships and funding sources, the Planet Hub combines thought leadership, technical expertise, and strategic collaboration to help countries advance their environmental and economic goals.

The Planet Hub will build on UNDP’s existing portfolio of over USD 5 billion in over 140 countries, as well as on key offers across UNDP. The Planet Hub’s theory of change rests on five mutually reinforcing service lines that together enable systemic transformation:

- Intergovernmental and UN System Coherence and Support

- National Policies, Strategies, and Planning

- Innovative and Integrated Solutions

- Scaled-up Finance

- Insights, Modeling, and Data

The Planet Hub will be made up of eight interconnected pillars, covering strategic areas of work to deliver its core objective, as well as a set of integrated functions and support that cut across pillars and help ensure cohesive offers and delivery of the Planet Hub. One critical component of the Planet Hub is the portfolio of support to countries on Climate and Nature Policy. The Climate and Nature Policy Pillar provides strategic leadership on integrated climate and nature policy development, implementation, and advocacy, supporting countries to address interconnected environmental challenges while advancing sustainable development objectives. The Pillar brings together expertise on climate policy, biodiversity policy, environmental governance, integrated planning frameworks, Multilateral Environmental Agreements, and science-policy interfaces. Working across all Planet Hub pillars and in close collaboration with governments, UN entities, international organizations, research institutions, and development partners, the Pillar promotes policy coherence, strengthens implementation of global environmental commitments, and supports countries in developing integrated approaches to climate action, biodiversity conservation, ecosystem resilience, and sustainable development.

Climate Transparency and implementation of Paris Agreement’s Enhanced Transparency Framework (ETF) are paramount to the vision of the Policies pillar, under the Planet Hub. UNDP has extensive experience supporting developing countries to meet international climate reporting requirements and works closely with UNFCCC, UNEP, GEF and other partners in this area.

The Climate Transparency - Global Support Programme Phase III (GSP III) will be jointly implemented by UNDP and United Nations Environment Programme UNEP (through UNEP United Nations Environment Programme

(CCC)), with project management and coordination responsibilities shared between UNDP and UNEP. Effective delivery therefore requires close day-to-day collaboration between the UNDP and UNEP teams, as well as coordinated engagement with the project's governance bodies, regional networks and technical partners.

In this context, UNDP is recruiting a Programme Analyst -Transparency Global Support Programme who will maintain and analyze the project's data and monitoring systems, track and report on programme results with particular attention to gender-responsive and youth-inclusive implementation, manage information flow between the global team and the project's regional networks, and prepare knowledge products and communication materials for the UNDP stream of GSP III.

Position Purpose

Under the direct supervision of the Global Support Programme Project Manager, and in close collaboration with the Chief Technical Lead and the Regional Network Coordinators, the Programme Analyst will maintain and analyze the project's data and monitoring systems; track and report on programme results, with particular attention to gender-responsive and youth-inclusive implementation; manage information flow between the global team and the project's regional networks; prepare knowledge products and communication materials in line with the project's Gender Action Plan and Stakeholder Engagement Plan; and provide analytical, documentation and administrative support to the project team.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

1.Ensure Data, Knowledge and Information Management

• Compile, structure and analyze project data, and prepare tables, charts and dashboards to support programme monitoring

• Support the development, updating, and dissemination of technical guidance, knowledge products, sectoral guidance documents, manuals, toolkits, catalogues, communication materials and other project outputs for global and regional audiences.

• Support the development and maintenance of project knowledge repositories, stakeholder databases, document management systems and digital archives, ensuring effective version control, accessibility and compliance with project partners’ information management standards.

• Apply standardized templates and agreed review procedures across knowledge products and communication materials to ensure consistency and coherence across project outputs.

• Assist in maintaining and updating the roster of local, regional and international experts supporting programme implementation.

• Support lessons learned exercises and prepare knowledge capture and synthesis notes across programme components

2. Monitoring, Results Tracking and Reporting

• Support implementation of the programme’s Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) framework through systematic data collection, validation, analysis and reporting.

• Maintain and update indicator-tracking and results-monitoring tools, ensuring that reported information is complete, traceable and supported by appropriate evidence.

• Contribute to the preparation of annual work plans, Project Steering Committee documentation, progress reports, Project Implementation Reports (PIRs), and other corporate reporting requirements.

• Support preparation and organization of documentation and evidence for mid-term review and terminal evaluation.

• Support systematic tracking of gender-responsive implementation and results in programme reporting, in line with the project's Gender Action Plan and UNDP's gender-marker requirements.

3. Promote Communications and Outreach

• Support the development and coordination of communication materials, outreach packages, newsletters, presentations, web content, promotional materials and dissemination products to increase the visibility and impact of programme results.

• Support implementation of the programme's communication and branding strategy, ensuring consistency of messaging, visual identity and positioning across all products and events.

• Provide communication and documentation support for global and regional events, workshops, technical exchanges, COP and SB sessions, Global Transparency Forum and other external engagements

• Support the preparation, dissemination and analysis of project surveys and communication products to strengthen stakeholder engagement and knowledge sharing.

• Coordinate the preparation of the yearly event planner, supporting coherence of messaging and communication priorities across project events.

4. Provide Programme Coordination Support

• Support internal team coordination, including documentation, drafting and dissemination of meeting summaries, communication workflows and internal updates.

• Support the delivery of technical and in-country assistance activities in coordination with the RNCs and thematic experts

• Prepare background documentation, analytical materials, technical templates and briefing notes for country missions

• Support the preparation of presentations, guidance notes, training materials and learning resources, and contribute to capacity needs assessments and regional training plans

• Support the exchange of country-level experience, lessons and knowledge products between UNDP's wider GEF Enabling Activities and CBIT portfolio and GSP III, and flag potential duplication to the Global Support Programme Project Manager

• Perform other related technical and programme support duties as required to ensure the effective implementation of the Climate Transparency Global Support Programme III.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: None

Competencies

- Core Competencies

Achieve  Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

Think  Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

Act  with  Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

Engage  and  Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

- Cross-Functional & Technical Competencies

Business Direction and Strategy & System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

2030 Planet-Agenda & Climate: Climate Change Adaptation: Climate-Resilient Infrastructure.

Business Management & Portfolio Management:

- Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment

- Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management

Business Management & Communication:

- Ability to communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience

- Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

Business Management & Monitoring & Evaluation:

Business Management & Digital Awareness and Literacy:

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Background

With offices in Copenhagen, Kuala Lumpur, Dakar, Amman, Panama City and Istanbul, the Global Shared Services Centre (GSSC) services over 180 countries, 40,000 personnel and more than 40 other UN Agencies and Organizations. Through its functional service lines, GSSC ensures high quality and timely delivery of human resources, financial and procurement services as well as information and innovative tools to its various clients and stakeholders. The GSSC is led by the Director, who reports to the Director of Bureau for Management Services (BMS).

Under the guidance and direct supervision of the ICT Analyst, the ICT Associate provides ICT services, support the management of ICT systems, provides daily tier 2 technical support to users of information management tools and technology infrastructure. The ICT Associate promotes a client-oriented approach.

The ICT Associate works in close collaboration with the Directorate, GSSC and non-GSSC teams, and UNDP HQ staff for resolving ICT-related issues, collaborates with other ICT Staff.

Duties and Responsibilities

Ensure effective ICT service delivery and operational support across the GSSC environment through:

- Acting as the second-level escalation point for critical ICT incidents and service disruptions.

- Supporting business continuity, disaster recovery, and operational resilience activities.

2. Manage Network Infrastructure and ICT Systems

Ensure reliable and secure ICT infrastructure through:

Ensure that the desktop and network resources are protected from malicious virus attacks and deploy countermeasures in the event of the attacks

jobs.title: Asociado/a de Proyecto: Especialista en Fortalecimiento Democrático y Cooperación Parlamentaria
jobs.description:
Uruguay ha sido tradicionalmente reconocido como una de las democracias más estables de la región y continúa ubicándose entre las democracias plenas a nivel mundial. Sin embargo, sostener y profundizar la calidad democrática requiere fortalecer de manera permanente la participación cívica y política, la confianza en las instituciones y la capacidad del sistema democrático para responder a nuevas demandas y transformaciones.

El Documento de Programa de País (CPD) 2026–2030 del PNUD en Uruguay busca contribuir a un desarrollo sostenible, justo, inclusivo y resiliente, en línea con la Agenda 2030 y las prioridades nacionales, desde un enfoque transformador de género, basado en derechos humanos e interseccional. Su Outcome 3 está orientado a fortalecer una gobernanza democrática centrada en las personas que contribuya al bienestar equitativo y al desarrollo inclusivo. En particular, el Output 3.3 apunta a alcanzar: «Instituciones públicas y un Parlamento con capacidades técnicas fortalecidas para promover una gobernanza colaborativa y deliberativa que mejore la calidad de las políticas públicas mediante la transparencia, el uso de evidencia y la innovación; articule el diálogo interinstitucional; garantice la paridad y una democracia inclusiva y abierta; y cuente con sistemas robustos de monitoreo, evaluación, rendición de cuentas y prospectiva».

El Informe Regional sobre Democracia y Desarrollo del PNUD 2026 documenta un momento de presión inédita sobre las instituciones democráticas de la región, marcado por la erosión de la confianza ciudadana y la dificultad de los sistemas representativos para responder a demandas cada vez más complejas. Ello representa una oportunidad para renovar el contrato democrático desde sus cimientos institucionales y desde PNUD se está impulsando la iniciativa Instituciones Democráticas para el Futuro, que pretende promover el fortalecimiento de capacidades para anticipar el cambio, ampliar la participación y la colaboración, sostener una esfera pública plural y confiable, y aprovechar las transformaciones digitales al servicio de las personas y de la democracia.

En línea con estas prioridades, desde 2023 la Oficina del PNUD en Uruguay ha venido consolidando una agenda de trabajo orientada al fortalecimiento democrático, combinando el desarrollo de capacidades institucionales con la generación de nuevos espacios de participación, diálogo e innovación.

Como parte de esta estrategia, el PNUD en Uruguay ha venido colaborando con el Parlamento como una contraparte central para, además de contribuir a su fortalecimiento institucional, ampliar los vínculos entre representación política y ciudadanía y generar espacios de articulación entre actores políticos, sociales e institucionales. Adicionalmente, el trabajo con juventudes políticas se ha consolidado como una línea relevante para ampliar y renovar la participación democrática a través del acompañamiento al fortalecimiento de la Juventud Interpartidaria. De manera complementaria, tanto a nivel nacional como regional, desde PNUD se ha venido impulsando una agenda de democracia paritaria orientada a promover la participación política de las mujeres y el posicionamiento de la agenda de igualdad en el quehacer parlamentario. Asimismo, la integridad de la información forma parte de esta agenda de fortalecimiento democrático y de la esfera pública.

En este marco, se pretende profundizar y articular estas líneas de trabajo mediante un enfoque sistémico de fortalecimiento de la gobernabilidad democrática, fortaleciendo las capacidades de las instituciones democráticas con un enfoque de futuros, ampliando la cooperación con el Parlamento y consolidando iniciativas en materia de participación ciudadana, integridad de la información, juventudes políticas, diálogo intergeneracional, democracia paritaria, gobernanza anticipatoria, transformación digital de la democracia e innovaciones democráticas, entre otras.

Alcance del trabajo

El/la Asociado/a de Proyecto en Fortalecimiento Democrático y Cooperación Parlamentaria trabajará bajo la supervisión directa del/de la Analista de Programa – Gobernabilidad Democrática y Efectiva de PNUD Uruguay, en coordinación con las demás áreas programáticas y operativas de la Oficina País, instituciones contraparte, socios estratégicos y otros actores relevantes. La posición brindará apoyo sustantivo, técnico-operativo y de coordinación para la formulación, implementación, seguimiento y gestión del conocimiento de proyectos e iniciativas vinculadas al fortalecimiento democrático, la cooperación parlamentaria, la participación ciudadana, la integridad de la información, las juventudes políticas, la gobernanza anticipatoria, la democracia paritaria, la transformación digital y la innovación democrática.

Sus principales funciones y responsabilidades serán las siguientes:

- Apoyar la formulación, planificación y desarrollo sustantivo de iniciativas de fortalecimiento democrático y cooperación parlamentaria.

- Apoyar el diseño, formulación y planificación de proyectos e iniciativas vinculadas al fortalecimiento democrático y la cooperación parlamentaria, incluyendo participación ciudadana, integridad de la información, juventudes políticas, democracia paritaria, gobernanza anticipatoria, transformación digital e innovaciones democráticas.

- Preparar insumos analíticos, antecedentes, notas conceptuales, propuestas, planes de trabajo, marcos de resultados, presupuestos y arreglos de implementación para consideración de la supervisión y de los equipos responsables.

- Contribuir al diseño y revisión de documentos de proyecto, acuerdos, propuestas de cooperación, términos de referencia y otros instrumentos programáticos, asegurando coherencia con el Programa País, los estándares corporativos del PNUD y los enfoques de derechos humanos, género, generaciones e interseccionalidad.

- Acompañar procesos de participación, diálogo, consulta y co-creación entre instituciones públicas, actores políticos, sociedad civil, academia, juventudes y ciudadanía, incluyendo espacios interpartidarios, intergeneracionales y multiactor.

- Promover la incorporación de metodologías, herramientas y enfoques de innovación democrática, gobernanza anticipatoria, generación de evidencia, análisis de tendencias y uso responsable de tecnologías emergentes en las iniciativas bajo su ámbito de trabajo.

- Identificar oportunidades de articulación, complementariedad y sinergia entre proyectos e iniciativas del Programa País, especialmente en aquellas áreas donde el fortalecimiento democrático, la participación, la inclusión y la innovación institucional puedan agregar valor transversal.

- Sistematizar información relevante sobre tendencias nacionales, regionales e internacionales en materia de democracia, gobernanza, participación, Parlamento abierto, integridad de la información y transformación digital, a fin de alimentar la formulación de nuevas iniciativas y la toma de decisiones programáticas.

- Contribuir a la implementación, seguimiento técnico-operativo y reporte de proyectos e iniciativas asignadas.

- Apoyar la planificación operativa anual, la programación de actividades, la elaboración de cronogramas y el seguimiento de productos, hitos, indicadores, riesgos, supuestos, compromisos de socios y utilización de recursos de los proyectos e iniciativas asignadas.

- Dar seguimiento a la implementación de actividades, identificando avances, alertas, cuellos de botella programáticos u operativos y posibles medidas de mitigación, para consideración de la supervisión y de los equipos responsables.

- Coordinar insumos y preparar borradores de informes de avance, informes corporativos, reportes a donantes, revisiones de cartera, comités de proyecto, auditorías, evaluaciones y ejercicios de cierre, según corresponda.

- Revisar la calidad, consistencia y oportunidad de la documentación programática y de gestión preparada para los proyectos e iniciativas bajo su ámbito de trabajo, proponiendo ajustes antes de su elevación.

- Mantener una articulación periódica con contrapartes, socios, consultores/as, proveedores y equipos internos, facilitando la coordinación de actividades y el flujo oportuno de información para la implementación.

- Preparar y dar seguimiento a términos de referencia, solicitudes de contratación, adquisiciones, viajes, pagos, acuerdos y otros procesos operativos necesarios para la ejecución de las iniciativas, en coordinación con Operaciones y conforme a las normas y procedimientos del PNUD.

- Apoyar la revisión de productos elaborados por consultores/as, instituciones socias o proveedores, verificando su consistencia con los términos de referencia, los resultados esperados y los estándares de calidad acordados.

- Contribuir a la aplicación de herramientas de gestión basada en resultados, gestión de riesgos, HACT, salvaguardas, seguimiento financiero, monitoreo y cierre de proyectos, de acuerdo con las orientaciones institucionales.

- Brindar apoyo técnico-operativo, logístico y de coordinación a misiones, reuniones, talleres, consultas, diálogos, procesos participativos, actividades de formación y otros espacios vinculados a los proyectos e iniciativas asignadas.

- Contribuir al desarrollo de alianzas, movilización de recursos, comunicación estratégica y gestión del conocimiento.

- Preparar análisis, mapeos de actores, perfiles de socios, notas de antecedentes y otros insumos sustantivos que contribuyan al desarrollo de alianzas estratégicas y oportunidades de cooperación en materia de fortalecimiento democrático y cooperación parlamentaria.

- Identificar oportunidades de financiamiento, cooperación técnica y alianzas con instituciones públicas, Parlamento, partidos políticos, sociedad civil, academia, organismos internacionales, sector privado y otros actores relevantes, para consideración de la supervisión.

- Contribuir a la elaboración de ideas de proyecto, conceptos, propuestas y documentos de movilización de recursos, asegurando coherencia con el CPD, las prioridades nacionales, el enfoque de gestión basada en resultados y los requisitos corporativos.

- Participar en reuniones técnicas con contrapartes y socios, presentar información sobre avances, necesidades y oportunidades, y facilitar acuerdos de trabajo dentro de su ámbito funcional y bajo la orientación correspondiente.

- Sistematizar buenas prácticas, innovaciones, metodologías, resultados, aprendizajes y desafíos derivados de los proyectos e iniciativas, contribuyendo a la generación de evidencia y al posicionamiento del PNUD como socio estratégico en la agenda democrática.

- Preparar notas conceptuales, minutas, informes, presentaciones, insumos de comunicación, productos de conocimiento y otros materiales dirigidos a distintas audiencias internas y externas.

- Contribuir a la difusión de experiencias, metodologías y aprendizajes en redes, comunidades de práctica, espacios de formación, intercambios regionales y actividades externas relacionadas con las líneas de trabajo bajo su responsabilidad.

- Apoyar la implementación de estrategias de comunicación de los proyectos e iniciativas, en coordinación con los equipos responsables, asegurando mensajes claros, inclusivos y consistentes con el posicionamiento institucional del PNUD.

La persona contratada estará bajo la supervisión directa del/de la Analista de Programa – Gobernabilidad Democrática y Efectiva de PNUD Uruguay. Trabajará en coordinación con la gerencia de la oficina (RR/DRR), las demás áreas programáticas y operativas de la oficina, así como con las principales contrapartes relacionadas con los temas asignados.

Competencias esenciales

Obtener resultados:

NIVEL 1: Planifica y supervisa su propio trabajo, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajos de calidad dentro del plazo establecido.

Pensar de forma innovadora:

NIVEL 1: Abierto a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, es pragmático en la resolución de problemas, realiza mejoras

Aprender continuamente:

NIVEL 1: Mente abierta y curiosa, comparte conocimientos, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con agilidad:

NIVEL 1: Se adapta a los cambios, gestiona de forma constructiva la ambigüedad y la incertidumbre, es flexible.

Actuar con determinación:

NIVEL 1: Muestra empuje y motivación, capaz de actuar con calma ante la adversidad, seguro de sí mismo

Participar y asociarse:

NIVEL 1: Demuestra compasión/comprensión hacia los demás, establece relaciones positivas.

Fomentar la diversidad y la inclusión:

NIVEL 1: Apreciar/respetar las diferencias, ser consciente de los prejuicios inconscientes, enfrentarse ante la discriminación.

Gestión de personas

La posición no tendrá responsabilidades de supervisión de personal.

• Capacidad para comunicarse de forma clara, concisa y sin ambigüedades, tanto por escrito como verbalmente; para adaptar los mensajes y elegir los métodos de comunicación en función de la audiencia. Requisitos mínimos del/ de la NPSA seleccionado/a

Mín. Requisitos de formación

• Se requiere educación secundaria

• Se tendrá debidamente en cuenta la titulación universitaria en ciencias sociales, ciencias políticas, derechos humanos o campo equivalente, pero no es un requisito.

Mínimo de años de experiencia laboral pertinente

Se requiere un mínimo de 6 años (con título de bachillerato) o 3 años (con título de licenciatura) de experiencia en organismos internacionales, en programas o proyectos vinculados a gobernanza democrática, derechos humanos y desarrollo con perspectiva de género, generacional e interseccional. Asimismo, se valorará especialmente la experiencia de trabajo demostrada con el Parlamento y actores políticos, así como en procesos de participación ciudadana, juventudes políticas, innovación democrática, gobernanza anticipatoria, esfera digital e integridad de la información.

Conocimientos necesarios

Experiencia en el uso de ordenadores, paquetes de software ofimático (MS Word, Excel, etc.) y sistemas de gestión basados en la web, y conocimientos avanzados de hojas de cálculo y paquetes de bases de datos.

Habilidades deseadas además de las competencias cubiertas en la sección de Competencias

Pensamiento estratégico y visión global

idioma(s) requerido(s)

Español (avanzado).

Inglés (avanzado).

Se valorará el conocimiento de otros idiomas oficiales de ONU

Los/as solicitantes deberán presentar los siguientes documentos:

a) CV y postulación en Quantum indicando todos los puestos ocupados en el pasado y sus principales funciones subyacentes, su duración (mes/año), las cualificaciones, así como los datos de contacto (correo electrónico y número de teléfono) del Candidato, y al menos tres (3) las referencias profesionales más recientes de supervisores anteriores.

b) Una carta de presentación (extensión máxima: 1 página) indicando por qué el candidato se considera apto para el puesto.

c) Los directivos podrán solicitar (ad hoc) cualquier otro material pertinente para evaluar previamente la relevancia de su experiencia, como informes, presentaciones, publicaciones, campañas u otros materiales.

Diversidad, inclusión y no discriminación

La Oficina del Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD) en Uruguay, comprometida con la igualdad de oportunidades, la diversidad y la no discriminación, promueve una cultura organizacional inclusiva, plural, respetuosa de las diferencias y alineada con el principio de no dejar a nadie atrás.

En este marco, invita a postularse a personas afrodescendientes, indígenas, migrantes, personas con discapacidad, personas LGBTIQ+ y otras personas pertenecientes a grupos históricamente subrepresentados o que enfrentan barreras para el acceso a oportunidades laborales. Asimismo, el PNUD alienta especialmente la participación de las mujeres en toda su diversidad.

El PNUD mantiene una política de tolerancia cero frente a cualquier forma de discriminación, acoso, hostigamiento, explotación y abuso sexual. Todas las personas que colaboran con la organización deben actuar con los más altos estándares de integridad, ética y respeto por los derechos humanos.

Participación con inclusión

Quienes requieran ajustes para participar en cualquier etapa del oceso (formatos accesibles, tiempo adicional, intérprete de lengua de señas, entrevista virtual) pueden solicitarlos a rrhh.uy@undp.org (Recursos Humanos). La solicitud es confidencial y no incide en la evaluación.

PSEAH

La persona seleccionada deberá adherir a los estándares de conducta del sistema de Naciones Unidas y a la política de tolerancia cero del PNUD frente a la explotación, el abuso y el acoso sexual; completar las capacitaciones obligatorias en la materia; y reportar toda situación de riesgo por los canales institucionales, con enfoque centrado en la persona sobreviviente.

jobs.title: Technical Project Associate
jobs.description:
1. Position Information

Office/Unit/Project

UNDP Türkiye Country Office / Programme / Preparedness, Response and Resilience Programme / Social Cohesion and Inclusion Support for Refugees in Türkiye

Title

Technical Project Associate

Level

NPSA 6

Duty station (City and Country)

Ankara, Türkiye

Type (Regular or Short term)

Regular

Office- or Home-based

Office-based (Premises of the Presidency of Migration Management - PMM)

Expected starting date

December 2026

Expected Duration

1 year with possible extension based on performance and availability of funds.

Position Number

00138782

2. Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, and culture. Individuals from minority groups, indigenous groups and persons with disabilities are equally encouraged to apply. All applications will be treated with the strictest confidence.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

UNDP is the leading United Nations organization in fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and planet. Learn more at undp.org or follow at @UNDP

The project aims to strengthen social cohesion in Türkiye by supporting the effective implementation of the national harmonization strategy. It enhances opportunities for meaningful participation in social, economic, and civic life, with a particular focus on women. Through a combination of institutional support, community-based initiatives, and targeted services, the project contributes to a more harmonious society and improves well-being for Syrians under Temporary Protection (SuTP), International Protection Status Holders and Applicants (IPSHA), and Turkish Citizens.

To expand access to decent employment, the project reinforces institutional coordination, regulatory frameworks, and labour governance systems while facilitating work permits and labour mobility across regions. It provides market-oriented vocational training, counselling, and job-matching services—especially in the green and digital sectors—and introduces tailored measures to increase women’s employability, including addressing care-related barriers. In parallel, the project supports voluntary relocation by delivering comprehensive resettlement and integration packages that help SuTP and IPSHA settle in new locations and participate effectively in local labour markets and community life.

The project also enhances language proficiency by scaling up accessible language and literacy programmes, with dedicated support for women and girls through enabling measures such as child-care provision. Additionally, it strengthens social cohesion by addressing cultural and social barriers, discrimination, and misinformation that hinder the participation of SuTP, IPSHA in Turkish society. These combined efforts foster mutual understanding, reduce tensions, and create an enabling environment for sustainable integration and cohesive development.

3. Scope of Work

Support the technical coordination and follow-up of project activities carried out within PMM and ensure the regular and timely flow of technical information, needs and inputs among PMM, UNDP and relevant institutions.

- Coordinate the planning, implementation and follow-up of activities carried out within PMM in line with the Project Document and annual work plans, and follow up the flow of technical information and inputs between relevant PMM units and the UNDP project team.

- Contribute to ensuring that project activities are carried out in alignment with PMM’s institutional priorities, relevant policy documents and strategies, and the work programmes of its central and provincial structures.

- Coordinate technical matters among PMM central units, provincial directorates of migration management, the UNDP project team and relevant institutions, and follow up the timely communication and resolution of technical requests, institutional views and decisions.

- Collect and consolidate technical inputs from relevant units for project outputs requiring PMM review or approval, and follow up the alignment of reports, guidelines, tools, presentations and other technical documents with PMM needs and institutional priorities.

- Contribute to the review of technical deliverables prepared by experts, responsible parties and service providers against PMM needs and the agreed technical scope, and share follow-up actions with the UNDP Project Manager and relevant PMM units.

- Collect, clarify and prioritize technical and operational needs raised by PMM units and provincial directorates, ensure their timely communication to the UNDP project team, and follow up the exchange of information required for their reflection in activity plans.

- Provide administrative and operational support to project activities organized in cooperation with PMM and relevant stakeholders, including meetings, workshops, consultations, trainings, field visits, missions and other events.

- Ensure that project-related documentation, correspondence, meeting records, approvals and supporting documents are properly filed, regularly updated and maintained in line with institutional procedures.

- Support the secure storage and archiving of project records containing personal data, sensitive information or information intended for internal use, in line with applicable legislation, institutional rules and confidentiality principles.

Support PMM’s social cohesion activities at central and provincial levels.

- Support PMM in the design, implementation, follow-up and evaluation of social cohesion activities carried out under the project.

- Contribute to the regular and systematic monitoring of social cohesion activities carried out by PMM central units and provincial directorates, and to the compilation and reporting of their results.

- Contribute to the development and maintenance of up-to-date tracking tools covering implementation status, participant profiles, level of outreach, challenges encountered, emerging needs and issues requiring follow-up in relation to activities carried out at central and provincial levels.

- Provide direct support to the design, implementation, monitoring and reporting of activities aimed at strengthening mutual cohesion, social interaction, a culture of coexistence and social participation between Turkish citizens and foreign nationals.

- Support the preparation of activity concept notes, agendas, background notes, briefing materials, participant lists, meeting notes and follow-up tables for social cohesion activities.

Reinforce PMM’s field presence through research, outreach, monitoring and analytical reporting.

- Support field-level research, outreach and monitoring activities undertaken by PMM to generate evidence on migration management, spatial concentration, social cohesion, labour market access and other project-related themes.

- Support the collection, recording and communication of field-level information on cases of social tension, local sensitivities and developments that may affect inter-community relations, in line with confidentiality and personal data protection principles.

- Assist in organizing and reporting on field visits, monitoring missions, consultations, workshops, roundtable meetings and other engagements with provincial structures and local stakeholders.

- Consolidate qualitative and quantitative information obtained from field activities, provincial directorates and relevant stakeholders; assess field findings in terms of implementation status, technical and operational needs, risks and issues requiring follow-up; and provide regular technical inputs to relevant PMM units and the UNDP project team.

- Support the translation of field findings into analytical information, mission reports, briefing notes, implementation status reports and other written inputs to support evidence-based decision-making.

- Develop and keep up to date integrated tracking tools covering project activities, decisions taken, identified risks, follow-up actions, responsible parties and target dates.

Support inter-institutional coordination, partnerships and stakeholder engagement.

- Establish and maintain regular communication channels with relevant public institutions, PMM units, labour market institutions, local authorities, UN agencies, civil society organizations, service providers and other project stakeholders.

- Support coordination with institutions relevant to foreign nationals’ access to formal employment, including labour market actors and public institutions responsible for employment, vocational training, work permits and social security.

- Coordinate the preparation of agendas and technical inputs for technical coordination meetings, consultations and working groups among PMM, UNDP and relevant institutions; record decisions, actions, responsible parties and target dates; and follow up their implementation.

- Support the collection, consolidation and follow-up of feedback, views and recommendations received from PMM, provincial institutions, project partners, stakeholders and beneficiaries.

- Contribute to the coordination of social cohesion-related activities among PMM central units, provincial directorates, local authorities, civil society organizations and other relevant stakeholders.

Support data collection, data management, analysis and evidence-based decision-making.

- Coordinate data collection from PMM units, provincial directorates, responsible parties, service providers and other relevant stakeholders within the scope of the project.

- Support the collection, management, interpretation and presentation of data on migration, labour markets, formal employment, spatial concentration and social cohesion activities.

- Support implementation of the project monitoring system in alignment with its Monitoring and Evaluation framework to ensure effective information sharing, provision of feedback and preparation of high-quality progress reports.

- Monitor existing and emerging technical, operational and field-level risks identified on the PMM side, communicate updated risk information to the UNDP project team, and follow up mitigation measures and actions agreed by the relevant parties.

Support project-related knowledge generation, knowledge sharing and capacity development.

- Support the organization of trainings, briefings, workshops, consultations and capacity-development activities for PMM personnel, provincial institutions and other relevant stakeholders.

- Contribute to the preparation and adaptation of training materials, guidelines, tools, presentations and other capacity-development documents developed under the project.

- Support the systematization and dissemination of project knowledge, lessons learned, good practices, tools, guidelines and other materials among PMM, UNDP and relevant stakeholders.

- Contribute to relevant knowledge networks, communities of practice and internal learning processes, as requested.

- Support the creation of high-quality information on project activities and their visibility among stakeholders; ensure careful selection of communication tools and tailor messages to take into account the overall socio-political and development context in Türkiye.

The Project Technical Officer performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of PMM and UNDP.

4. Institutional Arrangement:

The Project Technical Officer will be based at PMM premises in Ankara for the duration of the assignment and will report directly to the UNDP Project Manager. The incumbent will work in close coordination with the project team designated by PMM and relevant UNDP project personnel.

5. Competencies

Core

Achieve Results:

LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously:

LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility:

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination:

LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner:

LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

People Management (Insert below standard sentence if the position has direct reports.)

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies (insert up to 7 competencies)

Thematic Area

Name

Definition

Business Management

Working with Evidence and Data

- Ability to inspect, cleanse, transform and model data with the goal of discovering useful information, informing conclusions, and supporting decision-making

Business Management

Digital Awareness and Literacy

- Ability and inclination to rapidly adopt new technologies, either through skillfully grasping their usage or through understanding their impact and empowering others to use them as needed

Business Management

Customer Satisfaction/Client Management

- Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs. Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond clients’ immediate requests. Ability to anticipate client’s upcoming needs and concerns.

Business Management

Communication

- Ability to communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media, and other appropriate channels.

Business Management

Monitoring

- Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback on the consistency or discrepancy between planned and actual activities and programme performance and results.

Technical - Finance

Budget management

- Ability to support budgetary aspects of work planning process, drawing and management of team budgets

Technical – Procurement

Procurement

management

- The ability to acquire goods, services or works from an outside external source

6. Minimum Qualifications of the Successful NPSA

Minimum Education requirements

- Secondary education is required, or

- University Degree in Business Administration, Public Administration, International Relations, Social Sciences, Migration Studies, Law, Development Studies, or equivalent field will be given due consideration, but it is not a requirement.

Minimum years of relevant work experience

A minimum of 6 years (with secondary education) or 3 years (with a bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience is required.

Required skills

- Experience in migration, refugee-related studies, social cohesion, labour market participation, formal employment, work permit-related processes and/or similar development or humanitarian fields.

- Experience in supporting project/programme implementation, including planning and follow-up of activities and preparation of inputs for work plans, progress updates, reports, briefing notes, meeting minutes and/or other project documents.

- Experience in coordination with public institutions, local authorities, civil society organizations, international organizations, service providers, development organizations and/or other stakeholders.

- Experience in collecting, compiling, reviewing and/or presenting qualitative and/or quantitative information for monitoring, reporting, planning or decision-making purposes.

- Experience in providing administrative, operational and logistical support to meetings, workshops, trainings, consultations, missions, field visits and/or similar project activities.

- Experience in establishing and maintaining project records, correspondence, supporting documents, tracking tools, databases and/or filing systems.

- Experience in the use of computers, office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and web-based management systems, and advanced knowledge of spreadsheet and database packages.

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

- At least two years of experience in project/programme implementation within government institutions or in close cooperation with government institutions

- Experience in the implementation, monitoring and reporting of projects funded by the European Union and/or other international donors, and knowledge and/or experience of relevant donor visibility and communication requirements

- Experience in project cycle management, including results/logical frameworks, output and outcome indicators, work plans and activity schedules, monitoring and evaluation, risk identification and follow-up, and tracking of activity progress

- Experience in preparing analytical reports, progress reports, briefing/decision notes, presentations or similar technical documents for senior management, project partners and/or donors

- Experience in budget planning and follow-up, financial reporting, procurement and/or contracting processes within project implementation

- Experience in policy development, policy implementation or providing technical contributions to institutional processes in migration, social cohesion, employment, social policy, public administration and/or related fields

- Experience in developing project team work plans, task allocation, performance follow-up and team coordination

Required Language(s)

- Good command of Turkish and English.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Office/Unit/Project Description

UNDP’s Rule of Law Programme in Pakistan is working to strengthen the rule of law and to ensure equal access to justice and security services, particularly for women and marginalized groups across Pakistan in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) including the merged districts (MDs), Balochistan, and Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT). In close collaboration with a range of government, rule of law and justice sector institutions, the overall Programme aims to enhance and sustain peace and stability for the longer-term in Pakistan.

The Programme activities and interventions therefore directly correspond with the government of Pakistan’s strategies and commitments to rule of law and justice reforms, as well as improving the efficiency and effectiveness of institutions to deliver accountable and affordable security and justice services to the public.

The Rule of Law Programme implementation is guided by the following four strategic objectives:

- Policy, legal and regulatory frameworks strengthened to warrant people-centered, equitable, timely, affordable justice and security delivery to all people with an emphasis on women, marginalized and vulnerable groups, and digital technologies.

- Capacity of justice and security stakeholders (duty bearers) enhanced to deliver inclusive, timely, and accessible services to all people with an emphasis on women and digital technologies.

- Capacity of women, and the most vulnerable and marginalized (rights holders) strengthened to access referral pathways to justice and security.

- Justice and security sector institutional facilities enhanced to deliver inclusive, timely, and accessible justice and security services, through women friendly and gender-responsive infrastructure development support with an emphasis on flood resilience and green energy.

Against this backdrop, UNDP actions and interventions are aimed at restoring public confidence and service delivery in the formal justice and rule of law sectors through a range of initiatives i.e. policy development and reform, fostering justice and security sector governance, as well as oversight and accountability at an institutional level with emphasis on inclusive and gender-responsive programming. The overall engagement strategy, therefore, involves both federal and local levels. The Programme is implemented in partnership with the Judiciary, Police, Prosecution, Prisons, Probation and Reclamation, Bar Associations, Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and the academia both at federal and provincial levels.

The Project Travel and Logistics Associate will provide dedicated travel, mission, event-logistics and related administrative support for Rule of Law Programme activities. The Associate will facilitate timely and efficient arrangements for official travel, field missions, trainings, workshops, consultations, conferences and other programme activities in accordance with applicable UNDP policies and procedures.

The Associate will support travel planning and processing, logistical arrangements, travel documentation and claims, participant coordination, service-provider liaison and maintenance of accurate administrative records. S/he will contribute to smooth programme implementation by ensuring that travel and logistical requirements are anticipated, coordinated and followed through in a timely, accurate and service-oriented manner.

Scope of Work

Under the supervision of the Team Lead – Programme Specialist, the Travel and Logistics Associate will provide day-to-day travel, mission and event-logistics support for programme activities. The Associate will coordinate closely with programme personnel, operations colleagues, institutional counterparts and service providers to ensure timely, accurate and compliant arrangements.

The Associate will be responsible for the following functions:

a) Coordinate travel and mission arrangements.

- Process and coordinate official travel arrangements for programme personnel, consultants and other authorised travelers in accordance with UNDP travel policies and procedures.

- Support preparation and processing of travel requests, travel plans, itineraries, tickets, accommodation, terminal arrangements and other required travel documentation.

- Liaise with authorised travel service providers and relevant UNDP units to obtain appropriate travel options and facilitate timely issuance and amendment of travel arrangements.

- Support coordination of security-related travel requirements and ensure that required traveler and mission information is provided to the relevant focal points in a timely manner.

- Maintain an up-to-date travel and mission calendar and follow up on pending approvals, documentation and arrangements that may affect planned travel.

- Provide travelers with relevant administrative and logistical information before missions and support resolution of travel-related issues during implementation, as required.

b) Support travel claims, documentation and financial follow-up.

- Support travelers in completing required post-travel documentation and travel claims and check submissions for completeness before further processing.

- Maintain organised records of travel authorisations, itineraries, tickets, boarding passes, claims and other required supporting documentation in accordance with applicable record-management requirements.

- Coordinate with the Operations & Finance Analyst on travel budgets, advances, claims, reconciliations and other financial matters related to missions and programme travel.

- Follow up on outstanding travel documentation, advances and claims and support timely closure of completed travel actions.

- Maintain travel trackers and provide periodic information on travel status, costs, pending actions and completed missions for programme monitoring and planning.

c) Coordinate logistics for programme events and activities.

- Coordinate logistical arrangements for programme workshops, trainings, consultations, conferences, meetings and other events in collaboration with programme colleagues and institutional counterparts.

- Arrange venues, accommodation, local transportation, participant travel, interpretation, audiovisual equipment, printing, catering and other logistical services, as required and in accordance with applicable procedures.

- Support participant registration, attendance records, travel information, logistical communications and other administrative requirements for programme events.

- Coordinate logistical requirements with designated other team members while ensuring clear sequencing between substantive event planning and logistical arrangements.

- Liaise with vendors and service providers on approved logistical requirements and monitor timely delivery of agreed services, escalating issues to the responsible colleagues where necessary.

- Provide on-site logistical support during programme events and missions and facilitate timely resolution of practical and administrative issues.

d) Provide logistical and administrative support to programme implementation.

- Support arrangements for programme meetings, field visits, delegations and official visits, including schedules, transportation, accommodation and related logistics.

- Coordinate vehicle and transportation requirements for programme missions and activities with relevant UNDP service providers and administrative units.

- Support receipt, dispatch and movement of programme materials, documents and equipment associated with missions and events, as required.

- Maintain organised logistical records, service-provider information, contact lists and other administrative documentation needed for programme implementation.

- Support designated other team members with routine administrative coordination related to missions, events and field activities and ensure timely follow-up on agreed actions.

- Contribute to practical contingency arrangements for missions and events, particularly where travel conditions, security requirements or operational constraints may affect implementation.

e) Ensure compliance, coordination, service quality and effective records management.

- Ensure travel and logistical arrangements are processed in accordance with UNDP policies, procedures, applicable entitlements and approved programme budgets.

- Coordinate with designated other team members and relevant Country Office operations and administrative units to ensure appropriate sequencing, documentation and timely completion of travel and logistics actions.

- Provide relevant specifications, schedules and service information where procurement action is required for travel or logistical services.

- Monitor the quality and timeliness of travel and logistics services and promptly flag recurring service issues, operational risks or delays requiring attention.

- Provide travel and logistics information for programme workplans, implementation reviews, reports and management updates, as required.

- Keep abreast of relevant changes in UNDP travel and administrative procedures and support their consistent application within the Programme.

f) Support knowledge building, knowledge sharing and capacity building relevant to the project.

- Participate in training and organize briefings on internal procedures for the project personnel. Provide support to other capacity building activities, including to the design and delivery of tools, materials for workshops, or platforms that tap into the collective intelligence of communities and mobilize action.

- Provide support in the dissemination and sharing of relevant data and lessons learned within the CO and regionally. Keep pulse on emerging best practices nationally, regionally, and internationally that relate to the work of the project.

- Make sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice. Support compiling and systematizing project knowledge, products and tools as well as their wide distribution to partners.

Background

UNDP is the United Nations’ leading organization working on sustainable development, governance, peacebuilding, and climate resilience. In Kyrgyzstan, UNDP supports national efforts to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals through policy advice, programme implementation, partnerships, and resource mobilization.

The Sustainable Economic Development (SED) team supports senior management in formulating, implementing, and overseeing the UNDP Country Programme in the areas of development planning and financing, green and digital economic transformation, regional and local development, and inclusive growth. The team plays a central role in ensuring strategic coherence, strong national ownership, effective partnerships, and mobilization of resources.

UNDP Kyrgyzstan’s work is guided by the Country Strategy Note and Strategic Compact, which emphasize financial sustainability, selective portfolio management, strengthened partnerships and resource mobilization, development finance, digital transformation, and increased national ownership of development solutions.

Position Purpose:

Under the overall guidance of the Resident Representative and the direct supervision of the Deputy Resident Representative, the Programme Analyst - Sustainable Economic Development is part of the Country Office Management Team, responsible for programming and implementation within the Sustainable Economic Development portfolio.

The position contributes to the implementation of UNDP Kyrgyzstan’s CPD, and Strategic Compact and Country Strategy Note by ensuring selective, high‑impact programme delivery, strengthened partnerships and resource mobilization, and alignment between programme priorities, financial sustainability, and national development objectives.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Ensure Sustainable Economic Development policy development and high quality technical and policy advisory services:

- Provide technical and policy advice to government counterparts at national and sub national levels on sustainable economic development, development planning and financing, green and digital economic transformation, investment and trade promotion, and regional and local development.

- Contribute analytical and forward looking economic analysis to inform strategic positioning, policy dialogue, and programme development.

Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.
