- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

As the lead United Nations agency on international development, UNDP works in 170 countries and territories to eradicate poverty and reduce inequality. We help countries develop policies, leadership skills, partnerships and institutional capabilities to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals.

As outlined in the UNDP Strategic Plan 2026-2029, UNDP’s work is guided by four strategic objectives that together define our contribution to human development: expanding prosperity for all, strengthening effective governance, safeguarding a healthy planet and building crisis resilience. These objectives are enabled by three accelerators that drive transformative impact across our portfolio: digital and AI innovation, gender equality and sustainable finance. Through this integrated approach, UNDP supports countries to deliver tangible improvements in people’s lives and to advance sustainable development at scale.

UNDP, through its Sustainable Finance Hub (https://sdgfinance.undp.org/), supports partners in promoting financing for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). As an accelerator of the UNDP Strategic Plan, sustainable finance strengthens countries’ ability to mobilize, align and deploy finance at scale for national priorities. UNDP supports international and country level policy reform as a catalyst for system-wide change, stronger policy environments, better-functioning markets and more coherent financing strategies for sustainable development.

UNDP hosts the Secretariat of the Better Than Cash Alliance. The Better Than Cash Alliance, established in 2012, is an 80+ member partnership, including governments, corporates, industry bodies, international and regional organizations, partnering to promote the transition from cash to responsible digital payments thereby enabling meaningful financial inclusion, in order to reduce poverty, drive inclusive growth and accelerate the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals. The Alliance Secretariat delivers advisory services, supports advocacy, facilitates knowledge generation and exchanges across members, or partners, to advance equitable access to responsible digital payments and other financial services.

Billions of dollars in cash payments and transfers are made daily in emerging and developing economies, including payment of salaries, social welfare and relief, payments to suppliers, remittances, etc. The problems with these cash payments include a lack of transparency, accountability, and security, as well as inefficiency. Furthermore, the individuals who receive the cash payments are often part of the 1.3 billion excluded from the formal financial sector. This means they are excluded from access to a range of appropriate and affordable financial services to help them save safely, take advantage of economic opportunities, and reduce their vulnerability to risk.

Shifting these payments from cash to digital has the potential to improve livelihoods, particularly for women -who are twice as likely to be excluded from the financial system, providing them with more control over family finances, increasing personal security, and improving economic opportunities. The change to responsible digital payments, as an alternative to cash, further gives governments, development organizations, and the private sector a more transparent, time and cost efficient, and often safer means of disbursing payments.

The Better Than Cash Alliance Secretariat is hosted by UNDP with a globally distributed team based in Africa, Asia, and Latin America. The Alliance Management Support Team provides overall management of all operational, HR, and financial aspects of the Better Than Cash Alliance Secretariat work in full compliance with UNDP rules and regulations. The Team works to enhance the institutional effectiveness of the Alliance Secretariat in its core functional areas of accounts and finance, admin, and travel as well as operations and procurement.

Under the direct supervision of the Managing Director of the Alliance Secretariat, the Project Management and Coordination Analyst is responsible for contributing to project, financial, HR, and operations management, promoting a client-focused, quality, and results-oriented approach, working in close collaboration with the Secretariat’s Program Administrative Analyst, and the Program and Partnerships Specialist, as well as across the entire Alliance Secretariat team, and with UNDP HQ corporate operations, and UNDO Country and Regional Offices, where required. The position is strategically based with location in Kigali, Rwanda, as the Managing Director as direct supervisor, and the Head of Africa, leading the biggest budget of the Alliance’s work with 70% of resources allocated to work in Africa, are based in the same duty station.

Scope of Work

Reporting directly to the Managing Director, the Project Management and Coordination Analyst will ensure project support and day-to-day operations and will be responsible for the performance of the following duties and responsibilities:

Ensure effective project management and coordination in compliance with UNDP administrative requirements:

- Contribute to the corporate planning, monitoring, and reporting exercises;

- Contribute to the preparation of key program documents, such as the Project Document, Multi-year and annual Workplans, and further project reports, including narrative and financial reporting;

- Responsible for preparing, monitoring, and updating the program budget, including on Quantum, and constantly reviewing project revenue and expenditures, monitor budget implementation, prepare, and enter project budget revisions as may be needed. This further includes;

- Regular reporting and consultations on program delivery and budget execution with the Alliance Secretariat Global and Regional Implementation teams;

- Prepare of budgets/financial reports and other related inputs for stakeholder meetings such as the Executive Committee, and other required donor/partner reporting;

- Prepare financial authorizations to enable financial transfers/allocations, or other actions as needed to ensure smooth allocation/funds deployment processes, with close focus on any existing Letter of Agreements (LOAs);

- Review project accounts and initiate corrective actions and resolve issues on exceptional transactions, including budget errors;

- Ensure timely preparation and submission of requests for payment while coordinating inputs into the Payment tracker and full alignment with the existing Contracts;

- Contribute/respond to audit requests, program evaluation activities, as well as risk assessment procedures such as HACT (Micro Assessments, Spot Checks, Audits) and UNDP Private Sector Risk Assessment;

- Contribute to Human Resource processes for hiring, contract extensions, and other related activities, including supporting the drafting of position descriptions, hiring strategies, etc.

Ensure partnerships and coordination:

- Support in strengthening partnerships across UNDP/BPPS and especially the Sustainable Finance Hub, and with UNDP Country and Regional Offices and other UN agencies, where the Alliance Team requires support and coordinated efforts, especially regarding the organization and execution of activities on the ground in country;

- Contribute to the drafting, clearing and signing of contribution agreements with resource partners, and others such as Letters of Interest/Agreement, including managing agreements on the Quantum platform, and monitoring reporting requirements/timelines;

- Research and prepare, as needed, the Team updates on the use of any new tools/portals while ensuring full support and guidance throughout the roll out and implementation;

- Work in coordination with Project Management and Operations Analyst), and the rest of the team.

Facilitate knowledge building, knowledge sharing, and stakeholder guidance:

- Ensure facilitation of knowledge building and knowledge sharing, and provide guidance to stakeholders on financial matters;

- Synthesize lessons learned and good practices in programme and project finance;

- Contribute actively to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

The incumbent may also perform other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Project Management and Coordination Analyst will report directly to the Managing Director (Program Manager).

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results : LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pay attention to details, deliver quality work by the deadline;

- Think Innovatively : LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements;

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback;

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible;

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident;

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships;

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

Cross-Functional/Technical competencies

Business Management

- Project Management Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals.

- Operations Management Ability to effectively plan, organize and oversee different parts of corporate operations, simultaneously and in an integrated way, in order to convert the organization's assets into the best results in the most efficient way. Knowledge of relevant concepts and mechanisms.

Finance

- Financial planning and budgeting Ability to create and manage processes to achieve UNDP's long and short-term financial goals, including through planning, budgeting, forecasting, analyzing and reporting.

- Budget management Ability to support budgetary aspects of work planning process, drawing and management of team budgets

- Financial reporting and analysis Understands changes in regulatory, legal and ethical frameworks and standards for financial reporting in the public sector; Ability to extract, evaluate financial data, derive relevant findings and present them in a meaningful and coherent manner to facilitate effective decision making and performance monitoring; Understands the benefits of integrated reporting, including non-financial resources such as human, social and intellectual capital, and environmental and governance performance.

Business Direction and Strategy

- System Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Partnership Management

- Relationship management Ability to engage with a wide range of public and private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding.

Required Skills and Experience

Education

- Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Business Administration, Public Administration, Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field is required. Or:

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above-mentioned fields of study, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience

- Minimum of two (2) years (with master's degree) or four (4) years (with bachelor's degree) of relevant professional experience in finance, accounting, project management, programme management support or other closely related area is required.

Required skills

- Demonstrated experience in budget preparation, monitoring, expenditure analysis and financial reporting in line with donor and organizational requirements is required;

- Experience in financial reporting, quality assurance, and compliance, with established regulations, policies, or standards is required;

- Demonstrated experience using an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system for financial transaction processing and reporting is required.

Desired skills

- Demonstrated experience in developing and supporting the implementation of donor contribution and partnership agreements is desirable;

- Experience in overall operations for projects or programmes is desirable;

- Previous programme/project experience with UN is desired;

- Experience with the implementation of the UNDP HACT framework and supporting project audit exercises is desirable;

- Experience providing guidance to project personnel on budget and finance matters is desirable;

- Experience and knowledge of UN/UNDP financial rules, regulations, policies and procedures is desirable;

- Experience working in global or geographically distributed virtual teams is an asset;

- Experience and knowledge of IPSAS and/or IFRS is an asset.

Languages

- Fluency in written and spoken English is required

Professional Certificates

- Professional certification in accounting, finance or project management from a recognized international institution — such as ACCA, CPA, CIMA, CIPFA, PRINCE2 or PMP — is an advantage.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

Data Privacy

Please click here to view UNDP Data Privacy Statement

jobs.title: Economiste National(e) [Ouvert aux candidats Internes et Externes]
jobs.description:
Approche par niveaux

Conformément à l’engagement visant à préserver les capacités et à soutenir le personnel déjà en poste au sein de l’Organisation, la majorité des postes vacants du PNUD/FENU/VNU sont publiés selon un processus de candidature par niveaux, comme suit :

- Niveau 0 (Tier 0) : Personnel IP du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaire d’un engagement permanent (PA) ou à durée déterminée (FTA), dont le poste sera supprimé ou dont le contrat prendra fin ou ne sera pas renouvelé au cours de l’année 2026.

- Niveau 1 (Tier 1) : Autres membres du personnel du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaires d’un engagement permanent (PA) ou à durée déterminée (FTA).

- Niveau 2 (Tier 2) : Personnel du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaire d’un engagement temporaire (TA), personnel sous contrat PSA régulier, ainsi que les Volontaires des Nations Unies de catégories Expert et Spécialiste.

- Niveau 3 (Tier 3) ou aucun niveau indiqué : Tous les autres types de contrats au sein du PNUD/FENU/VNU et des autres agences, ainsi que les autres candidats externes.

Veuillez prendre connaissance du ou des niveau(x) indiqué(s), le cas échéant, dans l’intitulé de l’avis de vacance et vous assurer que vous remplissez les critères d’éligibilité requis pour soumettre votre candidature.

Contexte et justification organisationnelle

La Mauritanie poursuit la mise en œuvre de la Stratégie de Croissance Accélérée et de Prospérité Partagée (SCAPP 2016–2030), qui constitue le cadre central de planification du développement national. Cette stratégie vise à stimuler une croissance économique inclusive, diversifiée et durable, à réduire les inégalités et à renforcer la gouvernance, tout en intégrant les Objectifs de Développement Durable (ODD) de l’Agenda 2030 et les priorités de l’Agenda 2063 de l’Union Africaine.

Le pays dispose d’importants atouts économiques, notamment dans les secteurs minier, énergétique et agricole, mais reste confronté à des défis structurels tels que la dépendance aux industries extractives, la vulnérabilité climatique, la lente progression du Développement Humain, la persistance de la pauvreté multidimensionnelle, la faible inclusion économique des femmes et des jeunes. Dans ce contexte, la transition énergétique, portée par le potentiel de l’hydrogène vert, et le recours accru à des financements innovants offrent de nouvelles perspectives pour accélérer la diversification économique et la résilience du pays.

Le Programme des Nations Unies pour le Développement (PNUD) accompagne le Gouvernement mauritanien dans la mise en œuvre de la SCAPP et des ODD, en appuyant la formulation et la mise en œuvre de politiques publiques, le renforcement des capacités institutionnelles et la mobilisation de partenariats stratégiques.

Sous la supervision générale du Représentant Résident et la supervision directe de la Représentante Résidente Adjointe, l’Économiste National(e) apporte un appui stratégique à la Direction du PNUD en matière d’analyse économique, de planification prospective et de formulation de politiques publiques alignées sur les priorités nationales de développement.

En tant que conseiller(e) stratégique, il/elle contribue à positionner le PNUD comme un partenaire de confiance du Gouvernement mauritanien et des acteurs du développement dans la promotion d’une croissance inclusive, durable et fondée sur des données probantes. Son rôle consiste à anticiper les transformations économiques, sociales et environnementales, à éclairer les choix stratégiques du pays et à renforcer la cohérence des interventions du PNUD pour un impact systémique et mesurable.

L’Économiste National(e) soutient la transformation des approches de développement en intégrant l’innovation, la finance durable, la gouvernance, le genre et la transformation numérique dans la planification et la mise en œuvre des programmes. Il/elle contribue à positionner le PNUD comme catalyseur de solutions intégrées, au service d’une mise en œuvre plus efficace des politiques publiques et d’une mobilisation accrue des financements innovants pour accélérer la réalisation des ODD et soutenir les ambitions de développement national à long terme.

En collaboration étroite avec les institutions publiques, le secteur privé, la société civile, les partenaires techniques et financiers, les universités et l’Équipe Pays des Nations Unies (UNCT), il/elle favorise un dialogue structuré et une coordination renforcée des politiques économiques et sociales. Son action vise à générer des synergies intersectorielles et entre les niveaux national et local, à promouvoir la transformation du secteur privé, l’entrepreneuriat, l’employabilité et l’innovation au bénéfice des femmes, des jeunes et des groupes vulnérables.

Ainsi, l’Économiste National(e) contribue à renforcer le positionnement du PNUD en tant que laboratoire d’idées et acteur clé du développement en Mauritanie, pour transformer la vision nationale du développement en résultats concrets et durables.

En tant que Point Focal Genre du PNUD, l’Économiste National(e) assure l’appui du PNUD pour l’intégration transversale du genre dans les stratégies nationales de développement (i.e. SCAPP, SNIGG, SNEDD, etc.), le renforcement des capacités des parties prenantes, le développement de partenariats avec le secteur privé, ainsi que la promotion de la cohérence et des complémentarités entre les initiatives politiques et sectorielles, le tout encadré et aligné sur le Plan d’Action du Gender Seal Gold.

Enfin, l’Économiste National(e) peut être amené(e) à superviser et coordonner une équipe d’experts, de consultants nationaux et de personnel de projet, et à représenter le PNUD dans son domaine d’expertise, sur instruction du Représentant Résident.

Le PNUD adopte une approche par portefeuille pour s'adapter à l'évolution des besoins opérationnels et tirer parti des liens entre les différentes interventions afin d'atteindre ses objectifs stratégiques. Par conséquent, le personnel du PNUD est tenu de travailler avec d'autres unités, fonctions, équipes et projets au sein d'équipes multidisciplinaires afin de renforcer et de faciliter la collaboration horizontale.

Mission du Poste

L’économiste National(e) apporte un appui stratégique et technique à la Direction du PNUD Mauritanie et aux partenaires nationaux en matière d’analyse économique, de formulation de politiques publiques et de planification du développement, en cohérence avec les priorités nationales, la SCAPP et les Objectifs de Développement Durable. Il/elle contribue à une prise de décision éclairée à travers des analyses fondées sur des données probantes et une veille stratégique continue. Le/la titulaire du poste soutient la conception et la mise en œuvre de solutions de développement intégrées et innovantes, intégrant l’innovation, la gouvernance et l’égalité des genres. Il/elle appuie le dialogue politique, le renforcement des capacités, la mobilisation de partenariats et la production de connaissances afin de renforcer l’impact et le positionnement stratégique du PNUD en Mauritanie.

L’économiste National(e) exerce les fonctions suivantes :

Tâches et Responsabilités Principales:

1.Fournir des conseils stratégiques et techniques au PNUD, au Gouvernement, au Système des Nations Unies et aux partenaires, en matière de planification stratégique prospective et d’innovation pour le développement durable :

• Contribuer à repenser et à réorienter, de manière prospective et innovante, les programmes et stratégies nationales de développement, en appuyant le PNUD et le Gouvernement dans la planification stratégique, l’élaboration de politiques fondées sur des données probantes et la transformation des priorités nationales en actions concrètes et en impact durable.

• Appuyer la conduite de consultations, analyses prospectives et sectorielles approfondies pour anticiper les tendances, risques émergents et opportunités du développement, et éclairer la planification nationale et territoriale.

• Soutenir le PNUD dans l’identification et l’opérationnalisation des « paris stratégiques » (Big Bets), en se concentrant sur les leviers de transformation structurelle les plus prometteurs pour accélérer les progrès vers les ODD (transition énergétique, croissance verte, inclusion économique, innovation, financement du développement, gouvernance, numérique).

• Appuyer le PNUD et le Gouvernement - dans le cadre de l’opérationnalisation du « Government Development Financing (GDF) » - à mobiliser les capacités techniques et institutionnelles pour transformer les budgets nationaux en résultats de développement visibles et durables.

• Renforcer l’innovation stratégique du PNUD à travers la conception, mise en œuvre et suivi de Portefeuilles intégrés, en s’appuyant sur les trois accélérateurs du changement systémique : transformation numérique/IA, égalité des sexes, et finance durable.

• Appuyer le renforcement des capacités institutionnelles de gestion économique, en soutenant les politiques budgétaires et macroéconomiques, la transition vers le budget-programme, l’amélioration de la gestion des finances publiques, ainsi que le renforcement du système statistique nationale.

• Faciliter la mise en place et le suivi de mécanismes de gouvernance et de groupes de travail (intra et intersectoriels, thématiques, régionaux) pour renforcer la cohérence des politiques, la redevabilité et la planification collaborative du développement.

• Contribuer à la communication stratégique, le plaidoyer et le partage de connaissances en valorisant l’impact du PNUD sur les populations et le pays.

• Représenter le PNUD et participer aux initiatives nationales, régionales, et inter‑agences, contribuer aux groupes de travail thématiques, et capitaliser sur les réseaux de connaissances pour renforcer l’engagement et le positionnement du PNUD.

2.Soutenir la mise en place d’outils d’aide à la décision et le renforcement des mécanismes de coordination

- Appuyer le développement et l’institutionnalisation d’outils de pilotage et d’aide à la décision (tableaux de bord, modèles de simulation, systèmes de suivi-évaluation, outils d’analyse économique) permettant d’éclairer la planification stratégique et d’améliorer la cohérence des politiques publiques.

- Contribuer à cartographier, évaluer et consolider les systèmes nationaux de collecte, de gestion et de partage des données pour identifier les lacunes et opportunités d’amélioration, en lien avec les institutions nationales concernées.

- Promouvoir l’utilisation - par le PNUD, les institutions nationales et les partenaires - de plateformes numériques et d’outils d’intelligence artificielle pour renforcer la qualité des analyses et la prise de décision fondée sur des données probantes.

- Contribuer à la conduite, la diffusion et/ou l’exploitation d’études prospectives /stratégiques, d’analyses économiques/sociales/environnementales, et l’élaboration de note de politique, rapports analytiques, afin d’anticiper les évolutions, éclairer la planification à long terme.

- Renforcer, à travers les programmes du PNUD, les capacités techniques des institutions nationales et locales à exploiter les outils d’aide à la décision, notamment à travers des formations et appuis ciblés.

- Assurer le suivi, l’évaluation et la capitalisation des expériences liées à l’utilisation des outils d’aide à la décision, en documentant les bonnes pratiques et en formulant des recommandations pour leur extension à d’autres acteurs et secteurs.

- Soutenir le renforcement de la coordination intersectorielle et régionale afin d’assurer la cohérence des politiques et la complémentarité des interventions.

- Appuyer la mise en place et l’animation de dispositifs de gouvernance et de concertation (comités techniques, groupes de travail thématiques, plateformes de coordination) pour renforcer la redevabilité, la cohérence et l’impact collectif des politiques publiques.

3.Contribuer au développement de partenariats stratégiques et à la mobilisation de financements innovants

- Identifier, analyser et mobiliser les bailleurs de fonds et partenaires stratégiques (institutions financières, donateurs bilatéraux et multilatéraux, secteur privé, fondations, société civile, universités, centres de recherche, etc.) pour soutenir les trajectoires de développement inclusives et résilientes du pays, notamment à travers les programmes du PNUD.

- Utiliser les réseaux, outils et expertises du PNUD pour renforcer de la crédibilité et de l’attractivité économique de la Mauritanie à travers la préparation aux exercices de notation de crédit (credit rating) et la mise en œuvre de réformes structurelles pour renforcer la confiance des investisseurs et mobiliser des financements durables.

- Maintenir une veille stratégique sur les tendances de financement du développement, en particulier sur la baisse de l’Aide Publique au Développement (APD), afin d’orienter la mobilisation de ressources alternatives adaptées à l’évolution du contexte.

- Contribuer à la diversification des sources de financement du développement en Mauritanie, à travers la mise en place de stratégies/instruments financiers innovants (Cadre intégré de financement national, financement mixte, obligations vertes, fonds thématiques, finance islamique, fonds d’investissement à impact, philanthropie privée etc.).

- Élaborer des propositions de financement et des modèles économiques viables, et mener des négociations pour favoriser les investissements dans les secteurs prioritaires.

- Soutenir le renforcement des cadres de gouvernance pour assurer la coordination, transparence, redevabilité et durabilité des financements/partenariats mobilisés, et formuler des recommandations pour leur amélioration/extension.

- Faciliter des ateliers, forums, tables rondes et initiatives de mobilisation de ressource, pour promouvoir l’innovation dans les financements et partager les bonnes pratiques.

- Développer et animer un réseau stratégique de partenaires et capitaliser sur les expériences pour catalyser des investissements, maximiser les complémentarités et renforcer l’impact des interventions

4. Promouvoir le développement du secteur privé et la dynamisation inclusive de l’entrepreneuriat, de l’innovation l’employabilité et de, en faveur des femmes, des jeunes et des groupes vulnérables

- Appuyer le PNUD et les institutions nationales dans la conception et la mise en œuvre de politiques en faveur du secteur privé et les partenariats public-privé, afin de promouvoir l’emploi décent des femmes, des jeunes et des groupes vulnérables.

- Contribuer à la réalisation de diagnostics et de cartographies du tissu économique (PME, start-ups, initiatives féminines et jeunes), en identifiant les obstacles, les opportunités et les besoins pour renforcer l’inclusion économique, l’accès à l’innovation, au financement et aux marchés.

- Promouvoir l’investissement privé aligné sur les ODD en s’appuyant sur des outils stratégiques (SDG Investor Map, SDG Push) tout en renforçant le dialogue public-privé pour soutenir un développement durable, inclusif et créateur d’emplois.

- Appuyer la mise en relation et la collaboration stratégique du PNUD avec les acteurs du secteur privé afin d’orienter les investissements en faveur des start-ups, des PME et des infrastructures sociales et environnementales.

- Appuyer le développement de politiques/programmes intégrées sur l’emploi, la protection sociale, le secteur informel et l’économie sociale et solidaire (ESS), tout en alignant les interventions sur les priorités nationales et les transitions économiques et sociales.

- Appuyer les partenaires nationaux pour le développement de l’écosystème entrepreneurial, de l’innovation et de l’employabilité, en contribuant au renforcement des infrastructures d’appui (incubateurs, pôles d’innovation, laboratoires) et à la montée en compétences techniques.

- Contribuer au renforcement des synergies entre formation - employabilité -entrepreneuriat, en reliant les établissements de formation, les centres d’innovation, le secteur privé et le marché du travail.

- Promouvoir l’intégration des jeunes et des femmes dans l’économie numérique à travers des programmes de renforcement de capacités, d’incubation et de mentorat.

- Développer des initiatives conjointes entre PNUD et les agences du SNU, le secteur privé, les partenaires techniques et financiers, universités, centres d’innovation (notamment l’UNIPOD) et acteurs locaux pour cocréer des solutions qui renforcent l’inclusion et l’employabilité, au-delà des approches traditionnelles. Organiser et animer des actions de communication, de plaidoyer et de réseautage (forums, Bootcamps, hackathons, concours d’innovation, etc.) pour valoriser l’entrepreneuriat, stimuler l’innovation et renforcer la visibilité des initiatives du PNUD.

5.Promouvoir l’intégration transversale du genre dans les stratégies nationales et dans les interventions du PNUD, le renforcement des capacités des parties prenantes, et la promotion de synergies entre initiatives politiques et sectorielles, conformément aux objectifs du Plan d’Action du Gender Seal Gold.

- Collaborer avec les institutions nationales pour intégrer les considérations de genre dans la conception et la mise en œuvre des stratégies nationales (SCAPP, SNIGG, SNEDD, etc.)

- Appuyer les diagnostics et les cartographies des initiatives et programmes nationaux pour identifier les lacunes, opportunités et besoins en matière d’intégration du genre et renforcer l’efficience des politiques nationales existantes.

- Promouvoir une approche basée sur les ODD pour le suivi des engagements nationaux en matière de genre, en utilisant des outils stratégiques tels que le SDG Push et le SDG Investor Map.

- Développer et renforcer les mécanismes de coordination entre les secteurs clé (public, privé, société civile, etc.) pour amplifier la transversalité du genre dans les interventions nationales et partenaires.

- Participer au développement et à la mise en œuvre de programmes de renforcement des capacités des parties prenantes (institutions étatiques, ONG, partenaires du secteur privé) sur les enjeux liés au genre et aux synergies politiques.

- Accompagner le plaidoyer et la sensibilisation au niveau national, à travers l’organisation et la facilitation de forums, ateliers et événements stratégiques, pour la mise en avant du genre comme axe transversal dans le développement durable.

- Promouvoir et appuyer des initiatives conjointes et multisectorielles sous le Groupe PTF Genre, incluant le PNUD, les agences du SNU, les partenaires techniques et financiers, ainsi que les groupes communautaires, afin de cocréer des solutions adaptées aux enjeux de genre dans le pays.

- Appuyer le développement d’outils de suivi et évaluation dans les stratégies nationales pour mesurer l’impact des politiques et programmes liés à l’égalité des genres.

- Travailler étroitement avec les unités thématiques du PNUD pour assurer une transversalité accrue du genre dans toutes les interventions du Bureau de Pays.

- Élaborer des rapports réguliers sur l’état d’avancement des objectifs du Gender Seal Gold, incluant les progrès réalisés, les défis rencontrés et les recommandations pour un meilleur alignement.

- Diffuser et maintenir les bonnes pratiques et les leçons apprises sur l’intégration transversale du genre dans les initiatives politiques, stratégiques et opérationnelles.

Le/la titulaire accomplit toute autre tâche relevant de son profil fonctionnel, jugée nécessaire au bon fonctionnement du Bureau et de l’Organisation.

Responsabilités de supervision/gestion :

Ce poste peut impliquer la supervision de membres du personnel, y compris des experts, des consultants internationaux et nationaux et de personnel de projet appuyés par l'Unité des politiques et de la stratégie (USP) ; et requiert par conséquent la démonstration des compétences du PNUD en matière de gestion des personnes.

Compétences

Compétences Clés

Atteindre des résultats -Niveau 3 : Définir et aligner des objectifs ambitieux mais réalisables pour plusieurs projets, avec un impact durable

Penser de manière innovante -Niveau 3: Anticiper et atténuer de manière proactive les risques potentiels, et développer de nouvelles idées pour résoudre des problèmes complexes.

Apprendre en continu -Niveau 3: Créer et saisir des opportunités pour élargir ses horizons et diversifier ses expériences

S’adapter avec agilité -Niveau 3: Initier et promouvoir le changement de manière proactive, tout en gérant des priorités multiples et concurrentes

Agir avec détermination- Niveau 3: Aller au-delà des tâches ou obstacles immédiats et prendre des initiatives afin d’atteindre des résultats plus ambitieux

S’engager et nouer des partenariats-Niveau 3: Faire preuve de sens politique, naviguer dans des environnements complexes et promouvoir la collaboration inter-agences

Promouvoir la diversité et l’inclusion- Niveau 3: Reconnaître les avantages d’un environnement de travail diversifié et promouvoir activement l’inclusion.

Compétences transversales et techniques

Orientation stratégique et gestion -Pensée systémique: •Capacité à utiliser une analyse objective des problèmes et un jugement éclairé pour comprendre comment des éléments interdépendants coexistent au sein d’un processus ou d’un système global, et à évaluer comment la modification d’un élément peut avoir un impact sur les autres composantes du système;

Business Development-Facilitation du partage des connaissances: • Capacité à mobiliser et animer des individus et des communautés de contributeurs afin de favoriser la participation et le partage, en particulier avec des acteurs externes

Business Management -Gestion de portefeuille: •Capacité à sélectionner, prioriser et piloter les programmes et projets de l’organisation conformément à ses objectifs stratégiques et à ses capacités ; capacité à trouver un équilibre entre la mise en œuvre d’initiatives de changement et le maintien des activités courantes, tout en optimisant le retour sur investissement

Digital & Innovation -Data literacy: •Comprendre le potentiel ainsi que les limites de l’innovation fondée sur les données. •Capacité à utiliser une combinaison de sources de données (quantitatives, qualitatives ou en temps réel) afin de développer une compréhension approfondie, d’identifier des tendances et d’éclairer la prise de décision ou de repérer des opportunités nécessitant une analyse plus approfondie Programmes et politiques Politiques et engagement en matière de crises et de fragilité; •Utilisation des données et de l’analytique pour l’alerte précoce et la gestion des crises

Programmes et politiques -Intégration des ODD: •Analyse à l’échelle de l’ensemble de l’économie •Engagement avec des penseurs et experts du Sud global dans le cadre de la coopération Sud-Sud.

Digital & Innovation- Co-création: •Capacité à concevoir et à faciliter des processus permettant à un groupe diversifié de parties prenantes de résoudre un problème commun, de développer des pratiques ou de co-créer des connaissances.•Capacité à valoriser la diversité, à travailler avec un large éventail de parties prenantes, à comprendre leurs intérêts, perspectives et points de vue, et à les mobiliser comme source de créativité. •Capacité à faciliter des processus et à créer des conditions favorables à des contributions diverses, stimulant la collaboration et le partage;

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Un diplôme universitaire supérieur (Master ou équivalent) en Economie, Sciences Politiques, Développement, Sciences Sociales ou autres disciplines connexes est requis, ou

- Un diplôme universitaire de premier niveau (licence) dans les domaines susmentionnes combiné à deux années supplémentaires d'expérience qualifiante est pris en considération en lieu et place du diplôme universitaire supérieur.

Experience:

- Au minimum 5 ans (avec un Master) ou 7 ans (avec une Licence) d’expérience professionnelle pertinente au niveau national ou international dans la planification du développement, l’analyse économique, et le conseil en politiques publiques requis;

- Une expérience d’au moins 4 ans dans la conception, la gestion, le suivi et l’évaluation de projets et programmes de développement est souhaitable ;

- Une expertise confirmée dans l’analyse, le suivi et le développement des politiques économiques et sociales, avec capacité à formuler des recommandations stratégiques, notamment sur les thématiques émergentes, les transitions économiques et sociales, et les approches pro-pauvres est souhaitable

Langue(s) requise(s)

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Secretary-General’s Peacebuilding Fund (PBF) is the UN’s principal financial instrument for consolidating peace in countries affected by violent conflict, managed by the Peacebuilding Fund Branch of the Peacebuilding and Peace Support Office (PBPSO), on behalf of the Secretary-General and financially administered by the UNDP;s Multi-Partner Trust Fund Office (MPTFO) as a global pooled fund. Since its creation in 2006, Member States have contributed to its financing within the framework of the Strategic Plan 2017-2019 and 2020-2026. The PBF works transversally and supports integrated responses to meet the most urgent needs. It responds quickly and flexibly to political opportunities; and catalyzes processes and resources by demonstrating greater risk tolerance.

Mali has been a recipient of the PBF since 2014, with more than $90 million allocated to projects in Mali. The PBF portfolio has evolved since 2014, flexibly adapting to the context and aligning with the national peacebuilding priorities. It started with a focus on the implementation in Northern Mali of the 2013 Ouagadougou Preliminary Accord and the 2015 Algiers Peace Agreement, expanding the focus on Central Mali to respond to the spillover of the crisis since 2017. In 2019, the portfolio shifted to prevention in the South and continued stabilization efforts in the Center in 2019.

The current portfolio includes 8 projects with a total budget of more than $21 million, including two cross-border initiatives (one with Guinea, one with Mauritania and Senegal) and three initiatives funded through the PBF assessed resources for 2025. The current portfolio has a thematic focus on natural resources management, especially land, water and the role of women, peace dividends and socio-economic opportunities for youth and border communities. Two additional initiatives are in the pipeline for an additional $5 million funded through the PBF assessed resources for 2026. A Portfolio Evaluation concluded in early 2025, showing a strong national ownership, positive catalytic effects on Rule of Law initiatives, and positive impact of initiatives on natural resources management and support to local stakeholders and CSOs.

At the country-level, alignment of the Peacebuilding Fund portfolio with national priorities is ensured by the Joint Steering Committee, co-chaired by the Resident Coordinator and the Minister of Foreign Affairs. The UN Resident Coordinator is the lead interlocutor at the country level for the PBF. Therefore, the PBF Secretariat in Mali is established within the Resident Coordinator’s Office. PBF Secretariats are responsible for enhancing coherence of PBF projects at the portfolio level and for supporting the work of country-level Joint Steering Committees.

Position Purpose

The PBF Secretariat Coordinator main mission will be to lead the PBF Secretariat team in delivering its mandate, ensuring the effective governance, accountability and impact of the PBF portfolio in Mali, and effective functioning of the peacebuilding steering committee in Mali.

S/he will provide technical support to recipient entities and partners, technical and logistical support to the joint steering committee and technical committee ensuring the strategic impact of initiatives. S/he will also ensure the quality and timeliness of the monitoring, evaluation, communication, reporting, and auditing of results of the PBF portfolio in Mali. S/he will also ensure the communication and visibility of peacebuilding programs, as well as the implementation and follow-up of the recommendations from the evaluation of the PBF portfolio for the period 2019-2024.

S/he will be supervised daily by the RCO Head of Office under the direction of the Resident Coordinator of the United Nations system in Mali. S/he will work closely with the RCO Team and will be indirectly supervised by the Peacebuilding and Peace Support Office Program Manager in New York for strategic portfolio management and overall projects performance.

For administrative purposes, the PBF Secretariat is administered by UNDP on behalf of the UN Resident Coordinator and their Office and the Peacebuilding and Peace Support Office. The PBF Coordinator will be a staff member of the United Nations Development Program (UNDP). There is no formal substantive reporting line of the PBF Secretariat to UNDP in-country, only a Quantum-related reporting line respecting UNDP’s administrative role in the project, which allows the PBF Secretariat project to be managed/implemented.

Duties and Responsibilities

1) Manage the PBF Secretariat team to deliver its mandate, with a focus on governance, accountability and impact of the PBF portfolio in Mali

- Supervise the PBF Secretariat team and strengthen their capacities in line with the team mandate, for example in the fields of peacebuilding, conflict-sensitivity, gender-mainstreaming, M&E etc;

- Facilitate quality assurance processes for the allocation of resources and the management of the portfolio, ensuring compliance with PBF guidelines, in particular for reports and products developed by the recipient partners;

- Coordinate the overall management of the PBF portfolio, in coordination with the recipient organizations, the UN System in Mali, national stakeholders, civil society organizations and non-UN partners;

- Contribute to relevant reports/documents of the Office of the Resident Coordinator related to peacebuilding (Annual Strategic Report to PBF, UNSCDF report, CCA etc)

- Coordinate the knowledge capitalization process in relevant thematic areas, and document lessons learned, experiences and good practices from the PBF portfolio that could be useful for the design and implementation of similar initiatives, for organizational and external sharing and learning.

2) Support the functioning of the PBF Joint Steering Committee for strategic supervision and quality control of the PBF portfolio in Mali

- Support the Joint Steering Committee with secretarial tasks to facilitate inclusive decision-making, including the organization of meetings and field visits, preparation of working papers, drafting of reports and sharing of relevant documents;

- Monitor and disseminate decisions and recommendations made by the Joint Steering Committee, and portfolio evaluators, to ensure accountability and prioritization for the use of PBF resources;

- Ensure early warning and advice on solutions to the Joint Steering Committee, the Resident Coordinator, the implementing partners and the PBF of risks, delays and problems related to the implementation of the PBF portfolio;

- Liaise with the Peacebuilding and Peace Support Office for the preparation and follow-up of the Joint Steering Committee meetings.

3) Ensure the mobilization or resources and partnerships for the sustainability of the PBF portfolio in Mali and facilitate knowledge sharing

- Ensure visibility and dissemination of the PBF portfolio results and impact to mobilise new resources and partners;

- Collaborate with the RCO team for conflict analysis to guide national and cross-border programming and suggest entry points for mobilization of resources and partnerships;

- Communicate progress on the peacebuilding priorities to national authorities and technical and financial partners in order to encourage additional funding and to ensure sustainability of the results;

- Contribute to inclusive partnerships for peacebuilding in Mali, including national and local stakeholders such as private sector and civil society, as well as international partners and financial institutions.

- Provide sound contributions to knowledge networks, communities of practice, and digital knowledge platforms.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities:

Supervise the staff of the PBF Secretariat in Mali and coordinate the peacebuilding portfolio

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results -LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively -LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously -LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility -LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination -LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner -LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion -LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

People Management

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Direction & Strategy -System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

Business Management -Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritize and control the organization’s programmes and projects, in line with its strategic objectives and capacity; ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives and the maintenance of business-as-usual, while optimizing the outcome. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio

management

Business Management -Monitoring & Evaluation: Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are implemented effectively; Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results. Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming. Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools. Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

Business Development -Knowledge Generation: Ability to research information and to turn it into

useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

Partnership Management -Relationship Management: Ability to engage with a wide range of public and

private partners, build, sustain and/or strengthen working relations, trust and mutual understanding.

2030 Agenda: People -Gender: Gender Equality and Institutional Transformation

2030 Agenda: Engagement & Effectiveness -Effectiveness: RBM standards and practices for programming.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

Advanced University Degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Social Sciences, International Relations, Human Sciences, Law, or relevant related field is required. Or

A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of an advanced university degree

Experience:

- Minimum of 7 years (with master’s degree) or 9 years (with bachelor’s degree) in coordinating projects and/or activities at the national or regional levels, preferably in the area of peacebuilding, governance and/or conflict prevention is required.

- Experience and excellent knowledge of the national and sub-regional socio-political environment and context, in particular in the areas of peacebuilding, governance and/or conflict prevention are required.

- Proven expertise in developing conflict analysis and conflict sensitive programs, and providing coaching and technical support in relevant areas, such as peacebuilding, conflict-sensitivity, gender-mainstreaming, M&E etc is desired.

- Experience of coordinating multi-stakeholder processes, ensuring inclusion of diverse stakeholders such as the private sector and civil society organizations is desired.

- Proven leadership in the coordination of inter-agency activities in the United Nations system is desired.

- Proven capacity in the areas of financial management and resource mobilization is desirable.

- Experience and knowledge of the United Nations and its working practices, as well as its ongoing reforms will constitute an advantage.

- Proven track record of excellent oral and written communication skills with high-level interlocutors, particularly in the coordination of governmental and international organizations is desired.

- Proven track record of sound understanding of the concepts of human rights, gender, strengthening the role of women and young people in the peacebuilding process is desirable;

- Experience and knowledge of PBF procedures is advantageous.

- Experience and knowledge of peacebuilding issues in Mali and prior experience in the region would be an asset.

Language requierements:

Fluency in French language and English are required

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

Background

We are on the ground in 170 countries and territories, working with governments and people on their own solutions to global and national development challenges to help empower lives and build resilient nations.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Communications and Reporting Analyst will be responsible for designing and implementing a comprehensive communications and visibility strategy that effectively showcases the results, innovations, and lessons of the Nepal project. The Communications and Reporting Analyst will develop and manage communication materials, coordinate outreach with national and international stakeholders, and ensure alignment with UNDP and donor branding requirements. Key duties include documenting project achievements, producing multimedia content, strengthening media and partner networks, and supporting advocacy and knowledge exchange at national, regional, and global levels.

Design, Develop, implement and manage the project communication strategy:

- Oversee the design, layout, and production of communication outputs, ensuring adherence to UN editorial and branding guidelines.

- Maintain a digital library of media, photographs, and knowledge products.

- Provide quarterly updates and inputs to project progress reports, highlighting communication milestones and results.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP Morocco is seeking a Procurement and Travel Assistant to provide excellent support in procurement and travel, working in close collaborations with the Programme, Operations, and Projects of UNDP, as well as other United Nations agencies.

Under the direct supervision of the Procurement Associate, and the overall guidance and supervision provided by the Operations Coordinator, the Procurement and Travel Assistant will be responsible for providing a variety of office, agency and project support services. Primarily, the incumbent will act as the Procurement and Travel Assistant to various projects, agencies and initiatives. He/she will perform his/her functions in close collaboration with the other members of the Procurement Unit.

The Procurement and Travel Assistant provides support to office operations performing a variety of standard procurement and travel processes ensuring high quality and accuracy of work. The Procurement and Travel Assistant promotes a client, quality and results-oriented approach. She/he works in close collaboration with UNDP Operations and Programme staff and other UN agencies staff to exchange information and ensure consistent and quality service delivery.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Procurement and Travel Assistant will undertake the following tasks:

- Contribution to the implementation of operational strategies in the context of UNDP activities in support of UN agencies.

- Effective procurement and logistical support in the context of UNDP activities in support of the Country Office, UNDP projects and UN agencies.

- Support to travel management processes in the context of UNDP activities in support of the Country Office, UNDP projects and UN agencies.

- Support to knowledge building and knowledge sharing.

Ensures implementation of operational strategies, in the context of UNDP activities in support of the Country Office, UNDP projects and UN agencies, focusing on the achievement of the following results:

- Contribution to the implementation of UNDP operational strategies in the areas of responsibility, ensuring full compliance of administrative activities with UN/UNDP rules, regulations, policies and strategies.

- Provision of inputs to the Country Office administrative business processes mapping and implementation of the internal standard operating procedures (SOPs).

- Provision of inputs to the preparation of the results-oriented workplans of the Procurement Unit.

Ensures effective procurement and logistical support in the context of UNDP activities in support of the Country Office, UNDP projects and UN agencies, focusing on the achievement of the following results:

- Creation of purchase orders for procurement.

- Support to the organization of procurement processes including preparation of Request for Quotation (RFQ), Invitations to Bid (ITB) or Requests for Proposal documents (RFP), receipt of quotations, bids or proposals, and their pre-liminary evaluation.

- Maintenance of the filing system ensuring safekeeping of confidential materials.

- Extraction of data from various internal and external sources and contribution to the implementation of sourcing strategy, including pre-qualification of individuals and firms that can supply the project requirements.

- Coordination between requisitioners and prospective bidders for queries and clarifications.

- Minutes of pre-bid conferences, as needed.

- Provision to requisitioners of canvas matrix or preliminary evaluation of the quotations/bids/proposals received.

- Summary of evaluation findings and results.

- Preparation of appropriate contract instruments, and obtention of signatures of supplier and proper authority in UNDP.

- Follow up on deadlines, commitments made, actions taken and coordination of collection and submission of procurement reports to Head of Unit.

- Assistance in the provision of information for audit.

- Provision of information for preparation of cost-recovery bills for the procurement services provided by UNDP to UNDP projects and UN agencies.

Supports travel management processes for the Country Office, UNDP projects and other agencies at their request, focusing on the achievement of the following results:

- Creation of purchase orders for travel.

- Process of travel authorization and travel claims in line with travel entitlements for staff, consultants, UN Officials and visitors, ensuring that travel arrangements follow the UN rules of most direct route and most competitive prices.

- Support Travel System briefs on issues related to travel such as administrative matters, visas information, security, procedures, support projects in solution of processes and best practices dissemination;

- Analyse of quotation received form travel agents and airlines companies under UN Policies and procedures;

- Support to follow-up with contracted travel agent to ensure provision of high-quality professional services and most competitive prices.

- Provision of information to travelling staff including on entitlements, travel route and hotel arrangements.

- Provides reports to improve the liaison with travel agency and airlines in term of confirm bookings, discuss excess baggage charges, etc. and issues tickets in a timely manner.

- Supports negotiations of low-cost fare arrangements with the travel Agency to obtain the benefits of travel cost savings for client Agencies;

- Supports in the registration and evaluation of the Travel Agency Services quality and SLA metrics;

- Preparation of routine correspondence, faxes, memoranda and reports in accordance with Country Office Standard Operating of Procedures (CO SOP).

- Reconciliation of settlements to be paid by the Finance Unit.

- Assistance in the provision of information for audit.

- Provision of information for preparation of cost-recovery bills for travel services provided by UNDP-to-UNDP projects and UN agencies.

Support knowledge building and knowledge sharing within the Country Office, focusing on the achievement of the following results:

- Participation in trainings of the operations/projects staff on procurement and travel issues.

- Contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

The Bureau for Management Services (BMS) is the central operations Bureau in UNDP that supports the organization in the provision of management services. Drawing on sound analytics and risk-management approach, BMS provides policy, oversight, advisory and transactional services and solutions for UNDP to achieve programme and development results. In doing so, it keeps pace with the evolving needs and expectations of development partners and international best practice through strengthening and innovating business operations.

The provision of client-focused, integrated management services is a key element of the BMS operating model. General Operations must present to UNDP stakeholders, partners and clients a holistic service and lead the promotion and implementation of continuous improvements in efficiency and productivity. This role ensures internal control, vendor coordination, and the delivery of high quality, compliant operational functions for the organization. It helps achieve that through a focus on optimizing service delivery; including cross-unit integration towards innovation, promotion of best practices, and client-oriented solutions.

Under the guidance and supervision of the Travel Manager (P4), the Travel Analyst is responsible for day-to-day management of travel activities and provides analytical support to the administration and monitoring of travel-related services ensuring high quality and accuracy of work in order to obtain the optimum travel services. He/she analyzes and interprets rules and guidelines regarding travel and entitlements and provides solutions to a wide spectrum of complex issues related to travel. The Travel Analyst ensures proper monitoring of travel expenditures and internal cost, as well as their timely and accurate billing, settlement and cost recovery. The Travel Analyst promotes a collaborative, client-focused, quality and results-oriented approach in the delivery of travel services. He/she works in close collaboration with the partner agencies, Regional Hubs, Programme and Operations Teams at HQ and in the field, and travel related vendors to exchange information and ensure consistent service delivery.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

1.) Substantively contribute to formulation and implementation of UNDP Travel strategies and policies

- Contribute to the development of travel category strategy, analysis, and policy formation, leveraging industry best practices and insights to drive continuous improvement and innovation.

- Ensures effective implementation of operational strategies and travel-related management processes.

- Analyze travel data and prepare regular and ad hoc robust travel reporting and insights. Identify trends and opportunities for travel program, as well as potential cost savings and process improvements based on analysis of travel data.

- Effectively communicate with UNDP personnel and partner agencies the end to end travel process, the logic and rationale for the importance and benefits of the travel policy and program

- Interpretation of UNDP's travel policy, the Staff Rules, administrative circulars and financial regulations and rules on travel-related matters; take action in the best interest of the Organization and manage exceptions to travel policy

2.) Oversees effective implementation and monitoring of travel-related management processes

- Coordination with travel related vendors to ensure provision of high-quality professional service and most competitive price.

- Develop and maintain appropriate training materials on travel management and processes for personnel to ensure regular delivery.

- Approval of Purchase Orders and Invoices related to UNall Travel Requests and Travel Claims to make sure they are in line with travel entitlements for personnel and meeting participants, and that the travel arrangement follow the UN rules at the most competitive prices.

- Serve as alternate focal person for Travel Services Section to support travel arrangements for Senior Officer and travelers requiring exceptional ticket approval, which may include work after hours.
